### Mudra
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegosis-6f46) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/luckiys/ethdenvermudraproject1028192) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/dcab808c1df24fea969e406400958cd5) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> We review, analyze, and suggest. You take action.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![WalletConnect](https://img.shields.io/badge/WalletConnect-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![openrouter](https://img.shields.io/badge/openrouter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Managing a DeFi portfolio today is either completely manual, driven by gut feeling and Twitter threads, or fully automated by bots that move your funds without your consent. Both approaches fail: one leads to panic decisions, the other to blind trust in opaque algorithms. Mudra sits in the middle. Three specialized AI agents work together to protect you: a Watcher that monitors real-time market conditions like volatility, sentiment, liquidity, and drawdowns; a Strategist that computes a multi-factor risk score and proposes strategies tailored to your specific goal, whether that's saving for a house or maximizing yield; and an Executor that only acts after you cryptographically sign your approval through your wallet. The AI never has custody of your funds and never makes a move without your explicit consent. Every recommendation and every action is logged immutably to Hedera Consensus Service, creating a verifiable audit trail that no one can rewrite. Mudra is built for holders who want data-driven portfolio decisions without giving up control, for DeFi users who need risk monitoring but don't have time to stare at charts, and for anyone who wants a provable on-chain record of why every trade was made.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was getting the AI reasoning layer to work reliably on a free tier. We initially used Google's Gemini API, but the free tier has a hard limit of 20 requests per day per model, and since each session run triggers multiple AI calls (goal interpretation, risk reasoning, and strategy explanation), we'd burn through the entire daily quota in about six runs. We tried throttling, serializing requests, and adding exponential backoff, but the fundamental quota limit couldn't be engineered around. The solution was switching to OpenRouter, which provides access to multiple free models through a single API, letting us fall back gracefully if one model is overloaded. The second major hurdle was getting risk tolerance settings to actually persist. Because the app uses Next.js with server-side rendering, the standard React pattern of initializing state from localStorage silently fails since localStorage doesn't exist on the server, so the saved value would get overwritten with the default on every page load. We fixed this by hydrating from localStorage inside a useEffect after the component mounts on the client. Finally, integrating Hedera's SDK for the immutable audit trail required careful handling of different key formats (ED25519 vs ECDSA) depending on whether we were using the native SDK path or the EVM contract path,

**Use of AI tools and agents**

Mudra uses a three-agent architecture where each AI agent has a single responsibility and they operate in a strict sequential pipeline. The Watcher agent runs first, pulling live market data from CoinGecko and sentiment indicators like the Fear and Greed Index, funding rates, and ATH drawdowns, then computes a structured risk signal for the user's portfolio. That signal is passed to the Strategist agent, which uses an LLM (currently served through OpenRouter) to interpret the user's natural language goal, such as "saving for a house" or "maximize yield aggressively," and classify it into a risk profile that adjusts how the five risk components (concentration, volatility, sentiment, liquidity, drawdown) are weighted. The Strategist then generates a strategy recommendation with multiple candidate plans at different risk levels, picks the one closest to the user's stated risk tolerance, and uses the LLM again to write a plain English explanation of its reasoning. The Executor agent sits idle until the user reviews the plan and cryptographically signs their approval through their wallet using EIP-712 typed data signing. Only after that signature is verified does the Executor act, logging the approved plan and execution to Hedera Consensus Service as an immutable audit trail. Each agent also gets minted as an iNFT on Hedera with its "brain" (identity, capabilities, and session context) uploaded to 0G decentralized storage, making the agents themselves verifiable on-chain artifacts rather than just backend processes.

**Futurllama**

Mudra fits the Futurllama track because it represents the frontier of AI-agent architecture applied to DeFi. Rather than a simple chatbot or single-model wrapper, Mudra deploys three autonomous AI agents that collaborate in a pipeline, each with its own on-chain identity as an iNFT, to monitor portfolios, generate risk-adjusted strategies using real LLM reasoning, and execute only after cryptographic human approval. It combines multiple cutting-edge primitives in one system: multi-agent coordination, natural language goal understanding, on-chain agent identity, immutable audit trails via Hedera Consensus Service, and a next-gen UI that translates complex risk math into plain English anyone can understand. This is not incremental improvement to existing DeFi tooling but a fundamentally new way for humans and AI to collaborate on financial decisions, where AI handles the analysis at superhuman speed and humans retain full sovereignty over every action.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

When the Executor approves a rebalance, Mudra calls AegisScheduler.sol which invokes the Hedera Schedule Service system contract precompile to create an on-chain scheduled token transfer. No backend cron job, no centralized scheduler. The schedule tracker monitors the full lifecycle from CREATED to PENDING to EXECUTED or EXPIRED, with real HashScan URLs for every transaction. This directly satisfies the bounty requirement of initiating scheduling from a smart contract using Hedera's native Schedule Service.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Mudra is a fully autonomous 3-agent system where each agent (Watcher, Strategist, Executor) has its own on-chain identity, reputation score, and trust badge attested immutably on Hedera Consensus Service. Agents earn reputation based on the accuracy of their recommendations, and the Watcher even places prediction market bets on strategy outcomes that are settled post-execution, all logged to HCS. This is exactly what the bounty asks for: autonomous agents that interact economically, build verifiable trust over time, and operate transparently on Hedera infrastructure.

**“No Solidity Allowed” - Hedera SDKs Only**

Mudra includes a completely separate audit path that uses zero Solidity and zero EVM. Using only the Hedera JavaScript SDK, it creates an HCS receipt topic for logging every strategy approval, rejection, and execution as a structured JSON message, and mints a fungible HTS loyalty token (AegisPoints) awarded to users on successful execution. Every receipt includes the session ID, plan hash, signer address, and timestamp, creating a full audit trail built entirely with Hedera's native SDK.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

Mudra uses the Skybox AI API to generate unique 360-degree panoramic environments for each agent based on their personality and current risk state. The Watcher gets a command center aesthetic, the Strategist gets a war room, and the Executor gets a vault. As risk levels change, the environments dynamically regenerate to reflect the portfolio state, giving each agent a visual spatial identity that goes beyond a profile card.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

When the Strategist recommends a rebalance or risk reduction, Mudra fetches real-time swap quotes from the Uniswap Trading API to show the user exactly what the trade would look like, including output amounts, price impact, and gas estimates. This turns the abstract recommendation into a concrete, actionable trade preview. The integration uses the official v1/quote endpoint with proper slippage tolerance and swapper configuration.

### AI Battle Royale
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-battle-royale-dc53) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ArshanKaudinya/agentBattleRoyale) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agentBattleRoyale.replit.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> How agents think through high risk survival.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI API](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Our Motivation
We've all seen the debates about whether LLMs can truly reason or just pattern-match. When models face actual stakes - elimination, resource scarcity, time pressure - how do they perform? That question felt more interesting than building another SaaS wrapper.
Most hackathon projects are "pay me for this tool." We wanted to build something that pushes into research territory while still being entertaining to watch. The idea of agents fighting for survival with visible reasoning seemed like the perfect intersection - scientifically interesting and genuinely fun.
What hooked us was the existential question: how does an LLM behave when "death" is on the line? When Claude is at 3% health with zone damage ticking, does it panic? Does it calculate odds? Does it make desperate moves or stay rational? These aren't questions you can answer with a chatbot demo.
Turns out watching agents balance survival instinct against aggression, seeing them develop emergent strategies we didn't program, and reading their reasoning as they make life-or-death decisions is genuinely fascinating. Every game tells a different story. That's what made this worth building.

## Research Value

Transparent adversarial reasoning under time pressure.
Traditional RL agents are black boxes - you see actions but not the decision-making process. LLMs give us interpretable strategic thinking in real-time competitive scenarios.

This system generates a unique dataset:
- Multi-agent spatial reasoning on constrained grids
- Resource competition and risk assessment traces
- Theory of mind under uncertainty (predicting opponent moves)
- Survival vs aggression trade-off decisions
- Response latency as gameplay factor


## Use Cases

AI Safety Research:
Study how models balance competing objectives (immediate survival vs long-term strategy), handle adversarial pressure, and reason about incomplete information.

Model Benchmarking:
Compare reasoning quality across frontier models in identical high-stakes scenarios. Response time becomes measurable advantage - faster inference = tactical edge.

Prompt Engineering Testing:
Stress-test system prompts under adversarial conditions. Does the model follow strategy instructions when pressured? Do safety guardrails hold under competitive framing?

Training Data Generation:
Corpus of decision traces for fine-tuning models on strategic reasoning, spatial planning, and real-time decision-making.


## What Makes It Novel

Response latency = gameplay mechanic. Faster models act first each turn, creating natural speed hierarchy. Gemini's 1.8s vs Llama's 3.5s becomes positioning advantage.
Full observability. Every agent sees complete battlefield state simultaneously, then decides in parallel. No information asymmetry - pure reasoning competition.
Emergent strategy. Agents develop playstyles: mages kite at optimal damage range, scouts exploit mobility, tanks force endgame slugfests. Not programmed - discovered through optimization.

**Challenges we ran into**

## The Walking Simulator Problem
First test game was 17 turns of agents just walking toward the center while slowly dying to zone damage. Zero combat. We realized agents had no incentive to fight - survival was the only goal. We fixed it by spawning agents inside the safe zone so they weren't panicking about zone damage, then added contested item spawns between them to force early skirmishes.

## Getting Agents to Understand Spatial Strategy
Agents kept making bizarre positioning choices - moving away from low-health targets, ignoring items 2 tiles away, running into corners. They didn't grasp the tactical layout. We had to redesign how we describe the battlefield in the prompt: instead of just listing coordinates, we added distance calculations ("target is 7 tiles away"), zone status ("you are INSIDE/OUTSIDE safe zone"), and item proximity. Suddenly they started playing smart - kiting at optimal ranges, grabbing nearby items, staying near zone center.

## Defining the Right Incentives
Early agents were too passive - they'd defend forever or just collect items without fighting. We needed to make aggression rewarding. Added first blood bonus (+20 HP), made items spawn in contested areas rather than random corners, gave kill credit in the combat log. Once agents saw that attacking low-health targets had clear payoff, they started taking calculated risks instead of playing ultra-safe.

## Prompt Timeouts
Claude kept timing out because prompts were too verbose - 500+ words of game state description. Agents were overthinking simple moves. We stripped prompts down to ~150 words with only essential info, used clear formatting with sections, added concrete examples of valid actions. Cut response times in half and eliminated most timeouts.

**Hackathon Prizes**

## The Problem
Building multi-agent AI systems normally takes weeks - training RL agents, setting up game engines, building infrastructure. We had 7 hours to make GPT, Sonnet and Haiku fight to the death with visible reasoning.  

## How We Built It
Instead of writing boilerplate, we focused on architecture design. We specified the system requirements - parallel LLM execution, stateless turn resolution, zone mechanics - and Claude Code generated the backend implementation in 15 minutes. Game state management, API orchestration, timeout handling all production-ready.
Early testing revealed a pacing problem: agents spent too long repositioning before combat started. We adjusted the spawn algorithm to place agents inside the initial safe zone and refined the zone shrink mechanics to force earlier engagement. Claude Code refactored the spawn system and zone logic, then we iterated in Replit's live preview.
The initial UI had arcade game aesthetics that didn't match our research dashboard vision. We redesigned for a professional look - three-column layout, proper typography hierarchy, semantic color coding, interactive combat log. Claude Code implemented the complete redesign including 800+ lines of responsive CSS.
## What We Got
Complete battle royale in 7 hours with emergent strategic behavior. Mages maintain optimal damage range, scouts exploit mobility for hit-and-run tactics. Every match produces different outcomes.
The system surfaces agent reasoning in real-time. You see Claude calculating survival odds while GPT evaluates kill opportunities. The agents generate contextual commentary - aggressive when attacking, desperate when cornered.
Live play-by-play commentary, agent trash talk based on game state, transparent decision-making showing strategic thinking, interactive spectator controls. Deployed to production on Replit.

**The problem it solves**

Sukrit addresses the growing mental health challenges in academic institutions by making emotional support **accessible, safe, and stigma-free** for everyone in the ecosystem.

Students often hesitate to seek help due to fear of judgment, lack of awareness, or limited access to counselling services. Sukrit provides a private digital space where students can track their well-being, communicate confidentially with counsellors, and receive early support before issues escalate.

Teachers and counsellors, who are responsible for supporting others, frequently experience burnout themselves. Sukrit acknowledges this gap by offering them structured wellness support and a secure platform for communication and collaboration.

For institutions, understanding mental health trends is difficult without violating privacy. Sukrit simplifies this by providing **anonymous, aggregated insights** that help institutions identify patterns, allocate resources, and take preventive action—without exposing individual identities.

Overall, Sukrit makes mental wellness support easier, safer, and more ethical by:
- Reducing stigma around seeking help  
- Protecting user privacy by design  
- Enabling early intervention instead of crisis response  
- Helping institutions act responsibly without surveillance  

By integrating trust, privacy, and accessibility, Sukrit improves how mental wellness is supported in academic environments.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I faced while building Sukrit was **handling sensitive data securely while developing fast**. Since the platform deals with mental wellness information, even small mistakes could lead to privacy risks. For example, during early development, I accidentally committed a database connection string to the repository, which GitHub flagged as a leaked secret. I immediately revoked and rotated the credentials, removed the secret from the codebase, rewrote the Git history, and enforced strict use of environment variables. This experience reinforced the importance of treating security as a first-class concern.

Another challenge was **designing role-based access control** for students, teachers, counsellors, and institutions. Managing different permissions across dashboards and APIs required careful separation of logic and consistent validation. I addressed this by clearly defining role checks at the API level and keeping frontend access strictly aligned with backend authorization.

I also faced hurdles in **balancing privacy with analytics**. Institutions needed meaningful insights without exposing individual identities. I solved this by aggregating data at the database level and ensuring no personally identifiable information was returned in analytics queries.

Overall, these challenges helped shape Sukrit into a more secure, ethical, and well-structured platform.

**Best Innovation**

Sukrit fits strongly into the **Best Innovation track** because it introduces a **system-level innovation** in how mental wellness is approached within academic institutions.

Rather than building a generic mental health app, Sukrit redesigns the **entire support ecosystem** by bringing students, teachers, counsellors, and institutions onto a single platform , while strictly preserving privacy. This multi-role architecture itself is innovative, as it reflects how real academic systems function, not just individual users.

A key innovation is Sukrit’s **privacy-first-by-design approach**. User identities remain anonymous by default, sensitive data is never exposed in analytics, and trust is enforced technically rather than through policy promises. This makes mental health support safer and more approachable.

Sukrit also introduces a **mood-aware adaptive interface**, where the UI dynamically changes based on a user’s emotional state using principles of color psychology. This transforms the platform from a static tool into an emotionally responsive environment.

Additionally, Sukrit’s **ethically bounded AI companion** provides empathetic, non-clinical support without replacing professionals but showing responsible innovation.

Overall, Sukrit stands out in the Best Innovation track by combining **empathetic design, privacy-first architecture, ethical AI, and real-world scalability** into a cohesive, socially impactful system.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves
Reminisce bridges the terrifying gap between memory loss and daily life for individuals with early-stage Alzheimer's and Dementia.

Currently, patients rely on static notes or overwhelmed caregivers to navigate their day. When memory fails during a conversation or a walk, confusion escalates into panic instantly. Existing tools are passive—they store information but don't actively help when it matters most.


Reminisce changes this by acting as a proactive "Second Brain":


Restoring Social Dignity: Instead of asking "Who are you?" repeatedly, the patient sees a loved one, and our AR Vision instantly whispers, "This is Sarah, your daughter". It allows users to recognize faces and relationships in real-time, preserving their confidence during social interactions.

Breaking Confusion Loops: Patients often get stuck in repetitive questioning loops. Our conversational AI detects these patterns and gently guides the conversation forward (e.g., "You just asked about lunch; Sarah said she made pasta"), reducing frustration for both the patient and the family.

Preventing Panic Attacks: The system monitors vocal stress levels. If it detects disorientation or anxiety (Sundowning), it automatically triggers "Reality Grounding"—playing familiar music or showing reassuring family photos to calm the user down.

Relieving Caregiver Burnout: Family members can finally breathe easier. The web dashboard allows them to upload memories remotely, track the patient's "Confusion Levels" in real-time, and get immediate alerts if the patient wanders outside a safe zone.

> Catch Ghost Logins Before They Haunt Your Security

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

While building GhostLogin Detector, I faced several real-world development hurdles that tested both debugging skills and architectural thinking.

1️⃣ Auth0 JWT Verification Issues

Auth0 ke JWT tokens ko Spring Boot me verify karte time repeated 401 Unauthorized errors aa rahe the.
Fix: Proper issuer, audience, and JWKS configuration set kiya — then CORS rules adjust kiye. After that, the security layer became stable.

2️⃣ MongoDB Not Saving / Not Showing Database

Local MongoDB initially events store nahi kar raha tha, and show dbs me database dikh nahi raha tha.
Fix: MongoDB creates databases lazily — only after actual documents are inserted. After the first LoginEvent insert, the DB started appearing.

3️⃣ Device Fingerprinting Logic Conflicts

Different browsers same headers return kar rahe the, jisse device mismatch false positives generate ho rahe the.
Fix: More stable fingerprint hash build kiya using:

User-Agent

IP

Screen resolution (if available)

Browser entropy
This reduced mismatch noise significantly.

4️⃣ CORS & Frontend Communication Errors

React (5173) → Spring Boot (8080) me CORS block aa raha tha.
Fix: Global CORS config add kiya with allowedOrigin = http://localhost:5173.

5️⃣ API Rate Limit on GeoIP Lookup

Free GeoIP API cap hit ho raha tha testing ke time.
Fix: Added fallback & caching to reduce calls.

6️⃣ Cloud Storage Confusion (AWS → Cloudflare R2)

AWS on-boarding ke time card verification issue aaya, so I switched to Cloudflare R2, which works with S3-compatible APIs.
Fix: Backend storage service ko S3-compatible endpoints pe migrate kiya — no code rewrite needed.

These challenges helped refine the architecture, improve debugging hygiene, and build a much more reliable security system.

💡 The Problem It Solves

GhostLogin Detector tackles one of the biggest and most ignored digital risks today—

✔ Unauthorized Logins
✔ Stolen Credentials
✔ Account Takeovers
✔ Suspicious Device Access

Most platforms don’t notify users when:

Someone logs in from a new device

Login happens from another country

Time of login is abnormal

Browser fingerprint doesn’t match

Account behavior suddenly changes

GhostLogin Detector solves this by:

🔐 1. Monitoring Every Login Event

It tracks device details, location, IP, browser, OS — all in real time.

📍 2. Detecting Abnormal Behaviour Automatically

The risk engine checks:

Geo-location mismatch

Device mismatch

Time anomaly

IP reputation

Browser fingerprint change

And calculates a risk score (0–100).

🚨 3. Alerting Users Instantly

Suspicious login?
→ User immediately gets a warning notification.

🧠 4. Helping Platforms Prevent Account Takeovers

Companies can embed this system to catch:

Session hijacking

Credential stuffing

Password sharing

Unauthorized access

📊 5. Providing Security Analytics Dashboard

Admins get realtime analytics like:

Devices used

High-risk login count

Daily login activity

Suspicious trends

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

The biggest challenge was building a reliable risk detection engine. IP changes and geolocation mismatches triggered too many false alerts. I solved this by adding:

Geo tolerance ranges

Last-seen device memory

Time-based risk adjustments

Another challenge was integrating Auth0 authentication into Spring Boot. Incorrect issuer/audience values caused JWT failures. After reconfiguring the security layer and validating tokens with the JWKS endpoint, the system started working smoothly.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zerdinals-2f2d) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://zerdinals.com/mint) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Zcash inscriptions

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Zcash ecosystem currently lacks a native, trustless way to create, store, and trade digital assets such as artwork, tokens, and on-chain metadata. While many blockchains have vibrant inscription and NFT ecosystems, Zcash has no standardized infrastructure for creators or developers to mint digital assets directly on-chain.

This results in several problems:

No unified standard for on-chain digital assets on Zcash
Developers cannot easily build apps that rely on NFTs, inscriptions, or fungible token primitives.

No accessible tools for creators
Artists, builders, and communities have no platform to mint or showcase digital items using Zcash’s privacy-preserving features.

Missing ecosystem layer for innovation
Without inscriptions, Zcash lacks an important cultural and economic layer that boosts activity, user engagement, and tooling development.

No permissionless tokenization for communities
Projects cannot launch tokens, collectibles, or membership passes natively on the Zcash blockchain.

Zerdinals.com solves this by introducing the first full-featured inscription layer for Zcash, enabling anyone to mint digital art, metadata, and fungible tokens directly on-chain—creating a foundation for builders, creators, and new markets within the Zcash ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an inscription protocol on Zcash came with several unexpected technical challenges:

1. No Taproot Support on Zcash

Zcash does not have Taproot, which is commonly used in other chains (like Bitcoin) for inscriptions.
To overcome this, we engineered a custom approach using P2SH scripts and injected the inscription data into the reveal input. This required designing our own script structure and validation logic from scratch.

2. Lack of Developer Documentation

The Zcash ecosystem has very limited developer resources for advanced features like script manipulation, raw transactions, or indexing. We had to rely mostly on reading node source code and experimenting manually to understand how to safely embed and extract inscription data.

3. No Mature Libraries for Our Use Case

Existing libraries were incomplete or outdated, especially for:

raw transaction building

script decoding

advanced PSBT workflows
We had to implement many custom utilities to handle signing, encoding, hashing, and script parsing.

4. No Suitable Block Parser / Indexer

There was no indexer capable of reading blocks at scale and extracting inscription-specific data.
So we built our own high-performance bulk block parser, capable of scanning the entire chain, detecting inscription events, and indexing them for our marketplace and explorer.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our main challenges was building and demonstrating a real-time surveillance and escalation workflow within the limited hackathon time.

Instead of depending on a full physical CCTV infrastructure, we created a simulated CCTV/event engine that generates safety events and sends them to the control-room dashboard. We also had to make sure that the user-side interface and security dashboard clearly communicated the changing alert status.

We overcame these challenges by separating the system into independent frontend and backend components and using simulated events to demonstrate the complete **Sense → Verify → Escalate** workflow reliably during the demo.

**The problem it solves**

SafeHer addresses situations where women may feel unsafe but cannot actively reach for their phone or call for help.

It provides a proactive safety system that combines a user-side safety interface with a security control-room dashboard. SafeHer follows a **Sense → Verify → Escalate** approach: it detects potentially unsafe situations, verifies the event using contextual signals, and escalates the alert to the appropriate security personnel when necessary.

This helps security teams respond faster while reducing the need for the person at risk to manually trigger an emergency alert.

**Headless Checkout Blocked:** Because the test cards are currently failing, my end-to-end sandbox flow is blocked. My backend is fully built to securely extract the 16-digit Prava token and inject it into a headless Stagehand browser, but the headless script physically cannot fire until the Prava passkey checkout succeeds.

> Your interior designer, just a text away

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was not the room design model. It was getting the final purchase to work across stores. Most familiar merchants we explored still do not expose agent-ready catalog and checkout infrastructure, and Prava binds each approval to one exact merchant and amount, so a mixed cart cannot become one payment. We tested mandates, standard payment sessions and one-time cards, then traced failed callbacks and payment states until we confirmed this was an architecture constraint rather than a bug in our checkout code. We moved product discovery to Shopify UCP, where Toki could find live products with the details needed for checkout, and kept purchases from different stores sequential for now. A true multi-merchant cart with one approval is the next problem we want to solve.

**The problem it solves**

We recently moved into a new house where the basic furniture was already in place, but every room still felt bare and temporary. The space was functional, yet it had none of our personality and did not really feel like home. We knew the mood we wanted, but turning that vague idea into a room we could picture and products that would actually fit involved too much guesswork. So we built Toki, an interior design assistant that is always a text away. Send it a photo and talk to it normally. Toki helps shape the idea, shows how it could look in your actual room, finds products that match, and takes your final choices through checkout.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Through Prava, Toki creates a payment session for the exact merchant, product, and amount the user selected. The user reviews the purchase from iMessage and confirms it securely with Face ID or a passkey. We completed successful Visa sandbox transactions and return the payment result to the same conversation without exposing card details in the chat.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Toki already runs as a hosted service with a public iMessage number, a Vercel website, and a VPS backend. New users can text the number, share a room photo, explore designs, receive live products, and reach a working checkout without installing anything. We also built isolated conversation state, signed webhooks, retries, and duplicate-event protection so multiple people can use it reliably.

**OpenAI**

OpenAI provides the reasoning layer behind Toki. The model understands the room photo and conversation, develops a design direction, and decides when to visualize an idea, search for products, or prepare checkout using constrained tools. Prices, merchants, and payment details come from our backend rather than the model, which keeps the conversation flexible without letting it invent commercial information.

**iMessage Agent**

Linq is Toki’s main interface, not a notification layer. The entire experience begins with an inbound iMessage and continues through room photos, natural conversation, typing states, generated previews, product cards, and checkout links in the same thread. Realtime Linq webhooks let Toki respond to each message while preserving the user’s room, preferences, and current design direction.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

We designed Toki around something people already do: send a room photo to a friend and talk through ideas. There are no forms, filters, or new apps to learn. The conversation, visualizations, product cards, and purchase updates all stay inside iMessage, with Face ID or a passkey used only to approve the exact payment.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Toki turns a room photo and an iMessage conversation into a complete shopping journey. We help the user shape a design, preview it in their actual room, find live Shopify products, visualize the final choices, and complete checkout through Prava. The agent decides when to use each tool, while the user remains in control of every design and purchase decision.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem**: Traditional GitHub searches rely heavily on exact keyword matching, stargazers, or fork counts. High-quality newer projects or highly specific niche libraries often get buried deep within search results.

**Solution**: RepoGenius uses semantic vector embeddings (via ChromaDB) and LLM-powered query parsing (RAG) to understand the intent behind your search, surfacing contextual matches even if they don't share exact keywords. it can be used as a chrome extension at the time of repo searching in git hub

**Challenges we ran into**

Hybrid Ranking: Balancing semantic similarity with live GitHub metrics (stars/forks) for optimal results.

 API Latency: Minimizing delays while fetching live GitHub data and generating LLM explanations simultaneously.

 Intent Mapping: Training embedding models to recognize complex, abstract queries (e.g., "geofencing") without exact keyword matches.

 UI Integration: Overcoming Chrome Extension API constraints to smoothly embed results directly into GitHub's native interface.

**AI/ML**

this uses the RAG system . which is done through cosine similarity match

> Report Problems, See Solutions

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Existing civic platforms suffer from major inefficiencies that limit their effectiveness. Most systems focus only on collecting complaints but lack proper follow-through, which results in many issues remaining unresolved or ignored. They also fail to prioritize problems effectively, meaning urgent issues may not receive timely attention. Additionally, there is very little transparency in the resolution process, leaving citizens unaware of what action is being taken.
This creates a gap between citizens and authorities where problems are repeatedly reported but not properly managed. There is also no system to cluster similar complaints, optimize resources, or ensure accountability.
Zero Civic Sense solves this by transforming complaints into structured, prioritized, and actionable tasks, ensuring real-time tracking, user validation, and efficient resolution through prioritization, clustering, and escalation.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building the platform, I faced several technical and design challenges:
Two-Sided System Design: Managing both citizen and admin interfaces while keeping data consistent and synchronized.
Real-Time Updates: Implementing accurate complaint tracking and status updates across the system.
Priority Algorithm: Designing a system to rank issues based on urgency, location, and engagement.
Geolocation & Clustering: Handling map-based data and grouping nearby complaints using location services.
Media Handling: Managing uploads (images/audio) and integrating storage efficiently.
Third-Party Integrations: Working with external services like maps and cloud APIs.
Scalable Backend Structure: Maintaining a clean modular architecture (Routes, Controllers, Services).
Development Workflow: Coordinating multiple tools and environments smoothly.

> N‑Dimensional Liquidity AMM

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Stablecoin liquidity today is highly fragmented across different trading pairs and pools, which leads to inefficient capital usage, higher slippage, and unnecessary complexity for both traders and liquidity providers.

Most existing AMMs (like Curve Finance) support only a small number of tokens per pool (typically up to 3). This creates a major scalability issue:

> If we want to support thousands of stablecoins in the future (e.g., 10,000+), the same tokens would need to exist across many separate pools.

### What goes wrong in that scenario:
- **Liquidity gets fragmented** across multiple pools  
- The **same asset appears in different pools**, splitting depth  
- **Routing becomes complex** and inefficient  
- **Slippage increases**, especially when individual pools lack sufficient liquidity  

---

### Our approach

We introduce a **multi-asset AMM with liquidity concentration**, where many stablecoins share liquidity inside a single unified pool.

Instead of spreading liquidity thin across many pools, we:
- **Concentrate liquidity around the expected price range (≈ $1)**  
- Allow **multiple assets to share the same liquidity surface**  
- Maintain **deep liquidity where it matters most**  

This combines ideas from:
- Stablecoin-focused AMMs (like Curve)
- Concentrated liquidity (like Uniswap v3)

---

### What people can use it for:
- **Ultra low-slippage swaps** between many stablecoins  
- **Higher capital efficiency** for LPs via concentrated liquidity  
- **Single-pool liquidity management** instead of fragmented positions  
- **Consistent pricing** across a large set of correlated assets  
- **Future-proof infrastructure** for thousands of stablecoins  

---

### Why it matters:
As the number of stablecoins grows, traditional designs break down. This approach keeps liquidity **unified, concentrated, and efficient**, even at massive scale.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

The hardest part wasn’t just building the AMM—it was making the math work **at scale**.

### The real problem:
Designing an invariant that works for **thousands of assets (e.g., 10,000 stablecoins)** is extremely complex:
- Computation grows quickly with more assets  
- Maintaining stability across all tokens becomes harder  
- Finding the *right parameters* for pricing and liquidity distribution is non-trivial  

### What I actually did:
- Instead of jumping to 10,000 assets, I **scaled the system down to ~5 tokens/pools for the demo**  
- Even at this size, **tuning the math and parameters was difficult**  
- Small changes in values would break stability or give unrealistic pricing  

### The main difficulty:
- Figuring out **correct coefficients / invariant behavior**  
- Ensuring swaps stayed stable near peg  
- Avoiding situations where the pool behaves unpredictably  

### Key takeaway:
Even a small-scale version shows how hard this problem is. Scaling from 5 → 10,000 assets isn’t linear—it requires **serious optimization, better mathematical modeling, and likely new approaches to computation**.

**Best Build on Algorand**

## Why We Built on Algorand

We chose Algorand because it gives us the right base for a trading and liquidity protocol where speed, cost, and reliability matter on every transaction.

### Key benefits for TaurusSwap

- **Fast finality**  
  Transactions settle quickly and are final in seconds, which makes swaps and liquidity actions feel responsive.

- **Low, predictable fees**  
  Fees stay very low and stable, so users can trade, rebalance, and manage LP positions without high friction.

- **High throughput for active markets**  
  Algorand is designed for frequent on-chain activity, which helps support AMM interactions at scale.

- **No forking uncertainty**  
  Deterministic finality reduces rollback/reorg risk, which is important for accurate pool accounting and user trust.

- **Strong security model**  
  The network’s Pure Proof-of-Stake design provides strong security while staying efficient.

- **Good fit for real-world payments and stable assets**  
  Algorand has a strong ecosystem for tokenized assets and stable-value transfers, which aligns with our multi-token pool design.

- **Developer-friendly stack**  
  The tooling and SDK support make it practical to build and ship performant on-chain products.

In short: Algorand helps us deliver a DeFi UX that is fast, affordable, and dependable.

**The problem it solves**

In most cases, different tools are used for teamwork. For instance, there is the use of Google Slides for creating slides, the use of Zoom or Discord for communication, and the use of messaging apps for the sharing of ideas. However, the use of different tools for teamwork is a barrier to the efficient teamwork that is required for presentations.

The use of different tools for teamwork, especially during brainstorming, is a distraction, hence affecting productivity.

CollabCast helps to address the challenges that are associated with the use of different tools for teamwork. This is due to the fact that the application has integrated features for creating, editing, and presenting slides, hence facilitating teamwork.

One of the key challenges we had to deal with was the implementation of the real-time collaboration functionality for multiple users.

In order to synchronize the changes made to the slides by different users, we had to implement the WebSocket protocol with the help of Django Channels. One of the key challenges we were dealing with was to ensure that the updates made by any single user were reflected instantaneously for all the users.

Another challenge we had to deal with was the implementation of the cursor functionality for the users without any performance issues.

CollabCast meets the requirements of the Requestly Creative Use Challenge as it represents a creative application of modern web technologies to develop a collaborative productivity application.

In the application, the developer utilizes WebSockets through the Django Channels library to achieve a collaborative experience for users working on a presentation application. This involved effective handling of network communication to achieve the application’s goals.

CollabCast represents a creative application of modern web technologies to develop a collaborative productivity application. By incorporating features of real-time collaboration, voice chat, and cloud deployment, the developer demonstrates the potential for creating effective web applications to enhance productivity through collaboration.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegisaiscamdetector-d42b) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://aegis-ai-scamappdetector.lovable.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rv5PSrBOF74?si=GIIXie9aK2lT0PD8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AegisAI – Your digital Shield

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People install mobile apps every day without knowing whether they are safe or potentially harmful. Many scam apps disguise themselves as legitimate services and can steal personal data, track user activity, or cause financial loss through fake investments, gambling platforms, or predatory loan schemes. It is difficult for users to manually analyze permissions, reviews, and risk signals before installing an app.

This system helps users quickly scan and analyze apps to detect possible scams, risky behavior, or unsafe permissions. By combining AI analysis, review insights, and risk classification, it simplifies security checks and provides a clear risk level for each app. This allows users to make safer installation decisions, avoid fraudulent apps, and protect their data, privacy, and money.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was collecting reliable app data and reviews to determine whether an app is safe or potentially harmful. Many apps have mixed reviews, and some legitimate apps may appear suspicious due to a few negative comments. This made it difficult to build an accurate risk classification system.

Another challenge was integrating the scanning system with the Android app environment. Detecting installed apps, analyzing their permissions, and displaying meaningful results in a clean UI required careful handling of Android permissions and background processes.

To overcome these issues, we refined the dataset, improved the filtering logic for reviews and ratings, and optimized the scanning process to present clear risk levels such as Safe, Moderate, or High Risk.

### diversion-hackaut
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/diversionhackaut-26ea) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/RitochitGhosh/diversion-hackaut) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://diversion-hackaut.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1169262573?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Multitenant SaaS with Human In The Loop

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![RabbitMQ](https://img.shields.io/badge/RabbitMQ-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

we were planning a trip to Zero Point, Sikkim. We opened ChatGPT and asked: "How do I get the permits to visit Zero Point?" It gave us a beautifully written,
   confident answer — completely generic. It told us to "contact local authorities" and "check the official tourism website." We checked the official site. It hadn't been
  updated since 2019, had broken links, and zero conversational ability.

  We were stuck between two broken extremes: AI that's smart but blind to local truth, and official sources that are accurate but dead on arrival.

  That's when it clicked. Every domain — travel, legal, medical, HR, education — has the same crisis. Organizations have the knowledge, but it's locked in documents, in
  people's heads, in outdated PDFs. And general AI hallucinates when it ventures into that territory without grounding.

  ReviewIQ is the bridge. It lets any organization — a Sikkim tourism board, a law firm, a hospital, a university — deploy their own AI assistant that:
  - Speaks conversationally like ChatGPT
  - Draws from their verified knowledge base (uploaded docs, manuals, policies)
  - Searches the live web when needed
  - Has every AI response reviewed by a human expert before it reaches the user

  This Human-in-the-Loop design means the answer about Zero Point permits would come from actual permit officers validating an AI draft — not a hallucination dressed in
  confidence.

  Multi-disciplinary scalability:
  The same architecture works for a medical clinic (patients ask symptoms → doctor reviews AI draft → verified answer), a law firm (client asks about a case → paralegal
  reviews → response), a university admissions desk, a government grievance portal, or an enterprise internal knowledge hub. The abstraction is universal: domain knowledge +
  AI speed + human trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Building the RAG + Web Pipeline**
Getting RAG to work reliably was harder than expected. We started by storing embeddings as JSON strings in a text column and doing in-memory cosine similarity — it worked but was slow and fragile. We migrated to pgvector which required raw SQL via $executeRawUnsafe since Prisma can't handle vector writes natively. On top of that, a subtle infinite loop in our text chunker kept crashing the server with RangeError: Invalid array length — the chunk start pointer never advanced correctly past the overlap window.

**Implementing the Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer**
Designing the HITL flow meant the AI draft had to be fast enough that reviewers weren't waiting, but good enough that they weren't rewriting everything. Balancing model speed, output quality, and the review UI state — making sure edits, approvals, and rejections all propagated correctly across the system — took a lot of iteration to get right.

**RabbitMQ Integration with Graceful Fallback**
Wiring up RabbitMQ for the notification and event pipeline was straightforward in isolation, but making it resilient in a multi-tenant setup was not. We also needed the system to keep working even when RabbitMQ wasn't available, so we built a publisher that silently falls back to direct DB writes when the AMQP connection is down.

**Gemini API**

# How This Project Fits the Track

We built a platform where AI assists — but never decides alone. Every response generated by Gemini goes through a human review layer before it reaches the end user. That's the core of the product: using AI to handle the heavy lifting of drafting, routing, and retrieving context, while keeping a human accountable for the final answer.

Gemini powers the entire AI pipeline, and we chose it deliberately — not just because of the track.

---

## Why We Chose Gemini

**Multimodal by design**
Users often attach images alongside their queries — a photo of a permit form, a medical report, a damaged product. Rather than making a separate vision API call, Gemini handles text and images together natively in a single request using `base64 inlineData` parts. This kept our pipeline clean and our latency low.

**`gemini-embedding-001` for better RAG precision**
Most embedding models treat indexing and querying the same way. `gemini-embedding-001` doesn't — it lets you specify `TaskType.RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT` when storing chunks and `TaskType.RETRIEVAL_QUERY` when searching. That distinction meaningfully improved how accurately we retrieved relevant context from tenant knowledge bases.

**`gemini-2.5-flash` for the right speed-quality balance**
Our human-in-the-loop flow needs AI drafts that are fast enough that reviewers aren't left waiting, and good enough that they aren't rewriting from scratch. Flash hits that sweet spot — quick responses without sacrificing the quality that makes the draft actually useful.

**Free tier that held up under real usage**
For a hackathon demo, reliability matters. Gemini's free quota was generous enough that we rarely hit rate limits. We built exponential backoff retry logic anyway — but it barely fired.

**One API for the entire pipeline**
Routing, drafting, final generation, and embeddings all run through a single Google AI client. No switching between providers, no managing multiple API keys, no separate billing accounts. It simplified the architecture considerably.

**ElevenLabs**

**We added voice to ReviewIQ using ElevenLabs — two directions, one API key.**

Speak your question, and ElevenLabs transcribes it into the query box. Get your answer, hit play, and it reads it back to you in a natural voice. No typing, no reading walls of text.

One thing we were careful about: the API key never touches the browser. All voice calls route through our own backend, so we stay in control of rate limiting and security.

The reason this matters for ReviewIQ specifically — legal, medical, technical users are often on the move or thinking out loud. Voice just fits how they actually work.

**Auth0**

**Auth0 handles login. We handle the rest.**

We didn't write a single line of auth logic. Auth0 manages login, logout, and sessions — and hands us a verified user ID on every request. We take that ID, look up their role in our database (Admin, Reviewer, or User), and that drives everything they can or can't do.

No password hashing, no session headaches. We just asked "who is this?" and built on top of the answer.

### SynthChoice
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/synthchoice-2f37) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shero4/synthchoice) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://synthchoice.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/72896b78b68d45958e51911269c87988) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Simulate minds, Predict decisions.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redux-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![Simulator](https://img.shields.io/badge/Simulator-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional conjoint analysis (the gold standard for market research) costs $15k-$50k and takes weeks. You need to recruit real people, design surveys, wait for responses. Most startups and small teams just skip it.

SynthChoice does the same thing in minutes using AI-powered synthetic personas.

**What you can do:**

- Test how different customer segments react to your product vs competitors. Simulate 500 tech-savvy millennials choosing between MacBook, ThinkPad, and Framework laptops.
- Understand price sensitivity. How does a budget-conscious parent react to $999 vs $1299?
- Figure out which features actually matter. Does battery life beat screen quality for remote workers?
- Compare across demographics. See how an INTJ in Bangalore decides differently from an ESFP in New York.

**How it works:**

1. Define your experiment with alternatives (products/services) and their features
2. Configure synthetic agents with personality types, locations, traits
3. Watch agents make decisions in a visual SimWorld (think Gather Town meets market research)
4. Get preference shares, segment breakdowns, and the reasoning behind each choice

The visual simulation makes abstract data tangible. You can literally watch an agent walk to the MacBook shop, pick it up, and leave while explaining "I chose this for the M3 chip and build quality."

**Challenges we ran into**

### Building the Gather Town / Pokemon vibe

We wanted agents to feel alive, not just API responses. This meant building a 2D world with procedural buildings, animated characters, and product sprites that appear on shops.

The hard part: generating product sprites dynamically. Each alternative (like "MacBook Pro 14") needs a pixel-art sprite that shows up on its building.

We built a pipeline:
1. Web search for a product image using an AI agent
2. Fetch and convert to base64
3. Send to Gemini 2.5 Flash with a prompt that generates a 2x2 sprite sheet
4. Post-process to normalize colors and enforce grid alignment

This runs in parallel for all products. Buildings appear instantly, sprites pop in as they generate. Feels like loading into a game.

### Rolling window concurrency

With 100+ agents, we couldn't spawn all at once (lag) or run sequentially (slow). Needed a rolling window where ~10 agents are active at any time.

First attempt used `Promise.race()` but would deadlock when the queue emptied at the wrong moment. Rewrote it to a semaphore pattern where each agent completion triggers the next spawn. Now agents flow smoothly through the world.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Built almost entirely with Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.5):

- Full-stack architecture: Next.js 16, Firebase, Redux, PixiJS
- LLM orchestration layer that routes to Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter
- 700+ lines of PixiJS game logic for the SimWorld
- Rolling-window experiment runner with error recovery
- Modular prompt system for agent decision-making

The whole codebase (~15k lines) was developed in conversation with Claude, from architecture to debugging race conditions.

### Pulse
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pulse-75ec) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://pulse-two-sand.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Volatility Has a Pattern.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square) ![Thetanuts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Thetanuts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Crypto options markets have matured fast. Onchain options volume now reaches billions in monthly notional, and protocols like Thetanuts already provide the core infrastructure: strikes, expiries, vaults, and yield strategies. From a technical standpoint, the market works.

The problem is not access — it is reaction time.

In liquid options markets, pricing inefficiencies are extremely short-lived. Implied volatility can shift 5–15% within minutes, skew imbalances appear and disappear in under 30 seconds, and yield opportunities are quickly arbitraged away. For human traders, this creates a structural disadvantage: by the time they analyze the data, the opportunity is already gone.

Today, traders are forced to manually interpret fragmented signals:

- IV charts in one tab
- skew tables in another
- price action and yield metrics elsewhere

This cognitive load makes consistent, real-time decision-making almost impossible, even for experienced traders.

Protocols like Thetanuts expose raw options primitives, but they do not explain what matters right now. Traders see data, not decisions. As a result, most users either react too late or avoid options entirely due to complexity and timing risk.

Pulse solves this by acting as a real-time intelligence layer on top of Thetanuts.

Instead of asking users to analyze charts and Greeks, Pulse continuously monitors live onchain options data and detects statistically meaningful deviations, not surface-level price movement. When an opportunity appears, users see a clear, time-bound signal — not abstract metrics.

What users interact with is:

- volatility crush alerts
- mispriced options signals
- yield anomalies
- momentum-based setups

All already filtered, timed, and executable through Thetanuts.

Pulse does not make users learn options first.
It allows them to act correctly before the market reprices.

This problem only exists onchain:

- data is public and composable
- execution is permissionless
- settlement is instant

Pulse doesn’t replace traders.
It removes the latency between market behavior and human action.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was signal noise. Onchain options data fluctuates constantly, and early versions of Pulse produced too many alerts that were statistically insignificant. We solved this by introducing rolling baselines and deviation thresholds, ensuring signals only trigger on structural market shifts, not random volatility.

Another challenge was balancing real-time accuracy with performance. Polling data too frequently caused UI lag, while slower updates killed timing precision. We addressed this by batching critical metrics and refreshing them every two seconds, allowing Pulse to remain responsive without missing short-lived opportunities.

Finally, not every detected signal was immediately executable. Some opportunities failed due to liquidity depth or strike availability on Thetanuts. To fix this, we added a validation layer that checks protocol constraints before surfacing any signal, ensuring every alert users see can be acted on instantly.

**Thetanuts Finance Track**

Thetanuts offers powerful onchain options infrastructure, but options trading is still too complex for most users. Pulse makes Thetanuts simpler, more accessible, and more engaging by turning complex options data into clear, real-time signals.

Instead of charts and Greeks, users see actionable insights like volatility drops, mispriced options, and yield opportunities. AI helps surface these signals at the right time, so users don’t need deep options knowledge to get started.

Pulse uses an intuitive, real-time UI with countdowns and one-click execution, making options feel fast and understandable, not intimidating. This naturally supports engagement loops such as time-limited opportunities and repeat interactions.

Every signal and execution in Pulse is powered directly by Thetanuts smart contracts. Pulse acts as the intelligence and experience layer on top of Thetanuts, helping bring onchain options to everyday users.

### Orbitum
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/orbitum-0bbe) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/orbitum-hackathon) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.canva.com/design/DAG_5VnEBr8/QLSFdr2xabg_o2dBUA23JQ/view?utm_content=DAG_5VnEBr8&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h570ad53028) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5VX1Yvlv9Vk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Indonesian Sovereign Bonds Accessible to Everyone

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![nestjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/nestjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cobo Wallet](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cobo%20Wallet-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem (Market Gap)**
Indonesia has the largest Muslim market globally, yet retail access to high-yield (5%+), Shariah-compliant government bonds is restricted by high entry barriers and complex traditional brokerage processes.

Yield Gap: 5% annual returns in Indonesia vs. 2-3% globally.

Accessibility: Demand is 3x supply (Green Sukuk), yet retail investors are underserved.

**The Solution (Orbitum on Base)**
Orbitum tokenizes Indonesian Sovereign Funds and Sukuk on Base, lowering the investment threshold to as little as $500 for retail and $10,000 for HNWI.

Base L2: Ensures transactions are fast and cost pennies, making micro-investments viable.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9ddf3e7798c34c178a7d19c3acf8ee4a/4e035eb7-a886-4a26-9543-348d6ad4a539.png)

**Impact & Market Size**
- AUM Goal: Targeting $600M AUM (1% of Indonesia’s $60B Sovereign Fund).
- Scalability: Projected RWA market to exceed $10T by 2030; Orbitum positions Base as the home for Shariah-compliant RWAs.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9ddf3e7798c34c178a7d19c3acf8ee4a/2f64e81c-14fc-44d1-865e-fc4ba6414302.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Hurdle: On-chain vs Off-chain State Mismatch in Instant Buy & Sell
One of the biggest hurdles we faced while building Orbitum was maintaining data consistency between on-chain logic and off-chain systems, especially for the instant buy & sell feature of tokenized bonds.

Because bond pricing is governed by NAV management, the actual buy/sell price depends on:
- On-chain state (token supply, allowlist status, transaction execution)
- Off-chain data (updated NAV, bond parameters, indexer-derived state)

During early testing, we encountered a state desynchronization bug where:
- The smart contract executed a buy/sell correctly on-chain
- But the off-chain system responsible for pricing and authorization was still using an outdated NAV or allowlist state

This resulted in invalid EIP-712 signatures being generated, which caused transactions to revert on-chain due to mismatched parameters.

How We Solved It
We addressed this problem by improving both architecture and data flow:
- Event-Driven Indexing
 We redesigned the indexer to rely strictly on on-chain events (buy, sell, NAV update, allowlist changes) as the single source of truth, instead of inferred or cached state.
- Explicit NAV Versioning
 Each NAV update now carries a version / timestamp that is emitted on-chain and included in the EIP-712 signature payload, ensuring signatures are only valid for a specific NAV state.

- Strict Allowlist Validation
 We enforced allowlist checks at both:
 - Smart contract level (hard enforcement)
 - Backend level (signature generation is blocked if the address is not allowlisted)

- Backend Revalidation Before Signature Generation
 Before issuing an EIP-712 signature, the backend now re-validates:
 - Latest NAV version
 - Allowlist status
 - Contract configuration

This ensures that every signature matches the current on-chain state at the moment of execution.

Result
After these changes:
- Pricing became deterministic and consistent
- Signature reverts caused by stale off-chain data were eliminated
- The system became more resilient and auditable, which is crucial for a financial product like tokenized bonds

This hurdle ultimately helped us design a more robust on-chain/off-chain synchronization model, which is now a core strength of Orbitum.

**Base Track**

Indonesia has a $60B+ Sukuk & Bond market with attractive 5% yields (vs. 2% in developed markets). However, it remains inaccessible to 280M people due to high entry costs, complex brokerage onboarding, and lack of secondary market liquidity.

**The Solution (Built on Base)**
Orbitum is a Base-native Mini-App that fractionalizes Indonesian Sovereign Funds and Green Sukuk. 

**We leverage:**
Base L2: To provide near-zero transaction fees for retail investors.
Smart Wallets: Using Base's Account Abstraction to allow users to sign transactions without managing seed phrases, solving the "Poor Onboarding" challenge.

**Technical Execution**
Smart Contracts: Deployed on Base Mainnet to handle fractional ownership of RWA tokens.

**Market Impact**
Capture Strategy: Aiming for 1% of the Indonesian Sovereign Fund ($600M AUM).

User Base: Targeting 200,000 retail investors and 50,000 HNWIs in Indonesia.

> Save more, ride safer, together.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Daily commuting is expensive, inefficient, and often unsafe—especially for students and regular commuters traveling the same routes every day. Many people travel alone, paying full fares, struggling to find reliable co-riders, or feeling unsafe with unknown transport options.
RideBuddy solves this by enabling trusted ride sharing. It matches people traveling on the same route and time, helps them split travel costs, and ensures safety through verified users, female-only ride options, and easy coordination via WhatsApp. The result is a more affordable, safer, and smarter daily commute.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building RideBuddy, our biggest challenge was designing a smooth experience for matching riders based on route, time, seats, and preferences (like female-only rides) without making the UI feel complicated. We solved this by simplifying the ride creation flow, improving validations, and showing only the most relevant ride information in the browse and details screens.
Another major hurdle was building safe coordination between riders. Instead of creating a full in-app chat system (which would take more time and increase complexity), we integrated WhatsApp-based coordination so users can instantly connect and finalize pickup details.
We also faced issues with responsive mobile UI and state management (upcoming rides, ride history, saved amount updates). We fixed this by restructuring components, refining the layout for small screens, and properly handling loading/error states to make the app reliable and consistent.

> Empowering Citizens to Build Better Cities.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![iOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem Category: Innovation**

Urban civic issues such as potholes, damaged roads, garbage accumulation, water leakage, and broken public infrastructure are common in cities. However, the traditional process of reporting and resolving these problems is often inefficient and frustrating due to:

Lack of transparency in complaint handling

Delayed or ignored issue resolution

Poor communication between citizens, municipalities, and contractors

No accountability for responsible authorities

No incentives for citizens to report issues

As a result, many civic problems remain unresolved, negatively affecting public safety, urban living standards, and trust in governance.

UrbanMind solves this problem by digitizing the entire civic issue lifecycle — from reporting to resolution — through a role-based, transparent, and accountable platform.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Implementing Role-Based Access Control

Designing separate workflows and permissions for citizens, municipalities, and contractors while keeping the system consistent was challenging.

How I solved it:
Implemented role-based authentication and authorization on the backend and conditionally rendered UI components in Flutter based on user roles.

2. Real-Time Updates and Notifications

Keeping users informed without manual refreshes required a reliable notification system.

How I solved it:
Integrated OneSignal push notifications triggered automatically whenever an issue status changed.

3. Handling Image Uploads with Location Data

Synchronizing image uploads with accurate GPS coordinates under unstable network conditions was difficult.

How I solved it:
Used validated API payloads and cloud storage handling to ensure images and metadata were always linked correctly.

4. Managing Frontend and Backend in a Single Repository

Working with Flutter and Node.js in the same repository increased complexity.

How I solved it:
Maintained a clean folder structure, well-defined API contracts, and separate environment configurations.

5. Designing a Future-Ready Reward System

The reward system needed to work now and remain extensible for future blockchain integration.

How I solved it:
Implemented a modular, points-based reward layer that can be easily extended without changing the core logic.
