**The problem it solves**

Blockchain transactions are irreversible, hard to understand, and expensive to audit, which leaves users choosing between moving fast and risking scams or paying thousands for professional reviews. From honeypots and rug pulls to hidden unlimited approvals that wallets like MetaMask do not clearly surface, everyday users often have no idea what they are actually signing. Vigil changes that by giving you an instant AI powered forensic report on any transaction hash in seconds instead of weeks, for about 1 ADI which is roughly $0.42 instead of $5,000 or more for a traditional audit. It analyzes token flows, contract behavior, and approval risks, then cryptographically signs each report through a 0G Compute Node to ensure it has not been tampered with, while funding its own compute costs through x402 micropayments. Whether you are a retail user approving a swap, a DAO reviewing a treasury move, or a team verifying a token launch, Vigil helps you move quickly while staying safe.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Vigil definitely had its "hair-pulling" moments. We started with a persistent "Intrinsic Gas Too Low" error because we were sending ERC-8021 builder codes with our ADI payments. Standard transfers only need 21,000 gas, but that extra data required more "fuel," so we swapped hardcoded limits for dynamic estimation via eth_estimateGas.

Next, our Treasury Ledger kept vanishing. Since the data was only in-memory, every Next.js reload wiped our profits and made the agent look broke. We fixed this with a .treasury-store.json file for local persistence, adding a fallback for Vercel’s read-only serverless environment so it wouldn't crash in production.

Finally, we fought strict TypeScript errors that didn't like how MetaMask handles types, requiring us to explicitly define everything to unblock our Vercel builds. Since we didn't have a 0G Compute Node on hand, we built a cryptographic attestation layer to simulate the verifiable output, keeping our reports tamper-proof and bounty-compliant.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

During the development of the Vigil Audit Protocol, we utilized a specialized stack of AI coding tools and agents to maintain high velocity and ensure system reliability. Cursor served as our primary AI-powered IDE, providing the foundational workflow for real-time code generation and exploration. For high-level engineering, we relied on Claude 4.6 Opus to handle architecture planning, complex code refactoring, and deep debugging sessions, while Claude 4.6 Sonnet was instrumental in rapid iterative development, UI component logic, and translating forensic findings into concise reports. To ensure the robustness of the protocol under tight hackathon deadlines, we utilized Gemini 3.1 as a secondary validation layer to cross-check implementation details, identify obscure edge cases, and refine our final delivery.

**Futurllama**

Vigil complements Futurellama by providing tamper‑proof, cost‑effective on‑chain audit services that improve model governance and trust for LLM-driven apps. Merchants and apps can trigger verifiable DeFAI audits before or after LLM-driven actions, storing signed proofs for traceability and dispute resolution. The autonomous x402 funding model keeps inference costs predictable while enabling continuous monitoring and feedback into model retraining pipelines. Overall, Vigil adds accountability, provenance, and affordable verification to Futurellama-powered workflows.

**Best DeFAI Application**

Audit reports include verifiable DeFAI attestations from the compute node: computation proof, SHA‑256 verification hash, node signature, and timestamp. The forensic API simulates a 0G Compute Node that cryptographically signs outputs so results are tamper‑evident and auditable. This demonstrates verifiable decentralized inference and proof inclusion required by 0G Labs

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

The project implements the x402 payment flow: the forensic API returns HTTP 402 challenges and accepts X‑Payment authorization headers to unlock compute. The agent funds AI compute via autonomous x402 micropayments and streams execution logs for observability. EIP‑3009 style authorization and payment bookkeeping are demonstrated end‑to‑end. This addresses Kite’s agent‑native payment and orchestration criteria.

**ADI Payments Component for Merchants**

Vigil provides an embeddable ADI payment widget that accepts 1 ADI on ADI Testnet with on‑chain settlement, demonstrating merchant-facing payment UX. The terminal flow shows MetaMask chain switch and native ADI transfer confirmations. Merchant dashboard lets projects configure pricing and settlement wallets. This satisfies the ADI requirement for a clean, testnet-native merchant integration.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Vigil is self‑sustaining: it records ADI revenue and pays for USDC compute costs, tracking P&L in a treasury dashboard to show economic viability. Every transaction includes an ERC‑8021 builder code to mark provenance in calldata, and the system runs without human intervention once configured. These features meet Base’s requirements for autonomous, instrumented on‑chain activity and builder‑code usage.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

For most Indian professionals, relocating abroad is a massive "life event" that unfortunately comes with a mountain of paperwork and mental load. Currently, the process is completely broken and fragmented. A typical H1B mover spends weeks juggling 30+ open browser tabs, trying to tally US tax brackets against Indian city  expenses, scouring Reddit for safe neighborhoods in a city they've never visited, and manually tracking visa interview slots for themselves and their family.

**This "Information Chaos" leads to:**

- Financial Blind Spots: Not knowing the "In-hand" salary after Uncle Sam and the state government take their cut.
- Logistical Stress: Wasting hours on Google Maps trying to find a 1BHK that is both affordable and close to the office.
- Visa Anxiety: Missing critical documents or dates for dependent (H4) visas due to confusing USCIS timelines.

**The Solution: Pravasa.ai**

Pravasa.ai (meaning "Journey" in Sanskrit/Hindi) is an Agentic AI Architect that streamlines this entire "Videsh-Gamana". Instead of just giving you a list of links, we have built a coordinated team of AI agents that do the heavy lifting for you:

True-Net Financial Agent: It doesn't just "guess" numbers; it calculates your exact monthly take-home pay based on your filing status and target state taxes (like the 0% tax benefit in Florida).

Housing Scout Agent: It takes your "In-hand" budget and automatically identifies safe, commutable neighborhoods, saving you from the "Rent vs. Reality" shock.

Visa Timeline Agent: It builds a dynamic, day-by-day checklist for the primary applicant and dependents, accounting for the latest 2026 consular wait times.

**The Impact**

We have turned a multi-week long "headache" into a 3 minute personalized roadmap. By using Claude and Gemini, we ensure that your relocation isn't just a move, but a well-planned transition. Pravasa.ai ensures that you focus on your new career, while we handle the "how-to-get-there".

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. The "Hallucination" of Tax Calculations**

**The Challenge:** Initially, the Financial Agent was treating US tax laws like a creative writing prompt. It would often "guess" state tax percentages or provide outdated 2023 brackets instead of the 2026 data required for a realistic "True-Net" projection.

**The Fix:** We moved away from "Zero-Shot" prompting and implemented Grounding with Tool-Calling. We created a structured web search and forced the agent to call a specific function to fetch rates. This ensured that the math was based on "Ground Truth" rather than the model's training data.

**2. Orchestration Latency & Handover Failures**

**The Challenge:** Coordinating three specialized agents (Finance, Housing, Visa) in a linear sequence was incredibly slow. If the Financial Agent took 10 seconds to respond, the Housing Scout was stuck waiting, leading to a poor user experience.

**The Fix:** We optimized the Agentic Handover protocol using Django’s asynchronous tasks. We designed a "Parallel Reasoning" flow.

**3. Managing "Dependent" Visa Logic (The H4 Edge Case)**

**The Challenge:** A major hurdle was making the Visa Agent smart enough to handle family members. Initially, it would only generate a checklist for the primary H1B holder, completely ignoring the H4 dependent requirements like marriage certificate verification and joint appointment scheduling.

**The Fix:** We refined the System Prompt for the Orchestrator to include a "Dependent Awareness" logic gate. If the user profile includes a spouse, the Orchestrator injects a specific sub-task into the Visa Agent's queue to pull H4-specific document requirements.

> Skill Gap Diagnostic Tool

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional online learning often creates an illusion of competence. Learners follow step-by-step guides, successfully completing projects without actually mastering the underlying principles.

The Dependency Loop: Learners become reliant on guided instructions and freeze when faced with a blank editor.

Invisible Gaps: Advanced courses assume a level of prerequisite knowledge (e.g., "Closure" in JavaScript or "Backpropagation" in ML) that the student might have missed or forgotten.

Linear Roadmaps: Most platforms offer a "one-size-fits-all" path, ignoring that every learner has a unique "Swiss cheese" knowledge base with different holes.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a diagnostic engine is significantly harder than a standard chatbot. Here are the "boss battles" I faced during development:

Socratic Prompt Engineering: It was challenging to prevent the AI from "leaking" the answer. I had to iterate on system prompts to ensure the AI remains a persistent interviewer rather than a helpful assistant.

State Management in Async Loops: Handling the diagnostic "tree" logic required careful state management. If a user fails a question, the backend must instantly pivot to a "sub-topic" without losing the context of the original goal.

Latency vs. Intelligence: Originally, using larger models caused 5-10 second delays. Switching to Gemini 1.5 Flash allowed for sub-second responses while maintaining the reasoning capability needed to evaluate complex technical answers.

CORS & Production Security: Integrating a FastAPI backend with a Vite frontend required fine-tuning middleware to ensure secure data flow while allowing the seamless local development experience.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Emergencies are time-critical, but most response systems are **centralized, slow, and disconnected from the people who are actually closest to the incident**.

In many real-world situations:
- Ambulances and fire services take **10–30 minutes** to arrive.
- The **first 3–5 minutes** often determine survival.
- Trained people (doctors, nurses, CPR-certified neighbors) are **already nearby**, but they are **not alerted**.
- Tools like fire extinguishers, vehicles, or generators exist within the neighborhood but are **not mobilized**.

The result is a dangerous gap between **when help is needed** and **when help arrives**.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/5b49bbd96df7420d935319e8cc104c8d/52a579f5-462b-4953-a3a0-ed724d82f6dd.png)
---

## What This App Solves

This app transforms a neighborhood into a **real-time, skill-based emergency response network**.

Instead of waiting helplessly, people can instantly activate **verified nearby help**, reducing response time from **minutes to seconds**.

---

## What People Can Use It For

### Medical Emergencies
- Cardiac arrest
- Severe injuries
- Unconsciousness
- Seizures

**How it helps:**
- Alerts nearby CPR-certified users or medical professionals
- Enables life-saving intervention **before an ambulance arrives**

---

### Fire Emergencies
- Kitchen fires
- Electrical fires
- Smoke emergencies

**How it helps:**
- Alerts neighbors who have fire extinguishers
- Allows small fires to be controlled **before spreading**

---

### Security & Safety Incidents
- Harassment or assault
- Suspicious activity
- Domestic threats

**How it helps:**
- Alerts nearby verified users as witnesses
- Creates immediate deterrence through presence and visibility

---

## How It Makes Existing Systems Better

### Compared to Emergency Numbers
| Traditional Systems | This App |
|---|---|
| Centralized | Decentralized |
| Slow response | Instant local response |
| One-way communication | Live, real-time updates |
| No skill filtering | Skill-based alerts |

---

### Compared to WhatsApp Groups
| WhatsApp Groups | This App |
|---|---|
| Chaotic & noisy | Targeted & selective |
| Everyone gets notified | Only relevant responders |
| No live coordination | Real-time tracking |
| Easily ignored | High-priority alerts |

---

## Why This Is Safer and More Effective

- **Selective alerts** prevent panic and alert fatigue  
- **Real-time coordination** reduces confusion  
- **Verified users** increase trust and safety  
- **Location-based intelligence** ensures relevance  
- **Offline mesh support** enables use during disasters  

---

## Real-World Impact

- Saves lives during the **golden minutes**
- Prevents small incidents from becoming disasters
- Empowers communities to protect each other
- Reduces dependency on overloaded emergency systems

---

## In One Sentence

> This app helps people get the *right help from the nearest people* **before official help arrives**, making emergencies faster, safer, and more survivable.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into 

- **Environment variables not loading** caused MongoDB connection failures.  
  *Solved by loading *dotenv* before all imports and running the server from the correct directory.*

- **Geospatial queries returned no users** due to missing indexes and incorrect coordinate order.  
  *Solved by adding a 2dsphere index and standardizing coordinates to [longitude, latitude].*

- **Real-time alerts were unreliable** because socket connections changed on reconnect.  
  *Solved by re-registering socket IDs for users on every connection.*

- **Flutter command not recognized** due to missing PATH configuration.  
  *Solved by adding Flutter’s bin directory to the system PATH.*

- **CocoaPods failed on macOS** because of outdated system Ruby.  
  *Solved by installing a modern Ruby via Homebrew and correctly configuring PATH.*

**Key takeaway:** Most challenges were system-level (environment, tooling, real-time state), and solving them required understanding how the tools work together, not just writing code.

**Open Innovation**

## Relevance to the Open Innovation Track

Our project fits the **Open Innovation** track because it rethinks how emergency response can work by **breaking away from traditional, centralized systems**.

Instead of relying only on authorities, it **opens the system to the community**, allowing verified neighbors with the right skills and tools to help in real time. Anyone can contribute value simply by being nearby and prepared.

The solution is:
- **Decentralized** – not controlled by a single authority  
- **Collaborative** – powered by community participation  
- **Flexible** – can be adapted to cities, campuses, societies, or disaster zones  
- **Extensible** – open to future integrations with government, NGOs, or smart-city systems  

In short, the project uses **open, community-driven innovation** to solve a real-world problem in a new and scalable way, which is the core idea behind the Open Innovation track.

**The problem it solves**

1. Lack of early impact visibility
Construction impact is usually assessed after work begins, leading to complaints and damage. This tool enables prediction before execution.

2. Complex and scattered data
Environmental and construction impact data is difficult to interpret. The platform simplifies it into clear scores and visual insights.

3. Reactive CSR and sustainability planning
Companies often spend on CSR after issues arise. The system helps plan mitigation proactively and measure readiness.

4. Unclear decision-making for authorities and planners
Manual reports and subjective assessments slow approvals. The tool provides standardized, location-based impact evaluation.

5. Limited awareness for communities and workers
People affected by construction lack access to clear information. The platform improves awareness through maps and an AI chatbot.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Designing the scoring logic, assigning appropriate weights and dynamic multipliers while keeping the model explainable.
2. Limited data availability, impact-related data was fragmented, requiring study and consolidation from multiple sources.
3. Location-based data mapping, fetching contextual information like air quality and noise using latitude and longitude.
4. Defining a safe user flow, ensuring the system supports planning and decision-making without allowing data manipulation.
5. System deployment, deploying and configuring the full stack reliably on Vercel.

**Google Gemini**

We integrated the Gemini API to power an AI-based chatbot within the platform. The chatbot is used to help users understand construction impact results, risk levels, and suggested mitigation measures in simple language. We send contextual project and impact data as prompts to the Gemini API, and the responses are used to answer user queries related to safety, environmental risks, and sustainability awareness. This improves accessibility for non-technical users and makes the analysis easier to interpret without manually reading detailed reports. Additionally, it assists users in navigating to different sections of the platform seamlessly.

**The problem it solves**

In today’s e-commerce world, brands and sellers have lots of data but not much *real understanding* of it. 🛒💡

Marketplaces like Amazon and Flipkart offer simple dashboards that show sales, ads, and stock levels.
But they don’t explain *why things are changing* or give a full view of competitors or the overall digital shelf.

Because of this, businesses face several tough challenges:

- Sales drop without knowing why.
- Advertising costs go up but results stay the same.
- Products lose visibility without any warning.
- Stock shortages quietly hurt sales.
- Competitor moves are not noticed until it’s too late.
- Most tools just show what happened, not what caused it or what to do next.

# **⚠️ Core Problems in Current E-Commerce Operations**

**#1.
Data is scattered across different platforms** 📊
- Sales dashboards
- Ad platforms
- Inventory systems
- Keyword tools
- Pricing trackers

Teams switch between these tools, spreadsheets, and reports, leading to *slow and error-filled* decisions.

**#2.
No real cause-and-effect understanding 🔍**

When performance changes, sellers ask:
- Is it due to pricing?

- Did competitors take over visibility?

- Is inventory unavailable?

- Are ads hiding bigger problems?

Current systems don’t connect these signals, making it hard to know for sure.


**#3.
Problems are found too late ⏰**


Most issues are noticed only after revenue is lost, like:
- Visibility drops noticed days later
- Stock shortages found after sales fall
- Competitor price cuts realized too late

**#4.
Decisions are slow because insights come late and are disconnected ⏳**

- Decisions are reactive, not proactive
- Ad budgets are wasted without fixing real issues
- Growth opportunities are missed

# How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

**Before Stalligence** ❌️
- Manual analysis across tools
- Decisions based on guesses
- Delayed responses
- High operational effort

**With Stalligence** ✔️
- Automated intelligence
- Clear explanations of what’s causing changes
- Early alerts and predictions
- Faster and more confident decisions

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f33bbfa8fc304098a505ed0312df5b40/362fbac9-5959-4d00-bae2-c0efe1d95a68.png)

**Why This Matters** 🤔

*E-commerce is getting more competitive.*
Winning isn’t just about having more data; it’s about brands deciding ahead of the market, not after it! 🧠

**Challenges we ran into**

When we started building Stalligence for this hackathon-
 *everything looked simple on paper.* 📝 
Data was everywhere - prices, listings, rankings, stock status. 

But very quickly, we realized the real challenge wasn’t accessing data; it was the chaos behind it. 

We were working with various data sources including:  
- Marketplace APIs
- Advertising data 
- Inventory records 
- Product page information from the web

Each platform spoke a different language, data changed by the minute, and signals often contradicted each other. 

Turning this noisy, fragmented information into reliable intelligence became *our biggest hurdle.* 🎯


**#1. Inconsistent and Unstructured Data 🧩**

The data from APIs and product pages did not come in the same format.

Product names, SKUs, timestamps, and values were all mixed up and often had missing or repeated information.

**• *How we solved it* 🔧**

We made a structured process to handle this:
-First, we stored all the raw data in tables.
- Then we used SQL scripts to clean and standardize it.
- We created mapping tables to match different product identifiers.
- Finally, we built clean tables for analysis.

This helped turn messy data into something usable for deeper analysis.


**#2. Mapping Competitor Information to Our Data 🔑**

Competitor products did not use the same product IDs as our own, so comparing pricing, visibility, and availability was hard.

**• *How we solved it* 🔧**

-We used several methods to connect the data:
- Matching product titles to find similar items
- Using brand and category names to group products
- Finding products through shared keywords
- Applying manual checks to ensure accuracy

This allowed us to tie competitor data with our own product performance.


**#3. Finding the Root Cause Instead of Just Observing 👀**

At first, we saw things like a drop in sales, a lower ranking, or a price change.
The real challenge was figuring out *why* these things happened.

**• *How we solved it* 🔧**

We created logic to connect different signals:
- We looked at how visibility changes relate to sales
- We checked how availability gaps affect revenue
- We connected advertising performance to rankings
- We found out which signal had the biggest impact


 **#4. Handling Large Data Efficiently 🚀**

Collecting data frequently meant dealing with huge datasets and slow analysis times.

 **• *How we solved it* 🔧**

-We made the system faster by:
-Using SQL indexing to speed up searches
-Creating summarized tables like in OLAP systems
-Keeping raw data separate from processed data


**#5. Presenting Insights Clearly in the Interface 💡**

A dashboard full of numbers was hard to understand.
We needed a way to show results in a clear and useful way.

**• *How we solved it* 🔧**

-We designed the interface to:
-Highlight important signals visually
-Show how visibility, availability, and performance are connected
-Focus on insights instead of just showing data
 
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f33bbfa8fc304098a505ed0312df5b40/7560e842-0a69-4526-b519-f539e52b3c7b.jpeg)

# **》Outcome 💥**

By overcoming these challenges, we built a system that can:

- Bring together data from many different sources

- Connect market signals with product performance

- Provide clear and actionable insights rather than just raw data

**The problem it solves**

## The Security Gap Killing Startups

Every year, *43% of cyberattacks target small businesses, yet **60% of small companies go out of business within 6 months* of a breach. The problem? Security is either too expensive or too complicated for teams without dedicated security experts.

### The Broken Status Quo:

*Professional Penetration Testing:* Costs $10,000-$50,000 per engagement with 2-4 week turnaround times. Startups deploying weekly sprints can't afford to wait months between security audits.

*Enterprise Security Tools (Burp Suite, Acunetix):* Require 20+ hours of training, cost $400-$5,000 annually, and demand deep security expertise to interpret results. A junior developer shouldn't need a CISSP certification to understand if their code is vulnerable.

*Free Open-Source Scanners (OWASP ZAP):* Miss 70% of vulnerabilities in modern JavaScript frameworks because they only analyze HTTP traffic, not client-side DOM manipulation. Single-page applications built with React, Vue, or Angular render completely differently in a real browser.

*Cloud-Based SaaS Scanners:* Cannot test localhost or internal development servers, forcing developers to expose pre-production code to the internet just to run security checks. They also struggle with authentication flows and complex JavaScript state management.

### What DeGrime Actually Does:

DeGrime democratizes enterprise-grade security testing for the 2.5 million development teams that can't afford dedicated security personnel.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenge 1: Puppeteer Rendering Race Conditions

### The Problem:
Modern single-page applications (SPAs) don't load instantly. React components render asynchronously, forms appear after API calls, and input fields get dynamically injected via JavaScript. Traditional scanners just wait 2 seconds and assume the page is ready—missing 70% of the actual attack surface.

*The Bug:*
javascript
await page.goto('http://localhost:3000');
await page.waitForTimeout(2000); // Arbitrary wait
const inputs = await page.$$('input'); // Returns 0 inputs!


The search bar rendered 3.5 seconds after page load, but our scanner already moved on. We were scanning an empty skeleton.

### The Solution:
Implemented *smart waiting strategies* with multiple fallback mechanisms:
javascript
async function waitForDynamicContent(page) {
// Strategy 1: Wait for network to be idle
await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' });

// Strategy 2: Wait for specific framework signals
await page.waitForFunction(() => {
// React: Check if root is hydrated
return window.React && document.querySelector('[data-reactroot]');
}, { timeout: 10000 });

// Strategy 3: Mutation Observer for DOM changes
await page.evaluate(() => {
return new Promise((resolve) => {
const observer = new MutationObserver((mutations) => {
if (mutations.some(m => m.addedNodes.length > 0)) {
observer.disconnect();
resolve();
}
});
observer.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
setTimeout(() => resolve(), 5000); // Fallback timeout
});
});
}


*Impact:* Increased vulnerability detection rate from 23% to 89% on modern SPAs.

---

## Challenge 2: Dialog Detection Timing (The Alert Disappearing Act)

### The Problem:
XSS payloads trigger alert() dialogs, but Puppeteer's page.on('dialog') event listener wasn't catching them consistently. Sometimes the dialog appeared before our listener was registered. Other times, form submissions caused page navigations that destroyed the dialog before we could detect it.

*The Bug:*
javascript
await input.type('<script>alert("XSS")</script>');
await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); // Form submits
// Page navigates immediately, dialog never fires


We'd inject a valid XSS payload, see the alert flash on screen during manual testing, but the automated scanner reported "No vulnerability found."

### The Solution:
*Two-phase detection with race condition handling:*
javascript
// Phase 1: Register listener BEFORE navigation
const dialogPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {
const handler = async (dialog) => {
if (dialog.message().includes('GRIME-XSS')) {
resolve({ found: true, payload: dialog.message() });
await dialog.dismiss();
page.off('dialog', handler); // Cleanup
}
};
page.on('dialog', handler);

// Timeout fallback
setTimeout(() => resolve({ found: false }), 3000);
});

// Phase 2: Inject payload
await input.type('<script>alert("GRIME-XSS-TEST")</script>');
await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

// Phase 3: Wait for either dialog or timeout
const result = await dialogPromise;


*Bonus Fix:* Added page navigation blocking for critical tests:
javascript
await page.setRequestInterception(true);
page.on('request', (request) => {
// Block navigation during XSS testing
if (isTestingXSS && request.isNavigationRequest()) {
request.abort();
} else {
request.continue();
}
});


*Impact:* XSS detection reliability jumped from 60% to 98%.

---

## Challenge 3: SQL Injection False Positives (The Error Message Maze)

### The Problem:
We were detecting SQL injection by looking for database error keywords like "syntax error" or "MySQL". But legitimate applications sometimes return these strings in normal responses:

- Blog posts about SQL tutorials
- Error documentation pages
- Stack traces in development mode
- Database version strings in footer

*The Bug:*
javascript
if (response.includes('MySQL') || response.includes('syntax error')) {
return { vulnerable: true }; // FALSE POSITIVE
}


Our demo scanned a MySQL documentation site and reported 47 "critical SQL injections." Embarrassing.

### The Solution:
*Context-aware heuristic analysis with multi-signal correlation:*
javascript
function detectSQLInjection(originalResponse, injectedResponse) {
const signals = {
errorKeywords: 0,
responseChange: 0,
statusCodeChange: 0,
headerAnomalies: 0,
timingAnomaly: 0
};

// Signal 1: Database-specific error patterns
const errorPatterns = [
/you have an error in your sql syntax/i,
/warning: mysql/i,
/unclosed quotation mark after the character string/i,
/quoted string not properly terminated/i
];

if (errorPatterns.some(pattern =>
injectedResponse.body.match(pattern) &&
!originalResponse.body.match(pattern) // NEW error, not pre-existing
)) {
signals.errorKeywords = 3; // High confidence
}

// Signal 2: Response structure change
const originalLength = originalResponse.body.length;
const injectedLength = injectedResponse.body.length;
if (Math.abs(originalLength - injectedLength) > 500) {
signals.responseChange = 2; // Significant difference
}

// Si

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Finding a reliable local service provider is harder than it should be. People often rely on random online listings, social media posts, or word-of-mouth, which are not always trustworthy. Reviews can be fake, provider details are rarely verified, and once a payment is made, there is little accountability if something goes wrong.

On the other side, many skilled local professionals struggle to get visibility online. Even if they provide good service, they find it difficult to gain customer trust or compete with large platforms.

This creates a gap where customers feel unsafe or unsure, and genuine service providers miss out on opportunities.

**How the Project Helps**

This project provides a simple and trust-focused way to connect customers with local service providers.

People can search for nearby services, check whether a provider is verified, and book services with confidence. Payments are handled in a controlled manner so that money is released only after the service is completed. Reviews are allowed only after a real service is finished, which helps keep feedback genuine.

For service providers, the platform helps them reach nearby customers, build trust through verification, and receive fair payments without disputes.

**Why It Matters**

The platform makes local service discovery safer, reduces fake reviews, and adds accountability to the entire process. It saves time for customers and helps honest local professionals grow by earning trust, not just visibility.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

One of the main challenges was defining the scope of the project. A local service marketplace can easily become very large, and as a solo participant with limited time, I had to consciously avoid overbuilding. I solved this by narrowing the focus to a single niche and prioritizing trust-related features instead of trying to support every possible service.

Another challenge was handling trust and payments logically. Implementing a real escrow system is complex, especially within a hackathon. To overcome this, I designed a simplified escrow flow where payments are held in a pending state and released only after service completion. This allowed me to demonstrate the concept clearly without overcomplicating the implementation.

I also faced issues with location-based service discovery. Filtering providers accurately based on the user’s location and ensuring performance was tricky at first. I resolved this by simplifying distance calculations and caching nearby results instead of querying everything in real time.

Finally, managing everything alone — frontend, backend, database, and logic — was challenging. I handled this by building the core user flow first and adding features incrementally, testing each part before moving to the next.

Overall, these challenges helped me make better design decisions and focus on building a clean, functional, and realistic solution within the given time.

### Flick AI

> The Intelligent Desktop Assistant

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/Electron-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tesseract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tesseract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Open router](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20router-333333?style=flat-square) ![Glm 4.7](https://img.shields.io/badge/Glm%204.7-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Most AI assistants live inside a browser. Real work does not.

When people debug code, write emails, review logs, or take meeting notes, they do it inside native applications like editors, terminals, and desktop tools. To use AI, they are forced to stop what they are doing, switch windows, copy content, paste it into a chatbot, explain the context, wait for an answer, then switch back. Each step breaks focus and adds friction.

This interruption compounds. Thought flow is lost. Small errors creep in while copying. Time is wasted repeating context the system should already see.

FlickAI was built to remove that break.

Instead of asking users to bring their work to the assistant, FlickAI brings the assistant to the work. It lives on the desktop and sees exactly what the user sees on screen. Code errors, email threads, meeting notes, logs, and documents are understood directly, without uploads or manual explanation.

A developer hits a runtime error. FlickAI reads the stack trace from the terminal and explains the cause.  
A user stares at an unfinished email. FlickAI reads the thread and drafts a reply in the same tone.  
Meeting notes are scattered across the screen. FlickAI turns them into clear action items.

The result is a continuous workflow. No context switching. No translation layer between human intent and machine help. AI becomes part of the working environment instead of a separate destination.

FlickAI makes assistance immediate, embedded, and cognitively lighter, which is what daily work actually needs.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

One of the earliest blockers was inference rate limiting. During rapid testing, requests to the Cerebras API would occasionally stall or fail, which made iteration unpredictable. This was especially problematic because a desktop assistant depends on consistent, fast responses. The issue was later resolved when the Cerebras team increased rate limits for participants.

Tooling limits appeared next. We relied heavily on Cline for scaffolding, refactoring, and fast iteration. As development accelerated, rate limits began slowing changes, particularly during larger UI and architecture shifts. Support from the Cline team helped unblock this and restored development velocity.

Latency was a constant concern throughout development. Even small delays break the illusion of an always-present assistant. If responses feel slow, the product no longer feels native. This required careful attention to response streaming and UI feedback so the system appeared to think alongside the user rather than after them.

Screen understanding introduced another layer of complexity. Different types of on-screen content behave differently when captured. Code editors, terminals, images, and text-heavy documents each required separate handling. To maintain reliability, vision models had to be paired with OCR fallbacks instead of relying on a single method.

UX decisions also came with friction. We changed the interaction model mid-development, moving from a persistent sidebar to a floating, spotlight-style interface. Making this shift required extensive refactoring while preserving consistent behavior across the app.

Finally, coordinating Electron’s main and renderer processes added non-trivial complexity. Streaming AI responses, handling screen capture, and managing voice input all needed to stay synchronized, and keeping that stability was one of the most challenging aspects of the system.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

FlickAI is built on the principle of dual operation between the user and the system.

The user continues working normally inside native desktop applications. In parallel, FlickAI observes the same screen context, interprets intent, and produces immediate, task-specific assistance. There is no prompt engineering, no context switching, and no manual data transfer.

Human decision-making and machine perception run side by side. The user provides intent through action. The system provides reasoning through real-time understanding of visual and textual context.

This project embodies duality as two agents operating simultaneously in the same environment, each strengthening the other to reduce friction and increase execution speed.

> Strategy Over Brute Force in Space

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ONNX](https://img.shields.io/badge/ONNX-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Finding Habitable Planets: An Exo-Checkmate Approach

Finding a habitable planet is the ultimate needle in a haystack. NASA's TESS satellite beams down terabytes of light data, but current detection methods are effectively "brute force." They suffer from two critical flaws:

*   **Time-Blindness:** Traditional CNNs treat light curves as static images, often confusing Eclipsing Binary Stars (V-shape) for Planets (U-shape).
*   **High False Positives:** Existing models flag thousands of "candidates" that turn out to be noise or impossible orbits, wasting valuable astronomer time.

Exo-Checkmate solves this by treating discovery like a Chess Game, not a search query.

*   **Strategic Pruning:** Instead of scanning blindly, our "Strategist" layer filters out unstable or giant stars instantly, reducing compute load by 60%.
*   **Hypersonic Dual-View AI:** We built a multi-modal engine that fuses Shape (1D-CNN) and Sequence (LSTM) analysis. It doesn't just see the dip; it understands the temporal rhythm, distinguishing true planets from cosmic traps.
*   **Physics Verification:** We don't just guess. We validate every candidate with a Hill Stability (N-Body) simulation. If the orbit isn't physically stable, the "Judge" layer rejects it—Checkmate.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges and Solutions in Exo-Checkmate

Here's how we tackled the biggest hurdles in our planet-finding mission:

## 1. The "Data Scarcity" Crisis

Deep Learning models need thousands of examples, but there are only ~37 confirmed Earth-sized planets in the TESS dataset. Our LSTM initially failed because it had nothing to learn from.

**The Fix:** We built the "Frankenstein Method." We wrote a script to mathematically inject 10,000 synthetic planetary transits (using Quadratic Limb Darkening) into real stellar noise. This allowed us to train the model on "Infinite Data" before showing it a real star.

## 2. The "Time-Blind" AI

Our early CNN models kept flagging Eclipsing Binaries as planets because, at low resolution, a "V" looks like a "U."

**The Fix:** We pivoted to a Dual-View Architecture. We added a second "Head" (Bi-Directional LSTM) that looks at the entire 27-day timeline. By combining the Shape score with the Sequence score, we eliminated false positives caused by binary stars.

## 3. Crashing the Browser with Science

TESS light curves have over 20,000 data points. Trying to render these in a standard charting library crashed our frontend instantly.

**The Fix:** We implemented Scientific Binning and a custom HTML5 Canvas renderer. We average the data into "bins" to reduce noise and rendering cost while preserving the mathematical integrity of the transit signal.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shadownet-346c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TechSuvo108/SHADOWNET) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://shadownet-1eace.web.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/XQZ24-VpUTs?si=c87sjPRwCU8ZQUPg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Images speak, Privacy stays invisible

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

****🔐 Problem It Solves****

Most social platforms store messages as plain or encrypted text, making them easy targets for surveillance, censorship, data leaks, or long-term tracking. Even “secure” chats leave visible communication trails that can raise suspicion or be blocked entirely.

****💡 How ShadowNet Helps****

ShadowNet removes text from the equation. Messages are encrypted and hidden inside images using steganography, so there is no visible conversation or searchable text—only ordinary photos.

**🚀 What People Can Use It For**

- Journalists & whistleblowers to share information safely without obvious communication trails
- Users in censored regions to communicate where messaging apps are monitored or blocked
- Privacy-focused individuals who don’t want platforms storing their private chats
- One-time or sensitive sharing (Wi-Fi passwords, internal notes, exam details)
- Creative communities to hide art, poems, or Easter eggs inside images

**🛡️ Why It’s Safer & Easier**

- No text database → nothing to scan, log, or leak
- Server never knows the message content
- Looks like a normal social media feed
- Optional auto-delete and key-based access
- ShadowNet makes privacy invisible—by design.

**Challenges we ran into**

****🐞 Reliable Steganography Across Different Images****

One major challenge was ensuring that hidden messages could be reliably extracted after upload and download. Some image formats and compression methods (especially platform-side compression) were corrupting the hidden data.
**Solution**: I restricted encoding to lossless formats (like PNG) and performed all steganography on the client side to avoid server recompression.

****🔐 Key-Based Decoding & Wrong-Key Handling****

Handling cases where users entered the wrong key was tricky—there’s no obvious way to tell if decoding failed or the message was never there.
**Solution**: I added a verification checksum to the encrypted payload so the app can safely detect invalid keys without revealing anything.

****🌐 Performance & Large Image Sizes****

Processing high-resolution images caused noticeable delays in the browser.
**Solution**: I optimized by resizing images before encoding and offloading heavy processing to Web Workers to keep the UI responsive.

****🧠 UX Without Revealing the Magic****

Designing the app to feel like a normal social platform—without exposing the hidden-message concept to unintended users—was a balance challenge.
**Solution**: I separated public and private flows clearly, keeping encoding/decoding behind explicit actions while the feed remains indistinguishable from a regular gallery.

These challenges shaped ShadowNet into a more secure, usable, and realistic privacy-first platform.

**Software Development**

ShadowNet fits strongly into the **Software Development** track as it is a full-stack system built to solve a real-world privacy problem using core software engineering principles.

The project involves designing **secure client-side algorithms (encryption + steganography)**, building a scalable web application with authentication, feeds, and user interactions, and handling performance, UX, and data safety challenges. It focuses on system design, security-aware development, and practical implementation rather than just theory.

**ShadowNet** demonstrates how software can rethink traditional data storage models by treating images as carriers of information, showcasing innovation, robustness, and real-world applicability in modern software development.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem We Solve:
"The Visualization Gap."

The Issue: Millions of creators (founders, students, indie hackers) have brilliant product ideas but cannot communicate them visually. They are stuck between "Learn Blender for 6 months" or "Pay an agency ₹50k."

The Result: Ideas die in the "concept phase" because they remain abstract text instead of tangible prototypes.

Our Fix: We turn abstract text into a visual, rotatable 3D asset instantly, bridging the gap between "I have an idea" and "Here is what it looks like.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced multiple technical challenges while building the system. First, getting 2D AI models to “think” in 3D was difficult because they often produced impossible geometries, so we engineered strict camera-angle prompting to force consistent Front/Side/45° views for stable 3D reconstruction. We also solved the “stateless AI” problem by introducing Redis-based state management, allowing long 3D generations to run asynchronously while the frontend safely polls status even if users refresh. Balancing quality vs speed was another challenge — after experimenting, we tuned Trellis parameters to prioritize high-fidelity outputs instead of fast but low-quality blobs. Finally, integrating text-to-image and image-to-3D models was initially brittle, so we built a validation pipeline to handle formats and base64 conversions reliably, ensuring smooth handoff between AI systems.

No safe way for others to contribute to training

**What This Project Enables**

Explicit, memory-based AI learning

Clear separation between chat and learning

AI avatars defined by a master personality prompt

Gradual, controlled evolution of AI behavior

Trust-based contribution (owner > trainer)

Read-only trainer access without accounts

**What People Can Use It For**

Personal AI avatars that reflect real opinions and values

Long-term memory and knowledge backup

Mentorship and structured learning (MCQs, coaching)

Creator and professional AI personas

Consistent AI behavior across time and sessions

Ethical experimentation with evolving AI systems

**How It Makes Tasks Easier and Safer**

No repeated re-explanation of preferences

Reduced AI hallucinations and drift

Controlled collaboration without security risks

Faster, more relevant AI responses

Lower cost without model retraining

Full user control over what the AI learns

**Impact**

More trustworthy AI systems

Stronger alignment with human identity

Safer AI collaboration models

Scalable approach to personal AI identity

**Challenges we ran into**

***Challenges I Ran Into***

Separating chat from learning
Initially, it was tempting to treat every conversation as learning data. This quickly caused personality drift and noisy context. I solved this by clearly separating short-term conversations from long-term memories and allowing only explicitly saved inputs to become learning data.

Retrieving the right context from growing memory
As the number of memories increased, passing all past data to the AI became inefficient and inaccurate. I addressed this by using embeddings with cosine similarity to retrieve only the most relevant memories per query, combined with trust-based weighting and recency scoring.

Handling trainer contributions without accounts
Trainers needed visibility into the avatars they contributed to, but adding full authentication increased complexity and risk. I solved this by introducing token-scoped, read-only access tied to a single avatar, which allowed secure viewing without user accounts.

Preventing identity drift from conflicting inputs
Conflicting memories from owners and trainers caused inconsistent responses. I introduced memory weights so owner-provided memories always take priority, ensuring the AI stays aligned with the real person.

Balancing technical depth with hackathon constraints
Advanced features like real-time streaming and microservices were unnecessary and risky under time pressure. I chose a monolithic architecture with minimal dependencies, which made the system easier to debug, explain, and demo.

Keeping the system explainable to judges
Complex AI systems can be hard to justify during evaluation. I overcame this by designing clear, layered workflows for memory storage, retrieval, and permission checks, making each decision easy to explain and defend.

**Real-Time AI Systems & Continuous Intelligence**

we have used text to  speech and speech to text using the pathway . also regulated our  AI orchestration to get workflows and even chats in real time.

> Autonomous Kernel Defense Powered by Adaptive AI.

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![C#](https://img.shields.io/badge/C#-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: The "Static Defense" Paradox
In modern cybersecurity, hackers move at the speed of scripts, while defense moves at the speed of humans. Aegis-Win addresses three critical gaps that current security tools—like standard Windows Firewall or basic Antivirus—fail to close:

1. The "Zero-Day" Response Lag
The Problem: Traditional firewalls rely on signatures (known bad files) or static rules (manually blocked IPs). When a new "Zero-Day" exploit or a fresh "Command & Control" (C2) server is launched, your firewall is blind because it doesn't have a rule for it yet.

The Gap: It usually takes hours or days for security vendors to push an update to your machine. By then, the data is already gone.

2. The "Context-Blind" Filtering
The Problem: Standard firewalls don't understand intent. They see powershell.exe connecting to the internet and think it’s normal. They don't realize that PowerShell is actually being used to exfiltrate your browser passwords to a remote server.

The Gap: Most firewalls are "dumb"—they check ports and IPs but don't analyze the behavioral context of the process making the connection.

3. The "Manual Management" Burden
The Problem: Small businesses and individual users don't have a 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) to monitor logs. If a breach happens at 3:00 AM, there is no one there to write a firewall rule to stop the outgoing data theft.

The Gap: Security is currently reactive, not proactive. It requires a human to see the threat and manually click "Block."

In Short: Why Aegis-Win?
Current firewalls are like a locked door; Aegis-Win is like a smart security guard. While the locked door (Static Firewall) can be bypassed with a new key or a ladder, the smart guard (Aegis-Win) watches who is trying to leave, what they are carrying, and where they are going—and can decide to tackle them even if he's never seen that specific intruder before.

**Challenges we ran into**

Here is a concise, high-impact template for your hackathon submission. It’s designed to look professional while highlighting your deep technical skills.

Project Name: Aegis-Win
Tagline: The Self-Healing AI Firewall for Windows.
1. The Problem (The "Why")
Traditional firewalls are static and context-blind. They rely on manually updated IP blacklists and signatures. If a "Zero-Day" attack or a suspicious process (like a malicious PowerShell script) tries to exfiltrate data to a new IP, standard firewalls won't stop it because they lack the "intelligence" to understand the intent of the connection.

2. The Solution (The "How")
Aegis-Win bridges the gap between low-level system networking and high-level AI reasoning:

Kernel-Level Monitoring: Uses the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to intercept network events at the ALE (Application Layer Enforcement) layer.

AI Analysis: Suspicious traffic metadata (Process ID, Destination IP, Payload) is sent to a local LLM (Llama 3 via Ollama) for real-time risk assessment.

Self-Healing: If the AI detects a threat, Aegis-Win automatically injects a new high-priority Block Rule into the Windows Base Filtering Engine, severing the connection instantly.

3. Technical Challenges Faced
WFP Memory Marshalling: Managing unmanaged C++ pointers in C# (P/Invoke) to interact with the fwpmu.dll without causing system crashes (BSOD).

Latency vs. Security: Solved AI "slowness" by implementing Asynchronous Mirroring—allowing the first packet through while the AI analyzes, then severing the stream if a threat is confirmed.

False Positive Mitigation: Built a confidence threshold logic where the AI must score a threat >85% before an automated kernel block is triggered.

4. Technology Stack
System Core: C# (.NET) / Win32 API.

Security Layer: Windows Filtering Platform (WFP).

AI Brain: Python (FastAPI) + Ollama (Llama 3).

DevOps: Docker (for the AI microservice).

**Ethereum Track**

Cybersecurity & Privacy: For building an active defense system that stops Zero-Day exploits and data exfiltration at the kernel level.

Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning: For implementing an "AI Security Analyst" that performs real-time behavioral analysis of network traffic.

System & Low-Level Programming: For utilizing the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) and handling complex C#/C++ memory management.

Automation & Future Tech: For creating a "Self-Healing" infrastructure where the software writes its own security rules without human intervention.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problems It Solves:-

VisionCast addresses the "Information Blackout" that visually impaired users face when trying to consume video content. Specifically, it solves:

The "Visual Gap": Standard screen readers can read text on a website but are blind to the content inside a video file. VisionCast translates visual data (actions, facial expressions, scenery) into audio, making the "unseen" accessible.

The "Dialogue Clash" Issue: Traditional automated descriptions often speak over important dialogue or beautiful music. VisionCast solves this with intelligent audio mixing, ensuring the narrator only speaks during silence or lowers the background volume (ducking) effectively.

Dependency on Sighted Assistance: Blind users currently have to ask someone, "What just happened?" or "Who is on screen?" VisionCast gives them independence through its Interactive Q&A, allowing them to ask the AI directly.

Inaccessible Interfaces: Most video players rely on small buttons and mouse clicks. VisionCast solves this with a Voice Command Navigator, allowing users to control playback and navigation entirely with their voice.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Challenges I Faced in Making It
During development, we encountered and overcame three major technical hurdles:

Audio Overlap & Ducking Logic:

Challenge: It was difficult to program the AI to know when to speak. Early versions would narrate over key dialogues, ruining the plot.

Solution: We implemented an Audio Waveform Analyzer using FFmpeg. It detects human voice frequencies versus background music. If dialogue is present, the AI waits; if music is playing, the system automatically lowers the volume ("ducks") to let the narration come through clearly.

Real-Time Q&A Latency:

Challenge: When a user asked a question like "Why is she crying?", sending the entire video history to the AI model caused a 10-20 second delay.

Solution: We optimized this using a Vector Database (RAG - Retrieval Augmented Generation). We store small textual summaries of scenes every 10 seconds. When a question is asked, the system searches these text logs instead of re-processing the video, reducing the answer time to under 2 seconds.

Synchronization of Variable Length Audio:

Challenge: Sometimes the AI description was longer than the silent gap in the video (e.g., a 5-second description for a 2-second scene).

Solution: We built a "Smart Pause" mechanism. If the description is too long, the video visual stream automatically pauses to let the narrator finish, then resumes, ensuring the user never misses a detail.

**Best Innovation**

Best Innovation Track: How This Project Fits
The "Best Innovation" track typically looks for solutions that address significant real-world problems using novel technology without being constrained by a specific industry niche. VisionCast fits perfectly because:

Universal Social Impact: It addresses a global accessibility crisis. With over 2.2 billion people having vision impairment, this project isn't just a "feature"—it's a fundamental bridge to information, education, and entertainment, aligning with UN Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

Novel Application of Generative AI: Most AI projects focus on text or static images. VisionCast innovates by applying Multimodal AI (Video + Audio + Text) to create a dynamic, real-time media experience. It moves beyond simple "captioning" to "storytelling."

Redefining User Interaction: By replacing the standard Graphical User Interface (GUI) with a Voice-First User Interface (VUI), we are innovating how humans interact with media players. This technology isn't just for the blind; it has broader applications for hands-free media consumption (e.g., while driving or cooking).

Scalability: The solution is software-based and scalable. Unlike human-generated audio descriptions which are expensive and slow to produce, VisionCast can make any video accessible in minutes, democratizing access to content globally.

**The problem it solves**

## 🧩 The Problem It Solves

Road infrastructure issues like potholes are often reported inconsistently, with inaccurate locations, duplicate complaints, or missing evidence. This leads to unreliable data, delayed action, and poor visibility into real road conditions. Traditional reporting methods focus on collecting more complaints rather than improving data quality, making it difficult to identify genuine and unresolved issues.

**RoadWatch** addresses this problem by making pothole reporting accurate, verifiable, and safer for both users and evaluators.

---

## ✅ How RoadWatch Helps

- **Accurate Reporting:** Uses GPS‑verified locations to ensure road issues are mapped precisely.  
- **Evidence‑Based Submissions:** Mandatory photo uploads reduce false or unclear reports.  
- **Duplicate Prevention:** Backend validation blocks repeated reports of the same issue within a defined radius.  
- **Improved Safety:** Helps users identify hazardous road sections more reliably.  
- **Better Decision‑Making:** Clean, non‑redundant data makes evaluation and prioritization easier.

---

## 🚦 What People Can Use It For

- Citizens can quickly and safely report potholes using their smartphones.  
- Users can view all reported issues on a single interactive map for better awareness.  
- Judges or evaluators can easily assess impact through structured and validated data.  
- Teams and authorities can focus on unresolved issues instead of repeated complaints.

---

> RoadWatch simplifies civic reporting by prioritizing accuracy, validation, and data reliability over volume.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Maintaining a Transparent Commit History
Since hackathon judges evaluate Git activity, there was a risk of the project appearing as a single large code dump.

**How I solved it:**  
Using **Kiro IDE**, I followed a disciplined workflow where commits were automated and structured after roughly every small logical change (around 20 lines of code). After every few commits, the code was pushed and deployed. This ensured transparency, traceability, and a clean development timeline.

---

### 2. Managing Frequent Merge Conflicts
Switching between devices and making rapid changes caused unfinished merges and Git conflicts.

**How I solved it:**  
I resolved pending merges properly, reset local branches when needed, and adopted smaller, frequent commits to reduce conflict complexity.

---

### 3. Element Type Is Invalid (React Undefined Component Error)
The application crashed due to incorrect component imports caused by mixing default and named exports.

**How I solved it:**  
I reviewed each component’s export style and corrected import statements to ensure consistency across the project.

---

### 4. Module Not Found Errors
Several components failed to load due to missing dependencies or incorrect import paths.

**How I solved it:**  
I carefully installed required packages, fixed relative paths, and ensured consistent file naming to resolve these issues.

---

### 5. Environment Variable Misconfiguration
Incorrect or missing environment variables caused API and database connection failures.

**How I solved it:**  
I standardized environment variable usage, separated public and private keys correctly, and validated configurations before deployment.

---

### 6. Google Maps Not Rendering Properly
Maps failed to load due to API key restrictions and script loading issues.

**How I solved it:**  
I corrected API key permissions, ensured proper script loading, and verified map initialization logic.

---

### 7. Handling Inaccurate GPS Location Data
GPS readings were sometimes inaccurate, especially indoors or in dense areas.

**How I solved it:**  
I enforced a GPS accuracy threshold and blocked submissions until acceptable accuracy was achieved.

---

### 8. Preventing Duplicate Pothole Reports
Multiple users could report the same pothole, cluttering the dataset.

**How I solved it:**  
I implemented backend‑level duplicate detection to block reports within a defined radius of existing active issues.

---

### 9. Coordinating Frontend and Backend Validation
Frontend and backend validations were initially inconsistent, causing edge‑case failures.

**How I solved it:**  
I aligned validation logic on both sides and ensured backend validation remained the final authority.

---

### 10. Deployment Failures on First Attempt
Early deployments failed due to missing environment variables and build misconfigurations.

**How I solved it:**  
I tested all services locally, validated environment setups, and deployed incrementally to avoid cascading failures.

---

### 11. Integrating Multiple Services Under Time Pressure
The project involved frontend, backend APIs, database, maps, AI service, and deployment pipelines.

**How I solved it:**  
I integrated services one at a time, verified each step independently, and used clear error logging to isolate issues quickly.

---

### 12. UI Breakage Due to Rapid Styling Changes
Frequent UI changes caused layout and responsiveness issues.

**How I solved it:**  
I reused components, avoided unnecessary re‑styling, and tested layouts across screen sizes incrementally.

---

### 13. AI Service Stability
The AI service worked locally but faced reliability issues during deployment.

**How I solved it:**  
I tested the service thoroughly locally and then deployed it on **Render**, ensuring stable access for evaluation.

---

### 14. Making the Project Easy for Judges to Evaluate
A complex project can be hard to understand quickly during judging.

**How I solved it:**  
I built a dedicated **Impact page**, maintained clear documentation, and ensured features were easy to verify through the UI.

---

### 15. Balancing Feature Development vs Stability
There was constant pressure to add more features within limited time.

**How I solved it:**  
I prioritized core functionality, validation systems, and reliability over optional enhancements.

---

**The problem it solves**

** The Problem RepoShield-AI Solves**

Modern software development heavily depends on third-party GitHub repositories—for learning, building products, rapid prototyping, and hackathons. However, this convenience introduces serious security 

 **Malicious code **hidden in repositories (e.g. eval, exec, os.system, dangerous CI scripts)

** Exposed secrets like AWS keys, GitHub tokens, API keys accidentally committed**

** Obfuscated** or minified code that hides malicious intent

** Blind trust in repositories without understanding their real behavior**

 Existing tools often execute code, rely on black-box ML, or overwhelm users with noise and false positives

For students, developers, startups, and security teams, reviewing a repository manually is slow, error-prone, and unsafe.

 **How RepoShield-AI Solves It**

RepoShield-AI provides instant, explainable, zero-execution security analysis for GitHub repositories.

It allows users to scan any GitHub repository safely—without running a single line of untrusted code—and receive a clear, prioritized security report.

** What People Can Use It For**

 **Developers & Students**

Verify if a GitHub repo is safe before cloning or running it

Detect hidden malware, secrets, or risky execution patterns

Learn why code is dangerous through explainable findings

 Hackathons & Rapid Prototyping Quickly audit third-party dependencies and starter templates Avoid accidental leaks or malicious code during demos

Perform static security checks without executing third-party code

1.  Why RepoShield-AI Is Safer & Easier
2.  Zero Code Execution – No sandboxing, no runtime risks
3.  AST-Powered Analysis – Understands real code behavior, not just regex 
4.  Noise-Aware Scanning – Skips frontend assets, bundles, and false positives\
5.  Weighted Risk Scoring – Prioritizes dangerous capabilities over trivial warnings
6.  Access-Controlled Scanning – Public repos free, private repos protected. 
7. Explainable Reports – Every finding includes why it matters and how to fix it

**Real-World Impact**

RepoShield-AI turns repository security from a manual, risky, and expert-only task into a fast, deterministic, and accessible process.

It empowers developers to:

Trust before they build
Detect threats before execution
Make informed security decisions, not guesses

**In short: RepoShield-AI makes using GitHub repositories safer, faster, and smarter—for everyone.**

**Challenges we ran into**

Building RepoShield-AI involved multiple non-trivial challenges across security, performance, and system design. Below are some of the most significant hurdles and how I overcame them.

1**. Accurate Detection Without Executing Code
**
Challenge:
Most security tools rely on sandboxed execution or dynamic analysis, which is unsafe when scanning untrusted repositories. However, purely regex-based static analysis produces too many false positives.

Solution:
I designed an AST-based static analysis engine (Python AST) that understands actual code structure and intent:

Distinguished between harmless strings and real function calls Detected dangerous patterns like eval, exec, and subprocess only when contextually risky
Added explainable findings with why it matters and how to fix it This allowed zero-execution scanning while maintaining accuracy.

 2. **Eliminating Noise from Modern Frontend Repositories**

Challenge:
Frontend-heavy projects (React, Vite, MERN stacks) contain:
Minified bundles

SVG assets
Generated files
High-entropy strings that look like secrets but aren’t
These caused overwhelming false alerts.

Solution:
Implemented a noise-cancellation layer:

Skipped node_modules, dist, build, bundled assets Ignored SVGs and minified files intelligently Applied context-aware heuristics tuned specifically for MERN and frontend projects

Result: High signal, low noise security reports.

3**. Secure Private Repository Scanning
**
Challenge:
Scanning private repositories safely required:

OAuth authentication
Token security
Strong backend access control (not just frontend checks)
A naive implementation could expose private data or allow privilege bypass.

Solution:

Integrated GitHub OAuth with CSRF state protection

Implemented JWT-based authentication (short-lived access + refresh tokens)

Enforced server-side access control to gate private repo scanning

Encrypted GitHub tokens and restricted their scope

This ensured enterprise-grade security for private repository access.

** 4. Performance on Large Repositories**

Challenge:
Scanning large repositories (thousands of files) risked:
Long response times
Memory spikes
Poor user experience

**Solution:**

Used shallow Git clones (--depth 1)

Applied file size limits (>1MB skipped)

Ran analyzers in parallel

Streamed scan progress to the frontend in real time

This kept scans fast while preserving depth.

 5. Meaningful Risk Scoring (Not Just Alerts)

Challenge:
Simply listing vulnerabilities isn’t useful. Users need to know:

Which issues matter most

What to fix first

Solution:
Built a weighted risk scoring engine that:
Prioritizes dangerous capabilities over surface warnings
Adjusts severity using context and confidence
Produces a single, understandable risk score and level
This made reports actionable instead of overwhelming.

 6. Security & Cleanup Guarantees

Challenge:
Cloned repositories contain sensitive code and secrets. Leaving files behind was unacceptable.

Solution:

Isolated each scan in a temporary directory
Enforced secure cleanup after every scan (success or failure)
Added timeout and error-handling guards
No repository data persists beyond the scan lifecycle.

📋 1. Project Overview
We  built and deployed a our full-stack application Aether using Kiro framework for planning and AWS for infrastructure. Let me break this down systematically:

🎯 2. Kiro Framework Implementation
What is Kiro's Role in Your Project?
Kiro acted as the core planning and execution layer - essentially your project's "command center" that orchestrated the entire development lifecycle.
How Kiro Was Used:
•	Structured Workflow Mapping
o	Guided the team from ideation → development → deployment
o	Provided clarity at each development stage
o	Acted as a navigational system tying everything together
•	Hooks Implementation
o	What: Automated mechanisms that trigger actions at specific points
o	Why: To eliminate manual configuration updates
o	How: Automated configuration updates whenever infrastructure or code states changed
o	Example Use Case: When backend API changes, hooks automatically updated related configurations
•	MCPs (Model Context Protocols)
o	What: Communication standards between different modules
o	Why: To ensure consistent data flow across different parts of the system
o	How: Stabilized integration across toolchains
o	Areas of Use: 
	Frontend state management ↔ Backend API responses
	Backend logic ↔ Infrastructure states
	Cross-toolchain communication
________________________________________
☁️ 3. AWS Architecture & Deployment
Region Selection
•	Region: eu-north-1 (Stockholm)
•	Why Stockholm? Likely chosen for geographic proximity to your user base or compliance requirements
Infrastructure Components (Using Terraform)
3.1 Networking Layer
•	VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) 
o	Isolated network environment for your application
o	Public Subnets: For resources that need internet access (ALB, NAT Gateway)
o	Private Subnets: For secure resources (ECS tasks, databases)
o	Why segmented? Security best practice - backend services don't need direct internet exposure
3.2 Compute Layer - Backend
•	ECS Fargate Cluster
o	What: Serverless container orchestration service
o	Why Fargate? No server management - AWS handles infrastructure
o	Technology Stack: Node.js/Express
o	Containerization Process: 
o	Backend Code → Dockerized → Pushed to ECR → Deployed via ECS
o	Security: Environment variables securely injected (not hardcoded)
•	ECR (Elastic Container Registry)
o	What: Docker image repository
o	Why: Stores and versions your container images
3.3 Load Balancing
•	Application Load Balancer (ALB) 
o	What: Traffic distributor
o	Why: Distributes incoming requests across ECS tasks
o	Benefits: High availability, health checks, SSL termination
3.4 Frontend Hosting
•	S3 Bucket
o	What: Object storage hosting static files
o	Technology: Vite-built frontend
o	Why S3? Cost-effective, scalable static hosting
•	CloudFront CDN
o	What: Content Delivery Network
o	Why: Faster global content delivery, caching, HTTPS support
o	How: Sits in front of S3, caches content at edge locations
________________________________________
🔐 4. Authentication Flow (OAuth with Google)
Initial Problem
•	Mixed-content issues (HTTP/HTTPS conflicts)
•	JWT parsing location confusion
Solution Architecture
[User] → [Login Button]
   ↓
[Google OAuth Consent Screen] (Google Cloud Console)
   ↓
[User Grants Permission]
   ↓
[Callback to ECS Backend]
   ↓
[Backend Generates JWT Token]
   ↓
[JWT Sent to Frontend]
   ↓
[Frontend Decodes & Stores Token]
   ↓
[Authenticated State - User Logged In]
Key Decision: Frontend JWT Parsing
•	What Changed: Moved JWT decoding from backend to frontend
•	Why: Resolved mixed-content issues and simplified flow
•	How It Works Now: 
1.	Backend generates JWT (server-side secret remains secure)
2.	Frontend receives and decodes JWT (public claims only)
3.	Frontend manages authentication state
Configuration
•	OAuth credentials configured in Google Cloud Console
•	Callback URLs pointed to ALB/ECS endpoints
•	HTTPS enforced throughout (via CloudFront & ALB)
