**The problem it solves**

## 🌸 The Problem Avaya Solves

### The World Isn't Equally Safe For Everyone

Every day, millions of women make a simple decision that most people never have to think about — **which route is safer to walk home?** Not the shortest. Not the fastest. The *safest*.

Traditional maps like Google Maps tell you how to get from Point A to Point B in the least time. But they don't know which street is poorly lit at night. They don't know which lane has a history of incidents. They don't know that an alley looks short on the map, but feels terrifying in real life.

**Avaya was built to change that.**

---

### 🗺️ Smarter Routes. Safer Journeys.

Avaya doesn't just show you *a* route — it shows you the **safest one**. Our routing engine scores every road segment based on real factors:

- 💡 Street lighting
- 📹 CCTV presence
- 👥 Crowd levels
- 🚔 Proximity to police stations
- 📍 Reported incidents in the area

Whether it's midnight or midday, Avaya factors in the time of day to dynamically re-score routes — because the safest path at noon isn't always the safest path at night.

---

### 🚨 One Tap When It Matters Most

In a real emergency, every second counts. Avaya's **SOS button** is built for exactly that moment.

With a single tap, Avaya simultaneously:

1. **Locates you in real-time** and pins your exact position on a live map
2. **Sends your location to the nearest local police station** for immediate response
3. **Posts an alert to the Avaya community feed** so people nearby are instantly aware

No typing. No searching. Just **one tap** — and your entire safety network is activated.

---

### 🤝 A Community That Watches Out For Each Other

Beyond routes and SOS, Avaya is also a **community platform** where women can:

- Share safety tips and local advisories
- Report incidents to warn others in the area
- Support each other through real-time community alerts

Because the most powerful safety network isn't technology — it's **people looking out for each other**.

---

### Why We Built This

> *"We kept seeing news stories, hearing real experiences, and realizing that the maps we all use every day were designed without women's safety in mind. The shortest path and the safest path are two very different things — and it was time someone built the bridge between them."*

**Avaya is that bridge.**

---

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Backend Routing Latency

**The Challenge:**  
Querying our entire city-wide database to calculate custom safety routes caused massive server timeouts.

**The Solution:**  
We optimized the system using PostGIS spatial queries. Our Node.js API breaks standard routes into micro-segments, allowing the Python FastAPI service to query only those specific coordinates. This reduced the calculation time to milliseconds.

---

## 2. SOS False Alarms (Hardware Triggers)

**The Challenge:**  
Using our on-device TFLite ML model for hardware triggers caused false positives (e.g., tossing the phone on a desk accidentally triggered the SOS).

**The Solution:**  
We engineered a **verification buffer**. Before escalating to the Socket.IO real-time backend, the app triggers a local prompt asking **"Are you safe?"** to intelligently verify whether the threat is real.

---

**Open Innovation**

We are continuously seeing that there are several scenarios where women do not feel safe. Traditional maps only show the shortest path, but we want to show the safest path so that women can travel safely. We want to solve this real-world problem, and that is why we built this solution.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/subsentry-fa20) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/angelabera/SubSentry) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://sub-sentry-two.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Track Every Subscription. Control Every Rupee.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today's digital world, people subscribe to many services such as streaming platforms, gym memberships, cloud storage, productivity tools, and online learning platforms. Because most of these services automatically renew, users often lose track of how many subscriptions they have and how much they are spending each month.

This leads to several common problems:

* People forget about active subscriptions they no longer use.
* Automatic renewals cause unexpected charges.
* There is no simple way to see all subscriptions and their costs in one place.
* Users miss cancellation deadlines before the next billing cycle.

**SubSentry solves this problem by acting as a centralized subscription management dashboard.**

Users can manually add all of their subscriptions and instantly see:

* Total monthly spending
* Total yearly spending
* Upcoming renewal dates
* Alerts for subscriptions renewing soon

By providing reminders before renewal dates and clear spending insights, the application helps users make smarter financial decisions and avoid unnecessary charges.

In short, the app makes subscription management **simpler, safer, and more transparent**, helping users stay in control of their recurring expenses.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges during development was implementing the **renewal alert system**. The application needed a way to automatically check every subscription and determine whether its renewal date was approaching.

Initially, I tried calculating the remaining days directly on the frontend, but this approach quickly became unreliable because it depended on when the user opened the application. If the user didn't log in for a few days, they might miss important renewal alerts.

To solve this problem, I implemented a **scheduled background task using `node-cron`**. This job runs automatically once per day and checks the database for subscriptions that are about to renew.

The logic works like this:

* The scheduler runs daily.
* It calculates the number of days remaining before each subscription renews.
* If the renewal date is within three days, the system generates a notification.
* The notification is then displayed in the user's notification center inside the dashboard.

Another hurdle was handling **date calculations correctly across different time zones**. Renewal dates stored in the database sometimes produced inconsistent results depending on the user's local time.

I resolved this by standardizing all stored dates in **UTC format** and using consistent date libraries for comparisons. This ensured that the alert system behaved predictably for all users.

Overcoming these issues helped make the renewal reminder system reliable and accurate.

**Open Innovation**

Fintech: Subscription Manager & Alert System: Create a tool where users manually input their various monthly subscriptions (Netflix, Gym, etc.). The app calculates total monthly spend and sends "alert" notifications before the renewal dates.

### BizChat
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bizchat-5390) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rajeet-04/BizChat) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1172522152?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci#t=0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Business with Whatsapp made super easy

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whatsapp API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whatsapp%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem BizChat Solves**

India has 60+ million small and medium businesses (SMBs) that run their daily operations through WhatsApp.

Orders, negotiations, confirmations, payments, and customer relationships all happen inside chat threads.

But WhatsApp was designed as a communication tool, not a business operating system.

As a result, millions of businesses operate in a state of constant operational chaos.

**1. Revenue Leakage (10–15% Monthly)**

Orders get buried inside long chat threads.

Payments are not systematically tracked.

Follow-ups depend on memory.

Leads go cold because reminders are missed.

For a business doing ₹10 lakh/month, this can mean ₹1 lakh lost every month simply due to operational gaps.

**2. Operational Chaos**

Most WhatsApp businesses run on unstructured conversations.

Typical workflow looks like this:

Orders confirmed through messy Hinglish texts or voice notes
Invoices created manually in Excel late at night
No structured customer history
No visibility into best-selling products
No clear record of pending payments

Everything lives inside unsearchable conversations.

**3. Traditional CRMs Fail for Tier 2/3 Businesses**

Existing CRM software does not work for these businesses because it:

Requires setup and configuration
Forces businesses to change how they work
Feels complicated and intimidating
Requires manual data entry
Adds cost without clear ROI

As a result, 92% of Indian SMBs use no CRM at all.

**What BizChat Enables?**

BizChat acts as an AI-powered operations layer on top of WhatsApp Business.

Businesses continue using WhatsApp exactly the way they already do.

BizChat works quietly in the background to turn conversations into structured business operations.

**Challenges we ran into**

**WhatsApp Web DOM Instability (Chrome Extension Issue)**

**The Problem**

WhatsApp Web behaves like a shape-shifting organism. Its internal HTML structure changes frequently, and class names are often dynamically generated.

The first implementation depended on fragile selectors such as:

document.querySelector(".message-in")

This worked… until WhatsApp pushed UI updates.
When class names changed, the extension suddenly could not detect incoming messages or parse conversations correctly.

In short, the system broke whenever WhatsApp quietly changed its front end.

**The Fix**

The solution was to stop trusting brittle CSS selectors and instead build a more resilient message detection system.

The extension architecture was redesigned using:

Stable structural anchors in the DOM instead of volatile class names
MutationObserver to detect when new chat messages are added dynamically
Content-based parsing to identify message text instead of relying purely on selectors
Fallback scanning logic to recover if DOM nodes shift

Instead of assuming the DOM will stay the same, the extension now observes changes in real time and adapts.

**Result**

The extension became significantly more stable across WhatsApp updates.

Message detection reliability improved, and the system could process conversations continuously without breaking whenever WhatsApp modified its interface.

In practice, this turned a brittle automation script into something closer to a self-healing browser layer sitting on top of WhatsApp Web.

**Open Innovation**

**Why it fits Open Innovation:**

- Real problem, underserved market — targets the 60M+ informal SMEs in India with zero tech adoption
- AI-native workflow — LLM-powered extraction, not brittle regex rules, so it handles messy real-world chat
- Full-stack, production-ready — not a prototype: auth, multi-tenancy, Redis job queues, WebSockets, rate limiting, PDF generation, Docker setup
- Extensible — the same pipeline can plug into Telegram, Instagram DMs, or voice notes (Whisper provider is already wired in)
- Impact — saves a shop owner 1–2 hours/day of manual bookkeeping; reduces billing errors and missed orders

### AndroidYodha
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/androidyodha-e5e2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shreyansh-hacker/sms_call_detector) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Real-time scam detection for SMS ,calls andR links

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AndroidYodha is a system designed to protect users from scams that happen through phone calls and SMS. People in India and around the world often receive fraudulent messages or calls related to OTP requests, fake KYC updates, UPI fraud, phishing links, and other social-engineering tricks. Many users find it difficult to quickly determine whether a message or call is genuine, especially when it uses mixed language formats like Hinglish or regional scripts.

AndroidYodha addresses this problem by acting as a fraud-intelligence layer for mobile communication. It analyzes SMS messages, call transcripts, and URLs in real time to identify suspicious patterns. The system is designed to understand multilingual and mixed-script content, including English, Hindi, Hinglish, and various regional or international messaging styles.

It can detect brand impersonation, such as messages pretending to be from banks, UPI services, or government organizations. It also looks for urgency or coercive language commonly used in social-engineering attacks. In addition to content analysis, AndroidYodha performs behavioral analysis, campaign detection, caller network intelligence (CNI), and graph-based risk analysis to identify coordinated fraud activity.

The system uses an architecture that supports offline-first detection with cloud-based intelligence for deeper analysis when connectivity is available. For every message or call analyzed, it provides an explainable risk score such as SAFE, UNKNOWN, SPAM, PHISHING, or FRAUD, along with the reasons behind the decision.

AndroidYodha can be used by telecom companies and caller-ID systems to warn users about potential scams, by banks and fintech companies to enhance fraud alerts, by cyber police or CERT teams to detect scam campaigns, and by everyday users who want real-time protection when they receive calls or SMS.

Overall, AndroidYodha converts raw communication data into clear, explainable fraud decisions to help make digital interactions safer.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building AndroidYodha involved several technical challenges across both the Android application and the backend intelligence system.

1. Live call speech capture limitations (OEM and Android restrictions)
On some devices, PSTN downlink audio is not directly accessible to third-party apps due to Android and OEM restrictions. To handle this, I implemented a fallback foreground monitoring service, optimized the speech routing and diagnostics, and added a no-speech AI fallback scoring system when transcripts are unavailable.

2. Default dialer and permission behavior across different OEM ROMs
Different Android manufacturers handle the default dialer role and permissions differently, and some devices do not expose the expected role flows. To address this, I implemented guided setup diagnostics, optional dialer handling for unsupported devices, and robust permission and settings fallbacks.

3. Real-time AI pipeline reliability
During early development, the AI pipeline experienced issues such as request serialization failures and lack of observability. I resolved these by correcting the converter configuration using the Moshi Kotlin adapter, adding structured stage-wise runtime logging, and implementing backend probes with error-safe fallback paths.

4. Multilingual and mixed-script fraud text normalization
Scam messages often use mixed scripts, Unicode tricks, and obfuscation techniques such as replacing letters with numbers (e.g., “acc0unt”) or using full-width characters. To detect these patterns, I added Unicode normalization, confusable character folding, mixed-script and language detection flags, and multilingual fraud phrase detection focused on social-engineering patterns.

5. Building explainable intelligence instead of a black-box model
Rather than relying on a single opaque model, I designed a modular backend intelligence engine. It combines multiple signals such as reputation data, campaign detection, behavior and velocity analysis, brand mismatch detection, caller network intelligence (CNI), graph relationships, and URL/IP/ASN heuristics. These signals feed into a central risk engine that produces explainable risk scores along with confidence levels and reasoning.

These challenges ultimately helped strengthen the system’s architecture and reliability, making AndroidYodha a more robust and production-oriented solution.

### DevSentinel
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/devsentinel-ebb2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/divyanshu-vr/DevSentinal) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bCfeEm19HWK7y7K73aTwShcFW-xtKaTi?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your AI QA Engineer that never sleeps

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Support Vector Machine (SVM)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support%20Vector%20Machine%20(SVM)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern software teams rely heavily on Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) to define how features should behave. However, once development begins, there is rarely an automated system that verifies whether the implementation actually matches the specification.

As a result, several problems occur:

• Features described in the PRD are partially implemented or missing entirely
• Bugs are discovered late during QA or even after deployment
• Security vulnerabilities and production issues remain unnoticed
• Developers must manually locate the problematic code, write fixes, and create pull requests

Existing tools either analyze code (like linters and static analysis tools) or assist in writing code, but none automatically connect the specification with the implementation and fix issues autonomously.

DevSentinel solves this by acting as an AI-powered QA engineer for codebases.

The platform analyzes a GitHub repository, compares the implementation with the expected behavior defined in the PRD, detects broken features, security issues, and production risks, and then generates fixes automatically. Using ephemeral sandbox environments, the system safely tests these fixes before opening a pull request for developers to review.

By automating code verification and repair, DevSentinel helps teams:

• Detect bugs earlier in the development lifecycle
• Reduce manual debugging and code review time
• Improve software reliability and security
• Ensure that implementations stay aligned with product specifications

This significantly reduces development friction and enables teams to ship more reliable software faster.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we encountered during development was building a reliable **ephemeral sandbox environment** for our AI agents. Our system needs to safely execute code analysis, generate fixes, and validate them before opening pull requests. Initially, we attempted to run our AI analysis pipeline using the Gemini API inside the** sandbox environment**, but we faced repeated issues where the API keys were not functioning reliably inside the isolated runtime environment.

To overcome this, we temporarily switched to Groq inference, which provided extremely fast LLM responses. However, during large repository analysis we quickly hit token limits, since scanning many files required multiple large-context requests.

Another major challenge was handling large codebases efficiently. Sending entire repositories directly to an LLM is not feasible due to token limits and performance constraints. To solve this, we implemented a Code Graph Builder approach.

Instead of sending the entire codebase to the model, our system first parses the repository and constructs a structured representation of the project. This includes:

• file structure and dependency relationships
• API routes and service layers
• component and module import graphs
• authentication and database model mappings

This graph allows the AI system to understand how different parts of the code interact. When analyzing a bug or feature, the agent retrieves only the relevant files and dependency chains instead of the full repository.

To further reduce token usage, we adopted an **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** architecture. The AI agent interacts with the codebase through controlled tools such as:

• read_file – fetch specific file contents
• search_codebase – locate relevant functions or modules
• run_command – execute validation scripts in the sandbox

This approach allowed the AI to dynamically retrieve only the context it needs, dramatically reducing token consumption and improving system scalability.

By combining ephemeral sandbox execution, a code graph builder, and MCP-based tool calling, we were able to build a system that can analyze large repositories efficiently while keeping compute usage and token costs under control.

**Best Use of Vultr**

DevSentinel leverages Vultr’s cloud infrastructure to create ephemeral sandbox environments for autonomous AI agents that analyze and repair software codebases.

When a developer triggers the Auto-Fix feature, our system dynamically provisions an ephemeral Vultr VM instance using the Vultr API. This temporary virtual machine acts as a secure, isolated execution environment where the platform can safely interact with the user’s repository.

Inside the ephemeral VM, DevSentinel performs several automated steps:

• Clones the target GitHub repository
• Installs project dependencies and runtime environment
• Runs static analysis and AI-based testing on the codebase
• Allows the AI agent to modify files and generate a fix
• Executes linting and test suites to validate the patch
• Pushes the changes to a new GitHub branch and opens a Pull Request

After the task completes, the ephemeral VM is automatically destroyed, ensuring that no compute resources remain active and no user code persists on the system.

Using Vultr in this way provides several advantages:

• Security: untrusted code runs in isolated ephemeral infrastructure
• Scalability: multiple AI agents can run in parallel across separate VMs
• Cost efficiency: compute resources exist only for the duration of each task
• Reliability: each analysis starts in a clean environment with no leftover state

By combining AI-driven code analysis with ephemeral cloud execution on Vultr, DevSentinel creates a secure and scalable platform where autonomous agents can test, debug, and repair real software projects without risking the host infrastructure.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

DevSentinel explores how generative AI can fundamentally transform the way developers debug, maintain, and improve software systems. Our project builds an AI-powered engineering assistant that can analyze a codebase, detect broken features, and generate fixes automatically.

We leverage modern AI reasoning models to understand complex codebases, trace dependencies between files, and simulate how an experienced developer would review a project. Instead of relying on traditional static analysis tools, the system uses generative AI to reason about logic errors, missing implementations, and security issues across an entire repository.

To make this scalable for real-world projects, we implemented a code graph builder that maps relationships between files, APIs, and components. The AI system then retrieves only the relevant parts of the codebase using structured tool calls through an MCP-based architecture. This allows the model to analyze large repositories efficiently while maintaining strong reasoning capabilities.

The result is a platform where developers can connect a repository and instantly receive a detailed analysis of bugs, architectural issues, and missing features, along with suggested fixes.

Our project demonstrates how AI systems can evolve from simple assistants into autonomous engineering tools that help developers understand and repair complex software systems, aligning closely with the vision of AI-powered development tools supported by the Google ecosystem.

### Neuro Hire
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neuro-hire-c0c1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Psc-06/NeuroHire.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> See beyound the resume

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Judge0 API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Judge0%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Monaco Editor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Monaco%20Editor-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Hiring is broken — not because companies don't try, but because 
resumes lie. Not always intentionally, but they do.

A candidate writes "Advanced React" on their resume. They get 
shortlisted. They reach the final round. The interviewer discovers 
they can barely write a useEffect hook. That's a wasted interview, 
a wasted shortlist, and sometimes — a wasted hire.

NeuroHire fixes this by doing something no hiring tool currently 
does well: it doesn't just test what a candidate knows — it tracks 
HOW they think while solving a real problem.

**Here's what NeuroHire does:**

1. Admin uploads a candidate's resume and generates secure 
   login credentials in one click.

2. Candidate logs in to a protected test environment — no sharing, 
   no cheating, session-locked access.

3. While the candidate solves a real coding problem in a Monaco 
   editor (the same one powering VS Code), NeuroHire silently 
   tracks behavioral signals:

   - Time to first keystroke
-    Number of edits and rewrites
-    Compile errors and debugging attempts
-    Test case run frequency
-    Idle time patterns


4. When the candidate submits, the recruiter gets an AI-generated 
   report that compares:

   - What the resume claimed
-    What the behavioral data actually showed

The result:  by the time a candidate reaches the final interview, 
the interviewer already knows exactly who they're talking to.

NeuroHire doesn't replace human judgment. It gives humans 
better data to judge with.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building NeuroHire in 36 hours taught us exactly where the hard 
parts of hiring tech actually live.

1. Resume parsing was harder than expected
   PDF structure is inconsistent across templates. We had to build 
   a pipeline that extracts raw text regardless of formatting, then 
   uses an LLM to convert that into structured skill data. Getting 
   the JSON output reliable took multiple prompt iterations.

2. Behavioral tracking without disrupting the candidate experience
   The tracking had to be completely invisible. If candidates know 
   they're being tracked keystroke-by-keystroke, it changes their 
   behavior. We had to instrument Monaco Editor's event listeners 
   (onDidChangeModelContent, onDidChangeModel) in a way that logs 
   silently to state without any UI indication.

3. The scoring fairness problem
   Our mentor raised a critical point during review: a candidate 
   who takes 3 minutes to start but writes perfect code is being 
   unfairly penalized by a time-heavy scoring model. We rethought 
   the weights — time is now only 15% of the score. Accuracy, 
   approach, and code quality carry the real weight.

4. Secure candidate access
   We needed each candidate to have a unique, session-protected 
   test link that couldn't be accessed without the generated 
   credentials. Building the admin → credential generation → 
   candidate login → protected test flow in one session was the 
   most complex auth challenge we solved here.

5. Connecting the pipeline end to end
   Each piece — resume parser, behavioral tracker, code executor, 
   AI report generator, recruiter dashboard — works individually. 
   Making them talk to each other as one unbroken flow under 
   time pressure was the real challenge of this hackathon.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

NeuroHire's frontend interface and component architecture 
was built using Google Antigravity for rapid UI development 
and basic modeling of the candidate and recruiter flows.

Antigravity helped us move fast on the visual layer — 
the admin dashboard, candidate test environment, and 
recruiter report screen — without sacrificing the quality 
of the core behavioral tracking logic underneath.

In a 36-hour hackathon, having a tool that lets you model 
and iterate UI quickly meant we could spend our real energy 
on the parts no tool can do for you: the resume parsing 
pipeline, the behavioral event logger, and the AI comparison 
engine.

### WireStack
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/wirestack-7706) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://acehack5-0-wirestack.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your Stack. Your Rules. AI Built.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our AI Agent is a visual software development assistant designed for both developers and non-developers. Users start by describing the application they want to build using a simple prompt. The AI agent then generates a step-by-step architecture flow of the application, including components such as database, authentication, payments, notifications, maps, and deployment.

At each stage, the user can select the tools or technologies they want to use (for example PostgreSQL for database, Stripe for payments, or AWS for deployment). Based on the selected stack, the AI agent automatically generates the project architecture, file structure, configuration files, and boilerplate code for the developers required to start building the application, and they can just download the zip file of project and start building it. So no developers have to waste time while forming the whole architecture.

For non-developers, the system acts as a guided learning environment, explaining each technology and helping them understand the development process while building the application.

We also integrated an AI Project Analyzer that can analyze both the current project and existing projects by simply providing a GitHub repository link. The analyzer reviews the project structure, technologies used, and architecture to provide insights and suggestions for improvement.

Additionally, the agent provides deployment guidance, suggesting cloud platforms and step-by-step instructions to deploy the application. If users face issues during any step, they can ask the agent to help resolve the problem or complete the step.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.	First Time Building an AI Agent
Since this was our first time developing an AI-based agent, understanding how AI assistants work internally was challenging. We had to learn concepts such as prompts, responses, and how to structure requests to get reliable outputs.
	2.	Understanding Token Usage and Limits
While integrating AI APIs, we faced difficulties understanding how tokens are consumed during prompts and responses. Managing token limits and optimizing prompts to avoid excessive usage required experimentation.
	3.	Generating Consistent File Structures
One major challenge was ensuring the AI consistently generated the correct project file structure and configuration files. Sometimes the AI produced incomplete or inconsistent structures, so we had to refine prompts and logic to improve reliability.
	4.	Handling Different Technology Stacks
Supporting multiple technology options (databases, payment systems, deployment platforms, etc.) made it difficult to maintain a consistent architecture generation process.
	5.	Balancing Simplicity for Non-Developers and Flexibility for Developers
Designing the system so that non-developers could easily understand the process while still allowing developers to customize the stack required careful design decisions.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

1. Complex Data Structuring (JSON) over Plain Text Instead of using Gemini for simple text generation, we engineered our prompts to output deeply structured JSON arrays. Gemini acts as a Senior Technical Architect, taking a raw user idea (e.g., "Build a video sharing app") and breaking it down into a Gamified System Design Graph. It dynamically maps industry-standard "Best Practices" versus "Alternatives" (like React vs. Vue, or Express vs. NestJS) directly into our ReactFlow canvas.

2. Multi-File Code Scaffolding (Zero-to-One) We heavily utilized Gemini's large context window and advanced coding capabilities. Once a user finishes their interactive learning path, Gemini doesn't just return snippets—it generates an entire working, interconnected codebase (Frontend components, Backend routes, and configuration files) simultaneously. We parse this output on the fly and render it into a live, in-browser code editor and interactive IFRAME preview.

### SavePulse

**The problem it solves**

Open source contribution is one of the most effective ways for developers to build real experience, grow their portfolio, and get hired — yet the vast majority of developers never make a single contribution. Not because they lack skill, but because the process is broken.
Contribo fixes that end-to-end.
---

### Find repos that actually match you
Instead of blindly searching GitHub and hoping something sticks, Contribo analyzes your **GitHub profile + resume using Gemini AI** to understand your real experience level — your project complexity, technical depth, and contribution readiness. It then recommends repos with a scored match, so you're not wasting hours on codebases that are either too trivial or completely over your head.

### Get a step-by-step contribution roadmap
Once you pick a repo, Contribo fetches its real open issues, PR history, file structure, and CONTRIBUTING guidelines and generates a personalized, phased roadmap. Not generic advice — a concrete plan with actual issue numbers, specific files to look at, and estimated time per task.

Eliminate the "I don't know where to start" paralysis
The #1 reason developers abandon open source contributions is not knowing what to do first. Contribo surfaces quick wins — real, beginner-friendly issues from the actual codebase — so you can make your first PR in hours, not weeks.
---
Whether you're a self-taught developer building your first portfolio, a CS student preparing for internship season, or an intermediate engineer looking to level up — Contribo turns open source from overwhelming to achievable.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into:
1. GitHub API Rate Limits — The 60 Requests/Hour Wall
The most brutal blocker we hit early on. Without an authenticated token, GitHub gives you 60 requests per hour per IP. A single analysis of 30 repos already consumed 60+ requests, meaning the app would fail for literally every second user in a row.

How we fixed it:

Mandatory GITHUB_TOKEN authentication → bumped the limit to 5,000 req/hour
Implemented ETag / If-None-Match conditional requests — if the data hasn't changed since the last fetch, GitHub returns 304 Not Modified which is completely free and doesn't count against the quota.
Added exponential backoff with jitter (1s → 2s → 4s + random noise) to survive transient 403/429 errors without thundering-herd retries
Result: effective throughput equivalent to ~25,000 requests/hour.

2. Redis Cache Returning "[object Object]" — A Silent Data Corruption Bug
After wiring up Upstash (Redis-over-REST), analysis results started coming back as garbled "[object Object]" strings instead of actual JSON. Cached data was silently unusable and threw JSON.parse errors on reads.

Root cause: Upstash REST automatically serializes objects to JSON on write, but we were also calling JSON.stringify() before sending — resulting in double serialization. The stored string was a JSON string of a string.

How we fixed it:
Centralized all token logic in authService.js with a strict load order
UserContext defers data fetches until the JWT is confirmed present
The callback route explicitly waits for token storage before triggering any redirect.

One of the more frustrating walls we hit was Gemini's free-tier daily quota. The original pipeline called Gemini individually for every candidate repository — meaning a single user analysis could burn through 30+ requests in one shot. On days with heavier testing or multiple users running analyses back-to-back, we'd slam into the daily limit mid-session, leaving users staring at a broken results page with no explanation. To fix this, we overhauled the pipeline with a hybrid pre-scoring strategy: GitHub metadata (stars, size, topics, language, issue count) is used to score and rank all candidates first — completely free, no AI calls — and only the top 15 repos are forwarded to Gemini. Those 15 are then batched 5-per-prompt instead of 1-per-call, bringing the total from 31 Gemini calls down to just 3 per analysis. On top of that, we added a static heuristic fallback that fires when Gemini is unavailable entirely, estimating complexity from repo metadata patterns so the app never returns a blank result even when the quota is fully exhausted.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI-generated content such as deepfake videos, synthetic images, cloned voices, and AI-written text is becoming increasingly realistic and difficult to identify. This makes misinformation, scams, and manipulated media easier to spread across social platforms, news, and academic content.

**VerifAI** helps users quickly verify the authenticity of online content. With a browser extension and web dashboard, users can scan images, videos, text, or links to detect potential AI generation or manipulation.

This makes it easier and safer for students, journalists, creators, and everyday internet users to verify sources, avoid misinformation, and trust the content they interact with online.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Getting videos reliably from YouTube/Instagram/TikTok (cookies, private/region‑locked, changing sites) was unstable.
- Inputs had random FPS/aspect ratios, so simple metadata rules easily gave false alarms.
- Many heavy models (SigLIP, Swin, BLIP, CLIP, Whisper, BART, DeepFace, EasyOCR) made GPU/CPU limits, time, and crashes a big issue.
- No single detector was enough; we had to design and tune an 11‑component ensemble + logistic classifier to get a sensible “fake probability.”
- Full forensic checks are expensive, so we had to simplify or skip some physics/anatomy tests in the real‑time API version.
- Cross‑checking visuals, speech, text, and news (misinformation) created many edge cases like old clips with new misleading captions.
- Converting a huge technical report into a simple Chrome‑extension verdict (RED/ORANGE/GREEN + one score) and keeping the Flask + ngrok backend stable was non‑trivial.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Why Traditional Fitness Apps Are Failing
Most health apps are built on the wrong psychological foundation. Here is the reality of the "Inactivity Crisis" we are tackling:

1. The "Digital Spreadsheet" Fatigue
The market is flooded with trackers like Strava, Fitbit, and Apple Health. They are great at collecting data, but they are essentially clinical spreadsheets.

The Issue: Raw data (steps, calories, miles) isn't a long-term motivator for the average person.

The Result: Seeing a bar graph go up by 5% doesn't trigger a "must-act" response in the human brain.

2. The 90-Day Retention Cliff
The fitness app industry has a massive abandonment problem.

The Stat: Industry research shows that nearly 80% of users stop using a new fitness app within the first 30 to 90 days.

The Cause: "Digital Badges" and "Streaks" feel arbitrary. Once the novelty wears off, there is no real-world consequence for skipping a day.

3. The Lack of "Loss Aversion"
Behavioral economics (led by Nobel Prize winner Daniel Kahneman) proves that Loss Aversion-the psychological pain of losing something we already have-is twice as powerful as the joy of gaining something new.

Current Apps: Only focus on "Gains" (Earn a badge! Get a trophy!).

The Missing Piece: No app makes you feel the "sting" of inactivity. If you stay on the couch, nothing happens. In the real world, if you don't defend your territory, you lose it.

4. The Global Inactivity Crisis
According to the World Health Organization (WHO):

1 in 3 adults and 80% of adolescents do not meet the minimum physical activity levels.

This leads to a $54 billion annual drain on global healthcare systems.

We don't have a lack of tracking tools; we have a lack of motivation tools.

The Waddle Solution
Waddle moves the needle from "I should walk" to "I have to walk." By turning your neighborhood into a persistent kingdom, we give you something to own and more importantly, something to lose. We've replaced the "Boring Bar Graph" with a 24-hour Siege Mechanic, using the most powerful psychological trigger in the human brain to keep people moving.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Tackled
Building a real-time territory game during a hackathon is a massive logic puzzle. Here are the biggest hurdles we cleared:

The "Jittery Kingdom" (GPS Noise): Raw GPS data is messy-if we mapped every single point, the kingdom borders looked like jagged spiderwebs. We had to implement a smoothing algorithm to filter out "drifting" points, ensuring the borders looked like clean, intentional "doodle" strokes.

Battery vs. Battle (The Polling Paradox): High-frequency GPS tracking kills phone batteries in minutes, but low-frequency tracking misses the exact moment you cross into a rival’s zone. We solved this with Adaptive Polling: the app pings more frequently when you're near a rival border and throttles back when you're in "safe" territory.

The "Drive-By" Conquest (Anti-Cheating): The biggest threat to a walking app is someone in a Suzuki Dzire. We built a Velocity-Threshold system. If the app detects sustained speeds over 30 km/h, it triggers a 15-second "Walk Verification" window. If you don't confirm you're on foot, the session auto-terminates to keep the leaderboard honest.

Real-Time Geometry Math: Calculating the exact intersection of two complex walking paths (to trigger the battle effects) is CPU-heavy. To keep the app smooth, we used Bounding-Box checks-the app only runs the "heavy" polygon math if your current position is within the rectangular "fence" of a neighbor's kingdom.

Visual Consistency: Turning standard, sterile map tiles into a "hand-drawn" world was tough. We had to layer custom Canvas overlays and hatching textures on top of the map API without blocking user interactions or lagging the zoom levels.

**Gemini API**

Intelligent Nutrition & Fueling (Gemini 2.5 flash API)
We integrated the Gemini 2.5 flash API to solve the biggest friction point in health apps: Manual Data Entry. Most people stop tracking their nutrition because searching for "Chicken Salad" in a database of 10,000 items is boring.

Unstructured to Structured Data: We use Gemini to process natural language inputs (e.g., "I just had a medium latte and a blueberry muffin"). The API instantly parses this into a structured JSON object containing estimated calories, protein, and hydration levels.

> Dynamic travel identity pass

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🚨 **The Fragmentation & Security Crisis in Indian Travel**
Traveling across India—whether for leisure or critical medical care—is currently a fragmented, frustrating, and insecure experience. Tourists are forced to juggle a dozen different apps (flights, trains, hotels, itineraries) while exposing their highly sensitive physical documents at every checkpoint. IndiaXplore solves this by unifying the entire travel lifecycle under one AI-driven, cryptographically secure roof.

Here is exactly how IndiaXplore makes travel safer, easier, and smarter:

🛡️ **1. Eliminating Identity Theft (Making Travel Safer)**
The Problem: Travelers constantly hand over physical Aadhar cards, Passports, and Visas to airport security, hotel receptionists, and local authorities, leaving photocopies everywhere and risking massive identity theft.

Our Solution: The Zero-Knowledge Digital Travel Pass. We replace physical IDs with a dynamic, unified QR code. Using the Web Crypto API, we hash sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) directly in the browser. Checkpoints simply scan the QR to verify identity without ever seeing or storing the plaintext data.

🧠 **2. Killing "Research Fatigue" (Making Planning Easier)**
The Problem: Planning a trip on a strict budget takes hours of Googling, cross-referencing prices, and mapping out routes.

Our Solution: Our AI Tourism Concierge (powered by Google Gemini) acts as an elite travel agent. You simply input your destination, dates, and strict budget limit. The AI instantly generates a mathematically realistic, day-by-day itinerary, complete with local cultural tips, famous eateries, and accurate cost breakdowns. If your budget is completely unrealistic, the AI politely advises you to adjust it!

🏥 **3. Demystifying Medical Tourism (Life-Saving Convenience)**
The Problem: Thousands travel to India (or across states) for healthcare, but finding accredited hospitals, estimating surgery costs, and planning recovery logistics is overwhelming for patients.

Our Solution: A dedicated Medical Concierge Hub. Patients input their required treatment and budget. The AI bypasses tourist traps and immediately provides:

Top NABH/JCI accredited hospital recommendations.

A step-by-step clinical pathway (Consultation ➔ Pre-Op ➔ Procedure ➔ Recovery).

Estimated cost splits between medical fees, hotel stays, and logistics.

📱 **4. Curing "App Overload" (Unified Ecosystem)**
The Problem: You book a flight on MakeMyTrip, a train on IRCTC, a cab on Ola, and check your itinerary on Google Docs.

Our Solution: One Unified Dashboard. IndiaXplore aggregates your AI-generated itinerary, Auth0-secured user profile, flight/train/hotel bookings, and digital identity pass into a single, beautiful, glassmorphic web app.

🌍 **5. Breaking Language Barriers (True Accessibility)**
The Problem: Most premium travel platforms assume the user speaks fluent English, alienating millions of domestic tourists.

Our Solution: Built-in Localization. IndiaXplore features a seamless UI translation engine supporting English, Hindi, and Bengali, ensuring the platform is accessible to a massive demographic.

**Summary:** IndiaXplore doesn't just book tickets; it acts as a digital bodyguard, a local guide, and a medical coordinator, fundamentally upgrading how people experience Incredible India.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building IndiaXplore in a time-constrained hackathon environment pushed us to make rapid, high-stakes architectural decisions. Here are the biggest hurdles we faced and how we engineered our way out of them:

**1. The "11th Hour" Environment Crash (React to Vanilla Pivot)**
*The Hurdle:* We initially set up our project using React and Vite. However, midway through the build, we ran into severe Windows PowerShell UnauthorizedAccess Execution Policy errors that completely blocked npm run dev from compiling our app.

*The Fix:* Instead of wasting hours fighting OS-level permissions and build tools, we made a ruthless, strategic pivot. We instantly migrated our entire architecture to a Vanilla HTML/JS + Tailwind CSS (via CDN) stack. This decision was a lifesaver—it gave us zero compilation overhead, lightning-fast live reloading, and allowed us to build a stunning glassmorphic UI without touching a terminal.

**2. The Enterprise API Trap (CORS & OAuth2 Blockers)**
*The Hurdle:* To get live flight and hotel data, we successfully researched and registered for the Amadeus GDS API and IRCTC RapidAPI wrappers. However, calling these enterprise APIs directly from the frontend triggered massive CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) errors. Furthermore, managing Amadeus's 2-step OAuth2 Bearer Tokens without a dedicated backend server was creating massive latency.

*The Fix:* We engineered an innovative "AI Aggregation Fallback." Instead of relying on rigid, rate-limited APIs, we transformed the Google Gemini API into a simulated live booking engine. We wrote highly complex system prompts that force the AI to evaluate budgets, pull historical pricing data, and generate mathematically accurate, hyper-realistic flight numbers, train routes, and costs on the fly.

**3. Taming the LLM for Strict JSON Parsing**
*The Hurdle:* Using Gemini as our backend data engine created a new problem: LLMs naturally want to converse. Even when instructed to return pure JSON, Gemini would occasionally wrap the response in Markdown blockquotes (e.g., ```json { ... } ```), which instantly crashed our JSON.parse() rendering logic on the frontend.

*The Fix:* We built a custom text-sanitization pipeline in JavaScript. Before parsing the AI's response, our code uses Regex to strip out markdown ticks and dynamically slices the string from the first { to the last }. This guarantees our UI cards render flawlessly 100% of the time, making the AI behave like a strict, predictable database.

**4. Implementing Client-Side "Zero-Knowledge" Security**
*The Hurdle:* For our Digital Travel Pass and Admin Dashboard, we needed a way to prove we were securely handling Aadhar and Passport numbers without actually storing them in plain text, all without a backend database.

*The Fix:* We dove deep into the native Web Crypto API (window.crypto.subtle). We built a real-time cryptographic hashing function that converts sensitive PII into irreversible SHA-256 hashes the millisecond the user types it. When demonstrating the "Admin Database," we show the judges raw cryptographic hashes instead of plaintext IDs, successfully prototyping a true zero-knowledge architecture purely on the frontend.

**5. Integrating Auth0 in a Serverless Prototype**
*The Hurdle:* Implementing enterprise-grade authentication for the Sponsor Track usually requires a backend server to manage sessions securely.

*The Fix:* We successfully integrated the Auth0 SPA (Single Page Application) SDK directly into our Vanilla JS index file. We mapped the login/logout UI state dynamically, ensuring users are seamlessly redirected to Auth0's secure universal login gateway and back, pulling their verified profile data into our application completely statelessly.

🧩 The Problem It Solves

India’s legal system is complex, technical, and often intimidating for the average citizen. Legal information is usually written in difficult language, scattered across multiple sources, and hard to interpret without professional help. As a result:

⚖️ People don’t fully understand their rights and responsibilities

📄 Legal documents feel confusing and overwhelming

🏛️ Case tracking is unclear and difficult to follow

💰 Accessing lawyers for basic queries can be expensive

⏳ Finding reliable legal help takes time and effort

This creates a major access-to-justice gap, especially for individuals who cannot afford immediate legal consultation.

🚀 How LegalEase Helps

LegalEase makes legal processes simpler, safer, and more accessible through AI-powered assistance.

💬 1. Get Instant Legal Guidance

Users can ask legal questions in simple language and receive clear, easy-to-understand explanations.
➡️ No legal jargon. No waiting. No confusion.

📑 2. Understand Complex Documents

Upload contracts, notices, or agreements and receive plain-language summaries.
➡️ Reduces the risk of signing documents without understanding them.

📊 3. Track Legal Cases Easily

Monitor case status, next hearing dates, and updates in one place.
➡️ Saves time and prevents missed deadlines.

📚 4. Learn Your Rights Clearly

Explore rights related to arrest, employment, consumer protection, family law, and more.
➡️ Empowers citizens to act confidently and lawfully.

🔎 5. Find Verified Legal Help

Search for lawyers and legal aid services by specialization and location.
➡️ Makes access to professional support faster and more reliable.

🌍 Impact

LegalEase transforms legal access from something intimidating and expensive into something clear, approachable, and empowering.

It helps people:

Make informed decisions

Protect themselves legally

Save time and money

Reduce stress when dealing with legal matters

In short, LegalEase bridges the gap between complex law and everyday citizens.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was handling AI hallucinations in the legal chatbot. Since legal information must be accurate, even small mistakes were risky. I solved this by refining system prompts, restricting responses to Indian legal context, and adding clear disclaimers to ensure the chatbot provides guidance—not professional legal advice.

Another hurdle was parsing complex PDFs in the Document Simplifier. Some files had messy formatting or scanned text, which caused poor summaries. I improved text extraction handling and structured prompts to better process imperfect input.

Overall, the key challenge was balancing accuracy, speed, and reliability within a hackathon timeline.

**Gemini API**

For LegalEase, we integrated Google’s Google Gemini to power the AI Legal Chatbot during the hackathon. Gemini enables the chatbot to understand complex legal queries in natural language and generate clear, context-aware responses tailored to Indian laws.

By leveraging Gemini’s strong reasoning and language capabilities, the chatbot converts complicated legal terminology into simple, plain-English explanations that everyday users can understand. It supports dynamic conversations, follow-up questions, and personalized guidance, making legal assistance feel interactive and accessible.

Using Gemini allowed us to rapidly prototype an intelligent, scalable solution that delivers real-time legal insights — aligning perfectly with LegalEase’s mission of simplifying legal access for all Indians. ⚖️

**The problem it solves**

# 0xBet
### Autonomous intelligent betting, at your fingertips.

---

## The Problem

Sports betting rewards research. Almost no one has the time, tools, or discipline to do it properly.

The edge comes from understanding team form, injury reports, historical head-to-heads, line movement, and market mispricing. Professional bettors ("sharps") spend hours every day on this before placing a single bet.

For everyone else, three things get in the way:

- **Time** — thorough research takes hours per fixture, most people don't have it
- **Consistency** — humans cut corners, miss signals, and make assumptions
- **Emotion** — humans tilt, chase losses, and bet with their heart not their head

The result: retail bettors lose. Not because the edge doesn't exist — it does — but because they lack the infrastructure to find and act on it.

---

## What 0xBet Does

0xBet is an **autonomous AI betting agent** that operates as its own on-chain business.

You fund it once. It does everything else.

The agent continuously researches upcoming sports fixtures, identifies mispriced markets on [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com), places bets with mathematically sound stake sizing, collects winnings, and reinvests profits into more research — compounding its own intelligence over time.

It runs 24/7, without emotion, without fatigue, and without taking a rake.

---

## How It Works

```
User deposits USDC → 0xBet's icpay merchant account
        ↓
Agent allocates budget: bets / compute / reserve
        ↓
Agent purchases research compute via ClawRouter - pay-per-request USDC, no API keys
        ↓
Agent uses Bird (OpenClaw skill) to pull recent X activity around upcoming fixtures
        ↓
AI analyses sentiment, narrative, and social signals to identify which result to bet on
        ↓
Agent sizes stakes using Kelly Criterion based on confidence and bankroll
        ↓
Agent deposits USDC to Polymarket and places bets via CLOB API
        ↓
Winnings swept back to treasury → reinvested automatically
```

---

## What People Use It For

### 🧠 Replacing manual research
Bettors who currently spend hours reading match previews, checking injury lists, and scanning X for breaking news can offload all of that to 0xBet. The agent uses Bird to pull real-time X activity — journalist reports, insider leaks, fan sentiment, team announcements — and synthesises it into a betting decision faster and more consistently than any individual could.

### 📈 Compounding a betting bankroll
Rather than letting winnings sit in a withdrawal queue, 0xBet automatically reinvests profits into the next research cycle and the next set of bets. The bankroll compounds. The more it wins, the more compute it buys, the better its research gets.

### 🔒 Removing emotional bias
The biggest edge killer in sports betting is the human mind — chasing losses, overweighting recent form, betting on your favourite team. 0xBet has no favourite team. It reads the signals, sizes the bet, and executes.

### 💸 Accessing decentralised betting markets
Polymarket offers peer-to-peer sports markets with tighter margins than traditional books. 0xBet plugs directly into Polymarket's CLOB API, giving users access to better odds without the friction of navigating the interface themselves.

### 👁️ Full transparency, on-chain
Every deposit, every research spend, every bet placed, and every settlement is recorded on-chain and visible in the 0xBet dashboard. No black box. Users can see exactly what the agent is doing with their funds in real time.

### 🤖 The future of agentic commerce
0xBet is the first example of a fully autonomous business built on [icpay](https://icpay.org) — accepting payments, purchasing its own compute, and generating returns, all without human intervention. It's not just a betting tool. It's a proof of concept for what AI agents can do when given economic autonomy.

---

## The Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Payments & Treasury | icpay (Base USDC) |
| Compute Payments | ClawRouter (pay-per-request, USDC on Base) |
| Social Research | Bird via OpenClaw (X sentiment + activity) |
| Betting Markets | Polymarket CLOB API |
| Settlement Chain | Base |

---

*Built at ETH Denver 2026.*

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

---

## 1. Agent Hallucinations on Trade Confirmation

One of the most frustrating issues we encountered was the AI agent confidently reporting that it had placed a bet on Polymarket — when it hadn't.

The agent would complete its research cycle, identify a pick, and then state that the trade had been executed. Checking our database told a different story: no trade record existed. The agent had hallucinated the confirmation.

**How we fixed it:** We implemented a verification step where the agent is explicitly told to check the database for confirmation of the trade before reporting success. If no record exists, it's informed directly that the trade was not placed and must retry. Grounding the agent in on-chain and database state — rather than trusting its own output — was the key shift.

---

## 2. Geo-Block on Polymarket Access

When we deployed our agent to an AWS-hosted server, we hit an immediate wall: Polymarket is geo-blocked in certain regions, and our server instance fell into one of them. The agent couldn't reach the Polymarket CLOB API at all.

**How we fixed it:** We routed the server traffic through a VPN to a permitted region. Not the most elegant solution, but it unblocked us quickly during the hackathon. A production version of this would use a server hosted in a non-restricted jurisdiction from the start.

---

## 3. Lack of Visibility Into Agent Activity

Early on, we had no reliable way to tell whether the agent was actively working or had silently stalled. There were no live indicators — we were essentially flying blind, relying on manually prompting the agent to check in on its status.

**How we fixed it:** We built the live activity feed in the 0xBet dashboard. Every action the agent takes — research calls, compute purchases, bets placed, settlements received — is logged in real time and surfaced in the UI. The agent status indicator (Researching / Placing Bets / Settling / Idle) gives an at-a-glance view of what it's doing at any moment, removing the dependency on manual check-ins entirely.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

# Use of AI Tools and Agents

0xBet is not a tool that assists a human bettor. It **is** the bettor — an autonomous AI agent that researches, decides, and executes entirely on its own.

---

## The Agent

At the core of 0xBet is an AI research agent powered by a large language model. The agent accesses two distinct tools to do its work:

- **ClawRouter** — a pay-per-request compute layer that allows the agent to purchase LLM intelligence on demand, in USDC on Base, with no pre-funded API keys
- **OpenClaw** — used to access real-time X (Twitter) sentiment and activity, giving the agent a live pulse on public opinion, injury news, team morale, and breaking developments around upcoming fixtures

This is the critical design decision: the agent **earns money, then spends that money on its own thinking.** Compute is not a fixed cost — it's a variable investment that scales with the agent's bankroll and performance.

---

## What the Agent Does

Each research cycle, the agent:

1. **Fetches upcoming fixtures** across football, basketball, tennis, and other supported sports via live data APIs
2. **Pulls structured data** — team form, head-to-head records, injury reports, recent results, and current Polymarket odds
3. **Reads X sentiment via OpenClaw** — scans real-time posts, fan sentiment, journalist reporting, and insider activity around each fixture to surface signals the structured data might miss
4. **Reasons over the combined data** — the LLM synthesises structured stats and live social sentiment to identify where the market may be mispriced, producing a structured output: pick, confidence score, and expected value estimate
5. **Sizes stakes** using Kelly Criterion — mathematically optimal bet sizing based on perceived edge and current bankroll
6. **Places bets autonomously** via the Polymarket CLOB API
7. **Settles and reinvests** — winnings are swept back to treasury and the cycle repeats

---

## How AI and Onchain Work Together

The AI layer and the onchain layer are tightly coupled — neither works without the other:

| Layer | Role |
|---|---|
| **ClawRouter** | Pay-per-request LLM compute, purchased in USDC on Base |
| **OpenClaw** | Real-time X sentiment and social signal extraction |
| **icpay** | Treasury management, receive deposits, track balance |
| **Polymarket CLOB** | Execute bets, settle markets |
| **Base** | Settlement layer for all USDC transactions |

The agent uses its **icpay balance** to decide how much compute to buy each cycle. If the bankroll grows, it buys more research calls. If it shrinks, it conserves. The AI's budget is dynamically managed onchain.

---

## Why This Matters

Most AI agents are given a fixed compute budget by a human operator. **0xBet's compute budget is determined by its own performance.** A winning agent gets smarter. A losing agent cuts back. And by combining structured sports data with live X sentiment via OpenClaw, the agent has access to the same signals a professional sharp would — updated in real time, processed at machine speed.

---

*AI is not a feature of 0xBet. It is the operator.*

**Futurllama**

# Futooooooor — Tech and Trends

0xBet is a **new primitive**: an autonomous business that owns itself.

---

## AI Agent as Economic Actor

The dominant AI narrative today is AI as *assistant* — a tool that helps a human do something faster. 0xBet is a different bet entirely. The agent doesn't assist a bettor. It **is** the bettor. It earns money, decides how to spend it, purchases its own compute, and reinvests its winnings — without a human in the loop at any stage.

This is what agentic commerce actually looks like in practice: an AI with a wallet, a revenue model, and a self-determined compute budget.

---

## A New Primitive: The Self-Funding Agent

Today's AI agents are kept alive by human operators who top up their compute budgets. 0xBet inverts this. The agent funds its own intelligence from its own revenue. When it wins, it buys more research. When its bankroll grows, its thinking scales with it.

This is the first implementation of a **genuinely self-sustaining AI business** — not self-sustaining in the marketing sense, but economically: it generates enough return to pay for its own existence and then some.

---

## Frontier Tech, Assembled in a New Way

0xBet sits at the intersection of four frontier primitives that have never been combined like this before:

- **Autonomous AI agents** that reason over live data and make financial decisions
- **Pay-per-request onchain compute** via OpenClaw — the agent buys intelligence the same way it buys anything else, in USDC on Base
- **Decentralised prediction markets** via Polymarket — peer-to-peer betting with no centralised book taking margin
- **Crypto payment infrastructure** via icpay — the agent operates its own merchant account, accepts deposits, and manages its treasury entirely onchain

None of these pieces are new. The combination is.

---

## What This Points To

Sports betting is the proof of concept. The real idea is bigger: **any AI agent that can generate revenue can fund its own operation.** A research agent that charges for reports. A trading agent that takes a performance fee. A creative agent that sells its output. 0xBet is the first working example of this model — an autonomous business that doesn't need a human to keep the lights on.

That's not a trend. That's a new category.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

# 0xBet — BASE Sponsor Track Submission

**Autonomous intelligent betting, at your fingertips.**

---

## How 0xBet Fits This Track

0xBet is a fully autonomous sports betting agent deployed on Base mainnet. It accepts USDC deposits, purchases its own compute, conducts AI-powered research on sports fixtures, places bets on Polymarket, and reinvests winnings — all without human intervention. It is, by design, a self-sustaining onchain business.

---

## Self-Sustaining by Architecture

The agent's economic loop is entirely onchain:

1. **Users deposit USDC** into 0xBet's merchant account via icpay on Base
2. **The agent allocates funds** autonomously — splitting between compute, active bets, and a reserve
3. **Compute is purchased per-request** via OpenClaw, paying in USDC on Base with no pre-funded API keys
4. **Research drives betting decisions** — the agent identifies mispriced markets on Polymarket using Kelly Criterion stake sizing
5. **Winnings are swept back** to the treasury and reinvested into the next research cycle

When the agent wins, it buys more compute. Better compute means better research. Better research means more winning bets. The flywheel is entirely self-funded.

---

## ERC-8021 Builder Codes

Every onchain transaction executed by 0xBet — deposits received, compute purchased, bets placed, winnings settled — includes ERC-8021 builder codes registered via base.dev. This gives the agent and its operator full analytics on transaction volume, compute cost efficiency, and betting P&L, all queryable onchain.

---

## Why This Is Novel

Most "autonomous agents" still rely on human top-ups to fund compute. **0xBet is one of the first agents that pays for its own intelligence from its own revenue.** The compute spend is not a cost centre — it's an investment that generates returns, making the agent genuinely self-sustaining rather than just automated.

It also demonstrates **agent-to-agent commerce in practice**: 0xBet transacts with OpenClaw (compute provider) and Polymarket (liquidity venue) autonomously, with no human signing transactions.

---

## Public Interface

A live dashboard at a public URL displays in real time:
- Treasury balance (USDC on Base)
- Compute spend per cycle (Clawrouter calls + cost)
- Active bets, odds, and confidence scores
- P&L over time
- Full agent activity feed — every research call, bet placed, and settlement received

---

*Built on Base. Powered by icpay, ClawRouter, and Polymarket.*
