### RaktMatch
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/raktmatch-0ad1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Kake27/raktmatch) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/GOazY2krEtg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A Real-Time Blood Donation System

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our Real-Time Blood Donation System, **RaktMatch** provides a centralized, live platform that connects hospitals, blood banks, donors, and patients with instant blood availability updates.

 **What It Can Be Used For**

- Hospitals & Blood Banks: Track real-time blood inventory and respond faster
- Donors: Get notified when their blood group is urgently needed
- Patients: Quickly locate available blood without manual searching


**Why It’s Useful**
- Eliminates outdated blood stock data
- Reduces manual calls and miscommunication
- Enables faster, safer emergency response
- Improves transparency and coordination

**Result:** Faster access to blood, better coordination, and lives saved.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Real-time data synchronization**
Keeping blood inventory perfectly in sync across multiple users was tricky. Updates needed to reflect instantly without duplications or missed events.

*Solution:*
We used real-time database subscriptions and carefully handled state updates on the frontend to ensure changes were pushed and reflected immediately and reliably.

**2. Role-based access and data separation**
The platform supports different users (users, hospitals and blood banks), each with different permissions and views. Mixing this logic without breaking flows was challenging.

*Solution:*
We implemented strict role-based routing and backend checks, ensuring users could only access features meant for their role.

**3. Frontend–backend integration issues**
Synchronizing authentication and data between the frontend and backend caused issues like inconsistent user states and failed requests.

*Solution:*
We standardized API contracts, improved error handling, and added validation at both ends to keep the system stable.

**4. UI responsiveness and edge cases**
Making sure the application worked smoothly across devices especially for critical actions during emergencies required careful attention to layout and interaction edge cases.

*Solution:*
We tested across screen sizes and refined components to remain responsive without compromising usability.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/city-sentinel-8043) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mayankinkk/city-sentinel) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://city-sentinel-decider.lovable.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> For the city

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Leaflet.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Leaflet.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**City Sentinel** addresses the lack of a structured, transparent, and accountable system for reporting and resolving civic issues in cities. Common problems such as potholes, garbage disposal, broken streetlights, and road damage are often reported through informal channels, making them difficult to track, prioritize, and resolve efficiently.

**City Sentinel **provides a centralized platform where citizens can report issues with precise location data, while authorities can verify, prioritize, and manage them through a clear role-based workflow. By visualizing issues on a live map and tracking their status, the platform improves transparency, reduces response time, and helps civic bodies operate more efficiently.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing a role-based access system that balanced usability, functionality, and privacy. Defining clear responsibilities for citizens, moderators, authorities, field workers, and super admins required careful planning to avoid overlap and confusion.

Another challenge was handling user privacy, especially deciding what information should be visible publicly and what should remain restricted. This was addressed by implementing a privacy-first approach where reporter identities are anonymized for public users, partially masked for authorities, and fully accessible only to the super admin.

Integrating map-based issue reporting and ensuring smooth communication between the frontend, backend, and database was also challenging, but it significantly improved my understanding of full-stack development and real-world data flow.

### Real-time blood donation system
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/realtime-blood-donation-system-968e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vasudevdiyora/BloodConnect) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> lives matters

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In emergency medical situations, finding the right blood group quickly is a major challenge. Currently, hospitals and patients rely on phone calls, WhatsApp groups, and manual coordination, which is slow, unreliable, and stressful. Blood banks often do not have real-time visibility of donor availability or stock levels, leading to delays that can cost lives.

Our system solves this by providing a centralized digital platform that connects donors, hospitals, and blood banks in real time. It enables instant blood requests, live inventory tracking, and quick donor matching, reducing manual effort and response time. This makes the entire blood donation process faster, safer, more organized, and more efficient during critical situations.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing the system architecture to handle multiple user roles (donors, hospitals, blood banks, and admin) while keeping the data consistent and secure. Initially, managing authentication and role-based access using JWT caused issues where users were accessing wrong dashboards.

Another challenge was integrating the frontend with the backend APIs. Since the UI was ready but static, mapping each screen to real API responses and handling loading states took time. I also faced difficulties in synchronizing blood inventory updates in real time without creating data inconsistencies.

I solved these challenges by clearly separating concerns using a layered backend architecture (Controller, Service, Repository), implementing proper role-based authorization, testing APIs using Postman before connecting the frontend, and using reusable React components with centralized API handling. This made the system more stable, scalable, and easier to debug.

### The Why Engine
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/why-engine-explainable-ai-decision-transparency-system-f886) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PtlLuv27/TheWhyEngine.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/F-PEBZqkQpg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From black box to open book.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloud-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Our Vision: Making AI Understandable for Everyone**
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning now influence critical life decisions—from loan approvals and hiring to healthcare and criminal justice. However, most advanced AI systems operate as "black boxes," producing results without explaining how or why they were reached.

Why Engine was created to bridge this gap. We are an explainability system situated at the intersection of AI, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and ethical computing. Our goal is to transform complex decision logic into clear, human-readable insights that promote fairness and empower users to question automated decisions.

**The Problem We Solve**
While AI predictive performance has skyrocketed, its transparency has lagged. This lack of clarity creates several challenges:

*Trust Gap:* Users and business leaders struggle to trust a system they don't understand.
*Hidden Bias:* Without transparency, it is difficult to identify algorithmic bias or unfair treatment.
*Accessibility:* Existing XAI (Explainable AI) tools are often too technical for everyday users, requiring deep domain expertise to interpret.
*Regulatory Needs:* Modern laws increasingly demand a "right to explanation" for automated decisions.
*Analysis:* Applying advanced XAI techniques like feature importance and rule extraction to "black box" predictions.
*Translation:* Converting complex technical data into natural language that anyone can read.
*Interaction:* Providing an intuitive dashboard where users can explore "what-if" scenarios by adjusting input factors to see how outcomes change.

**Key Features:**
*Top 3 Reasons:* Instantly see the primary factors driving any decision.
Confidence Indicators: Understand how certain the AI is about its prediction.
*Fairness Monitoring:* Integrated indicators to highlight potential bias or disproportionate influence.
*Interactive Visualizations:* High-quality charts and sliders designed for non-technical stakeholders.

**Our Commitment to Responsible AI**
We believe that AI should be a reliable partner, not a mystery. By prioritizing transparency, accountability, and user-centric design, Why Engine helps organizations build ethical AI systems that people can truly trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Complexity vs. Clarity:** Advanced models like deep neural networks lack inherent interpretability, making it difficult to reveal how decisions are reached.
**Actionable Insights:** Users affected by negative decisions often lack specific details on what factors influenced the outcome or how to improve it.
**Bias Detection:** Identifying algorithmic bias or unfair treatment is nearly impossible without transparent explanations.

**Trust and Accountability:** Blindly relying on AI for high-stakes decisions like loan approvals or hiring can lead to ethical and legal risks.
**git and github:** Coding and managing record was challenging.

***SOLUTION:-***

**Complexity vs. Clarity:** Advanced models like deep neural networks function as "black boxes," making it difficult to reveal the reasoning behind their decisions.
**Actionable Insights:** Users affected by negative outcomes often lack the specific details needed to understand or improve their situation.
**Bias Detection:** Identifying algorithmic bias or discriminatory features is nearly impossible without transparent, explainable decision logic.
**Trust and Accountability:**Blindly relying on AI for high-stakes decisions like hiring or loans can lead to serious ethical and legal consequences.
**Git and GitHub:** Managing version history and resolving merge conflicts was solved by using modular commits and forced synchronization to maintain a "clean" final codebase.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

**The "Scene" is the Black Box:** Our system treats the opaque, complex decision-making process of a machine learning model as an unstructured "scene" that needs to be understood.

**"Semantic Segmentation" is Explainability:** We "segment" this scene by breaking down the final prediction into its most influential components—the input features. More importantly, we assign semantic meaning to these segments. Instead of just showing that 'Feature X had an importance of 0.7,' our GenAI flows translate that numerical data into human-readable insights, such as, "Your high credit score was the primary reason for this decision."

**"Offroad" is the Model's Internal Logic:** This process is equivalent to navigating difficult "offroad" terrain. The internal logic of a complex model is not a simple, paved road; it's an intricate, non-linear landscape. Our tools, like the "what-if" sliders and counterfactual analysis, act as the vehicle that allows users to explore this terrain safely and understand how it works.

Ultimately, our project embodies **Duality** by creating a bridge between two distinct worlds: the complex, numerical world of the machine's prediction and the semantic, narrative world of human understanding. We turn a computational scene into a human story.

### CypherKey
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cypherkey-027b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Mansi-Mishra-D/CypherKey) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Protect your secrets with CypherKey.

![Visual Studio Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Visual%20Studio%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Markdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/Markdown-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**CypherKey** addresses the need for simple, local text privacy. In an age where digital communication is often monitored, this tool allows users to manually encrypt sensitive messages before sending them.

**Key Solutions**:
**Privacy Protection**: Transforms readable text into secure code that cannot be understood without a secret shift key.

**User Control**: Unlike automated encryption, the user chooses their own unique shift number (1-25) for added security.

**Data Integrity**: The algorithm ensures that original formatting, such as spaces and capitalisation, remains intact for easy readability after decryption.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges & Learnings**:
**Logic Complexity**: My biggest challenge was implementing the modulo arithmetic (% 26) required for the Caesar Cipher. I had to ensure that if a user chose a high shift number, the letters would correctly wrap around from 'Z' back to 'A' without breaking the program.

**Preserving Data Integrity**: I spent time refining the code so that non-alphabetical characters, like spaces and punctuation, remained untouched. This was critical so that the decrypted message would be a perfect match to the original input.

**GitHub Workflow**: As I was working solo, I had to learn how to properly initialise a repository and upload my source files directly from my local environment to share my work professionally.

**AOPS**

I am submitting CypherKey to the AOPS track as a contribution to open-source privacy utilities. Built entirely in Java, this project provides a transparent and accessible way for users to understand and implement basic encryption logic. By keeping the source code open and well-documented, I aim to help other beginners learn the fundamentals of string manipulation and security algorithms in a real-world application.

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 1. AK-DSKIT

AK-DSKIT aims to simplify the complete Data Science and Machine Learning workflow into intuitive one-line commands. However, because the library covers a wide range of modules (cleaning, EDA, preprocessing, modeling, evaluation, explainability, AutoML), users can face challenges such as inconsistent method behavior (especially method chaining/return types), unclear error messages for common failure cases (missing target column, invalid file path, unsupported model name), and limited validation for edge cases. These issues reduce the reliability of the end-to-end pipeline and make the learning curve steeper for new users. Strengthening API consistency, tests, and documentation helps ensure the toolkit remains trustworthy and easier to adopt.

## 2. Open World Holidays Framework

Open World Holidays Framework provides holiday information for a large number of countries, subdivisions, and financial markets, where correctness is critical for real applications. Even minor issues—incorrect holiday dates, missing subdivision holidays, inconsistent naming, or localization gaps—can lead to incorrect outputs in production systems. Since the library supports multiple input formats (date objects, date strings, timestamps), many entities, and optional localization behavior, it is naturally prone to edge cases and regressions if not strongly validated. Improving entity accuracy, strengthening regression test coverage, enhancing localized holiday name outputs, and upgrading documentation directly increases trust in the library and reduces maintenance overhead for maintainers.

**Challenges we ran into**

While exploring the AK-DSKIT codebase and running the demo suite locally, I ran into a few practical issues:

## Import confusion (Ak-dskit vs dskit)
Initially I tried importing using the package name directly, which caused import errors. I resolved it after reading the docs carefully: the correct usage is pip install Ak-dskit but import is from dskit import dskit.

## Optional dependency errors (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost/SHAP)
Some advanced demos/modules require optional libraries that are not installed in the base version. Running certain demo scripts caused missing module errors. I solved this by installing the appropriate extras (e.g., pip install Ak-dskit[full] / feature-specific extras) and documenting which demos require which dependencies.

## Method chaining inconsistency in some workflows
In a few cases, chaining operations failed because some methods return a result instead of returning the updated dskit object. I worked around this by separating calls (e.g., storing intermediate outputs), and I plan to improve API consistency by standardizing return behavior and adding regression tests.

These hurdles helped me better understand the library’s design and identify areas where small improvements (docs, error handling, and tests) can significantly improve usability.

**The problem it solves**

**Project 1: Multi-Gaussian Overlap Integrals**
Extends overlap integrals from one or two basis functions to arbitrarily many Gaussian basis functions, enabling analytical evaluation of intracules, extracules, higher-order density powers, and complex interparticle interactions.

**Project 2: Efficient 2-Electron Integral Evaluation**
Improves the performance and correctness of 2-electron integrals in GBasis by replacing an inefficient algorithm with recursive methods based on Obara–Saika and Head-Gordon–Pople, including support for non-Coulomb interactions.

**Project 3: Open world holidays framework**
The project improves the reliability of the holidays framework by fixing inaccurate holiday data, enabling localized holiday names, improving documentation, and optimizing performance for real-world, large-scale usage.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Project 1: Multi-Gaussian Overlap Integrals**
Maintained compatibility with existing GBasis code while handling the natural sparsity of multi-Gaussian overlaps using screening and sparse representations, and validated correctness through stepwise testing.

**Project 2: Efficient 2-Electron Integral Evaluation**
Carefully implemented complex recursion schemes in pure Python, ensured correctness for high angular momentum cases, and validated results against PySCF and existing GBasis implementations.

**Project 3: Open world holidays framework**
The key challenges in this project were handling the complexity of country-specific holiday rules, ensuring backward compatibility while adding new features like localization, and working with limited or unclear documentation. Additionally, performance improvements needed to be carefully balanced with correctness, and special cases such as leap years and observed holidays required thorough testing to avoid regressions.

### Filobo
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/filobo-abaf) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://filobo.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI Desktop Assistant

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem

Students, developers, and creators constantly accumulate files — lecture PDFs, datasets, screenshots, invoices, resumes, project assets — across multiple domains like study, finance, hackathons, and portfolios.

Existing file management tools either:

• Automatically reorganize files without consent
• Use rigid rules that don’t adapt to the user
• Lack explanations for why a file was moved
• Break trust by acting silently in the background

As a result, users:

Lose control over their own files

Fear automation that might break workflows

Avoid smart tools due to lack of transparency

Spend hours manually organizing or searching

The core problem is not organization — it is lack of trust, explainability, and human control in AI-driven file management.

💡 Our Insight

Automation without trust fails.

AI systems must:

Explain why they suggest something

Ask before acting

Learn from user decisions

Be reversible and safe

File organization is a high-risk personal task — once trust is broken, users abandon the tool.

🚀 Solution — Filobo

Filobo is a human-guided, explainable AI assistant for workspace organization.

Instead of acting autonomously, Filobo:

✔ Observes files inside a safe workspace
✔ Suggests improvements with clear reasons
✔ Shows confidence levels transparently
✔ Requires explicit human approval
✔ Learns from accept/reject feedback
✔ Supports undo for safety
✔ Never deletes files
✔ Never acts silently

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Balancing Automation with User Trust

The biggest challenge was resisting full automation.
It was technically easy to auto-move files, but doing so would break user trust. Designing a system that only suggests, always asks for confirmation, and clearly explains why a suggestion exists required deliberate architectural decisions in both backend logic and UI flow.

2. Designing Explainable AI Without ML

Another challenge was making the system feel intelligent without using heavy machine learning models.
I had to design rule-based reasoning that still feels transparent and explainable, including confidence scores, human-readable reasons, and visible learning from accept/reject actions.

3. Safe File System Access

Interacting with the real file system is risky.
I had to strictly sandbox all operations inside a demo workspace, validate paths carefully, prevent deletions, and support undo — ensuring zero risk to user data while still demonstrating real backend behavior.

4. Human-in-the-Loop Interaction Design

Building a robot-led interface that guides the user step-by-step was challenging.
The robot had to:

Initiate tasks

Explain every action

Confirm before changes

React emotionally (approve/reject states)

This required careful state management between frontend UI, robot behavior, and backend responses.

5. Making Learning Visible

“Learning” often happens invisibly in AI systems.
Here, the challenge was to visually show learning — adjusting confidence, hiding rejected suggestions temporarily, and explicitly telling the user what Filobo learned from their decision.

6. Premium UI Without Libraries

Creating a premium, polished interface using only HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript (no React, no UI libraries) required careful attention to spacing, animations, glassmorphism, and micro-interactions — especially under hackathon time constraints.

7. Keeping the Demo Judge-Friendly

Finally, the hardest part was ensuring that a judge could understand the product without verbal explanation.
Every interaction, robot message, preview, and confirmation had to clearly communicate:

“The AI is assistive, explainable, and always under human control.”

🌟 What This Taught Me

These challenges reinforced that good AI design is more about interaction and trust than raw automation — a lesson that strongly shaped Filobo’s architecture.

**AOPS**

Area of Operations (AOPS)

Filobo operates in a local, sandboxed digital workspace where users manage personal and professional files related to:

📚 Study & academics

💼 Finance & documents

🚀 Hackathon & project assets

🧑‍💻 Career & portfolio files

Its AOPS is intentionally limited to ensure safety, trust, and explainability.

Filobo never scans or modifies the entire system.
It only observes and suggests actions inside a defined workspace.

How the Project Fits the Track / Theme (TI)

Filobo fits into Trusted AI / Human-Centered Systems / Productivity Tools because:

✔ It uses AI-like reasoning to assist, not automate
✔ Every action is explainable and reversible
✔ The user remains in full control at all times
✔ Learning happens only through explicit human feedback
✔ Safety and transparency are first-class design principles

Why This Matters

Most AI productivity tools focus on speed and automation.

Filobo focuses on:

Trust

Human approval

Explainability

Safe interaction

This makes it suitable for real-world, high-stakes environments where user data matters.

### Exsh
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/exsh-afaa) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bUGCImFEEykOSMo7JCzX08ns9pqGgLs8/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=109124650291566957733&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A Simple Unix-like Shell Built in C

![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Before this change, the command execution logic in the shell did not clearly separate parent and child process responsibilities and had limited handling for process creation failures. This could lead to unclear execution flow, harder debugging, and unpredictable behavior when command execution failed.

By improving the use of the fork() system call in executer.c, this change makes process execution safer and more reliable. Users and contributors can now rely on consistent command execution, while learners can more easily understand how a Unix-like shell creates and manages processes. The improved structure also reduces the risk of orphaned or improperly terminated processes, making the shell easier to maintain and extend in the future.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges I faced was managing the execution flow between the parent and child processes created using fork(). At first, it wasn’t always clear which parts of the code should run in the parent process and which should execute in the child. This sometimes caused unexpected behavior, such as commands running more than once or not behaving as intended.

Another difficulty was handling failure cases, especially when fork() or exec failed. Without proper checks, the shell could continue running in an unstable state or leave child processes improperly handled. I solved this by adding clear error checks and making sure child processes exit cleanly whenever command execution fails.

Debugging these process-related issues was also tricky because problems don’t always show up immediately. To deal with this, I tested the shell using both valid and invalid commands and closely monitored return values and exit statuses. This helped me confirm that the shell stays responsive and behaves correctly after each command execution.

**AOPS**

The Exsh project aligns well with the AOPS (Advanced Operating Systems & Programming Systems) track because it focuses on low-level system programming concepts that are fundamental to operating systems. The project involves implementing and improving a Unix-like shell using the C programming language, which directly interacts with the operating system through system calls.
My contribution specifically improves process execution using core OS mechanisms such as fork(), exec, and wait(). These system calls are essential for process creation, execution, and synchronization in Unix-based operating systems. By refining how parent and child processes are managed, the project demonstrates practical understanding of process lifecycle management, error handling, and execution control.
Overall, the project emphasizes hands-on experience with operating system internals and system-level programming, making it a strong fit for the AOPS track.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ctp-serial-datalink-transport-protocol-3acd) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b7vRJYkvXE6VRsT5aibgjSUj8AONbjhh/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114728054261284826241&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From scratch a serial communication protocol in C

![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded Systems](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20Systems-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

When working with serial communication, data is usually sent as a continuous stream of bytes. Without a proper structure, it becomes hard to know where one message starts or ends, or whether the data received is complete and correct. This can lead to confusion, bugs, and unreliable communication.

CTP solves this by defining a simple way to send and receive structured messages over a serial connection. It helps break raw data into clear packets and makes communication more predictable. Along with making serial communication easier to manage, the project also helps learners understand how low-level communication works instead of treating it as a black box.

### DivyaDhrishti
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/divyadhrishti-4ce8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/HeckerOO1/Search_engine) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/WsykFyVT0v0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Weekend%20of%20Code%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://weekendofcode2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Ranks trustworthy, fresh results in emergencies

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: The "Infodemic" During Disasters
In a major emergency, search engines face a "Trust-Speed Paradox." While users need information immediately, the first wave of data is often unverified rumors, sensationalized social media posts, and panic-driven misinformation.

DivyaDrishti solves the following critical issues:

Noise vs. Signal: During disasters, official government alerts are often buried under viral, high-emotion content. DivyaDrishti identifies and prioritizes official "ground truth."

Panic Amplification: Traditional algorithms reward engagement (clicks/shares). DivyaDrishti detects "Sensational Scores" and suppresses content designed to cause panic.

Verification Lag: It bridge the gap between a disaster occurring and official news being published by analyzing the "reliability" of early sources in real-time.

API Dependency: It provides a resilient, decentralized way to gather life-saving information using RSS and direct feeds, ensuring the system works even when major social platforms or expensive APIs are restricted.

The "DivyaDrishti" Edge
Unlike a standard search engine that asks "What is popular?", DivyaDrishti asks "What is true, and is it safe to show right now?"

**Challenges we ran into**

When building a system that bridges the gap between Static Training Data and Live Information Flow, the hurdles are usually more about logic than simple syntax errors.

Here are three specific, high-level challenges you can present for your evaluation, along with the "wise" solutions you implemented.

1. The "Schema Mismatch" Hurdle
The Bug: When I moved from my curated dataset to live RSS feeds, the data structures didn't match. RSS feeds provide a summary and a pubDate, while my model was trained on content and timestamp. The model couldn't "see" the data because the keys were different.

The Solution: I built a Data Normalization Layer. Before the model ever touches live data, a script "cleans" the incoming feed. It maps different source formats into a single "Master Schema."

Action: I wrote a mapping function that forced all inputs into the exact JSON format used in my training set.

2. The "Keyword Overload" False Positive
The Bug: Early in testing, the Emergency Mode triggered incorrectly. A news article about a "Movie about an Earthquake" had the same keywords as a "Real Earthquake." The system saw a high frequency of the word "Earthquake" and mistakenly entered Emergency Mode.

The Solution: I implemented Source-Weighting logic. I realized that a keyword spike should only trigger an emergency if it comes from source_type: official or source_type: news.

Action: I added a rule: "Only trigger Emergency Mode if at least 30% of the keyword volume comes from Trusted or Official sources." This stopped the "pop-culture" false alarms.

3. The "Scraping Block" Barrier
The Bug: While trying to get live data without APIs, some government and news websites blocked my automated scraper. This meant I had no "Live Signal" to rank, making the search engine useless.

The Solution: I shifted from Aggressive Scraping to Polite RSS Ingestion. Instead of trying to "read" the whole website like a bot, I used the public RSS endpoints which are designed for machines.

Action: I implemented a "User-Agent" header to identify my system and set a "Crawl-Delay" of 5 minutes. This respected the website's server limits and prevented my IP from being blacklisted.

💡 Pro-Tip for your Evaluation:
If they ask, "What was the biggest challenge?", answer:

"The biggest challenge was teaching a machine the difference between viral news and critical news. Most algorithms think 'viral' means 'important,' but in a disaster, 'viral' often means 'rumor.' Overcoming that bias by using my Sensationalism Score was the breakthrough of this project."

Team **Neural Nexas** -- [sourabh verma](https://github.com/sourabh-verma18), [Tanishk Varshney](https://github.com/HeckerOO1)

### RehabAI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/physiopath-3fd5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Nightfury2062/RehabAI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://rehab-ai-khaki.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI assistant for post-surgical rehab

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0ad707dbb64f44be9681124f281ae984/b6bfbc78-9c8c-408a-b828-50979874d65d.jpeg)After surgery, most patients are discharged with a written summary and a generic physiotherapy chart that is hard to understand and even harder to follow in daily life. People often forget exercises, perform them incorrectly, or skip sessions because they don’t know what to do when, especially when they have busy schedules. Access to regular physiotherapy guidance is also limited by time, cost, and availability, which can slow recovery and increase the risk of stiffness, pain, or re-injury.

How RehabAI

RehabAI makes post-surgery rehabilitation simpler, safer, and easier to stick to. By reading a patient’s discharge summary and understanding the exact procedure performed, it generates a clear, personalized rehab plan with the right exercises at the right time. It fits physiotherapy sessions into the user’s daily schedule, shows step-by-step instructions, and tracks progress over time. This helps patients stay consistent with rehab, reduces confusion and guesswork, and acts as a reliable day-to-day guide alongside professional medical advice.

**Challenges we ran into**

AI API Integration Issues
Issue: The first efforts to use Claude API needed paid credits (at least $5), which was not possible in a student hackathon project.
Solution: Replaced it with the free tier API at Google Gemini which offered vast quotas (15 request/min, 1,500 per day) that was ideal to use during development and demonstrations.
Lesson: API pricing and free tier limits are always something to research before entering into a technology stack.

The Version Deprecation of Gemini API.
Issue: It began with the use of the package of google-generative-ai that raised depreciation warnings. Attempted to migrate to the new genaid package of Google but faced problems with model compatibility (model errors with gemini-2.0-flash-exp and gemini-1.5-flash models).
Problem solution: Returned to the older and more reliable package of google-generative with gemini-1.5-flash model, and accepted the deprecation warning given the time constraints of the hackathon.
Learning: Sometimes it is preferable to work on degraded code than to maintain cutting-edge code in a time-sensitive project such as a hackathon. Can refactor later.

Environment Variable Management.
Problem: This is my first experience in dealing with the environment variables in a proper way. Hardcoded API keys, followed by a real API key with .env.example accidentally pushed to GitHub (security risk!).
Solution:
Using python-dotenv in local development.
Developed adequate .gitignore to avoid .env file.
Create an example of .env, .env.example.
Configured environment variables individually in Render deployment.
Lesson: Security-first principle - secrets should never be placed in version control. Use the environment variables in all sensitive information.

Database Design Decisions
Issue: Have to follow up usage analytics but did not know which database to use and how to structure it to get a prototype in a short period.
Resolution: SQLite has been used due to its simplicity (no external database setup needed) and a dedicated database.py module has been created to organize the clean code. Saved entire rehab plans are in JSON format to be flexible.
Lesson: In the case of MVPs and hackathons, simplicity is preferable to scalability. SQLite is ideal with prototypes and it can be scaled to PostgreSQL/MySQL when necessary.

CORS Problems in the Development.
Issue: Frontend (Vite on port 5173) was not able to connect to the backend (FastAPI on port 8001) because of the restrictions of Cross-Origin Resource Sharing.
Solution: FastAPI added CORS middleware and with proper settings.

**AI**

RehabAI uses Artificial Intelligence to understand unstructured medical documents and convert them into clear, personalized rehabilitation plans. The system analyzes a patient’s discharge summary using a language model, identifies the type of surgery performed, and generates a phase-wise physiotherapy plan grounded in verified rehab guidelines. This allows complex medical text to be transformed into actionable, easy-to-follow instructions.

AI is also used to personalize the rehabilitation experience. Based on the user’s age, medical details, and daily availability, the model helps adapt exercise recommendations and schedules them into realistic time slots. By combining AI-driven understanding with rule-based safety checks and validated rehab data, RehabAI demonstrates a responsible and practical use of AI to solve a real healthcare accessibility problem.

Team **Wayfinders** -- Parnit Gupta, [Samyak Verma](https://github.com/therealsamyakverma), Muhammad Ashraf, Rohit Kunnath

### Aegis Protocol
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegis-protocol-da60) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/promad130/SafeVault) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your Data. Your Control

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Common problems:

-You don’t know which devices are logged into your account

-You can’t remotely revoke access if a device is lost

-File storage often lacks verifiable audit trails

-Session management is opaque or nonexistent

-Sensitive actions happen silently, without user visibility

-Aegis Protocol solves this by acting as a secure digital vault that puts the user fully in control.

##What people can use it for

-Securely store sensitive files (documents, images, videos)

-Access their vault across multiple devices safely

-View all active login sessions in real time

-Remotely revoke compromised or unused devices

-Download files securely with controlled access

-Audit every critical action (logins, uploads, deletions, revocations)

##Why it’s safer

-Strong authentication with rotating refresh tokens

-Device-bound sessions (not just accounts)

-Forced logout support for lost devices

-Immutable audit logs for transparency

-Secure file handling with cloud object storage

#In short:
Aegis Protocol makes secure storage transparent, verifiable, and user-controlled rather than implicit and opaque.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

This project had several non-trivial engineering challenges:

1. Session Security & Token Rotation

Designing a secure authentication flow that supports:

Short-lived access tokens

Rotating refresh tokens

Device-bound sessions

Remote revocation

The challenge was ensuring tokens stayed valid for normal use (e.g. file uploads) while still expiring safely.
This was solved by implementing refresh-on-demand logic and strict session validation on every request.

2. Multi-device Session Management

Tracking sessions across devices required:

Separating devices from sessions

Preventing revocation of the current session

Keeping the session list consistent and accurate

This was solved by introducing a dedicated session model tied to devices and enforcing server-side checks.

3. File Storage & Download UX

Files were stored correctly but initially ended up in app-scoped directories, making them invisible to users.

This required:

Understanding Android storage behavior

Correctly handling permissions

Writing files to user-visible directories (Downloads)

Once fixed, downloads behaved exactly as users expect.

**Software Development**

Aegis Protocol is fundamentally a full-stack software engineering project that focuses on designing and implementing secure, scalable application architecture.

The project involves:

Backend API design with authentication, authorization, and session management

Secure data modeling for users, devices, sessions, vault items, and audit logs

Frontend application development with real-time state management

Client–server communication with strict contract enforcement

Integration of external services (object storage, token systems)

Handling real-world edge cases like token expiry, device loss, and forced logouts

Rather than being a single feature or prototype, Aegis Protocol demonstrates how to design, build, and integrate multiple subsystems into a cohesive, production-ready application.

Team **Thre idiots** -- Uttaran Chowdhury, [Dhruvin Davada](https://github.com/promad130), Tanmay Srivastava

### Loan For Tomorrow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/loan-for-tomorrow-223e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SeraphinJR/lft-project) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/S30vmaGRi3c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20For%20Tomorrow%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-for-tomorrow-25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Creating accessible loan services for everyone

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Micro-finance relies on trust, but the current system for verifying that trust is broken. To audit a single loan, a bank officer must physically travel to remote locations. This creates a massive bottleneck:

- It is Slow: Dispatching humans takes days or weeks, meaning funds sit idle instead of reaching the farmer when they need it most.
- It is Expensive: Fuel and manpower costs eat up the tiny profit margins of micro-loans.
- It is Unreliable: A physical inspection is only as good as the inspector. Humans can be bribed, tired, or fooled by 'borrowed' assets (fraud). 

The Result: Banks are forced to treat honest borrowers like suspects, delaying urgent funds just to prevent fraud.

**Challenges we ran into**

Rural Connectivity: Overcoming intermittent network access in deep rural zones by using an offline-first architecture that queues uploads and syncs automatically.

Digital Fraud: Preventing attempts to bypass verification (like GPS spoofing or fake uploads) by implementing metadata analysis and AI-driven image forensics.

User Adoption: Bridging the digital literacy gap for non-tech-savvy beneficiaries through a high-contrast, visual-first interface with minimal text.

Team **Brochachos** -- [Simon Binu](https://github.com/simonknowsstuff), [Johan Abraham](https://github.com/JadedAlgorithms), [Seraphin Raphy](https://github.com/SeraphinJR)

### MineGaurd
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/minegaurd-4c44) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](http://13.61.21.101:3000/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/nM6JKM4LzUk?si=olDp4qVpGhfqNsv0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20For%20Tomorrow%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-for-tomorrow-25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From Subjective Inspection to Automation

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**MineGuard** solves the critical "blind spot" in illegal mining enforcement by replacing dangerous, slow, and subjective manual inspections with an automated, forensic-grade satellite auditing system.

### 1. Eliminates Physical Risk (Safety)

Illegal mining zones are often controlled by mafias, making field inspections life-threatening for officers. MineGuard allows authorities to monitor sites remotely, removing human inspectors from dangerous conflict zones while ensuring 100% coverage.

### 2. Transforms Subjectivity into Science (Forensics)

Current enforcement relies on visual "guesses" or simple 2D maps, which are easily challenged in court. We provide **"Triple-Lock" Volumetric Intelligence**—using Riemann Sums, Simpson’s Rule, and 3D TIN models—to calculate the exact volume () of extracted earth. This turns satellite data into irrefutable legal evidence.

### 3. Recovers Lost Revenue (Impact)

By precisely quantifying the stolen volume (e.g., 10.1 Million ), the system allows State Mining Departments to calculate exactly how much royalty was evaded. It enables the immediate issuance of scientifically backed show-cause notices to recover millions in lost public funds.

### 4. 1000x Efficiency Boost (Speed)

A manual survey team takes **5–7 days** to inspect a single mine. MineGuard scans and analyzes a site in **12–15 seconds**. This allows a small vigilance team to monitor thousands of mines across an entire state simultaneously, detecting illegal encroachment the moment it happens.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into : 

- Spectral Threshold Calibration: Our initial runs yielded zero detection area due to generic NDBI thresholds. We overcame this by conducting a statistical analysis on 20 known mining vs. non-mining samples, mathematically deriving a custom optimal threshold of 0.07 to ensure accurate identification.

- Volumetric Visualization: Conveying depth data on a flat screen was a major hurdle. We integrated the Plotly library to render interactive, true-to-scale 3D "Digital Twins," allowing users to visualize the pit topology intuitively.

- Eliminating False Positives: Ensuring forensic-grade accuracy was difficult with a single sensor. We solved this by engineering our proprietary "Triple-Lock" Model, which fuses Optical (Sentinel-2), Radar (Sentinel-1), and Depth (DEM) data to cross-verify every pixel before flagging it.

### SkyWatch AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/skywatch-ai-ff14) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sanchit0-1/skywatch-ai) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/sLPNUFHPzoQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNITR%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknitr7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Real-time intelligence for moving worlds

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ubuntu](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ubuntu-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pinecorn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pinecorn-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our SkyWatch AI is a specialized flight intelligence platform built on a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and Pathway-based architecture. It is designed to solve the problem of travel uncertainty by transforming raw aviation data into actionable, predictive insights.

🛠️ The Problems It Solves
Travelers and logistics managers often struggle with fragmented information. Standard trackers tell you where a plane is, but SkyWatch AI tells you why it’s there and when it will actually arrive by accounting for variables a human cannot calculate in real-time.

**1. The "Information Gap" in Delays**
**The Problem**: Traditional apps only update a delay once the airline officially announces it—often when it's too late to change plans.

**The SkyWatch Solution**: By using Pathway-based processing, our AI monitors the "incoming" flight (the plane's previous leg). If the incoming aircraft is stuck in a storm or delayed at a previous gate, SkyWatch calculates the "knock-on" effect instantly, predicting your delay hours before the airline board does.
**
2. Weather Volatility**
**The Problem**: A clear sky at your departure airport doesn't mean a clear path.

**The SkyWatch Solution**: The RAG framework pulls real-time METAR (Meteorological Aerodrome Reports) and TAF (Terminal Aerodrome Forecasts) data. It analyzes these against the flight’s specific pathway, identifying turbulence or headwind conditions that will affect fuel consumption and speed.

**3. Inaccurate ETAs**
The Problem: ETAs are often based on "ideal" flight times, ignoring air traffic congestion.

**The SkyWatch Solution**: Our AI cross-references historical landing patterns with current runway traffic and taxi-in times. This provides a "True-arrival" time, allowing users to coordinate pickups or connecting flights with precision.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. The "Stale Data" Problem (RAG Latency)**
**The Challenge:** In a standard RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) setup, documents are indexed and then retrieved. However, flight data changes every second. We initially found that the AI was retrieving flight positions that were 5–10 minutes old, making the "Real-time" claim inaccurate.

**The Solution:** We implemented Dynamic Context Injection. Instead of relying solely on a static vector database, we built a "Hot-Path" architecture. When a user asks about a flight, the system bypasses the traditional index for telemetry and hits a live API buffer. This "fresh" data is then merged with the "long-term" RAG data (like airport layouts or historical weather patterns) in the prompt window.

**2. Pathway Complexity & Logic Loops**
**The Challenge:** Calculating the "Knock-on" effect (where a delay in Flight A causes a delay in Flight B) created massive computational overhead. Our initial Pathway logic would get stuck in recursive loops trying to predict an entire airline's fleet movement for the day.

**The Solution**: We moved to a Graph-Based Dependency Model.

We treated each aircraft as a node and each flight leg as an edge.

By using Pathway’s reactive programming, we ensured the system only recalculated the "downstream" flights specifically linked to the delayed aircraft, rather than the whole database. This reduced CPU usage by nearly 40%.

**3. Interpreting "Aviation Speak" (METAR/TAF Data)**
**The Challenge**: Weather reports for pilots are written in highly condensed code (e.g., KJFK 121651Z 31012G22KT 10SM SCT250). Standard LLMs occasionally hallucinated these values, misinterpreting wind speeds or visibility ranges, which is a significant safety risk.

**The Solution:** We built a Regex-based Pre-Processor. Before the weather data reaches the AI, a custom script "translates" the aviation code into plain English:

Raw: 31012G22KT → Processed: Wind from 310 degrees at 12 knots, gusting to 22 knots. This ensured the AI had a 100% accuracy rate in interpreting weather conditions before calculating the ETA.

**4. Token Overflow with Global Data**
**The Challenge:** When tracking a long-haul international flight, the amount of data (weather stations along the path, NOTAMs, air traffic control zones) exceeded the LLM's "context window," causing the model to "forget" the original flight number or destination mid-analysis.

**The Solution:** We utilized Hierarchical Summarization.

The RAG system fetches all data.

A smaller, faster "Summarizer" model condenses the weather into "Impact Zones."

Only the high-impact data (e.g., "Severe turbulence over the Rockies") is passed to the main SkyWatch AI.

**Real-Time AI Systems & Continuous Intelligence**

Our application SkyWatch AI is using pathway connectors for data ingestion from APIs providing real-time data. The Pathway continuously senses the change in the existing data by tracking the API continously. 

Then we are using windowing for dividing the data like we are taking a session time of  minutes and OpenSky API allows API calls every  second , means we are getting 6 data in each window.

Then we are using llm xpack for integrating gemini flash 2.5.

Output connectors also used for data output.

Thus our project SkyWatch AI comes under Pathway Track and it fetches real-time data then EXTRACTS it, TRANSFORMS it, and LOADS it (ETL) to calculate delays( if any ) and Estimated Time of Arrival.

> Check eligibility for loans

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. The Problem: The "Black Box" of Banking
Traditional loan systems are frustrating for two main reasons:

Lack of Transparency: When a bank rejects a loan, they rarely tell you exactly why. This leaves the user stuck, not knowing how to improve their financial future.

Static Scoring: Many banks rely on old-school credit scores (like FICO) which might ignore younger people or freelancers who have a good income but no "traditional" credit history.

2. The Solution: Explainable AI (XAI)
Loan-Lens doesn't just say "Yes" or "No." It uses Explainable AI to turn a rejection into a financial roadmap.

What it does: It analyzes the "weight" of different factors (like Debt-to-Income vs. Credit Score).

The Result: It provides a personalized Transparency Report. If you are rejected, the AI says: "Your income is great, but your debt is too high. Reduce your debt by $200/month or lower your loan request to be approved."


Uses: How it makes our life easier?

1. Students/First-time Borrowers- Helps them understand which financial habits (like missing a small bill) are hurting their chances.

2. Small Business Owners- Safely simulates "What-If" scenarios—e.g., "If I earn $5k more this year, will I qualify for a bigger shop loan?"

3. Bank Officers - Acts as a "Decision Support Tool," making it safer by removing human bias and ensuring every decision follows the same logic.

**Best Innovation**

1. The Move from "Black Box" to "Glass Box" AI
Most financial institutions use "Black Box" models—AI where even the bankers don't know why a decision was made.

The Innovation: Loan-Lens implements Explainable AI (XAI).

The Pitch: "Our innovation lies in transparency. By using Feature Importance (Random Forest logic), we turn a rejection into a conversation. We aren't just predicting a 'No'; we are providing a 'How-to-Fix' roadmap."

2. Financial Inclusion for the "Unbanked"
Standard credit scoring systems are often outdated and biased against students or early-career professionals.

The Innovation: Multi-dimensional Data Analysis.

The Pitch: "Instead of relying solely on a single credit number, our model analyzes a holistic profile (Employment + Income + Education + History). This allows us to find 'creditworthy' individuals that traditional banks might overlook, promoting financial equity."

3. Real-Time "What-If" Simulation Engine
Currently, applying for a loan is a high-stakes "one-shot" process. If you fail, you wait months to try again.

The Innovation: Interactive Simulation.

The Pitch: "Loan-Lens allows users to experiment with their own data in a safe sandbox. Users can ask: 'What if I paid off $2,000 of debt? How does that change my approval probability?' This gamifies financial health and empowers the user before they ever step into a bank."

4. Scalability: The "API-First" Approach
Innovation isn't just about the code; it's about how it fits into the world.

The Innovation: A plug-and-play middleware.

The Pitch: "Loan-Lens is designed as a modular service. It can be integrated as a Browser Extension for e-commerce sites (Buy Now, Pay Later) or as a Mobile Widget for neo-banks. We have built the 'intelligence layer' that can live anywhere financial decisions are made."

### SafeNav
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/safenav-78ec) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AitijhyaCoded/SafeNav) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://safe-nav-kohl.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/QuhLuNmztU8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackxios%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackxios2k25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Know the risk before you take the road

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Core Challenge:**
Urban commuting becomes hazardous and unpredictable during monsoon seasons. Heavy rainfall leads to sudden waterlogging and flash floods, turning familiar routes into dangerous traps. Standard navigation apps often prioritize the shortest path without accounting for real-time flood severity, leading vehicles into deep water, causing breakdowns, traffic gridlock, and significant safety risks.

**SafeNav** bridges this gap by treating "safety from waterlogging" as a critical navigation metric alongside distance and time.

🎯 **Key Capabilities & Use Cases**

🧠 **Algorithmic Safety (Custom Dijkstra Implementation)**
The Problem: Most safety routing is just a simple "avoid area" block. It doesn't calculate the trade-off between a 20km detour and a slightly wet road.
The Solution: SafeNav uses a custom Random Forest Classifier and Dijkstra’s Algorithm that calculates edge weights based on a formula: Distance × (1 + Flood Risk + Rain Intensity).
Use Case: It finds the "Safest Shortest Path". It won't send you on a massive detour for a minor puddle, but it will reroute you completely to avoid deep water. It mathematically balances safety vs. efficiency.

🗺️ **Visualizing the Invisible (Risk Heatmaps)**
The Problem: Flood warnings are often text-based ("Heavy rain in Sector 5") which is hard to visualize while driving.
The Solution: The Area Risk Insights and RiskMap components generate dynamic heatmaps.
Use Case: Users can look at the map and instantly see "Red Zones" (High Risk) overlaying the city. This allows for intuitive "at a glance" decision-making before even starting the car.

🤝 **Community-Powered Intelligence (Crowdsourcing)**
The Problem: Satellites and sensors can't see everything. A burst pipe or a blocked drain is often only known by locals.
The Solution: The Report Issue feature allows users to drop pins on waterlogged areas, which immediately updates the risk model for everyone else.
Use Case: If a user ahead of you reports "Knee-deep water," your route automatically adjusts to avoid that specific street, creating a Waze-like community safety net.

🤖 **ML-Driven Predictive Analysis**
The Problem: Rain doesn't always mean floods. It depends on drainage, topography, and soil.
The Solution: The backend uses Scikit-learn models (flood_risk_classifier & flood_severity_regressor) to analyze environmental factors and predict severity.
Use Case: It distinguishes between "wet roads" (safe to drive) and "severe waterlogging" (unsafe), preventing false alarms while catching real threats.

**SafeNav** isn't just a map; it's a survival tool not only for the monsoon but for all seasons and road hazards. By combining Dijkstra's algorithm for mathematical safety optimization, Machine Learning for risk prediction, and Crowdsourcing for real-time ground truth, it ensures that your journey is not just fast, but dry and safe.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building **SafeNav** was an ambitious journey that pushed us beyond simple CRUD operations into complex algorithms and AI integration. Here are the major hurdles we faced and how we overcame them:

**The "Safest vs. Shortest" Algorithmic Dilemma**
**The Hurdle:** Initially, our focus was purely on finding the safest path. However, our mentor challenged us: a safe path is useless if it takes 3 hours for a 20-minute trip. We needed to balance safety with efficiency.
**The Solution:** We implemented a custom Dijkstra’s Algorithm. Instead of standard distance weights, we created a composite "Edge Weight" formula. This formula mathematically weighs distance against flood risk and rain intensity. This allowed the system to find the "sweet spot"—a route that is significantly safer but not unreasonably longer.

**Data Scarcity & Quality**
**The Hurdle:** Finding a high-quality, real-world dataset for urban flood prediction was incredibly difficult. Public sensor data is often sparse or unstructured.
**The Solution:** We had to compromise and adapt. We sourced a "good enough" dataset from Kaggle to train our initial models. While not perfect, it allowed us to build a robust ML pipeline (ml_prep.ipynb) that can easily be retrained once better, localized data becomes available.

**Testing "Rain" on a Sunny Day**
**The Hurdle:** Our system relies on live weather data from the OpenWeather API to trigger warnings. Testing the "Monsoon Mode" features was difficult when the actual weather outside was clear and sunny.
**The Solution:** We had to build a robust testing environment where we could manually inject or mock weather parameters. This ensured our risk assessment logic worked correctly regardless of the actual forecast outside.

**Infrastructure Costs vs. Hackathon Constraints**
**The Hurdle:** Our mentor suggested adding a crowdsourcing feature where users upload images of hazards. However, cloud storage solutions (like AWS S3 or Cloudinary) usually require credit cards or paid tiers, which wasn't feasible for us.
**The Solution:** We engineered a local file storage system within our FastAPI backend. We save uploaded images directly to a local uploads/ directory and Firestore Database contains all the texts and serve them via static file mounting. This proved the concept perfectly without incurring infrastructure costs.

**Moving from Hardcoded to Generative AI**
**The Hurdle:** We initially hardcoded the "Severity Reasons" (e.g., "Risk is High because X"). It felt robotic and didn't account for complex combinations of factors.
**The Solution:** We integrated Google Gemini AI. Now, we pass the environmental parameters to Gemini, and it generates a dynamic, natural-language explanation of why a specific area is risky. This made the app feel much more intelligent and user-friendly.

**Expanding the Scope of Hazards**
**The Hurdle:** We started with just waterlogging. Our mentor pushed us to make it a complete safety app by including potholes, accidents, and road blockages.
**The Solution:** This required refactoring our database schema and frontend reporting forms. We created a flexible "Hazard Type" system that allows the map to render different icons and risk weights depending on whether the issue is a flood or a car accident.

**The UI Challenge: Interactive Route Selection**
**The Hurdle:** One of our biggest technical blockers was the map UI. We wanted to show multiple route options (e.g., "Route A: Fast but Risky" vs. "Route B: Safe but Slow") and let the user click to choose one.
**The Outcome:** Managing the state for multiple interactive GeoJSON layers in Leaflet proved to be extremely complex. While we successfully visualized the routes, making them fully interactive and selectable was a UX challenge we are still refining. It taught us a lot about the limitations of mapping libraries and state management.

**Best Innovation**

**SafeNav** redefines urban mobility by shifting the core objective of navigation from Efficiency (Speed) to Well-being (Safety). While existing giants like Google Maps optimize for the fastest route, SafeNav innovates by calculating the safest route using a novel multi-layered approach:

**Algorithmic Innovation:** We built a custom Weighted Dijkstra Algorithm that doesn't just measure distance—it mathematically quantifies "risk" by fusing real-time variables like crime reports, street lighting data, and live weather conditions into the pathfinding logic.

**Hyper-Local Resilience:** Our unique "Monsoon Mode" addresses a specific, often-overlooked urban crisis—flooding. By combining crowdsourced hazard reporting with live weather APIs, we create a dynamic "Safety Layer" that helps users navigate climate-related
challenges in real-time.

![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Core ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/Core%20ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🛑 The Problem It Solves
Urban flooding creates uncertainty and risk during daily travel. People don’t know which areas are waterlogged, which routes are safe, and decisions are often based on delayed or unreliable information.

✅ How It Helps
This project makes flood‑time decision‑making easier and safer by:

Predicting flood‑prone and waterlogged zones in advance

Showing safer routes, not just the shortest ones

Using real‑time data and citizen reports to improve accuracy

Helping citizens, emergency services, and authorities act before situations become dangerous

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
No labeled flood data: There are no official labeled flood datasets for the city, which made supervised learning difficult.
Solution: I used unsupervised clustering and anomaly detection to generate pseudo‑labels, then trained supervised models on top of them.

Rainfall data inconsistency: Initial satellite rainfall exports contained metadata instead of usable numeric values.
Solution: I refined the data extraction pipeline to obtain proper precipitation values and aggregate them meaningfully for the model.

Integrating ML with routing: Combining flood risk predictions with real road networks for safe routing was non‑trivial.
Solution: I embedded the ML risk scores directly into graph edge weights so routing algorithms could naturally avoid high‑risk zones.

Testing extreme flood scenarios: Real flood conditions can’t be reproduced on demand during development.
Solution: I used API mocking and request interception to simulate extreme rainfall and flooding scenarios for reliable testing and demos.

**Creative Use**

We used Requestly for regex‑based API mocking and script injection to simulate extreme flood scenarios in real time, enabling rapid testing, parallel development, and a live demo without modifying backend or production code.
