### <CodeJudge AI/>
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lesscodejudge-aigreater-d9c2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Tarunjit45/CodeJudge-binary.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://code-judge-binary-eight.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/UoO_L2_JIsY?si=JtwsRXpQlA43tGpq) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Let's see if your project survives reality.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CodeJudge AI is designed to solve the "Trust & Quality Crisis" in high-speed software development (hackathons, MVPs, and rapid prototyping).

Here is how it simplifies complex tasks and protects your time:

The Problem: "Innovation without Integrity"

The "Prompt Injection" Era: It is now easy to generate thousands of lines of code with AI, but most of it is a "house of cards"—fragile, unauthenticated, and full of hidden security holes.

The Judge's Nightmare: In any hackathon, judges have 5–10 minutes to review a project. They usually only see the frontend demo, which says nothing about the backend’s resilience or if the code was stolen/pre-made.

The Developer's Blind Spot: Under time pressure, developers skip testing and security. They don't know where their project will "snap" until it's too late.

 The Solution: How CodeJudge AI Makes it Easier & Safer

1. For Hackathon Judges: Instant "Integrity Filter"
Existing Task: Manual code reviews that take 30+ minutes per project.
The CodeJudge Way: A 60-second Deep Scan and Timeline Truth check. Judges get an instant "Authenticity Score" and an "Innovation Verdict," letting them focus only on the truly original, high-quality projects.

2. For Recruiters: High-Fidelity Pre-Screening
Existing Task: Sending out boring LeetCode tests that don't reflect real-world engineering skills.

The CodeJudge Way: Candidates submit a real GitHub repo. CodeJudge launches a Chaos Simulation to see how they handle edge cases, error states, and security threats—giving a much truer signal of their "Production Ready" skills.

3. For Developers: "The Brutal Mentor"
Existing Task: Manually writing unit tests and security checks for an MVP.
The CodeJudge Way: A "one-click mentor" that roasts your project's logic and identifies the exact Breakpoint where it will fail. It doesn't just find bugs; it generates vivid fixes and architectural preventions, making your "fast code" actually survive production.

4. For Tech Leaders: Standardizing Quality
The Ease: It creates a "unified resilience metric" (the CodeJudge Score). Instead of subjective opinions on what's "good code," teams can use objective Battle-Pass metrics to decide if a project is ready for the next level.

**Challenges we ran into**

** Technical Challenges We Overcame**

1. The "Silent" AI Failure (Backend Reference Errors)
The Hurdle: During the initial integration of the AI Review Engine, the system would crash silently. We discovered a ReferenceError where a variable named sig (project quality signals) was being called but was actually defined as q.
The Solution: We implemented a more robust metadata-mapping layer in the 

ai-review.js
 service to ensure that the AI prompt is always built with validated data, regardless of how the project is structured.

2. GitHub API "Tunnel-Vision" (Incomplete Scans)
The Hurdle: Our Deep Scan was initially too restrictive—it only looked for index.js or app.js. This meant modern projects using TypeScript (.tsx) or Python (.py) would show as "0 files fetched," giving the AI nothing to analyze.
The Solution: We rebuilt the Deep Scan filtering logic with a broader recursive tree search. It now intelligently prioritizes 10+ core files across any tech stack (React, Next.js, Django, Rust) to give the AI a complete understanding of the project's logic.

3. The "State Corruption" Bug (LocalStorage SyntaxError)
The Hurdle: As the app grew, we found that refreshing the browser would sometimes break the UI with a SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON. This happened because some state values were being saved as literal undefined strings in localStorage.
The Solution: We created a Safe Parsing Utility (

safeParse
) for the frontend state. It handles corrupted or missing strings gracefully, providing safe fallbacks and ensuring the user never gets stuck on a blank screen.

4. Complex Pipeline Flow (Non-Linear Navigation)
The Hurdle: Managing a multi-step pipeline (Submit → X-Ray → Attack → Score) is tricky. Users were getting "stuck" on the Breakpoint screen because the AI Review and the Chaos Simulation were running in parallel and sometimes the UI button didn't know which one was done first.
The Solution: We completely decoupled the Navigation Engine from the Analysis Tasks. By making each screen "self-initializing," we ensured that even if one part of the analysis fails or is slow, the user can always proceed through the fixes and see their final score.

5. AI Logic Hallucinations (Consistency Check)
The Hurdle: Sometimes LLMs would output "valid results" but in an invalid JSON format, causing the whole review to fail.
The Solution: We implemented JSON String Sanitization (regex-based cleaning) on all LLM responses to extract strictly valid objects before parsing, making the AI behavior 100% predictable for the frontend.

**Open Innovation**

Here is the "Reduced Engine" version of the pitch—perfect for a 2-minute judge presentation or a one-page summary:

The Half-Reduced Pitch: "The Battle-Pass for Innovation"
The Problem: In the AI era, hackathons are flooded with boilerplate and AI-generated projects. Judges are overwhelmed, and quality is hard to verify.

The Solution: CodeJudge AI is a dynamic resilience tester. We don't just "read" your code; we battle-test it in three steps:

Deep Scan (X-Ray): We pull the full GitHub structure and analyze it for AI signatures and timeline authenticity.
Chaos Attack: We launch a real-time "Chaos Simulation" (Breakpoints) to find where the logic actually snaps.
The Verdict: A brutal AI Roast + a Resilience Score, giving judges an instant "Yes/No" signal on project quality.
Why it wins Open Innovation: It moves evaluation from static scores to survival testing. It’s the first infrastructure that protects the integrity of innovation.

Technical Highlights (For the Q&A):

SSE Streams: Live attack feedback.
Multi-LLM Logic: Gemini (Logic) + Grok (Personality).
Deep Integrity Engine: Detects AI-boilerplate and commit-history hacks.

### VoiceForge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/voiceforge-ea4d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/senapati484/VoiceForge) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_mlmzxOxoTs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your knowledge. Our agents. Real phone calls.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webhook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webhook-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![mongoose](https://img.shields.io/badge/mongoose-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small businesses lose customers every day to missed calls, expensive human agents, and rigid IVR systems that can't actually hold a conversation. There's no simple tool that lets a non-technical business owner deploy a smart phone agent that genuinely understands their business — until now.

**Challenges we ran into**

Context window — You can't dump a 50-page PDF into every call. We pre-generate a compact knowledge file from all uploaded docs at agent creation, so the agent already knows the business before the first call even starts.
Webhook latency — Vapi needs a response in under 500ms or the conversation breaks. Serverless functions cold-start too slowly, so we run an always-on Express backend on Railway — webhook arrives, answer goes back in under 400ms.
Silent middleware bug — Vapi sends raw JSON buffers for signature verification. If express.json() runs before express.raw(), the body gets pre-parsed and verification silently fails. One line of middleware ordering, hours to diagnose.
Embedding dimensions — Switched from OpenAI (1536 dims) to Gemini (768 dims) mid-build. Pinecone returned zero results with no error — just the agent saying "I don't know" to everything. Rebuilt the index at 768 dims and re-ingested everything.
Campaign calling — First version called all CSV contacts simultaneously. Vapi rate-limited us and users burned credits instantly. Rewrote it as a sequential loop with credit checks before every single call.
Data isolation — Multiple businesses on one Pinecone index is a privacy risk. Solved with per-user Pinecone namespaces — Company A's knowledge is physically unreachable from Company B's agent, not just filtered.

**AI/ML**

VoiceForge is a complete AI Voice Agent platform that enables businesses to create intelligent voice assistants for both inbound (receiving calls) and outbound (making calls) scenarios. Built with modern tech stack including Next.js, Express, MongoDB, and Vapi.

### NyayaSetu
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nyayasetu-39a7) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1174083368?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--Nocturne%202.O-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-nocturne-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Bridging Citizens and Justice with AI

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India’s judicial system faces a massive backlog of pending cases, with millions of cases waiting to be resolved across various courts. A significant reason behind this issue is that many citizens lack clear guidance about legal procedures, required documents, and the viability of their cases before approaching the courts.

For most people, understanding legal processes is difficult. Legal information is scattered, technical, and often requires consulting professionals even for basic guidance. As a result, individuals frequently file cases without adequate preparation or understanding, which contributes to delays, inefficient case handling, and increased burden on the judiciary.

NyayaSetu aims to address this gap by providing an AI-powered platform that helps citizens understand their legal situation before filing a case. By analyzing user-described legal issues, the system identifies similar past cases, estimates possible outcomes and timelines, and guides users on the required documentation.

This helps citizens make informed decisions, prepare cases more effectively, and reduces unnecessary or poorly prepared filings—ultimately contributing to a more efficient justice system.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was working with legal text data. Legal case descriptions are often long, complex, and written in technical language. Converting these texts into a form that an AI model can understand and compare effectively required careful preprocessing and experimentation with NLP tools.

Another challenge was implementing semantic similarity for case matching. We needed a way to compare a user’s problem description with past case summaries in a meaningful way. We solved this by using sentence embedding models from Hugging Face (MiniLM) and calculating similarity scores using machine learning libraries.

We also encountered difficulties in structuring the legal dataset. Since there is no single standardized dataset for all types of Indian legal cases, we had to curate and structure case summaries manually so that the system could use them for similarity search and prediction.

On the engineering side, integrating the frontend (React) with the backend (FastAPI) while ensuring smooth API communication required debugging request handling and response formatting.

Despite these challenges, iterating quickly during the hackathon helped us build a working prototype that demonstrates how AI can assist citizens in understanding legal situations before approaching courts.

> Give a Skill, Get a Skill

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jinja2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jinja2-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bootstrap 5.3.3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bootstrap%205.3.3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask 3.1.3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask%203.1.3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Quality education is expensive. 

Whether it's a coding bootcamp, a music lesson, or a language class, learning a new skill almost always comes with a price tag that many people simply can't afford. 
Yet at the same time, millions of people already possess valuable skills that others would love to learn — and they're sitting on them for free. 
SkillSwap eliminates the cost barrier entirely by turning knowledge into currency. Instead of paying for classes, users trade skills with each other — you teach me Python, I'll teach you guitar — creating a symbiotic learning relationship where both people walk away richer in knowledge, not poorer in their wallets. 
No subscriptions, no hourly fees, no gatekeeping — just people helping people grow.

1 ) Create a profile listing the skills you can teach and the skills you want to learn
2 ) Get matched with someone whose strengths fill your gaps and vice versa
3 )Agree on a schedule, conduct your sessions, and rate each other afterward
4) Build a trust score that the wider community can rely on when choosing who to learn from

Unlike existing platforms where you pay per hour and learn from pre-recorded videos with no personal feedback, SkillSwap gives you a real human who is personally invested in teaching you well — because their own learning depends on it. Every session is inherently fair. Both people give equally, and both people gain equally.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we faced but overcame: 

• Designing the message UI in HTML was difficult, managing layout, alignment, and responsiveness; solved by simplifying structure and using basic CSS styling.

• Implementing the skill matching logic was challenging due to inconsistent user inputs; improved by standardizing skill names and using simple comparison techniques.

• Faced issues connecting frontend and backend APIs; resolved by debugging endpoints, checking routes carefully, and ensuring correct data formats were sent.

• Encountered errors while integrating database with backend; fixed by verifying connection strings, handling promises properly, and checking MongoDB configuration step by step.

• Managing time while learning new tools and fixing bugs was tough; overcame it by focusing on MVP features and avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Team **ByteMe** -- Garima Singh, Adithya Sharma, Avin Shrivastava, Yashashree Saha

> Find Your Dream Team

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students and researchers waste significant time and energy trying to find the right teammates for hackathons, class projects, and startup ideas. The typical process involves posting in scattered Discord servers, group chats, or spreadsheets — with no way to evaluate skills, track who's available, or communicate in one place. Teams end up unbalanced (all frontend devs, no backend), people join too many teams, and coordination is chaotic.

How CollabX Solves It:

CollabX is a centralized platform where users create skill-tagged profiles and post team openings with specific skill requirements. Project owners list exactly what roles they need (e.g., "React, Python, UI/UX"), and applicants with matching skills can discover and apply to join. Owners review applications, accept or reject, and manage their roster — including kicking members, delegating a team leader, and sharing invite codes for direct joins. Built-in real-time messaging eliminates the need for external chat tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, the project detail page would randomly show "Project not found" even when the project existed and the API returned data successfully. After debugging, we discovered the issue was in our error handling — a single try/catch block wrapped both the API call and the DOM rendering. When a JavaScript rendering error occurred (like accessing a property on a null team member), the catch block assumed the API had failed and displayed "Project not found."

Fix: We separated the API fetch and rendering into independent try/catch blocks, and added null-safety checks on the members array. This ensured rendering bugs were reported accurately instead of being masked as missing data.

Team **DietCode** -- Vaibhav Vasistha, Parth Chawla, [Archit Sahoo](https://github.com/4rch1t), [Mohakk Malvankar](https://github.com/mohakkm)

### Devise
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/devise-6f10) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Yashhzzz/Devise-Merged) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://devise-ui.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/CxKo6UmDt-A) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNova%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknova-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> See Every Tool. Stop Every Risk.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Since ChatGPT launched, employees at every company started using AI tools on their own. ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Midjourney, Perplexity, and hundreds more, in browsers, IDEs, and desktop apps. The company has zero visibility into any of it.

Devise solves three simultaneous crises from a single deployment.

The first is shadow IT and security risk. Over 80% of employees use unapproved AI tools, and 38% share confidential company data through them without any approval. There's no audit trail, no policy enforcement, and regulators are starting to ask questions nobody can answer. Devise detects every AI tool in use, approved or not, and flags high-risk activity in real time.

The second is the adoption blindspot. Leadership spends crores on AI licenses and transformation programs but has no real data on whether employees are actually using them. Decisions get made on stale surveys. Devise gives teams a live view of which tools are being used, by which departments, how often, and whether that's growing or shrinking.

The third is budget bleed. 78% of IT leaders face unexpected AI charges and 30%+ of AI budget is wasted on unused or duplicate subscriptions. Devise tracks every active subscription, flags zombie licenses that are paid for but never used, and attributes spend down to the team level.

What sets Devise apart is that it uses two complementary detection layers working together. A Chrome extension catches browser-based tools and a Python desktop agent catches IDE extensions, native apps, and direct API calls, together giving complete coverage across every surface AI is being used on. And critically, it never captures content. Only metadata about which tool was used, when, and by whom. No keystrokes, no clipboard, no conversation content. That privacy boundary is what makes enterprise deployment legally viable in the first place.

**Challenges we ran into**

The first thing that burned us was Firestore timestamps. Firestore returns dates as its own proprietary Timestamp objects, not native JS Dates. Passing them directly into React components caused silent "Invalid Date" errors across every chart and table in the dashboard and they were annoyingly hard to trace. We ended up building a centralised normalizeDate() helper inside our api.ts service layer that converts everything, Firestore Timestamps, ISO strings, Unix numbers, into a consistent ISO string before it ever reaches the UI.

Then came composite index crashes. Firestore requires manually created composite indexes for any query that combines multiple where and orderBy clauses. During development, adding a new filter to the live feed would silently crash an entire dashboard section with a completely opaque Firebase error. 
We worked around this by wrapping non-critical stat queries in try/catch blocks so a missing index degrades gracefully instead of nuking the whole view.

The messiest one was process attribution on Windows for the desktop agent. Using psutil to monitor active processes worked cleanly on macOS but on Windows, a lot of AI-related activity runs under generic host process names like msedgewebview2.exe or node.exe. The process name alone told us almost nothing. We had to build a secondary layer that cross-references each process's open network connections against a registry of known AI API IP ranges and domains to actually figure out what tool was being used underneath.

Team **Astrax** -- Mouriyan Gandhi, [Kavin G](https://github.com/gkavin2527), [Yash A](https://github.com/Yash13606)

Today, the legal system is not broken—but it’s inaccessible.
For a common person, understanding their legal rights—especially in cases like cybercrime or harassment—is overwhelming and confusing. As a result, millions never take action.

At the same time, lawyers spend countless hours on manual research and document analysis, slowing down justice itself.

LawGenie bridges this gap.
We use AI to turn complex legal problems into simple, actionable guidance, and instantly connect users with the right lawyers—while giving professionals powerful tools to speed up research and decision-making.

In short, we make justice understandable, accessible, and faster—for everyone.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

The increasing use of generative AI tools in workplaces has led to the rise of Shadow AI, where employees use external AI systems without proper monitoring or security controls.

While these tools improve productivity, they create serious risks such as:

Accidental sharing of sensitive company data

Exposure of proprietary source code

Leakage of credentials, API keys, and internal documents

Sharing of personally identifiable information (PII)

Traditional security systems are not designed to analyze AI prompts or understand user intent, making it difficult for organizations to detect when sensitive information is being shared with AI platforms.

How Our Solution Helps

Our solution introduces an AI Privacy Proxy that acts as a protective layer between users and external AI tools.

People can use this system to:

Secure AI Usage in Organizations

Employees can safely use AI tools for coding, documentation, and research without risking data leakage.

Prevent Sensitive Data Exposure

The system detects confidential information in prompts and automatically blocks or redacts it before it reaches the AI model.

Protect Intellectual Property

Developers can use AI assistants while preventing the accidental sharing of proprietary code or internal algorithms.

Enable Responsible AI Adoption

Organizations can adopt AI technologies while maintaining security, privacy, and regulatory compliance.

Impact

By adding a real-time monitoring and governance layer, our solution allows organizations to benefit from AI productivity while keeping their data secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

1️⃣ Detecting Sensitive Data Accurately

One of the main challenges was accurately identifying different types of sensitive information such as credentials, personal data, and proprietary code within user prompts.

Solution:
We implemented a hybrid detection pipeline combining multiple techniques like Named Entity Recognition, PII detection, regex-based scanners, and intent analysis to improve detection accuracy.

2️⃣ Handling Multiple Input Formats

Users may share sensitive information not only as text but also through images or screenshots.

Solution:
We integrated OCR-based text extraction so that any text inside images can also be scanned and analyzed by the system.

3️⃣ Intercepting AI Prompts Across Platforms

AI tools are accessed through different environments such as web browsers and developer IDEs, making it difficult to monitor all interactions.

Solution:
We developed browser and IDE integrations to demonstrate how AI interactions can be intercepted and analyzed before reaching external AI models.

4️⃣ Balancing Security with Usability

Blocking too many prompts could disrupt normal workflows and reduce productivity.

**Digital Privacy and Data Protection**

The problem statement highlights the growing issue of Shadow AI, where employees use external AI tools such as chatbots and coding assistants without organizational oversight. While these tools improve productivity, they create serious risks such as data leakage, intellectual property exposure, and privacy violations.

Traditional security systems are not designed to analyze AI prompts or understand user intent, which makes it difficult to detect when sensitive information is being shared.

Our solution addresses this gap by introducing an AI Privacy Proxy, a security layer that monitors and analyzes prompts before they are sent to external AI models.

1️⃣ Monitoring AI Interactions

Our system intercepts prompts from common environments where employees interact with AI tools, such as web-based AI platforms and developer environments.
This allows organizations to gain visibility into how AI is being used.

2️⃣ Detecting Sensitive Information

The intercepted prompts are analyzed through a hybrid detection pipeline that includes:

Named Entity Recognition to identify personal or organizational information

PII detection to detect sensitive personal data

OCR-based extraction to read text embedded in images

Intent analysis to understand whether the user is attempting to share confidential information

This enables the system to detect credentials, personal data, proprietary code, and internal company information.

3️⃣ Policy-Based Governance

Once the prompt is analyzed, a policy engine applies organizational rules to determine the appropriate action:

Allow safe prompts

Redact sensitive data automatically

Block prompts that contain critical information

This ensures that sensitive data never reaches external AI systems.

4️⃣ Enabling Safe AI Adoption

Instead of restricting AI usage completely, our solution enables organizations to use AI tools safely by adding a governance and monitoring layer.

This helps balance innovation and productivity with security and compliance.

**The problem it solves**

Risk of Non-Payment:
It uses a programmable escrow system where the client deposits funds first, ensuring the freelancer gets paid once the work is verified.

Slow and Expensive Cross-Border Payments:
Instead of relying on traditional systems like SWIFT, the platform automates settlement and releases payments instantly after conditions are met.

Compliance and Tax Complexity:
The system automatically calculates and reports tax liabilities based on international standards influenced by OECD guidelines.

Lack of Trust in Remote Work:
By using AI verification, escrow locking, and immutable settlement certificates, the platform creates transparency and accountability between clients and contractors.

**Challenges we ran into**

Handling Large GitHub Repositories for AI Verification
Sending full repositories to Google Gemini would consume many tokens and increase cost. We solved this by implementing indexing and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) so only relevant code chunks are analyzed.

Cross-Border Compliance Complexity
Different countries have different tax rules and digital service regulations influenced by frameworks from organizations like OECD. Designing a system that flags tax liability without illegally withholding funds was challenging.

Simulating Financial Infrastructure in a Hackathon Environment
Real banking integrations are difficult to access quickly, so we had to create sandbox escrow wallets and payment simulations to demonstrate programmable settlement logic.

Ensuring Trust Without Blockchain
Many escrow systems rely on blockchain, but our challenge was building a transparent and auditable settlement system using traditional databases and cryptographic hashes to maintain an immutable audit trail.

Workflow Automation Between Multiple Systems
Coordinating triggers from GitHub, AI verification, and settlement workflows required careful orchestration using automation tools and backend APIs.

**FinTech**

Nexus Escrow fits the Financial Technology (FinTech) track because it builds a programmable escrow payment infrastructure for cross-border freelance work. It securely holds client funds, automates payment settlement, and splits payouts with platform fees and tax-liability reporting. By reducing settlement delays, improving payment trust, and handling compliance for international transactions, it solves key challenges in modern digital finance.

> PhosAI -See what your prescriptions don't tell you

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional medical systems rely on isolated pairwise checks (Drug A vs Drug B). However, patients with complex conditions often take 5 or more medications, creating "blind spots" in safety.

Phos AI solves this by mapping polypharmacy as a biological graph. It detects cascading interactions—where Drug A affects a metabolic enzyme (like CYP3A4), which in turn changes how Drug B is processed, potentially leading to toxic levels of Drug C. By tracing these multi-hop pathways, Phos AI uncovers secondary and tertiary risks that standard clinical tools completely miss.

**Challenges we ran into**

Data Volume & Complexity: Processing and querying a massive clinical database (over 1.4GB) of drug-enzyme-target interactions required optimizing our Neo4j graph structure for high-performance traversals.
Graph Synthesis: We faced the challenge of turning complex "spider-webs" of biological data into something a doctor can use in seconds. We solved this by implementing an AI synthesis layer that translates multi-hop graph cascades into plain-language clinical safety verdicts.
Polypharmacy Scaling: Ensuring the system stayed accurate as the number of drugs increased required fine-tuning our "risk-weighting" algorithm to prevent alert fatigue while catching critical dangers

**HealthTech**

Phos AI directly transforms the "HealthTech" landscape by solving one of the most persistent and dangerous challenges in modern medicine: polypharmacy. While current clinical tools rely on linear, pairwise checks (Drug A vs. Drug B), Phos AI leverages graph theory and biological path tracing to illuminate "invisible cascades"—indirect interactions where one medication affects an enzyme or transporter, causing a dangerous secondary effect on a third medication.

How Phos AI fits the HealthTech track:

Clinical Decision Support: We transition drug safety from a "red flag" system to a high-fidelity visual workspace. By mapping biological pathways in a live Neo4j graph, clinicians can see why an interaction is risky, not just that it exists.
AI-Driven Synthesis: Using state-of-the-art LLMs, we synthesize complex pharmacological data into 3-tier safety verdicts (SAFE, CAUTION, DANGER) and provide actionable "Smart Swap" suggestions, reducing the cognitive load on physicians.
OCR & Vision Integration: To bridge the gap between physical medicine and digital analysis, we’ve integrated Vision AI to extract medication names directly from prescription images, streamlining the clinical workflow.
Quantifiable Outcomes: Our goal is the reduction of preventable adverse drug events (ADEs), which cost the healthcare system billions annually. Phos AI provides the clarity needed to handle complex pharmacological regimens with precision and light.

> Navigate the hidden dependencies of your codebase!

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![AST](https://img.shields.io/badge/AST-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Mapping Cross-Language Dependencies in Polyglot Codebases Modern enterprise applications are
typically built as polyglot systems, where different layers of the architecture databases, backend
services, and frontend interfaces are implemented using different programming languages and
frameworks. While this architecture improves modularity and scalability, it also introduces significant
challenges in tracking how data and logic propagate across system boundaries. 
Conventional static analysis tools are largely confined to single language environments, making them
ineffective at identifying dependencies when information moves between components through APIs,
schemas, or service interfaces. As a result, seemingly small changes such as modifying a database field
or backend variable can silently affect distant parts of the application. This challenge focuses on
exploring methods to trace and map dependencies across language and service boundaries, enabling
clearer visibility into how changes in one part of a distributed codebase may propagate throughout
the broader system

**The problem it solves**

Drug discovery is broken.

Finding one approved drug costs $2.6 billion and takes 12 years. 
90% of candidates fail at the very first step — designing the molecule. 
Not in clinical trials. Not in patients. At step one.

The reason is simple: medicinal chemists are guessing. One molecular 
structure at a time. From a chemical universe containing more possible 
drug-like molecules than atoms in the observable universe (10^60 structures).

787,000 people die every year from antibiotic-resistant infections.

Not because scientists stopped trying. Because finding the right molecule

cannot access the tools that exist — Schrödinger charges $1,000/month,

inaccessible to academic researchers in developing countries.

We built the open-source solution.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/a238fe72a6ce4a848b255f9724e90b8c/d9206613-fe24-465b-b3c7-254d390ef71b.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

The first major wall hit us before training even started — RDKit was compiled against NumPy 1.x but our system had NumPy 2.0.2, causing an immediate _ARRAY_API not found crash that required careful dependency downgrading without breaking the entire environment. Once past that, Apple's MPS backend on the M4 presented its own challenges — not all PyTorch operations are supported, requiring careful tensor placement and memory management completely different from standard CUDA workflows. Training itself delivered the biggest shock: MolT5 epoch 1 took 7 hours 48 minutes instead of the expected 1.5 hours because HuggingFace was simultaneously downloading the 308MB model weights during training — a brutal discovery at hour 8 of a 48-hour hackathon. We adapted by pre-downloading all weights and setting TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, cutting subsequent epochs to 1.5 hours each. Midway through the project, an external AI agent modified our generate.py and broke the generation pipeline entirely — the model started outputting English words like "These", "Thanks", "Our" instead of SMILES strings, a textbook hallucination failure we had to debug under time pressure by restoring correct beam search parameters. The same agent introduced GEN_BEAMS=1 in our config, silently disabling beam search and causing severe output repetition — the same molecule generated every run. We identified this as the root cause of the diversity problem and fixed it to GEN_BEAMS=5, which combined with our Morgan fingerprint Tanimoto filter and GNN subgraph scoring gave us mathematically guaranteed diverse outputs. Checkpoint format mismatches between finetune.py and generate.py required writing format-agnostic loading logic. Graph construction edge cases in ZINC250k — disconnected fragments, atoms with no bonds — required defensive guards throughout the GNN pipeline. And overarching everything was the fundamental time constraint: full MolT5 training would require 78+ hours we didn't have. The strategic decision to ship 5 epochs achieving val=0.5931 over waiting for a perfect model was the right call — 86-94% validity beating published benchmarks proved the architecture works even undertrained.

**Electrothon 8.0 Honors Track**

We are all girls team Participating in this project

**IQ AI**

we have created a generative model

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

MolGen is an end-to-end AI pipeline for generative drug molecule discovery. The system takes plain English property descriptions or explicit pharmaceutical targets and generates novel, chemically valid, drug-like molecules in under 60 seconds — solving the computational pre-screening step that traditionally costs pharmaceutical companies months of manual chemistry work.
The Problem
Drug discovery costs $2.6 billion per approved drug and takes 12 years on average. 90% of candidates fail at the very first step — molecular design — because medicinal chemists are manually guessing structures one at a time from a chemical space containing 10^60 possible molecules. This is not a science problem. It is a search problem. The molecules that cure Alzheimer's, defeat antibiotic-resistant infections, and treat rare diseases exist somewhere in that space. We are simply searching it too slowly.
The System
MolGen is built on two original trained models working in a generate-then-filter pipeline.
The first model is MolT5-small — a T5 transformer architecture with 77 million parameters, pretrained on chemistry and fine-tuned by us on 47,500 paired training examples drawn from the ZINC250k pharmaceutical database. Each training pair consists of a property description and its corresponding SMILES string. The encoder reads the input description through 6 transformer layers with multi-head self-attention and cross-attention, producing contextual representations of the desired molecular properties. The decoder generates SMILES strings autoregressively using beam search with GEN_BEAMS=5 — maintaining 5 candidate sequences simultaneously at every character position. Temperature 1.3 flattens the probability distribution for chemical diversity. Top-p 0.92 nucleus sampling removes low-probability garbage tokens. 10 batches of 5 beams produce 50 total candidates per request. The model was fine-tuned using AdamW optimizer with learning rate 3e-4, cosine learning rate schedule with 200-step linear warmup, and gradient clipping at 1.0. Validation loss reached 0.5931 after 5 epochs on Apple M4 MPS hardware.
Every generated SMILES string passes through RDKit chemical validation — seven simultaneous checks including syntax parsing, valence validation, ring closure verification, aromaticity perception, kekulization, sanitization, and stereochemistry validation. Molecules failing any check are immediately discarded. 88-94% of generated candidates pass validation — significantly exceeding the published benchmark of 60-70% for graph-based generative models. Each valid molecule is canonicalized to prevent duplicate representations and deduplicated using a canonical SMILES seen-set.
The second model is an original Message Passing Neural Network trained from scratch on 50,000 ZINC250k molecules. Molecules are represented as graphs — atoms as nodes with 13-dimensional feature vectors encoding element type (one-hot over 10 element classes), formal charge, ring membership, and aromaticity — and bonds as edges with 4-dimensional bond type vectors (single, double, triple, aromatic). The MPNNLayer architecture runs 4 rounds of message passing: each round computes atom-to-atom messages via a 516-to-256 MLP (concatenating source atom 256-dim, destination atom 256-dim, and bond features 4-dim), aggregates messages by summation, and updates atom representations with a residual connection and LayerNorm for training stability. After 4 rounds each atom carries a subgraph fingerprint — a learned representation of its complete 4-bond chemical neighborhood. Global mean pooling collapses all atom representations into a single 256-dimensional molecule vector. Three independent prediction heads output QED (with Sigmoid activation), LogP (no activation, unbounded), and TPSA (Sigmoid scaled by 200) simultaneously. The model was trained with composite MSE loss normalized across all three targets to prevent scale-induced gradient imbalance, using Adam optimizer with ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler. Training converged to 0.007 MSE after 10 epochs — validating the model's prediction accuracy against known pharmaceutical property values.
The subgraph representations learned by message passing directly solve the same-answer problem in generative chemistry. Structurally similar molecules have different atomic neighborhood environments — different subgraph fingerprints — producing different GNN representations and different reward scores, naturally separating near-duplicate candidates in the ranking. This is reinforced by a Morgan fingerprint diversity filter: we compute 2048-bit subgraph hash vectors (radius=2 Morgan fingerprints) for every valid molecule and remove any pair with Tanimoto similarity above 0.85 — meaning more than 85% subgraph pattern overlap. This provides mathematically guaranteed structural diversity in the final output, not probabilistic.
The composite reward function — 0.5 × predicted QED − 0.2 × |predicted LogP − target LogP| − 0.001 × |predicted TPSA − tar

**The problem it solves**

The solution addresses the complexity involved in integrating and managing multiple blockchain networks within industrial systems.

Through **ChainMerge**, it makes the addition of new blockchain networks significantly easier and faster, saving substantial development time and effort. It provides a unified interface for interacting with different chains, enabling consistent and efficient RPC querying across multiple blockchain nodes.

ChainMerge also introduces unified error handling, which simplifies debugging and monitoring across networks. In addition, it reduces code repetition, management costs, and the manual parsing work typically required when dealing with multi-chain blockchain systems, allowing developers to build and maintain scalable blockchain applications more efficiently.

This streamlined approach improves overall system maintainability and reliability while enabling organizations to expand their blockchain infrastructure without major architectural changes.

The** ChainMerge SDK** is designed to act as a unified developer toolkit for interacting with multiple blockchains through a single interface. Instead of writing separate integration logic for every blockchain, developers can use the SDK to perform common operations such as RPC calls, transaction queries, and data retrieval across different chains in a standardized format. The SDK handles response normalization, error management, and data parsing internally, allowing developers to focus on building applications rather than dealing with chain-specific complexities.
[NPM Package ChainMerge](https://www.npmjs.com/package/chainmerge-sdk)

We have also developed a browser extension built on top of our ChainMerge SDK that helps analyze blockchain transaction hashes. The extension fetches transaction data using our SDK and then leverages the Gemini API to generate clear, human-readable explanations by analyzing the JSON response. This makes blockchain data easier to understand and helps developers or users quickly interpret complex transaction details.

[ChainMerge Backend API - Render](https://chainmerge-api.onrender.com)
[ChainMerge Backend API - Google Cloud](https://chainmerge-api-651850437266.us-central1.run.app)

These projects are:

[Integrating IQ AI](https://github.com/new-webby/Integrating-IQ-ai)
[Arbitraging AI Agent](https://thenigerianprince67.vercel.app)

**Challenges we ran into**

Some of the key challenges faced during development included working with low-level implementations in Rust, which required careful handling of memory, system-level logic, and blockchain-specific structures. 
Another challenge was publishing and configuring the NPM package, ensuring it was properly structured, versioned, and compatible for external developers to easily integrate into their projects. 
Additionally, decoding and managing data across eight different blockchain networks within the system introduced complexity, as each chain has its own formats, RPC responses, and interaction patterns. 
Handling these differences while maintaining a unified interface required significant effort in standardization and testing

**Ethereum Track**

This project is highly suitable for the Ethereum Track because it focuses on improving the developer infrastructure and interoperability within the Ethereum ecosystem and EVM-compatible chains. 
Many industrial and decentralized applications today interact with multiple EVM-based networks such as Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, and Polygon. ChainMerge simplifies this multi-chain development by providing a unified SDK that standardizes RPC interactions, error handling, and data parsing across different chains. 
This significantly reduces development complexity and enables builders to integrate Ethereum and other EVM networks more efficiently. Additionally, our integration of IQ AI for on-chain governance assistance enhances decentralized decision-making, aligning closely with Ethereum’s principles of open governance and decentralized innovation. 
By improving multi-chain accessibility, developer experience, and governance tooling, ChainMerge contributes to building a more scalable and developer-friendly Ethereum ecosystem.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

This is an open-innovation project aimed at addressing key low-level challenges in the industrial blockchain ecosystem.
 As blockchain adoption grows across industries, integrating and managing multiple blockchain networks becomes increasingly complex and inefficient. Our solution tackles this problem by introducing ChainMerge, an innovation designed to simplify the integration process between different blockchains. By providing a streamlined and scalable approach.
 ChainMerge enables organizations to seamlessly add and connect multiple blockchain networks within their infrastructure. This significantly improves interoperability, reduces integration overhead, and allows businesses to leverage the strengths of different blockchain platforms more efficiently.

**IQ AI**

In addition to our chain addition algorithm, we have incorporated IQ AI to build an on-chain governance assistant agent that enhances how governance processes are handled within blockchain networks. Using IQ AI, the agent helps analyze governance proposals, summarize important details, and assist participants in making more informed decisions. This improves accessibility, transparency, and efficiency in governance while enabling communities and organizations to manage decentralized systems more effectively

**Solana**

This project is well suited for the Solana Track because it focuses on improving multi-chain interoperability and developer tooling, which is essential for applications that interact with Solana alongside other blockchain ecosystems. 
ChainMerge simplifies the process of integrating Solana with other networks by providing a unified SDK that standardizes RPC querying, error handling, and data parsing across different chains. 
This reduces the complexity developers usually face when working with Solana’s high-performance architecture while also managing interactions with other blockchains. By making it easier to query transactions, decode blockchain data, and integrate Solana into multi-chain systems, ChainMerge helps developers build scalable applications that leverage Solana’s speed and efficiency. 
Additionally, the project demonstrates practical use cases such as AI-powered transaction analysis and governance assistance, showing how Solana-based systems can be integrated into intelligent, multi-chain infrastructures.

### CityQuest
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cityquest-ca70) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ayush1229/CityQuest) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/Nk0HiTqLDkk?feature=share) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turns every place into a questline

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Direction API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Direction%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional map apps get you from Point A to Point B as fast as possible. CityQuest turns the journey itself into an adventure. It is a gamified, AI-powered travel companion that transforms any real-world city into a live RPG map, encouraging users to explore, learn, and step outside

1, Apps like Google Maps or Apple Maps are purely utilitarian. They are designed to minimize travel time and optimize routes. They treat the world as a grid of traffic data, making travel—especially walking in a new city or even your own college campus—feel like a chore.
How CityQuest Solves It: By overlaying an RPG engine onto the real world. Buildings become Taverns and Academies, and walking down the street triggers AI-generated "Side Quests." It shifts the user's mindset from "How long until I get there?" to "What can I discover along the way?"

2. Tourists and locals constantly walk past historical landmarks, hidden gardens, or interesting local businesses without ever looking up from their phones. We are disconnected from the rich history and culture immediately surrounding us.
How CityQuest Solves It: The AI Quest Generator and the Lore Capture system. By reading live Google Places data, the app dynamically generates "Trivia" or "Discovery" quests specifically about the user's exact coordinates. When they complete it, the app forces them to use their camera to capture the real-world location, automatically generating a "Lore Scrapbook" that teaches them the history of the place they just found.

3. Most travel guides, AR games, and interactive maps are incredibly heavy (150MB+). They drain storage space, require massive data downloads, and alienate users with budget smartphones or limited data plans.
How CityQuest Solves It: The Thin-Client Architecture. By offloading the heavy computing to cloud AI (OpenRouter/Gemini via Firebase) and utilizing native OS features (like the device gyroscope and camera), CityQuest delivers a massive, dynamic, infinite game world in a package that is under 60MB.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Bypassing API Limits with Category Deep-Scanning

The Problem: The New Google Places API restricts nearby searches to just 20 results, which left my game map completely empty around campus.

The Solution: we wrote a custom Node.js script that loops through specific categories (hospitals, restaurants, schools) individually. This bypassed the generic limit, scraping and mapping the entire area into my database.

2. Optimizing 2.5D sprite Rendering with a Tiered Priority Mapper

The Problem: Real-world locations have messy, overlapping tags (e.g., both pharmacy and store), which confused my Flutter map logic and caused repetitive, incorrect sprites.

The Solution: we engineered a Tiered Priority Mapper to evaluate high-value tags first. To prevent visual repetition, I used the quest ID's hashCode to instantly randomize sprite variations without adding heavy processing overhead.

3. Ensuring Zero Downtime with AI Waterfall Architecture

The Problem: Relying solely on the Gemini API for live quest generation risked a complete app crash if the service timed out or rate-limited me during a live demo.

The Solution: we built a fault-tolerant backend. If Gemini fails, the system instantly catches the error and falls back to OpenRouter to query available open-source models (with a tertiary hardcoded safety net), guaranteeing uninterrupted gameplay.

4. Delivering True AR in a 56MB App

The Problem: Adding a Pokémon Go-style AR capture mechanic using true ARCore/ARKit SDKs would have bloated my lean 56MB app to over 100MB and crashed my emulators.

The Solution: we implemented the model_viewer_plus package to bypass custom AR engines entirely. By handing the 3D rendering directly to the phone's native OS (Google Scene Viewer / Apple Quick Look), we achieved a flawless AR experience with zero app bloat.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Track 1: Electrothon Winners (Theme: Labyrinth of Enternum)
We built CityQuest specifically to answer this theme. While most apps want you to stare at a screen, we built an app that gamifies looking up. We took the mundane aspects of daily life—walking across campus or exploring a new city—and turned them into an interactive RPG experience. By tying real-world movement to AI-generated side quests, AR artifact hunting, and achievement badges, we successfully gamified reality and gave users a genuine reason to step outside and explore.

**Google Cloud**

Track 2: MLH Google Cloud
Our app’s architecture relies on a continuous, self-sustaining loop of Google Cloud technologies. We didn't just plug in a single API; we built an end-to-end ecosystem:

Google Maps SDK: Serves as the immersive 3D game engine and UI canvas.

Google Places API (New): Deep-scans the user's physical coordinates to extract rich, real-world data and map 3D sprites.

Google Gemini API: Takes that real-world location data and dynamically generates context-aware "Trivia" and "Discovery" quests in real-time.

Directions API: Calculates the exact street-level route to guide the player to their AI-generated destination.

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

Google Gemini API: Takes that real-world location data and dynamically generates context-aware "Trivia" and "Discovery" quests in real-time.

**The problem it solves**

# OptiSync 👁️
### Eye Fatigue Measurer using Face Mesh Analysis

> A full-stack **Ocular Wellness Ecosystem** that monitors eye health in real time and prevent Digital Eye Strain (DES).

---

## 🚩 The Problem

Over **2.1 billion people** suffer from Digital Eye Strain — yet most solutions are just glorified timers. OptiSync is different. It *actually measures* your fatigue using biological markers and responds intelligently.

---

## 💡 What It Does

OptiSync uses **MediaPipe ** to continuously provide Eye Aspect ratio which is then coverted into blink rate and cognitive strain level using logic around this project

---

## ✨ Key Features

### 🔬 Precision Ocular Tracking
- Detects blinks, partial blinks, and prolonged staring
- BPM below 15? Strain score rises automatically
- Look away and rest? Score reduces as a reward

### 🌐 Works Everywhere
- A **Chrome Extension (MV3)** injects a live strain widget into every webpage
- Delivers OS-level notifications no matter what you're doing online

### 🚨 Progressive Alert System
- **Mild fatigue (40%+)** → Gentle nudge notification
- **Critical fatigue (80%+)** → Mandatory therapy session triggered

### 🧘 Therapy Modules
| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| 20-20-20 Rule | Monitored session — look 20ft away for 20 seconds |
| Palming Audio | Guided sensory deprivation to restore rod/cone cells |
| Infinity Eye Tracker | Eye-muscle reset following an orbital path |
| Posture Hazard Sensor | Detects if you're sitting too close to the screen |

### 📊 Health Analytics
- **Node/Express/MongoDB** backend logs hourly strain and blink history
- Track long-term ocular health trends over days and weeks

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| AI Engine | MediaPipe Face Mesh, JavaScript (ES6+) |
| Frontend | React 18, Vite, Glassmorphism CSS |
| Extension | Chrome MV3, Service Workers, Content Scripts |
| Backend | Node.js, Express.js |
| Database | MongoDB (Local/Atlas), Mongoose |

---

## 👥 Team
- **Arnav Singh**
- **Raghav Singh**
- **Sangram Borude**
-**Soham**

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🧱 Challenges We Ran Into

Building OptiSync came with some real engineering hurdles. Here's how we tackled each one:

---

## 🔋 1. Battery Efficiency

Running a real-time AI face mesh engine 24/7 is expensive on system resources.

**How we solved it:**
- Implemented **adaptive frame sampling** — the MediaPipe engine only processes frames when motion is detected, reducing unnecessary CPU cycles
- Throttled the strain-score update interval to avoid redundant recalculations
- The **Chrome Extension** uses a lightweight content script that only *listens* for score updates broadcast from the dashboard — it runs no AI logic itself
- Result: Minimal battery drain compared to running a full CV pipeline on every frame

---

## 🔐 2. Protecting User Data

Webcam access and health metrics are deeply personal — privacy was non-negotiable.

**How we solved it:**
- **All AI processing happens 100% on-device** — the webcam feed never leaves the user's browser
- No raw video or images are stored anywhere; only derived metrics (strain score, BPM) are logged
- The MongoDB backend stores **only anonymized numerical data** — no biometrics, no personally identifiable information
- Users have full control to clear their history log at any time

---

## ⚙️ 3. Running in the Background

Browser tabs get throttled or frozen when hidden — a major problem for a continuous monitoring tool.

**How we solved it:**
- Implemented **custom Web Workers** to offload the AI engine from the main thread, preventing it from being killed when the tab loses focus
- Used **Chrome Extension Service Workers (MV3)** to maintain a persistent background process that keeps the strain score alive across all tabs
- Added a **visibility state listener** that gracefully pauses and resumes the MediaPipe engine to save resources when the dashboard is minimized

---

## 👁️ 4. Actually Reducing Eye Strain

Most apps just set a timer and call it a day. We wanted real, measurable relief.

**How we solved it:**
- Built a **science-backed Therapy Modules Library** with interactive exercises:
  - **20-20-20 Rule** — enforced with real detection, not just a countdown
  - **Palming Audio** — guided sensory deprivation to restore rod and cone cells
  - **Infinity Eye Tracker** — active eye-muscle relaxation along an orbital path
  - **Posture Hazard Sensor** — alerts when the user is sitting dangerously close to the screen
- Therapy sessions are **triggered automatically** at critical strain thresholds (80%+), not left to user willpower
- The **Restorative Bonus** system actively rewards users for closing their eyes and looking away, reinforcing healthy habits through positive feedback

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tdadmin-c10d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Shlok1729/TDA.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/6aNY1DnTD5c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Advanced way to see data

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![SciPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SciPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional AI models for time-series forecasting—whether in finance, medicine, or industry—are fundamentally reactive. Because they rely on historical patterns, they are "blind" to unprecedented "Black Swan" events like sudden market crashes or mechanical failures. In noisy environments, these models struggle to distinguish between random fluctuations and actual structural decay, leading to catastrophic lagging indicators that only signal a problem after the damage is done. There is a critical void for a system that can detect the hidden geometric fractures in data, shifting the paradigm from simple pattern matching to proactive structural health monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was overcoming dependency incompatibilities between modern Python versions and established TDA libraries, which necessitated a mid-project migration and the manual implementation of feature extraction logic using ripser and persim. Additionally, calibrating the signal-to-noise ratio for the "Fragility Index" proved challenging; high-volatility assets like Bitcoin produced significant "jitter," requiring the development of custom rolling-mean smoothing and Z-score thresholding to eliminate false positives. Finally, implementing real-time animations in Streamlit required complex state management and placeholder synchronization to ensure that live point-clouds, persistence diagrams, and gauges updated seamlessly without UI lag or element ID conflicts.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Our project is a cross-domain powerhouse designed to solve critical "Early Warning" challenges across three distinct industries. In the FinTech & Web3 track, we demonstrate a leading-edge "Market Fragility Meter" that predicts crashes in Bitcoin and S&P 500 by detecting structural fractures weeks in advance. For the HealthTech track, we apply the same topological foundation to ECG signals, identifying cardiac arrhythmias that traditional monitors often miss in noisy environments. Finally, in the Industry 4.0 / IoT track, we showcase a "Predictive Maintenance" study for industrial turbines, detecting microscopic structural wear in vibration geometry before mechanical seizure occurs. This proves our engine is not just a niche tool, but a foundational framework for Geometric Intelligence across the world’s most critical infrastructures.

**The problem it solves**

Astronauts on long-duration space missions face serious challenges including physical health risks, mental stress, isolation, and limited real-time medical support. Monitoring their overall condition and predicting their health status before returning to Earth is difficult. Astro_Friend solves this by continuously tracking physical and mental health data, analyzing trends, and providing AI-driven support through a mood-aware chatbot, helping mission control better monitor astronaut well-being and prepare medical assistance in advance.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Astro_Friend, I faced several challenges such as integrating multiple technologies including React, Node.js, MongoDB, AI APIs, and machine learning logic into a single system. Managing consistent user IDs across different modules like health vitals, chatbot, and photo gallery was also challenging. Another difficulty was securely storing and retrieving user data while ensuring smooth communication between the frontend and backend. Additionally, implementing mood detection and making the chatbot respond appropriately based on the user's emotional state required careful design and testing.

> ( A tool to detect and stop phishing websites )

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Render](https://img.shields.io/badge/Render-333333?style=flat-square) ![Snowflake](https://img.shields.io/badge/Snowflake-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We developed PhishShield, a Chrome extension that protects users from phishing and social engineering attacks while browsing. The extension analyzes the authenticity of a visited website using multiple techniques such as domain age analysis, URL similarity detection, and login form detection. It also integrates AI-based analysis using the Gemini API to identify suspicious language or phishing patterns on webpages. Based on these signals, the system calculates a confidence score and warns users if a website appears risky. Additionally, the extension prevents users from copying, pasting, or entering sensitive information on suspicious websites, thereby reducing the chances of credential theft and financial fraud.

### SafeHer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/safeher-a64b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/muskankasat/SafeHer_Frontend) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> More freely, more safely

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement

Women traveling alone often face uncertainty about the safety of the areas they pass through, especially in unfamiliar cities or during late hours. Existing navigation platforms focus on the fastest or shortest routes, but they do not consider personal safety factors such as unsafe neighborhoods, poorly lit streets, or areas with reported incidents.

Because of the lack of accessible safety information, many women must rely on guesswork, personal experience, or word of mouth to determine whether a route or location is safe. In emergency situations, quickly reporting incidents or sharing location with trusted contacts can also be difficult.

There is currently no widely accessible platform that combines real-time safety awareness, community-driven incident reporting, and safety-based navigation in a single system.

As a result, women often restrict their mobility, avoid traveling alone at certain times, or feel unsafe while commuting.

SafeHer addresses this gap by providing safety-aware navigation, live safety heatmaps, and emergency assistance tools that help women make more informed travel decisions and move through cities with greater confidence.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced During Development

One of the most difficult parts of building SafeHer was implementing the safe-route navigation system. While the concept seemed straightforward initially — finding the shortest path while avoiding unsafe zones — the actual implementation turned into a long debugging session that lasted almost the entire night.

Our approach relied on building a custom road graph and running an A* pathfinding algorithm that considers safety scores for different nodes. However, multiple issues surfaced during development.

First, we encountered problems with graph connectivity. The initial dataset contained nodes from different geographic regions, which meant the algorithm sometimes tried to route between cities that had no connecting edges. This frequently resulted in the system returning “No route found”.

Second, mapping user clicks on the map to the nearest graph node turned out to be more complex than expected. Small coordinate mismatches caused the algorithm to select incorrect nodes, which made route generation fail even when the map appeared correct.

Another major challenge came from handling node identifiers. The graph stored nodes with unique IDs, while the algorithm internally assumed array indices. This mismatch caused the pathfinding algorithm to reference incorrect nodes and break traversal.

On top of this, we implemented safety filtering so that nodes with safety scores below a threshold would be avoided. While this was important for the core concept of SafeHer, it unintentionally disconnected parts of the graph, making some routes impossible to compute.

Throughout the night we repeatedly refactored the routing pipeline, debugging node selection, validating neighbor connections, rebuilding the graph structure, and adjusting the A* implementation to correctly interpret node IDs and distances.

Although frustrating at times, this debugging process helped us better understand spatial data structures, graph traversal algorithms, and the challenges involved in real-world navigation systems. By the end of the process, we were able to stabilize the routing pipeline and significantly improve the reliability of the system.

This experience reinforced an important lesson for us: building location-aware systems requires careful alignment between datasets, graph structures, and algorithm design.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Women often face safety risks while traveling, navigating unfamiliar areas, or booking accommodations. Current navigation and travel platforms optimize for speed or cost but do not prioritize safety, leaving women without reliable tools to identify safe routes, report incidents quickly, or access verified women-friendly services.

We built SafeHer, a women-focused safety platform that provides AI-powered safe route navigation, real-time safety heatmaps, verified accommodations, and instant emergency reporting. The system analyzes safety data, community reports, and location intelligence to guide users through safer routes and safer locations, while enabling quick SOS alerts and direct incident reporting.
