![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Building on-chain AI agents is still too fragmented. Teams usually have to wire together wallet auth, payments, trade execution, and monitoring across multiple tools and scripts. That makes systems brittle, hard to demo, and risky to operate.

## What People Can Use It For

- Running multiple autonomous agents that can execute tasks and interact through APIs.
- Simulating real agent economies (payments, trades, activity) for demos and testing.
- Operating live agent workflows from one dashboard instead of scattered scripts.
- Tracking agent performance, payment status, and execution history in one place.

## How It Makes Existing Work Easier and Safer

- **One control surface:** unified dashboard + API for agent lifecycle, activity, and payments.
- **Less custom glue code:** built-in auth/session and payment flows reduce integration overhead.
- **Safer testing:** mock/simulated execution lets teams validate behavior before using real funds.
- **Operational visibility:** auditable logs and status traces make debugging and incident response faster.
- **Faster iteration:** teams can spin up and orchestrate many agent behaviors quickly from terminal/automation scripts.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I ran into

One of the biggest hurdles was with **KiteAI Chain’s Facilitator**. The piecewise/streamed flow was inconsistent in our setup, so parts of the pipeline would fail or return partial outputs. I worked around this by adding strict retries, timeout guards, and a fallback path so the app could continue even when the facilitator path was unstable.

Another major blocker was the **Uniswap Trading API on Monad testnet**. Even though Monad support was indicated, routing/quote calls were unreliable and swaps wouldn’t execute end-to-end. I handled this by gating the feature behind a network capability check, adding clearer user-facing errors, and using a fallback swap path for unsupported or unstable routes instead of letting the flow silently fail.

Other issues included:
- **RPC instability/rate limits on testnet** causing intermittent failures.
- **Gas/nonce edge cases** leading to stuck or dropped transactions.
- **Token metadata mismatches** (like decimals/symbol assumptions) causing incorrect quote amounts.

I got through these by building a more defensive integration layer: better logging, network checks before execution, retries with backoff, and fallback logic per dependency. That turned hard failures into predictable, debuggable behavior.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

We use AI in two layers:

1. In-product AI features that help users complete core tasks such as summarization, extraction, classification, and content generation.
2. Developer AI agents that assist with engineering work like code changes, testing, security review, and documentation.

How they work together:

- Orchestration: A coordinator routes each request to the right model or specialist agent based on task type.
- Specialization: Different agents handle focused jobs such as coding, review, or domain analysis.
- Shared context: Agents use the same project context, policies, and task state so outputs stay consistent.
- Human control: Engineers review important outputs, approve high impact actions, and handle exceptions.
- Safety and quality: Guardrails, validation checks, and test runs are applied before changes are accepted.
- Traceability: Runs are logged with prompts, actions, and results so decisions can be audited.

In practice, this creates a hybrid workflow where AI speeds up execution and humans provide direction, approval, and final accountability.

**New France Village**

Defi Defi Defi Defi Defi Defi summer 2026

**Best Use of Quicknode Monad Streams**

**How Synoptic uses QuickNode Streams**

QuickNode Streams push block data to your app instead of you polling. You set up one stream and one webhook; QuickNode handles delivery, reorgs, and retries. You don’t run indexing infra or block-range loops. That’s the core benefit: [real-time and historical data in one pipeline](https://www.quicknode.com/streams), with predictable delivery and no manual ETL.

Synoptic uses Streams as the single intake for that pipeline. One Monad stream sends blocks to your webhook. You use a Streams filter so QuickNode does the heavy work before delivery: ERC-20 transfers with decoded recipient and amount, contract deployments, and method selector counts. Your app receives already-enriched blocks and writes them into stream_blocks, derived_transfers, and derived_contract_activity. One subscription feeds block progression in the dashboard, transfer-based analytics, and contract activity. No separate indexers or RPC loops for each of those.

That same store backs your marketplace. SKUs like orderflow imbalance, contract momentum, selector heatmap, launchpad watch, and LP range signal are all queries over those tables. So the pipeline that creates the data-derived products is Streams-first: ingest and transform at the source, then expose specific views as paid SKUs that agents (or users) can pull via x402. What’s uniquely useful is push-based ingestion, filter-at-source so you don’t do heavy decoding in-app, and one pipeline powering both live chain view and sellable data products.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

**How Synoptic uses KiteAI**

Kite is built as [the first AI payment blockchain](https://docs.gokite.ai/): infrastructure for autonomous agents to transact with identity, payment, and verification. Its [Core Concepts](https://docs.gokite.ai/get-started-why-kite/core-concepts-and-terminology) describe a three-tier identity model (user as root, agent as delegated authority, session as ephemeral), a **Kite Passport** that works like a cryptographic identity card (selective disclosure, capabilities and spending limits, binding to an owner), and an **Agent Payment Protocol** aimed at instant settlement, micropayments, and pay-per-use. Kite is [x402 compatible](https://docs.gokite.ai/) for agent-to-agent intents and verifiable message passing, with native stablecoin support so payments settle on-chain. For [agentic commerce and digital services](https://docs.gokite.ai/get-started-why-kite/key-use-cases-and-players), the idea is that merchants can verify payment and delegation proof, and the Passport gives users and agents a clear, cryptographically verifiable chain from user to agent to action.

Synoptic plugs into that stack. You authenticate with a wallet (owner signs a challenge and gets a session). That owner is the root of trust for the agent. Identity linking ties an agent to an owner and a payer address so the server knows who is allowed to pay on behalf of whom. Gated resources (oracle price, trade quote and execute, marketplace SKUs) return 402 Payment Required with a Kite-style challenge (scheme, network, payTo, asset, maxAmountRequired). The client (or an agent with Kite MCP) obtains a payment token, retries with an x-payment header, and the server calls the Kite facilitator to verify and settle. After a marketplace purchase, Synoptic records the outcome and can attest it on Kite so there is a verifiable proof of payment and delivery. So in practice: wallet auth and identity link give you a Passport-like binding (owner and payer), x402 gives you pay-per-call on oracle, trading, and data products, and attestation gives you an on-chain record that the paid action happened. One chain of identity and payment from login to settlement to proof.

**Integrate the Uniswap API in your platform**

**How Synoptic utilizes Uniswap**

Synoptic is an agent-native control plane for on-chain trading and data. We integrate the Uniswap Trading API as the execution layer for swaps and pricing.
Our agent server calls the Trading API for quote generation and transaction building. Agents (or users) request a swap via our API; we forward to the Trading API for route optimization and transaction encoding, then handle signing and broadcast via the user’s RPC. We use the API for exact-input quotes and swap construction across supported chains (including Monad where we run agents). We also use Uniswap-derived pricing for our oracle endpoint (e.g. ETH/USDT) so gated data products have a consistent price source.
We follow the documented flow: API key auth, POST to the quote endpoint, then swap build and client-side signing/broadcast. Balance checks, allowance handling, and nonce management sit in our stack; the Trading API is the single source for quotes and encoded transactions. That keeps our integration simple and lets us add new chains and routing types by staying on the official API instead of maintaining custom contract integration.
In short: the Uniswap API is the swap and pricing backend for Synoptic’s agent-driven trading and paid data products.

> "Sniff, Crawl, Demo. Good Dog. Great Demo"

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creating product demo videos today is painfully manual. Someone has to screen-record themselves clicking through every feature flow, re-record when the UI changes, hire an editor/designing studio every time you change something and repeat for every feature. DemoDog automates this entirely.

Give it a URL and a feature description (e.g., "show the checkout flow"), and it:

Autonomously explores the website using an AI agent to discover and execute the feature flow end-to-end
Captures rich metadata about every interaction - what was clicked, how important it is to the demo, whether it's noise (cookie banners, popups) vs. the core feature action
Produces a polished studio quality demo video  - with AI voiceover, Automated Zooms, with absolutely zero editor intervention, even if the page requires authentication (we take auth input from the user pre-hand whenever required)

It replays the flow with intelligent pacing (slowing down on critical steps, skipping noise) and visual click highlights so viewers can follow along

The result: demo videos that stay current with your product, generated in minutes instead of hours, with no manual recording, editing, or re-shooting when the UI changes. Just re-run with the same feature description.

We eventually envision Demodog to not merely be operational for demos, in fact, we ideally want our agent to document the entirety of an Enterprise's flow (even internally). It would ideally crawl through entirety of internal set of tools, documents, even videos, and produce a concise-sized studio quality videos. We pair it up with right security configs, and we get a video first Knowledge Sharing inside an Enterprise.

**Challenges we ran into**

- getting the visual context from the recorded mp4 after the exploration and recording stage, and making a studio quality output out of it 
- nailing the browser recording stage, by making sure exploring stage produces just enough metadata (too little metadata and the recording stage is blind — it doesn't know what matters. Too much and it hallucinates actions or over-animates irrelevant clicks)
- nailing the sync between the input and output video, granular chunking of video, setting up intermediate sync points that verify the sync
- making the recorder flow precise even though instructions from exploration flow were really vague, required a lot of intermediary prompting, required classification of a lot of metadata, edge case determination was one of the core problems while transitioning from exploration flow to recording flow.

**The problem it solves**

Modern LLMs tend to struggle with very long context windows. Once the context reaches around 200k–500k tokens, the context rot problem starts to appear, as mentioned in the Everything Claude Code repository.

Claudeyyy addresses this by keeping track of all the actions taken by Claude Code. Whenever it begins repetitive or irrelevant tool calls, it corrects the model by supplying a small, compact chunk of contextual information and nudging it back in the right direction. **Challenges we ran into**

I initially wanted to do everything on the web, but we cannot operate Claude Code directly from the web.

So, I had to run it in the terminal and then push the JSON config to the web for comparison. Other than that, testing Claude for hallucinations was a bit challenging. Sometimes it calls the same file read operation twice or even three times to read specific parts. This made it difficult to determine whether it was random exploration or a targeted read.

> Make AI Ads by chatting with whatsapp

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whatsapp API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whatsapp%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fal](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fal-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude Agent SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Agent%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We make AI videos for Burger King, ITC, Aashirvaad, PNB. Price range: ₹50K to ₹3L per video.

Shopkeepers in Gujarat pay agencies ₹1,000-1,500 for basic promo videos. Most can't afford even that. They post blurry photos on WhatsApp Status instead.

What if we gave them the same production quality at ₹130?

Share product photo and offer. Get storyboard. Once good to go, make video. All on WhatsApp.

This saves them from waiting 3-5 days for an agency, and back and fourth.

We've had this thesis for a while. Today we shipped it, thanks to Claude + Replit made that possible.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.⁠ ⁠We kept hitting a "Stream closed" error when our agent sent WhatsApp messages. It turned out to be a bug in the Claude Agent SDK’s MCP layer, not our code. When the agent called multiple tools quickly (like sending several messages in one turn), the SDK sometimes closed the stream too early. It got worse when users sent new messages while the agent was still running, so multiple runs overlapped. To make this reliable at scale, we’d add per-user locks so only one agent run per user runs at a time, and we’d reduce how many tool calls we make per turn.

2.⁠ ⁠The biggest headache was getting the agent to handle video generation without crashing. Videos take forever to make - like 1-2 minutes for the AI to generate voiceover, find clips, and stitch everything together. But the agent session times out way before that.
So what happened? Agent starts making the video, session dies, video generation keeps running somewhere in the background, but the agent never knows it finished. User gets nothing on WhatsApp even though the video actually got made.
Spent way too long debugging why videos were generating but not sending. Logs showed everything working but users saw nothing.
Fixed it by splitting things up - agent just acknowledges the request immediately and kicks off video generation as a background task. That task runs separately, does all the heavy work, and sends the video directly to WhatsApp when done. No more timeout issues.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Dependify automates the modernization and refactoring of entire GitHub codebases using AI.

### What can people use it for?
- Instantly update outdated code to modern standards (e.g., Python 2 → 3, old React → hooks, etc.)
- Refactor legacy projects for better readability, security, and maintainability
- Open pull requests with all changes, ready for review
- Save hours (or days) of manual code review and migration

### How does it make tasks easier/safer?
- No need to manually search for outdated patterns—AI scans the whole repo
- Automated, multi-agent verification ensures changes are correct and safe
- Live progress and before/after code comparison for transparency
- Reduces risk of human error in large-scale migrations

### Who is it for?
- Developers inheriting legacy codebases
- Teams wanting to modernize projects quickly
- Open source maintainers looking to keep dependencies and syntax up to date

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Debugging Modal containers** — running AI agents inside serverless containers meant we couldn't just `print()` and see output. We had to figure out logging, secrets management, and handling cold starts across 100 parallel containers
- **Self-healing verification loop** — getting the Verifier agent to actually fix broken refactors was tricky. We designed a multi-model pipeline where Haiku checks, Sonnet diagnoses, and Haiku fixes — getting them to communicate properly took multiple iterations
- **Real-time Supabase sync** — making the dashboard update live as files are processed across dozens of containers simultaneously. Handling race conditions and ordering of status updates (Reading → Writing → Verifying → Verified) was a real challenge
- **Git automation at scale** — programmatically forking repos, creating branches, staging hundreds of files, and opening PRs through the GitHub API without hitting rate limits or auth issues
- **LLM output parsing** — AI models don't always return clean JSON. We built robust parsing with fallbacks for markdown-wrapped responses, partial outputs, and malformed JSON

> While you sleep, it ships

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![SSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/SSH-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Training ML models on remote GPU machines is the reality for most AI teams and labs — but the developer experience is still broken:

- **No browser, no dashboards**  
  SSH sessions on remote clusters don't support TensorBoard or W&B without painful port forwarding. You're often flying blind.

- **Wasted GPU hours**  
  When loss plateaus or gradients explode, engineers notice late, manually tweak hyperparameters, and restart. Every idle minute burns expensive compute.

- **Context switching kills flow**  
  Jumping between terminal, browser dashboards, and code editors fragments the debugging workflow.

---

## What OpenGraphs Does

**OpenGraphs is a terminal-native ML experiment tracker with a built-in AI agent that auto-diagnoses and fixes training issues — entirely from your SSH session.**

- **Real-time TUI**  
  Metric graphs, training logs, and agent chat in one Rust-powered terminal UI (ratatui). No browser required. Fully SSH-friendly.

- **AI Agent Chat**  
  Ask the agent anything about your training run. It reads your metrics, logs, and full codebase to provide targeted answers.

- **Tool-calling with DSPy ReAct**  
  The agent doesn't guess — it investigates using tools before responding:
  - read_metrics
  - log_tail
  - search_codebase
  - read_file
  - explore_codebase
  - additional internal tools

- **Codebase exploration via DSPy RLM**  
  Uses Reasoning Language Models to deeply explore and understand your codebase structure before suggesting fixes.

- **Auto-refactor mode (--auto)**  
  Detects alerts (loss stall, threshold breach), generates a unified diff, applies it to your training script, and restarts training automatically.

- **Checkpoint & rollback**  
  Every code change is checkpointed. If a fix fails, it automatically rolls back to the last working state.

- **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)**  
  Works with Claude, OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API. No vendor lock-in.

- **Configurable alerts**  
  Set threshold and stall-detection rules via environment variables. The agent triggers automatically when conditions are met.

---

## Who Is This For

- ML engineers training on remote GPU clusters (Lambda, Jarvislabs, vast.ai)
- Teams that cannot justify W&B or Neptune subscriptions
- Terminal-first developers who want AI-assisted training debugging without leaving SSH

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Bridging Rust and Python over Unix Sockets

The TUI is written in Rust (ratatui) for performance, while the AI agent runs in Python (DSPy). We needed reliable IPC between the two, so we built a custom JSON-newline protocol over Unix domain sockets — each message is a single JSON object terminated by.

Key challenges included:

- Handling connection timeouts and daemon-not-running states
- Keeping the Rust side non-blocking so the TUI never freezes while waiting for the Python daemon
- Ensuring robust message parsing and recovery from partial failures

---

### 2. Chat Messages Disappearing Due to a Polling Race Condition

The TUI polls the daemon every 2 seconds for updated chat history. When a user sends a message, the LLM may take 10+ seconds to respond. During this window, polling overwrote the locally displayed message with stale server history that didn't yet include the user's message.

Solution:

- Added a "sending" flag that temporarily suppresses chat history polling while the agent is processing.
- This ensures the user's message appears immediately and remains visible during inference.

---

### 3. Getting DSPy ReAct to Chain Tools Reliably

The agent uses DSPy's ReAct module with 8 custom tools. Achieving logical tool chains required careful prompt design and iteration control. For example:

list_metrics → metric_tail("loss") → read_training_file → diagnose → propose fix

Challenges:

- Too few iterations resulted in shallow analysis.
- Too many iterations caused looping behavior.

Final configuration:

- 30 maximum tool iterations
- 80 maximum LLM calls

This balance produced reliable reasoning without excessive looping.

---

### 4. Safe LLM-Generated Code Patching

Allowing an LLM to modify training scripts is inherently risky, so we implemented multiple safety layers:

- Checkpoint before every edit  
  Copies the training file and serializes run state into ".og_checkpoints/".

- Strict unified diff validation  
  The diff must target exactly one file and match existing code context line-by-line.

- Atomic writes  
  Changes are written to a ".tmp" file first, then atomically replace the original.

- Auto-rollback  
  If any step fails (invalid diff, context mismatch, apply error), the checkpoint is automatically restored.

---

### 5. Rendering Rich Agent Output in a Terminal Widget

Agent responses include multi-line diagnoses and syntax-highlighted diffs. We implemented custom rendering in ratatui with:

- Green for additions ("+")
- Red for removals ("-")
- Cyan for hunk headers ("@@")
- Bold dim styling for file headers ("---" / "+++")

All content is displayed inside a scrollable list widget with proper word wrapping to maintain readability in the terminal.

This is meant for having assistance during the training runs that usually many AI engineers do on a day to day basis.

**The problem it solves**

# Admitra

## The Problem

India isn't one market - it's dozens. Each region has its own language, cultural references, festivals, and aesthetics. Yet most brands blast the same generic Hindi/English ad everywhere. A Durga Puja reference lands in Kolkata. A generic "festival sale" banner lands nowhere.

Creating truly localized content today means hiring regional agencies at 2-3 lakhs per region, waiting weeks for delivery, and repeating this for every market. Small brands simply can't do it - so they either skip regional markets entirely or run poorly localized campaigns that waste ad spend.

## What Admitra Does

Admitra uses the Claude Agent SDK to orchestrate an end-to-end AI creative agency. From a single product photo and brief, a Claude-powered agent handles the entire pipeline: brand analysis, creative strategy, native-language copywriting, and visual production across 9 Indian languages and 10+ festival themes.

The agent doesn't just translate - it culturally adapts. It knows that Onam needs gold-and-white palettes with pookalam motifs, that Hinglish works for metro youth but formal Hindi works for tier-2 cities, and that a Pongal ad needs sugarcane imagery with natural Tamil script - not English copy awkwardly converted.

The SDK's streaming input mode, tool hooks, and session management let the agent research, strategize, draft copy, propose creatives for user approval, generate images (via fal.ai), animate videos (via Kling AI), and iterate - all within a single interactive conversation. What used to take regional agencies weeks and lakhs now takes minutes from one brief.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. Unicode Shell Escaping Broke Indian Language Prompts

The agent constructs image generation prompts containing Telugu (తెలుగు), Hindi (हिन्दी), and other Indic scripts with nested quotes and em-dashes. Initially, these params were passed as a `--params` CLI argument to the action-proposer script. Shell escaping mangled the Unicode text - the agent wasted 2 turns retrying before failing.

**Fix:** Switched to piping params JSON via stdin (`echo '{...}' | npx tsx propose-action.ts`). Stdin bypasses shell interpretation entirely, so Unicode text, nested quotes, and special characters pass through cleanly on the first attempt.

## 2. Keeping the SDK Generator Alive During Multi-Turn Tool Execution

The Claude Agent SDK's streaming input mode requires an async `function*` generator to yield messages to `query()`. The problem: the generator would complete after yielding the initial user message, but the SDK needs it to stay alive while the agent executes tools across multiple turns (sometimes 5+ turns of research, questions, and proposals).

**Fix:** After yielding the user message, the generator awaits a Promise that only resolves when the AbortController's signal fires. This keeps the generator suspended but alive for the entire multi-turn conversation, and cleanly terminates when the session completes or is cancelled.

## 3. Session Pipeline State Getting Wiped Across Chat Turns

Video generation depends on finding previously generated ad images in the session pipeline. But `createSessionDirectories()` was unconditionally resetting `session.pipeline` every time the chat handler ran - even for existing sessions. This meant when the user continued a session to generate a video, the pipeline was empty and video gen failed with "No ad images found."

**Fix:** Added a guard (`if (!session.pipeline)`) so pipeline state is only initialized once per session, preserving assets across multiple chat turns.

## 4. Intercepting AskUserQuestion to Route Through WebSocket

The Claude Agent SDK's AskUserQuestion tool is designed for CLI interactions. We needed it to render as interactive question cards in the browser. The SDK doesn't natively support custom UI for this tool.

**Fix:** Used the SDK's `canUseTool` callback to intercept AskUserQuestion calls. When the agent invokes it, the callback broadcasts the questions to the frontend via WebSocket, then awaits a Promise that resolves when the user responds. The answers are injected back into `updatedInput` so the SDK sees a normal tool response. AbortSignal handling prevents dangling promises on cancellation.

## 5. Duplicate Singletons Causing Ghost State

Two SessionManager instances were being created - one in `session-manager.ts` and another in `ai-client.ts`. This caused "Session directory ready" to log twice and, worse, the sessions stored in one instance were invisible to the other, leading to intermittent "session not found" errors.

**Fix:** Enforced a single singleton owned by `session-manager.ts`, imported and re-exported by all other modules.

## 6. Cloudflare Containers vs Workers for Deployment

The backend uses the Claude Agent SDK which spawns child processes, relies on filesystem APIs, and maintains long-running WebSocket connections - none of which work in Workers V8 isolates. The Cloudflare Sandbox SDK only supports `wsConnect()` for WebSocket with no HTTP proxy method.

**Fix:** Used Cloudflare Containers (Durable Objects backed by Docker containers), which provide a full Node.js runtime. The Worker handles routing - static assets for the React SPA, and `container.fetch()` for API/WebSocket requests to the backend container.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem Raksha Solves

Digital fraud has become increasingly sophisticated, with scams now relying more on social engineering than technical exploits. Voice scams, impersonation attacks and AI-generated deception exploit human trust, urgency and fear which is making even cautious users vulnerable.

Most existing solutions focus on spam blocking or post-incident reporting, offering limited protection during the actual interaction where scams succeed. Raksha addresses this gap by focusing on **how scams behave**, not just where they originate.

---

## How Raksha Helps

Raksha provides **proactive, real-time scam detection** during live conversations. Instead of relying only on blacklists or keyword matching, it analyzes conversational patterns, linguistic signals, and behavioral cues to identify potential fraud as it unfolds.

Raksha improves user safety by:

- Detecting scam-like conversation patterns rather than just known numbers  
- Providing real-time risk assessment during calls or interactions  
- Warning users before financial loss or sensitive data exposure occurs  
- Protecting non-technical and vulnerable users from manipulation  
- Shifting fraud prevention from reactive to preventive  

---

## Why This Matters

Fraud prevention tools are typically reactive they act after scams are detected. Raksha shifts the model toward **active defense**, assisting users at the exact moment risk appears.

By addressing the human factors exploited by scams, Raksha closes the gap between traditional spam filters and modern, adaptive fraud tactics.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

Building Raksha involved several practical challenges across the Flutter, Android, and accessibility layers.

One of the early hurdles was dealing with Dart and Flutter environment inconsistencies. Version mismatches and dependency conflicts occasionally caused build failures and unexpected runtime behavior, requiring careful package management and configuration fixes.

We also encountered challenges integrating Android accessibility features. Ensuring that the app could properly interact with system-level services, handle permissions, and behave reliably across devices required multiple iterations and testing. Accessibility APIs often behaved differently depending on OS versions and device settings, which added complexity.

Another significant challenge involved Text-to-Speech (TTS). Achieving consistent voice output, managing latency, and handling interruptions during real-time interactions proved non-trivial. Differences in device TTS engines and audio focus handling created edge cases that needed additional logic and fallback handling.

Addressing these issues required repeated debugging, device-level testing, and adjustments to ensure stable behavior in real-world scenarios.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Raksha strongly aligns with this track by addressing a highly prevalent problem in India which is the rapid rise of digital fraud and scam calls. India consistently ranks among the most targeted regions for social engineering attacks, including fake banking calls, OTP scams, impersonation fraud and voice-based deception. These attacks often exploit trust, urgency and fear rather than technical vulnerabilities, making them difficult to prevent through traditional spam filters alone.

Raksha tackles this problem through a proactive, real-time defense approach. Instead of depending solely on blacklists or known scam numbers, the system analyzes conversational patterns and behavioral signals during live interactions to identify potential fraud as it unfolds. This is particularly relevant in the Indian context, where many scams originate from new or spoofed numbers and frequently bypass existing protections.

By focusing on user safety, accessibility, and prevention, Raksha represents a solution designed for real-world conditions and challenges specific to the Indian digital ecosystem.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creating short visual stories is still too expensive and
  slow for most Indian users.
  Today, a single 30–60 second story video usually needs
  multiple tools and specialists: script writer,
  illustrator, storyboard artist, editor, and motion/video
  creator. That process is hard for:

  - independent creators in tier-2/tier-3 cities,
  - teachers and NGOs making local-language explainers,
  - small businesses creating regular social content on
    tight budgets.

  Toon Flix solves this by converting one text idea into a
  complete comic-style video through coordinated AI agents:
  story planning -> script -> characters -> storyboard
  frames -> shot videos -> merged final output.

  Result: faster creation, lower cost, and far less
  technical friction for Indian storytelling use cases.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Multi-agent workflow reliability
     Coordinating 8 agents in sequence with user
     confirmation checkpoints was complex. I solved it with
     a centralized orchestrator, explicit stage mapping, and
     WebSocket event-based handoffs.
  2. Service integration mismatches (LLM/Image/Video APIs)
     Different providers return different payload formats
     and failure modes. I added a service abstraction layer,
     provider factory logic, and improved error handling
     around response parsing and retries.
  3. Video pipeline consistency
     Keeping character/story consistency across shots is
     difficult. I added image-to-image and image-to-video
     reference flows to improve visual continuity across
     scenes.
  4. Real-time UX under async workloads
     Long-running generation needed transparent progress. I
     implemented live run status events (run_progress,
     run_awaiting_confirm, run_completed) so users always
     know what stage is running.
  5. Deployment and local dev stability
     Ensuring reproducible setup during hackathon time
     pressure was critical. I containerized with Docker
     Compose (Postgres + Redis + backend + frontend) for
     fast team onboarding and consistent runs.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Toon Flix directly fits the Build for India track: it
  helps Indian creators, educators, and small businesses
  turn story ideas into short visual videos in minutes, even
  without design or editing teams.
  It is India-first in three ways:

  - Language diversity: supports prompts and workflows that
    can be adapted to Hindi + regional-language
    storytelling.
  - Cost sensitivity: automates scripting, character design,
    storyboarding, and video generation in one pipeline,
    reducing production cost and time.
  - On-ground usability: built for rapid prototyping and
    iterative feedback so teams can generate explainers,
    social content, and educational stories quickly.

  This is a working end-to-end prototype with a live UI,
  real-time agent orchestration, and exportable video
  output.

> Not just what to insure, but why and when.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people buy insurance out of fear and pressure, not from a clear view of their real risk. They’re shown price lists instead of being told whether they actually need cover right now, how much, and for what. This leads to over‑insurance when they’re safe and dangerous gaps when something goes wrong, so people lose trust in insurance altogether. InsureSense fixes this by turning personal and real‑time data into a clear risk score and simple advice on when and what to insure, before showing any plans.
Young people like us are also confused by fine print, complex terms, and biased advice from agents or ads. InsureSense cuts through this by giving simple, unbiased, data‑backed explanations so you understand your risk and feel confident before buying anything.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. One major challenge was the lack of accessible insurance APIs, so for our MVP we had to design and curate our own insurance datasets instead of relying on existing data sources.  
2. We initially tried a dual‑backend architecture (Node.js main backend plus a Python microservice for the agentic logic), but free‑tier API restrictions made it hard to call external APIs from Python and then relay results back to Node.js, so we finally merged the agentic system directly into the Node.js backend to keep things reliable.  
3. We also kept hitting API rate limits because our early design triggered many third‑party calls in a single request, which forced us to refactor our flow, cache results where possible, and reduce unnecessary calls to stay within limits.

**AI/ML**

InsureSense fits the AI/ML track because it uses conversational AI and machine‑learning based risk scoring to turn raw user inputs and live external data (travel, health alerts, accidents, climate, jobs) into a personalized insurance risk score and recommendation in real time. Our models analyse the user’s profile plus real‑time signals to decide whether they should buy now, wait, or adjust coverage, and then rank plans by how well they match that risk and budget instead of just by price.

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pymongo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pymongo-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Campus placements usually suffer from **lack of visibility**.

- Students don’t know where they stand.
- Placement cells don’t know which skills are weak.
- Recruiters cannot quickly see talent availability.
- Training programs are often planned without data.

This project builds a **Placement Intelligence System** that converts raw student data into actionable insights.

It helps answer questions like:

- How many students are ready for a company?
- Which department is lagging?
- Which skills are in shortage?
- What should the placement cell train next?
- What are the chances of a student getting shortlisted?

The system provides dashboards, analytics, predictions, and gap detection.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building the system required solving multiple real-world engineering challenges.

### 1. Data Normalization
Students entered skills in different formats and cases.
I implemented normalization and auto-registration of new skills into the master schema.

### 2. Complex Filtering Logic
Combining skills + CGPA + coding + aptitude + department together was tricky.
I redesigned backend APIs to support dynamic multi-parameter filtering.

### 3. MongoDB ObjectId Errors
Passing wrong IDs from frontend caused crashes.
Solved by validating IDs and mapping company names to IDs.

### 4. Recharts Interaction
Handling click events on bars and navigating with filters required custom routing logic.

### 5. Machine Learning Integration
Ensuring training columns match prediction columns was difficult.
I created a fixed feature builder and consistent CSV schema.

### 6. Deployment Issues
Build tools could not detect backend/frontend correctly.
Solved by restructuring project and defining proper start commands.

Each challenge improved the architecture and made the system more production-ready.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves:

Urban cities struggle with civic negligence and low citizen engagement.

Issues like overflowing garbage bins, broken streetlights, potholes, water leakages, and vandalism are common — not because solutions do not exist, but because:

- Citizens often ignore small civic problems
- People assume someone else will handle it
- There is low awareness of civic responsibility
- Reporting systems feel disconnected from daily life
- There is no engaging way to teach civic sense
- Traditional awareness campaigns are passive and often ineffective. There is a clear gap between urban infrastructure management and citizen participation.

How CivicSense Solves This
 – Civic Sense Simulator gamifies civic responsibility.
- Instead of telling people what to do, it allows them to experience the consequences of their choices in a simulated city environment.
- Through an interactive exploration-based simulation:
- Players encounter real-life civic issues
- They make decisions in real-time

Each decision affects their Civic Sense Score

They receive feedback based on their responsibility level
This approach creates:

1. Behavioral awareness
2. Decision-based learning
3. Active civic engagement
4. A deeper understanding of social responsibility

What Can People Use It For?

1.  Learn civic responsibility through interactive simulation
2.  Understand the consequences of ignoring public issue
3. Educational tool for schools and colleges
4. Government & Municipal Bodies
5. Civic awareness campaigns
6.  Public engagement tool
7.  Smart city initiative promotion
8.  Hackathons & Policy Innovation
9.  Model for participatory governance  

 It transforms civic responsibility from a passive concept into an active experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

Initially i was trying to make it like a simulation usiing godot engine , but the more i am going in depth the more i felt that i am learning a lot new tings in it and started to feel like a lot of errors are occuring which are almost going to difficult to dealt with. So , i just made it in simple version.

1. Creating a Real Game-Like Experience

One of the biggest challenges was ensuring the project did not feel like a simple quiz or form-based application. Designing a smooth, exploration-based simulation with player movement, interaction triggers, and immersive gameplay required careful planning of the game loop, rendering logic, and event handling.

2. Balancing Realism and Simplicity

We wanted the civic issues to feel realistic while keeping the system lightweight enough to build within a short deadline. Finding the balance between visual detail and performance optimization was a key challenge.

3. Interaction and Collision Detection

Implementing proximity-based interaction (triggering actions only when the player approaches an issue) required managing coordinate systems, collision boundaries, and event listeners accurately.

4. State Management

Tracking score, completed issues, and player progress across multiple scenes required structured state handling. Ensuring that decisions correctly updated the score and reflected in the final result screen was critical.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves
FresherCompass addresses the confusion and lack of structured guidance that students and freshers face while choosing and preparing for their career paths.
Many students:
- Don’t know which domain suits them (development, core, analytics, etc.)
- Prepare randomly without understanding their strengths
- Lack structured self-assessment tools
- Feel overwhelmed by too many career options
- Don’t receive personalized feedback early in their journey

Traditional career guidance is either:
- Generic
- Expensive
- Not data-driven
- Or not easily accessible
## What People Can Use It For

FresherCompass provides a structured and interactive system where users can:

- Create an account and build a profile
- Complete a guided questionnaire
- Assess their interests, comfort levels, and strengths
- Receive dashboard-based insights
- Track their growth direction
- Access intelligent assistance for career queries

It transforms vague self-doubt into structured clarity.

## How It Makes Tasks Easier

Instead of “I don’t know what to prepare for”
Users get:

- A guided self-evaluation
- Organized inputs about their abilities
- A centralized dashboard
- Directional clarity
This reduces:
 - Random preparation
 - Decision paralysis
 - Misaligned effort

**Challenges we ran into**

## Handling Strict Model Constraints in Production

One major challenge was ensuring that questionnaire responses were saved reliably without causing database errors.

During development, certain form fields (like Likert-scale responses) were assumed to always have values. However, when a user skipped a field or submitted incomplete input, the database threw NOT NULL constraint failed errors.

How we solved it:
- Reviewed model definitions and form handling logic
- Ensured required fields were enforced properly
- Added validation safeguards before saving responses
- Improved consistency between frontend form design and backend model constraints

This significantly improved stability and prevented runtime crashes.

## Deployment Environment Differences (Local vs Production)

The biggest hurdle came during deployment.
The application worked perfectly locally, but production introduced new challenges:

- Dependency issues caused by OS differences (Windows vs Linux)
- Environment variable configuration problems
- Missing database migrations on first deploy
- Static files not loading correctly

These issues resulted in 500 Internal Server Error responses initially.

How we solved it:
- Cleaned and simplified the requirements.txt
- Configured Gunicorn and WhiteNoise correctly
- Automated database migrations in the startup command
- Verified environment variables on the hosting platform

This experience helped us understand the importance of production readiness beyond just writing working code.

## Debugging Without DEBUG Mode

With DEBUG = False in production, Django hides detailed error messages.
This made identifying the root cause of failures more difficult.

How we handled it:
- Used platform logs to trace request failures
- Temporarily enabled debugging in controlled situations
- Narrowed down failing routes (e.g., dashboard rendering after questionnaire submission)
- This improved our ability to debug systematically rather than guessing.

What We Learned:
- Deployment is a separate engineering challenge from development.
- Small configuration differences can cause major runtime issues.
- Clean architecture and careful validation prevent cascading failures.
- Logging and structured debugging are critical in production systems.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/campusiq-e2fa) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/wizardwithcodehazard/CyberDevs_AMUHACKS5.0) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cyber-devs-amuhacks-5-0.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ihmN-fwnSqU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AMUHACKS%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://amuhacks-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Placement Readiness Made Predictable!

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**CampusIQ** solves the critical challenge of late-stage placement readiness discovery, where students and Training and Placement Officers (TPOs) often identify skill gaps only when the placement season has already begun.

### **The Problem It Solves**

In traditional campus environments, evaluating a student's employability is a manual, infrequent, and often subjective process. CampusIQ transforms this into a continuous, data-driven intelligence pipeline.

#### **For Students: Closing the Gap Early**

* **Instant Resume Optimization:** Instead of waiting for a manual review, students use AI-driven analysis (powered by Gemini Flash Latest) to receive immediate ATS scores and suggestions for improvement based on layout and content clarity.
* **Objective Technical Validation:** The system performs a "GitHub Deep Dive" to verify technical claims through automated repository analysis, ensuring a student's portfolio reflects their actual coding complexity and activity.
* **Holistic Readiness Tracking:** Students receive a **Placement Readiness Score (PRS)**, a proprietary 0-100 metric that balances CGPA with technical skills, GitHub activity, and resume quality, preventing high grades from masking poor technical readiness.
* **Predictive Eligibility:** The **Company Match Service** allows students to see exactly which companies they are currently eligible for and identifies specific missing skills or CGPA requirements they need to address to qualify for their target roles.

#### **For Administrators (TPOs): Strategic Campus Oversight**

* **Batch-Level Intelligence:** Using **Groq LPU inference**, admins can analyze data for hundreds of students in milliseconds to generate targeted training interventions, such as scheduling specific workshops for a batch's identified weaknesses.
* **At-Risk Identification:** The "Power BI-style" Admin Command Center visualizes campus-wide skill distribution, allowing TPOs to identify at-risk students months before placement season begins.
* **Automated Matching:** The system automates the matching of student profiles against company criteria (tier, role, branch, and skills), significantly reducing the manual effort required to filter candidates for recruitment drives.

### **How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer**

* **High-Speed Analysis:** Traditional batch analysis that could take days of manual review is completed in under a second (0.8s for 500+ students), enabling real-time decision-making.
* **Context-Aware Parsing:** By piping image bytes directly to AI Vision, the system "sees" resumes like a human recruiter, preserving layout context that traditional OCR often loses.
* **Data-Driven Objectivity:** It removes human bias from the initial screening process by using weighted algorithms (PRS) and direct API-based activity tracking (GitHub) to measure readiness.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building **CampusIQ** presented several technical and design challenges, particularly in balancing high-speed processing with the need for deep, visual intelligence. Below are the key hurdles encountered and the strategies used to overcome them:

### 1. The Speed-to-Insight Gap: Groq vs. Traditional Models

* **The Challenge**: A major goal for the **Admin Command Center** was to analyze large batches of student data (e.g., 500+ students) and generate training interventions in real-time. Standard LLMs often resulted in latency of over 10 seconds for these batch operations, which degraded the administrative user experience.
* **The Solution**: We integrated **Groq LPU (Language Processing Unit)** using the **Llama-3** model. By leveraging Groq’s high-speed inference, we reduced batch analysis time from roughly 12.5 seconds to just **0.8 seconds**. This allowed the system to generate "strategic recommendations"—such as scheduling specific workshops for certain student groups—almost instantly.

### 2. Precise Resume Extraction without OCR

* **The Challenge**: Traditional OCR libraries (like Tesseract) often struggle with complex resume layouts, frequently losing the "visual context" that human recruiters use to parse sections.
* **The Solution**: We bypassed standard OCR by piping image bytes directly into **Gemini 2.0 Flash**. This "Vision-first" approach allows the AI to "see" the resume exactly as a human would, preserving layout context and identifying key technical skills and project details with much higher accuracy.

### 3. API Rate Limits and Cost Efficiency

* **The Challenge**: Using a single high-tier model for both visual analysis and text logic was both expensive and prone to hitting rate limits during heavy usage (e.g., during a campus-wide mock placement drive).
* **The Solution**: We implemented a **hybrid AI architecture**:
* **Gemini 2.0 Flash** is dedicated solely to **Vision tasks** (Resume Parsing) where its visual understanding is unmatched.
* **Groq LPU (Llama 3.3 70B)** is used for **text-heavy logic** (GitHub profile analysis, company matching, and batch recommendations), providing a more cost-effective and faster inference for text data.



### 4. Dynamic Scoring Consistency (PRS)

* **The Challenge**: Designing a **Placement Readiness Score (PRS)** that didn't unfairly penalize students with a lower CGPA but exceptional technical skills was difficult.
* **The Solution**: We developed a proprietary weighted algorithm that balances four distinct pillars: **CGPA (30%)**, **GitHub activity (20%)**, **Resume quality (20%)**, and **Assessment scores (30%)**. This ensures that high academic performance cannot mask a lack of technical depth, and vice versa.

### 5. Frontend Complexity and UI Design

* **The Challenge**: Creating a "Power BI-style" dashboard that remained easy to navigate was a significant design hurdle.
* **The Solution**: We utilized a **Next.js** framework with a modular component architecture (e.g., `IntelligenceGrid`, `DigitalTwinSection`) to maintain a clean, modern UI while handling high-density data visualizations for both students and administrators.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Rebound: Personalized Academic Recovery Engine
Tagline: The first LMS-integrated platform that uses Generative AI and cognitive load metrics to prevent student burnout before it happens.

The Silent Crisis
Higher education faces a retention crisis rooted in mental health. 87% of students report overwhelming anxiety, leading to a 40% dropout rate for first-year students in some demographics. Existing Learning Management Systems (LMS) like Canvas or Blackboard are purely administrative, they list deadlines but ignore the human capacity to meet them. When a student falls behind, these tools offer no path forward, only a growing list of overdue tasks that accelerates paralysis.

The Solution: Dynamic Workload Adjustment
Rebound is not a planner; it is an intelligent recovery engine. We reverse-engineered the habits of successful students and codified them into a platform that adapts to user state.

By synthesizing deadline urgency, grade weightage, and self-reported stress levels, Rebound calculates a Recovery Priority Score (RPS) for every assignment. When a student enters "Crisis Mode" (high stress, high backlog), the system automatically restructures their entire workload to prioritize cognitive momentum over chronological deadlines.

Key Innovations
1. The Recovery Engine (Algorithmic Prioritization)
Our proprietary algorithm dynamically adjusts the student's dashboard based on their mental state.

High Stress State: The system suppresses low-impact tasks and surfaces "quick wins" to break paralysis.
Stabilized State: The system re-introduces long-term projects and "Deep Work" blocks.
2. Generative Task Decomposition
Large, vague assignments are the primary cause of procrastination. Rebound utilizes Google Gemini Flash 1.5 to instantly deconstruct complex syllabi (e.g., "Final Research Paper") into atomic, actionable subtasks with estimated completion times, removing the cognitive load of planning.

3. Predictive Risk Analytics for Educators
We shift student support from reactive to proactive. The Educator Dashboard aggregates behavioral data, missed micro-deadlines, spiking stress logs, and stalled progress, to flag "At-Risk" students weeks before their grades collapse. This allows institutions to intervene with support when it still matters.

4. Grade Impact Simulation
Students often suffer from "catastrophic thinking." Our Grade Simulator allows them to model future outcomes (e.g., "What is the minimum grade I need on the Final to pass?"), restoring agency and reducing anxiety through data.

Technical Implementation
Frontend: React.js with TailwindCSS for a distraction-free, accessible UI.
Backend: Node.js & Express.js architecture.
Database: MongoDB Atlas with complex aggregation pipelines for analytics.
AI Integration: Google Gemini API for context-aware task breakdown and the 24/7 "Study Buddy" tutor.
Future Roadmap
LMS Integration: OAuth flow for seamless Canvas/Blackboard assignment syncing.
Stress Detection: By checking the workload
Institutional API: Providing universities with anonymized, aggregate wellness data to inform policy.
Built by Team Couch Potato for AMUHacks 5.0

When implementing the task divider suggestions we have to choose between offloading it to AI systems or use prebuilt standard templates.

Then there comes the adaptability issue. we made the platform easy that students of any age group or background will find it easy to get help from.

### ModelFlow

> From Notebook to Production

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Deploying a machine learning model into a real-world production environment is significantly more complex than training it.
While ML education and experimentation have grown rapidly, most trained models remain confined to local notebooks due to the need for cloud infrastructure knowledge, API development, server configuration, scaling, and security management.

This gap between model training and production deployment prevents students and early-stage ML developers from building, sharing, and showcasing real AI products.

**ModelFlow** simplifies ML deployment by automating the entire process from model upload to live inference endpoint — without requiring any cloud or DevOps expertise.

Users can:

1. Upload a trained ML model
2. Instantly receive a production-ready inference API
3. Share a live demo URL for real-world usage

All infrastructure setup, routing, and scaling are handled automatically in the background.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Handling Model Compatibility and Runtime Errors**
One of the main challenges was ensuring that uploaded ML models could be reliably loaded and executed in a production environment. Different models had varying dependencies and input formats, which sometimes caused runtime failures during inference.

*How we addressed it:*
We introduced basic model validation checks and standardized the inference interface, ensuring consistent input/output handling before deployment.


**2. Exposing a Live Inference Endpoint Securely**
Making the deployed model accessible via a public URL without overcomplicating networking was challenging, especially during development and testing.

*How we addressed it:*
We used NGROK to securely expose inference services during development and carefully configured Nginx as a reverse proxy to route requests in production.


**3. Managing Scalability Without Overengineering**
Designing for scalability without introducing unnecessary complexity (such as container orchestration) was a balancing act, especially within hackathon constraints.

*How we addressed it:*
We leveraged AWS EC2 with Auto Scaling Groups and an Application Load Balancer, allowing the system to scale based on demand while keeping the architecture simple and feasible.


**4. Keeping the Platform Beginner-Friendly**
A key goal was to completely abstract cloud and DevOps complexity. However, this made error handling and user feedback more challenging.

*How we addressed it:*
We focused on clear UI feedback and automated backend workflows so users only interact with high-level actions like uploading a model and accessing a live endpoint.

> Turning regulations into real-time compliance

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

RuleMind is built to remove developers from compliance updates and make compliance instant. Instead of hardcoding rules, regulations are stored as structured data that admins can edit directly. RuleMind automatically checks every transaction against active rules. It works like a compliance brain between banking systems and transactions.

**Challenges we ran into**

This domain was new to our team, as this was our first experience building a fintech project. A significant portion of our effort was dedicated to understanding the underlying systems, assessing the reliability of our solution, and validating that it solves a real-world problem.
The next hurdle was to think how the backend will work in coordination with the bank and the payment portal.

**Open Innovation**

RuleMind fits the Open Innovation track by rethinking how regulatory compliance is designed, implemented, and maintained in financial systems.

Today, compliance enforcement relies on manual interpretation of regulatory documents and hardcoded logic embedded across multiple services. This approach is slow to adapt, difficult to audit, and prone to human error. RuleMind introduces a flexible and open architecture where regulations are modeled as structured, configurable rules stored as data rather than code.

This approach enables institutions to adapt quickly to regulatory changes without redeploying systems, encourages collaboration between compliance teams and developers, and allows the same engine to be reused across banks, fintechs, and regulatory contexts. By exposing compliance logic through APIs, dashboards, and reports, RuleMind creates an extensible platform that can integrate with diverse systems rather than being tied to a single application or workflow.

RuleMind also supports future innovation by design. Its rule-based foundation allows advanced capabilities—such as AI-assisted regulation analysis, cross-institution benchmarking, and jurisdiction-specific rule sets—to be added incrementally without altering the core system.

By transforming compliance from a closed, static, and code-dependent process into an open, configurable, and interoperable system, RuleMind demonstrates how open innovation can modernize a critical yet traditionally rigid domain.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🚨 The Problem InsureGenie Solves

Insurance is meant to protect people during critical moments — accidents, medical emergencies, or financial loss — but in reality, it often becomes a source of confusion and stress.

❌ What’s Broken Today
- Policy documents are complex and jargon-heavy, making them hard to understand for non-experts.
- Claim rejections happen due to procedural mistakes, not because users are ineligible.
- Buying insurance is guesswork, with people overpaying or under-covering due to a lack of guidance.
- Users don’t know what to do when an incident happens, what documents to submit, when, and how.

✅ How InsureGenie Makes It Better
InsureGenie is an AI-powered insurance assistant that acts as a decision copilot, not just a chatbot.

🔹 What People Use It For

1️⃣ Claim Assistance (Safer & Stress-Free)
- Upload insurance documents.
- Get a clear, step-by-step claim procedure tailored to their policy.
- Understand required documents, deadlines, and common mistakes.
- Reduce chances of claim rejection due to incomplete or incorrect filing.

2️⃣ Smarter Insurance Buying
- Tell InsureGenie about your situation (e.g., buying a car).
- Get context-aware insurance recommendations based on real needs.
- Avoid overpaying or missing critical coverage.
#Why It Matters
- Saves time during emergencies.
- Reduces financial risk caused by claim errors.
-Makes insurance accessible to non-technical and first-time buyers.
-Improves trust between users and insurance systems.

In short: InsureGenie turns insurance from a confusing obligation into a guided, user-friendly experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

⚙️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building InsureGenie wasn’t just about making things work — it was about making them work reliably, securely, and simply within hackathon constraints.

🧩 1. Handling Unstructured Insurance Documents
The challenge: 
Insurance policies come in PDFs, scanned images, and inconsistent formats. Extracting meaningful information from them without breaking user trust was difficult.

How we solved it:
- Used temporary document processing instead of permanent storage.
- Designed prompts to extract only relevant sections (claim steps, exclusions, deadlines).
- Added fallback logic to guide users even when documents were partially unreadable.

☁️ 2. Stateless Backend with AWS Lambda
The challenge:
AWS Lambda is stateless by nature, which made it tricky to maintain context across multiple user interactions.

How we solved it:
- Implemented session tokens passed between requests.
- Used lightweight metadata objects to preserve conversational context.
- Kept business logic modular so each function remained independent and scalable.

 🔐 3. Data Privacy & Security Concerns
The challenge:
Handling sensitive insurance documents raised serious privacy concerns, especially in a hackathon environment.

How we solved it:  
- Avoided storing user documents entirely.
- Ensured documents are processed only in-memory.
- Clearly communicated consent and advisory-only usage to users.

🧠 4. Avoiding Hallucinations in AI Responses
The challenge:
AI models can sometimes generate confident but incorrect advice — which is risky in insurance scenarios.

How we solved it:
- Restricted AI outputs to document-grounded responses only.
- Added disclaimers and uncertainty handling when information was missing.
- Focused on procedural guidance instead of legal interpretation.

⏱️ 5. Building Under Hackathon Time Constraints
The challenge: 
Balancing frontend UX, backend logic, and AI integration within limited time was tough.

How we solved it: 
- Prioritized two core features instead of building everything.
- Chose serverless architecture to move faster.
- Focused on clean UX and reliability over feature bloat.

> Key Learning: 
Simplicity, security, and clarity matter more than complexity, especially in real-world problem-solving.

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

Although InsureGenie uses advanced technologies, its overall design emphasizes simplicity and clarity. The system is built with a modular architecture, focusing on two core features rather than unnecessary complexity. This makes the project easy to understand, extend, and learn from, making it suitable for beginners exploring AI, cloud computing, and real-world problem-solving through technology.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

InsureGenie aligns with:
SDG 1: No Poverty 
SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities
By reducing the financial risks faced by individuals due to insurance claim rejections or poor insurance decisions. Many people lose rightful claim benefits simply because they are unaware of correct procedures or documentation requirements. By making insurance guidance accessible and easy to understand, InsureGenie helps users protect themselves from avoidable financial losses.

**Open Innovation**

The insurance ecosystem is traditionally complex, opaque, and difficult for everyday users to navigate. InsureGenie rethinks this interaction by introducing an AI-powered assistant that bridges the gap between insurance policies and real-life user situations. Instead of forcing users to understand lengthy policy documents, the project innovates by bringing clarity, personalization, and decision support directly to the user.

**Emerging Technologies**

InsureGenie is fundamentally built on emerging tech and uses it to solve a real, high-impact problem.

#Emerging Technologies is the Best Match because:

-AI-first product
InsureGenie uses Large Language Models to understand insurance documents and provide contextual guidance — a core emerging technology.

-Serverless cloud architecture
Built using AWS Lambda + API Gateway, showcasing modern, scalable backend design.

-Document intelligence
Interpreting unstructured insurance documents using AI is a cutting-edge use case.

### Pawsitivity
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pawsitivity-2ec4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> India's one-stop, for all pet needs.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Pet parenting is a full life journey, but the support system is scattered.

Today, owners bounce between Google searches, social media posts, clinic calls, Maps tabs, and chat groups to do basic things like find a trusted vet nearby, get quick guidance, ask for help, adopt responsibly, or reunite with a lost pet. Good advice gets buried, bad advice spreads, records and memories stay unorganized, and in urgent moments people lose time and confidence.

**Pawsitivity solves this by putting the whole pet lifecycle in one place.** It turns confusion into clear next steps by combining:
- a structured community for **celebrations, advice, and lost and found**
- **Care Circles** for trusted support from your people
- **Ask AI** plus messaging to get quick direction and follow-up
- **nearby vets and pet care services** so help is actionable, not just information
- **help boards and events** to coordinate real community support
- **adoption** to connect pets with families
- a **Memory Vault** and **Rainbow Bridge** space for the emotional parts most apps ignore

Result: less searching, faster help, safer decisions, and a single home for everything that matters in a pet’s life.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Scope management:** fitting a “one-stop, birth-to-end-of-life” product into an MVP without the app feeling bloated.  
- **Feature prioritization:** choosing what to build first (maps, community, AI/help, profiles, reminders, etc.) under time pressure.  
- **Supabase data design:** creating tables/relations for users, pets, posts, locations, saved services, and reports without constant schema changes.  
- **Maps integration:** location permissions, fetching nearby services, distance sorting, and keeping results accurate and fast.  
- **Data quality for locations:** incomplete/duplicate listings, verifying services, and deciding how to handle reviews/ratings.  
- **Cross-feature bugs:** one feature (maps or auth) breaking another because everything is connected.  
- **UI/UX complexity:** keeping navigation simple while covering many journeys (new pet, emergencies, senior care, end-of-life support).  
- **Deployment & keys:** managing environment variables and API keys (maps) across dev/demo builds without last-minute failures.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

Pawsitivity fits the **SDG** track because it improves wellbeing for people and animals, strengthens community support, and promotes more responsible care.

- **SDG 3: Good Health and Well Being**  
  Healthier pets support healthier people. Pawsitivity helps owners manage care across the full life cycle, from early vaccinations and nutrition to illness support and end-of-life guidance, which reduces stress and improves wellbeing.

- **SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities**  
  It connects owners to nearby vets, shelters, rescues, and services, making communities safer and more supportive. Features like lost and found and local resources help neighborhoods respond faster.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ca9cfa92f73a45bbbfa1095614ef5ada/373cfb5d-cfa1-402a-87a0-f871b6d2d03f.png)


- **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production**  
  By encouraging proper care, adoption awareness, and informed choices, it reduces harmful or impulsive decisions and supports more responsible pet ownership over time.

In short, Pawsitivity supports SDGs by making pet care more accessible, community-driven, and responsible from birth to end of life.

**Open Innovation**

**Pawsitivity** fits the Open Innovation track because it is a **one stop hub for pet owners**, supporting every stage of a *pet’s life from birth to end of life*. It combines community knowledge, local resources, and smart tools in one place, so people do not have to jump between apps, forums, and websites.

It is creative and innovative because it connects pet **parents, shelters, vets, groomers, and neighbors** into a shared system where help and information improve as more people contribute, from early care and training to emergency support and compassionate guidance later on.

> Make Invisible Plastic Visible

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Figma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Figma-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

“Imagine savoring a meal, believing it to be clean, pure, and safe—only to discover it carries invisible microplastics. These tiny invaders are not just around us—they are inside us, silently disrupting hormones, growth, and long-term health. Pregnant women and children are the most vulnerable, yet no one can see, measure, or prevent their personal exposure. Traditional lab tests and environmental monitoring are too slow and impersonal, leaving families defenseless against this hidden, pervasive threat that lurks in every bite.”

“The core issue is that microplastic exposure is invisible, cumulative, and highly individualized. Every person consumes a unique combination of microplastics daily, but there is no real-time way to track it, assess risk, or take preventive action. Without personalized monitoring and actionable insights, people continue to face silent, long-term health consequences—turning ordinary meals and products into potential hazards.”

**Challenges we ran into**

“While tackling the invisible threat of microplastics, we faced several key challenges. Detecting microplastics in everyday food and products in real time was extremely difficult, as they are microscopic and often mixed with complex materials. There was also a lack of personalized exposure data—most studies and lab tests focus on environments, not individuals. Translating scientific findings into actionable, easy-to-understand insights for everyday users required designing smart algorithms that balance accuracy with simplicity.

One of the biggest hurdles was creating a single, unified model capable of real-time learning and tracking. It needed to detect microplastics instantly, generate a daily plastic intake score, provide awareness, and suggest preventive actions—all tailored for pregnant women and babies. Combining these multiple objectives into one seamless system required blending AI, computer vision, and predictive modeling, while ensuring it remained fast, accurate, and easy to use. Balancing real-time performance with personalized insights was a complex but critical challenge to make invisible risks visible and actionable.”

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

MicroTrack AI fits the Beginner’s Track because it focuses on solving a real-world problem using simple, understandable logic and a prototype-based approach. The project demonstrates clear user flow, basic AI concepts, and practical impact without relying on complex or production-level machine learning.
