### Crewd
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/crewd-9cd0) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.crewd.fun/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/FZwvt3ZGDfM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Monetize your alpha

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RPC Solana API](https://img.shields.io/badge/RPC%20Solana%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Right now, most “alpha groups” live on Telegram, and anyone can fake a screenshot or leak the chat.
Crewd fixes that by making communities on-chain and token-gated.
If you hold the token, you’re in. If not, you’re out — no drama.

-People can use it to:
-Share alpha safely
-Run paid communities
-Keep access verifiable and trustless

It basically turns group chats into secure, on-chain memberships.

**Challenges we ran into**

Honestly, the hardest part was getting token-gated access + chat permissions to behave perfectly.
At one point, people without the required token could still peek inside a group—definitely not ideal for alpha chats.

I ended up rewriting the access flow so the backend always decides who gets in, not the frontend. Once that was done, the system finally clicked.

> Protect your IP with AI detection and response

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem Project SHIELD Solves
The Growing Crisis of Digital Content Theft
In today's digital landscape, content theft has become a $300+ billion global problem. Every day, thousands of creators, artists, photographers, writers, and businesses lose revenue and reputation due to unauthorized use of their intellectual property. Project SHIELD addresses this critical challenge head-on.

💔 Real-World Problems We Solve
1. The Manual Monitoring Nightmare
❌ Before Project SHIELD:
Creators spend 10-20 hours per week manually searching for stolen content
Using basic Google reverse image search with limited coverage
Missing violations on file-sharing sites and marketplaces
No systematic way to track where content appears
Exhausting and often ineffective manual searches
✅ With Project SHIELD:
Automated scanning across 20+ platforms in minutes
AI-powered detection finds matches humans would miss
Continuous monitoring without manual effort
Real-time alerts when violations are detected
Get your time back to focus on creating, not policing

2. The Legal Process Burden
❌ Before Project SHIELD:
Writing DMCA notices requires legal knowledge
Each takedown takes 30-60 minutes to draft properly
Finding correct recipient contacts is time-consuming
Tracking multiple takedown requests becomes overwhelming
Legal consultation can cost $200-500 per incident
✅ With Project SHIELD:
AI-generated DMCA notices in under 30 seconds
Professional legal language automatically included
Automatic recipient identification for each platform
Built-in case management and tracking system
Save thousands in legal fees annually

3. The Scale Problem
❌ Before Project SHIELD:
Content can be stolen and redistributed across hundreds of sites
Impossible to monitor every platform manually
By the time you find one violation, it's been shared dozens more times
Small creators can't afford enterprise monitoring solutions
Violations compound faster than you can respond
✅ With Project SHIELD:
Multi-platform scanning covers social media, file-sharing, and marketplaces
Detects violations across the entire web simultaneously
Scales from individual creators to enterprise portfolios
Affordable pricing for creators of all sizes
Stop the spread before it becomes unmanageable

4. The False Positive Challenge
❌ Before Project SHIELD:
Basic tools flag everything, creating noise
Spend hours reviewing irrelevant results
Miss real violations while sorting through false matches
No confidence scoring or verification system
Leads to alert fatigue and missed threats
✅ With Project SHIELD:
AI-powered similarity analysis with 95%+ accuracy
Smart confidence scoring filters false positives
Risk-level classification prioritizes critical violations
Visual and content-based verification
Focus only on genuine threats to your IP

🎨 Who Benefits From Project SHIELD?
📸 Photographers & Visual Artists
Problem: Photos stolen for commercial use without permission
Solution: Automatic detection across stock photo sites, social media, and e-commerce platforms
Result: Recover unauthorized usage fees and protect portfolio value
✍️ Writers & Content Creators
Problem: Articles plagiarized across content farms and blogs
Solution: Document fingerprinting detects copied text even with minor modifications
Result: Maintain content authenticity and SEO rankings
🎥 Video Creators & Filmmakers
Problem: Videos reuploaded to multiple platforms without credit
Solution: Frame-by-frame analysis identifies stolen video content
Result: Protect ad revenue and creator recognition
💼 Businesses & Brands
Problem: Marketing materials, logos, and product images used by competitors
Solution: Comprehensive brand asset monitoring across the web
Result: Protect brand integrity and market positioning
🎓 Academic & Research Institutions
Problem: Research papers and educational materials republished without attribution
Solution: Document analysis tracks unauthorized academic content distribution
Result: Maintain academic integrity and proper citation

🚀 How Project SHIELD Makes Life Easier
⏱️ Time Savings
Before: 20 hours/week monitoring + 2 hours per takedown
After: 5 minutes to upload + automated scanning and takedowns
Savings: 95% reduction in IP protection time
💰 Cost Savings
Before: $200-500 per legal consultation + lost revenue from theft
After: Subscription fee + automated legal tools
Savings: Thousands annually in legal and recovery costs
🛡️ Protection Coverage
Before: Limited to what you can manually find (maybe 10% of violations)
After: Comprehensive web-wide scanning

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into
🚧 Challenges We Ran Into
Looking back, we were probably way too ambitious for a hackathon! As a two-person team, we tried to build a complete AI-powered copyright protection system with multiple complex APIs, real-time updates, and a full-stack application. It was a wild ride.

🎯 The Scope Reality Check
We wanted to integrate Google Gemini Vision, Perplexity AI search, WebSockets, MongoDB, Redis, Auth0, and a full Next.js frontend. Yeah... that's a lot for a weekend hackathon. We learned real quick that "production-ready" and "hackathon timeline" don't always mix well.

🔍 Google Gemini Vision Integration
Getting the file analysis working was trickier than expected. Different file types (images, PDFs, videos) all needed different handling, and Gemini's responses weren't always consistent. We spent way too much time debugging edge cases like corrupted files and API timeouts.
What worked: We built a solid backend processor that can handle multiple file types with proper error handling. Check out our test files in the backend folder - they show everything works!
What didn't: We ran out of time to connect it to the frontend properly.

🔎 Perplexity AI Search
Creating smart search queries and filtering results to find actual copyright violations was harder than we thought. We had to figure out how to target specific platforms like Instagram and YouTube, then parse through tons of results to find real matches.
The trade-off: We focused on building a working backend instead of rushing a buggy integration. The code is there and tested, just not hooked up yet.

⚡ Real-Time WebSocket Hell (and Learning!)
This was honestly the hardest part. Moving from mock data to actual real-time WebSocket updates was a nightmare at first. Managing connections, keeping everything in sync, handling disconnections... it taught us so much but wow, it was challenging.
The frontend worked great with mock data, but getting live data flowing through WebSockets revealed all kinds of timing issues and edge cases we hadn't considered. We got the backend WebSocket server working, but ran out of time to fully integrate it with the frontend.
Silver lining: We learned a TON about async programming and real-time data handling. Painful but valuable.

🔗 The Integration Gap
Here's the honest truth: we didn't finish connecting the frontend to the backend in time.
We had to choose - rush a buggy demo or present clean, working components. We went with quality over completion. The frontend works beautifully with mock data, the backend APIs are fully functional and tested, but they're not talking to each other yet.
For judges: Everything is implemented and testable in the backend! Check out
backend/test_gemini.py
and
backend/test_perplexity.py
to see it working.

💭 What We Learned
Good stuff:
We built something really ambitious and didn't give up
Our code is clean and well-organized
Both AI APIs work great when tested individually
We got WebSockets working on the backend
What we'd change:
Start with a simpler MVP and build up
Connect frontend and backend from day one
Test with real data earlier instead of using mocks
Biggest lesson: In hackathons, a working simple thing beats an incomplete complex thing. But hey, we learned way more building this ambitious project than we would have with something easy!

🚀 The Bottom Line
Yeah, we didn't finish everything. But we're actually proud of what we built in such a short time. The foundation is solid, the code is clean, and honestly? Finishing this post-hackathon will be way easier than starting from scratch.
Sometimes the best learning comes from biting off more than you can chew. We definitely did that, and we're better developers for it.

[BHANU SINGH](https://github.com/Bylerma)

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/real-time-code-editor-a894) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://vedsync.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Code. Sync. Create."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1️⃣ Collaboration Delay

Traditional code editors don’t allow multiple developers to work on the same file at the same time, causing:

Merge conflicts

Long review cycles

Confusion between team members

A real-time editor solves this by giving instant updates like Google Docs but for code.

2️⃣ Slow Debugging & Development

Team members often wait for:

Screenshots

Screen sharing

Sending updated files

This slows down development.
A real-time editor lets everyone see live changes, speeding up debugging and helping teams fix issues together instantly.

3️⃣ Remote Team Issues

In remote setups:

Communication gaps

Version mismatches

Delay in mentoring juniors

A real-time editor ensures everyone stays in sync, no matter where they are.

4️⃣ Merge Conflicts in Git

Large teams waste time resolving:

Branch conflicts

Outdated commits

Overwritten code

Real-time sync eliminates most conflicts by keeping everyone on the same version instantly.

5️⃣ Onboarding & Teaching

Teaching or mentoring becomes difficult when:

Students can’t show changes live

Mentors need to guess errors

A real-time editor gives live visibility, making teaching, code reviews, and pair programming easier.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into
1. Real-time Sync Conflicts

One of the biggest hurdles was preventing conflicts when multiple users edited the same line at the same time. Initially, changes were overwriting each other.
Solution: I implemented a debounce system and event-based updates, ensuring each user’s keystrokes were processed in the right order without losing data.

2. DOM Rendering Lag

Rendering changes instantly in the editor caused small UI lags, especially during rapid typing.
Solution: I optimized DOM updates using React’s virtual DOM and reduced unnecessary re-renders, which significantly improved typing smoothness.

3. WebSocket Connection Drop

During development, the WebSocket connection between the client and server would unexpectedly disconnect.
Solution: I added automatic reconnection logic and heartbeat pings to keep the connection stable.

4. Handling Cursor Positions

When multiple users typed at once, keeping each user’s cursor in the correct position was tricky.
Solution: I stored user cursor metadata on each update event and recalculated cursor offsets after each incoming change.

5. Managing State Between Client & Server

Sometimes, the editor state on the server and client would go out of sync.
Solution: I introduced a versioning system for editor updates so each update was processed in the correct order.

6. CORS Issues While Connecting React Frontend & Node Backend

Local development caused CORS errors when the frontend tried to hit the Express server.
Solution: Enabled proper CORS configuration in Express and created a proxy in the React development server.

7. UI/UX Breaks Due to CSS

Some CSS components broke when the editor expanded or when multiple user avatars appeared.
Solution: I used flexbox-based layouts and improved CSS responsiveness to ensure a stable UI.

Building real-time applications with WebSockets is often error-prone:

-  Event names are strings → easy to mistype.

- Payloads are unstructured → server/client mismatch can crash apps.

- No easy way to validate data at runtime.

**TypeSocket** makes real-time development safer and faster by:

-**Providing typed events end-to-end (TypeScript).**

- **Validating data at runtime with Zod schemas.**

- **Offering a minimal, predictable API for sending/receiving events.**

Developers can now build dashboards, chats, multiplayer games, or any real-time features without worrying about invalid data or fragile event handling.


**Quick highlight / use case:**

- Instantly validate events between server & client with TypeScript + Zod.

- Build real-time apps (chat, dashboards, multiplayer features) with confidence.

- Minimal setup, predictable API — no more stringly-typed chaos.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Runtime vs TypeScript safety**: Initially, I thought TypeScript types were enough to ensure safe data, but they disappear at runtime. I integrated Zod to validate incoming event data.

**Schema ↔ Router synchronization**: Making sure that Zod schemas and TypeScript event types stay in sync was tricky. I solved it using a mapped type (z.infer) over the schema object to generate TS types automatically.

**Auto-generated client**: Figuring out how to generate client-side helper methods from the server schema required understanding JSON serialization of Zod schemas and dynamically creating TypeScript methods.

**Error handling & unknown events**: Handling unknown events and ensuring the server doesn’t crash when receiving malformed messages took careful design of validation + safe send helpers.

Each challenge taught me how to think about real-time system safety and predictable API design

**Best Use of GitHub**

This project is hosted on GitHub and demonstrates a creative use of real-time event-driven architecture with TypeScript and Zod. The repository includes:

- **Fully typed events with runtime validation**

- **Clear documentation for both server and client usage**

- **Auto-generated client code to simplify integration**

- **Modular folder structure and examples to help developers quickly understand and use the library**

By highlighting architecture, design decisions, and usage patterns, the repo showcases how developers can build safe and structured real-time apps efficiently.

**The problem it solves**

Gita Space addresses the challenge of making the Bhagavad Gita's 700+ verses accessible and relevant to modern life. The platform intelligently curates topic specific verses, provides real time references with Sanskrit text, transliteration, and translations in the sidebar during conversations, and ensures every AI response is grounded in authentic scripture, transforming the Gita from an intimidating ancient text into an interactive, daily companion for spiritual growth and practical wisdom.

2. Chat state persistence

**Best Use of GitHub**

Gita Space leverages GitHub as its core infrastructure, making it a perfect fit for the Best Use of GitHub track. The entire project is powered by GitHub in three fundamental ways: First, all verse data, including Sanskrit text, transliterations, translations, and audio files for 700+ verses across 18 chapters, is stored directly in a GitHub repository, eliminating the need for traditional databases. Second, the AI conversation feature fetches topic-curated JSON files (duty, fear, anger, stress, etc.) directly from the repository using GitHub's Contents API, ensuring every response is grounded in version-controlled, authentic scripture. Third, the daily verse email subscription system runs entirely on GitHub Actions workflows, automatically sending spiritual wisdom to subscribers every day without any external cron jobs or servers. By treating GitHub as both a content management system and automation platform, this project demonstrates how repositories can serve as complete application backends, workflows can replace traditional scheduled tasks, and version control can preserve the integrity of sacred texts while making them globally accessible through modern AI interfaces.

**The problem it solves**

Githhub - https://github.com/AyushBurde/NoteWave-AI
Youtube - https://youtube.com/shorts/-O4m9umWwAA?feature=share

NoteWave-AI is designed to solve the pain points of remote meetings in Indian workplaces. It tackles manual, error-prone, and time-consuming tasks related to meeting recordings, transcription, and notes

🔹 Real Problems Teams Face

People forget to record meetings, losing valuable discussions.

Manually taking notes is distracting and prone to errors or omissions.

Existing tools fail to understand Indian English accents or Hinglish.

AI transcription tools often mess up Indian names, making action items confusing.

Premium tools like Otter.ai are expensive and not accessible to every team.

🔹 How NoteWave-AI Solves These

Automatic Meeting Capture: Start recording instantly from the browser; no manual recording required.

Accurate Transcription: Deepgram + Groq AI understands Indian English accents, Hinglish, and Indian names.

Actionable Summaries: Automatically extracts key points, decisions, and action items with assigned owners.

Post-Meeting Convenience: Summaries, transcriptions, and decisions can be exported or shared safely with your team.

Privacy-First: All sensitive API keys and recordings stay on your server; no data leaks.

Cross-Platform Ready: Works with both Google Meet and Zoom, simplifying remote collaboration.

🔹 How It Makes Tasks Easier / Safer

Time-Saving: No more manual note-taking or post-meeting summarizing.

Error-Free: Reduces miscommunication by accurately capturing what was said.

Accessible: Free and easy to use, making AI meeting assistance available to every team.

Reliable: Ensures important discussions and action items are never lost.

🔹 Use Cases

Remote Teams: Ensure every meeting is captured, even if someone forgets to record.

Project Management: Generate actionable tasks and track decisions automatically.

HR / Administration: Maintain compliance and accurate minutes of meetings (MOMs).

Startup Teams: Small teams can leverage AI without paying for expensive transcription services.

**Challenges we ran into**

🔹 1. Real-Time Audio Capture & Transcription

Challenge: Capturing audio directly from the browser in real-time while ensuring accurate transcription was tricky.

Solution: We integrated Web Audio API for real-time recording and Deepgram API for robust speech-to-text processing. This combination allowed us to listen, process, and extract meaningful insights from meetings without lag.

🔹 2. Handling Indian Accents & Hinglish

Challenge: Most existing transcription tools struggled with Indian English accents and mixed Hindi-English speech (Hinglish). Names like “Rajesh” or “Sneha” were often misinterpreted.

Solution: We fine-tuned our pipeline using Groq AI + Llama 3 to intelligently recognize Indian English pronunciations and Hinglish phrases, resulting in accurate transcriptions and actionable summaries.

🔹 4. Chrome Extension Integration

Challenge: Building a Chrome extension that auto-captures Google Meet/Zoom meetings is complex and would take more than 5–7 hours (requires dealing with browser permissions, audio capture, and security).

Solution: For now, we built a working prototype of the extension UI and popup to demonstrate the concept. The actual extension integration is planned for future work, so judges can see the roadmap without risking time during the hackathon.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chefbuddy-84d7) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/4XYMNYF2awM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Ctrl+Alt+Vibe-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ctrlaltvibe.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Kitchen Buddy~cook like chef , even on busy days

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![copilot](https://img.shields.io/badge/copilot-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Food Wastage Due to Unknown or Misjudged Expiry Dates

Most households don’t know the real shelf life of groceries.
People guess expiry based on memory or packaging — which is often missing, rubbed off, or confusing.
This leads to:

* Throwing food away too early
* Eating food too late (health hazard)

Your system accurately predicts expiry before it becomes unsafe, reducing waste and improving safety.

2. Lack of Visibility Into What's About to Expire

People regularly forget what’s in their fridge or pantry.
They buy duplicates, ignore old items, and find spoiled food later.

Your system provides:

* Smart reminders
* Expiry countdown
* Priority ranking of food items
  So users know *exactly* what needs attention today, tomorrow, this week.

3. No Intelligent Link Between Expiry and Meal Planning

People buy groceries but don’t know what to cook with what’s expiring soon, so food still gets ignored.

Your system links:

* Expiring items → Suggested recipes
* Dietary preferences → Personalized meals
* Inventory → Auto meal generation

This ensures nothing goes to waste and users always know what to prepare.

4. Health & Safety Risks From Consuming Near-Expiry or Expired Food

Many foods look fine even when unsafe.
Consumers rely on guesswork.

Your model predicts:

* Conservative expiry estimates
* Exact safe consumption windows
* Alerts before risk begins

This improves public health awareness, especially for:

* Meat
* Dairy
* Baby foods
* Fresh produce

5. Lack of Standardization Across Shops

Not all stores label foods properly.
Some products sit on shelves for days before customers buy them.
Expiry is not always relative to purchase date.

Your system corrects this by:

* Estimating manufacture → retail → purchase timeline
* Knowing average store shelf time for categories
* Predicting safer expiry windows

This gives users accurate expiry even without a printed date.

6. Time Lost Manually Tracking Groceries

People don't track:

* Leftover quantities
* Purchased items
* Expiry dates
* What’s in their fridge

Your platform automates all of this.

Users simply input:

* Item name
* Purchase date

And the system does the rest.

---

7. No Unified System Combining Inventory + Expiry + LLM Intelligence

Currently:

* Recipe apps exist
* Grocery apps exist
* Expiry reminder apps exist

But none combine:

* Expiry prediction
* Real-time reminders
* Personalized meals
* LLM-based suggestions
* Smart grocery advice

You unite them into one ecosystem, giving a complete experience.


8. Financial Loss From Wasted Groceries

Food waste ≈ lost money.
Your system helps users:

* Cook before expiry
* Avoid repurchasing
* Reduce wastage
* Track what they’re using the most

This stretches their grocery budget effectively.

9. Sustainability & Environmental Impact

Food waste leads to:

* Methane emissions
* Resource waste
* Increased carbon footprint

Reducing household waste contributes directly to sustainability goals.

Your app positions itself as:

* Eco-friendly
* Sustainable
* Waste-reducing
  Very hackathon-friendly.

---

10. Cognitive Load & Decision Fatigue

People hate deciding:

* What to cook
* What’s fresh
* What needs to be used today
* What should be bought next

Your AI assistant reduces user stress by:

* Automatically suggesting meals
* Tracking inventory
* Predicting expiry
* Giving shopping advice

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Collecting accurate shelf-life data
   Different foods have different shelf lives depending on storage, brand, processing, and category. Finding consistent, reliable, generalizable shelf-life estimates was difficult because no single source provides them. Combining scientific data, retail patterns, and real-world averages required effort.

2. Estimating expiry without a manufacturing date
   Most users only know the day they bought the item. Predicting an expiry window without knowing when the shopkeeper received or stocked the item made the logic complex. This required approximations, assumptions about pre-shelf time, and category-based predictions.

3. Designing a safe and conservative prediction system
   The model needed to be safe by predicting expiry earlier, not later, to avoid health risks. Tuning these safety margins while still keeping predictions realistic was challenging.

4. Handling different categories of groceries
   Each category behaves differently: dairy lasts 2–7 days, vegetables depend on humidity, packaged foods last 3–6 months, and frozen items can last even longer. Creating a system flexible enough to handle all categories required detailed rule-building.

5. Integrating the expiry predictor with an LLM
   The LLM had to read inventory, understand expiring items, and generate recipes. Making the expiry prediction output clean enough for the LLM to process and designing prompts that consistently gave structured results took multiple attempts.

6. Creating a meal planner that feels personalized
   Users have different tastes, allergies, and preferences. Ensuring the model learns from these inputs and produces meal suggestions that feel natural and personalized was a challenge, especially with prompt engineering.

7. Ensuring the UI remains clean and enjoyable
   The project needed to look aesthetic, old-recipe-paper themed, and still display structured info like ingredients, expiry dates, and suggestions. Balancing aesthetics with usability required UI experimentation.

8. Building a database or local storage logic
   Storing items, dates, expiry predictions, meal histories, and user preferences was another challenge. Managing state, handling updates, and keeping everything synced with the LLM output took careful planning.

9. API rate limits and cost constraints
   Using an LLM for recipe generation, suggestions, and personalization can become expensive. Optimizing calls, caching results, and designing efficient prompts was essential to stay within limits.

10. Creating a simple input flow for users
    Most users will not manually type detailed grocery info. Designing a minimal input system (item name, purchase date) while still producing good predictions was tough. Adding optional fields without overwhelming the user required thoughtful decisions.

11. Achieving consistent results from the model
    LLMs sometimes give different outputs for the same prompt. Making the model stable, predictable, and structured required tuning and fixing prompt patterns.

12. Connecting all modules into a seamless experience
    Inventory tracking, expiry prediction, recipe generation, reminders, UI, and AI responses all had to work as one system. Integrating them smoothly was one of the biggest challenges.

13. Time constraints of a hackathon-like environment
    Building a functional prototype in limited time meant cutting unnecessary complexity while still delivering a polished, impressive product. Deciding what to prioritize was not easy.

### RaipurOne
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/raipurone-3429) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Vaibhav9526/RaipurOne) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C8od_qO4BTY&feature=youtu.be) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBIOS%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbios2k25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> One stop solution for ALL civic issues.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Cities lack a unified and efficient way for citizens to report civic issues. Existing systems are fragmented, hard to use, or limited to one platform. Because of this, people often face:

- Difficulty submitting complaints with proper context (photos, location, descriptions).
- Delays caused by misrouted or unstructured complaints.
- No transparency or updates once a complaint is submitted.
- No reliable way to check how safe a place is before traveling.
- Limited accessibility for users who prefer WhatsApp or Telegram instead of dedicated apps.

RaipurOne solves these problems by providing a single platform where citizens can submit complaints through a mobile app or through WhatsApp/Telegram bots. The system supports text, images, and live location, ensuring complete and structured reports.  
AI is used to classify and route complaints to the right department and assign priority.  
The Travel Saathi module offers time-based safety scores, weather and AQI integration, and contextual risk insights, helping users make safer travel decisions.  
All updates are sent back to users instantly, creating a smoother and more reliable civic reporting experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Media Upload Normalization
WhatsApp (via Twilio) and Telegram send media in different temporary formats.  
To handle this, I built a custom media proxy that:
- Downloads temporary media URLs  
- Normalizes formats  
- Uploads them to Supabase Storage  
- Attaches the correct metadata and paths to the complaint entry

### Twilio Rate-Limit Handling
Twilio’s WhatsApp API has strict message rate limits.  
Messages were failing silently during testing.  
To fix this, I created an `outbound_queue` system that:
- Stores failed outbound messages  
- Retries them using exponential backoff  
- Ensures delivery even under heavy load

### AI Routing Inconsistency
LLM-based routing was inconsistent depending on how a user phrased the complaint.  
I implemented a hybrid approach:
- A lightweight offline keyword classifier inside the mobile app  
- Backend AI for refinement when available  
This made department routing far more stable.

### Expo File Upload Issues
Expo returns different URI structures across platforms (Android, iOS, Web).  
Uploads to Supabase failed due to MIME type conflicts and FormData formatting.  
I resolved this by setting explicit MIME types, fixing FormData encoding, and adjusting Supabase bucket upload policies.

### Location Data Differences
Bots and mobile apps send location coordinates in different shapes (lat/lng vs. nested objects).  
I built a `normalizeLocation()` utility to convert all location formats to a single consistent schema.

> A financial advisor

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Instant Expense Tracking
Upload a bank statement → Lumen auto-categorizes all transactions and shows charts in seconds. No spreadsheets, no manual work.

2. Safer Budget Monitoring
No bank login, no credentials, no storage of PDFs. Just upload statements manually. Far safer than traditional budgeting apps.

3. Financial Health Score
A simple 100-point score based on savings rate, bill habits, budgeting discipline, and emergency fund readiness—plus clear suggestions to improve.

4. AI Financial Advisor
Ask anything about savings, budgeting, or investments. Free, 24/7, context-aware, and privacy-safe.

5. Fraud & Anomaly Detection
Flags duplicate charges, suspicious transactions, sudden spending spikes, and forgotten subscriptions.

6. Privacy-First Design
PDFs deleted in under 10 seconds, no bank credentials collected, only last 4 digits stored, no data sharing.

7. Spending Insights
Shows trends like “Dining up 40% this month” or “Subscriptions cost ₹4,200/month,” helping users cut unnecessary expenses.

8. Bill & Subscription Predictions
Reminds users about recurring bills and renewal cycles so they avoid late fees.

9. Tax-Friendly Summaries
Helps identify tax-saving opportunities and categorizes expenses for easier filing.

10. One-Click Data Control

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/2615d7e482834996aa71abe7f95d8463/d4d8b977-f22a-4859-b882-7c7557ca63e4.jpeg)
Export or delete all data anytime — full transparency and user control.

**Challenges we ran into**

Key Bug/Hurdle We Faced & How We Solved It

1. Env File Not Loading
Spaces around = in .env.local broke Node.js parsing.
Fix: Enforced strict formatting — no whitespace allowed.

2. Constant 429 (Rate Limit) Errors
Fix: Added retry logic, 3-second delay, and automatic fallback to mock AI. Rate errors disappeared.

3. Model Name 404 Errors
Fix: Switched to the correct versioned model name: gemini-1.5-flash-001.

4. JSON Mode Not Working
Fix: Moved to a model that supports native JSON mode, solving formatting failures.

5. Financial Score Bug
Early linear formula gave wrong results.
Fix: Added tier-based scoring aligned with real financial benchmarks.

Big Lessons:
Keep env files clean, use versioned models, handle rate limits early, test with real data, and always keep fallback logic.

**AI/ML Innovations**

Lumen uses Google Gemini as the core intelligence behind all financial features:
1. AI-Driven Financial Analysis
Automatically categorizes transactions into 15+ spending categories.
Detects anomalies like unusual spending or duplicates.
Predicts budgets and future spending based on history.

2. Conversational AI Advisor
Gemini-powered chatbot answers questions on budgets, savings, and investments.
Maintains recent context for smooth multi-turn conversations.
Gives privacy-safe, generic financial suggestions.

3. Smart Insights Engine
Analyzes 30-day history to highlight trends and spending spikes.
Predicts upcoming bills/subscriptions.
Generates personalized saving tips.

4. Technical AI Integration
Uses Gemini 1.5 Flash via REST API + JSON mode for structured outputs.
Handles rate limits automatically with retries and fallback mock responses.

5. AI Innovation
Privacy-first: AI only sees extracted summaries, never raw statements.
Real-time categorization during upload.
Adaptive and safe responses without revealing sensitive data.

> Financial Assistant

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![pyTesseract](https://img.shields.io/badge/pyTesseract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Managing personal and small-business finances is often time-consuming, fragmented, and reactive. Users typically rely on manual spreadsheet entries, inconsistent app ecosystems, or partial solutions that lack context and intelligence. Routine tasks like recording expenses, identifying unusual transactions, and finding past records demand significant effort and technical skill. Financial insights often remain inaccessible to users who are not data-savvy.

LUMEN solves this by automating transaction collection, enabling intelligent search, and offering anomaly detection and natural language interaction—all in a unified platform. It reduces human effort, minimizes financial oversights, and empowers users to manage their finances proactively.

**AI/ML Innovations**

LUMEN integrates multiple AI/ML components to enhance traditional financial tracking:

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) provides interactive conversational querying, enabling users to ask natural language questions like “What was my biggest spending category last month?”

Vector-based semantic search (FAISS + embeddings) allows fast retrieval of similar transactions and contextual insight.

Anomaly Detection using Isolation Forest and statistical methods helps identify unusual or potentially fraudulent activity.

LLM-based extraction (from Gmail/SMS) enables automated parsing and structuring of raw message data into actionable records.

These AI and ML components transform LUMEN from a basic tracker into an intelligent financial assistant, making it a suitable and strong entry for an AI/ML-focused track.

### EduVault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/eduvault-7732) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/akashgouda-01/EDUVAULT-FINAL) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknauts-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknauts.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your Achievements. One Secure Place

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem EduVault Solves**

Today, student achievement records are scattered, unverified, and difficult to manage.
Certificates come from email, WhatsApp, Google Drive, PDFs, photos — with no single place to track everything.

This creates several major problems:

 **1. Lost or misplaced certificates**

Students frequently lose old certificates or don’t have them ready during placements.

 **2. Manual & time-consuming verification**

Faculty must manually check each certificate for authenticity — leading to delays, errors, and frustration.

 **3. No easy way to showcase all achievements**

Students struggle to present a complete portfolio to recruiters, scholarship committees, or higher studies.

 **4. Institutions struggle during NAAC/NIRF accreditation**

Collecting department-wide activity data is extremely slow and unreliable.

 **5. Fake & tampered certificates are increasing**

Without proper validation, institutions and recruiters receive unverified or manipulated documents.

EduVault solves all of these — in one system.

**Challenges we ran into**

**CHALLENGES WE RAN INTO AND HOW WE OVERCAME IT**

1. OCR Inconsistency With Different Certificate Formats
Challenge:

Certificates came in different layouts, fonts, resolutions, and backgrounds.
OCR would sometimes extract wrong text or miss key details like event name and date.

*How We Overcame It:*

We fine-tuned preprocessing by:

i) Converting images to grayscale
ii) Increasing contrast
iii) Applying thresholding
iv) Cropping unnecessary regions

This improved text extraction accuracy significantly.
We also built a fallback manual-entry option when OCR confidence was low.

2. Handling Concurrency in Verification Tasks
Challenge:

When multiple students uploaded certificates simultaneously, the backend had difficulty managing parallel verification jobs.

*How We Overcame It:*

We used Goroutines + Worker Pools in Golang to handle tasks concurrently without blocking the system.
This allowed smooth, scalable background processing.

3. Structuring a Clean, Scalable Database Model
Challenge:

Storing diverse student activities (certificates, events, categories) in a clean schema was confusing initially.
We faced normalization issues and redundant data.

*How We Overcame It:*

We reorganized our schema using:

Relationship mapping
Activity-type classification
Optimized indexing

This made queries faster and improved analytics performance.

**The problem it solves**

RICOS_PROTO_1 addresses the chaos and delays in crisis response caused by fragmented communication and lack of coordination across organizations. People use it to report incidents, track emergencies on a live map, and collaborate directly with responders, government, and NGOs, making relief efforts coordinated, faster, and safer for everyone involved.​​

It brings every stakeholder:- public, government, volunteers onto a single dashboard, reducing information silos and confusion.​​

Real-time updates and ground-level video feeds help decision-makers act without delays, improving safety and reliability.​​

AI-powered routing delivers the right teams to the right places, while multilingual chat support ensures no language barrier stands in the way of urgent collaboration.​

**Challenges we ran into**

A major hurdle was building reliable real-time communication (WebSockets/HTTP sync) and making chat and geospatial updates instant and robust. Handling multilingual chat involved chaining third-party APIs, which often failed or returned poor translations. Resource routing delayed due to limited real-world data, so fallback logic and simulations were introduced for smarter dispatches.​​

When key bugs like duplicated messages or lost updates hit, problems were broken down into modules, tested with mock data, and refined through fast iteration and frequent feedback with contributors. Prioritizing edge-case testing kept issues manageable and project momentum steady.​​

### Inventory Management

> Solution to Problem 7 of KodeKalesh 2025

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![APIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/APIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Solution to problem statement "Large-scale supply chains operate as sprawling networks with volatile dependencies, where minor disruptions—logistical delays, demand fluctuations, or supplier inconsistencies—can propagate unpredictably. Industries often lack the ability to anticipate these perturbations due to opaque data flows and poor synchrony between nodes. This results in inventory mismatches, operational downtime, and significant financial inefficiencies. "

Key points of solution are as follows : 
Delays

Weather Delay

When fog is expected, our website will fetch the current quantity of crops and notify the user if the quantity of a crop is low. Using the weather API, it will check if fog is expected in the coming days. Based on this, the system will inform the businessman how many days earlier they should place an order so that the order arrives on time.

Our system will be automated. Using weather data and inventory data, it will calculate how long the inventory will last. With the help of the weather API, it will also check how long the delivery might take. Using this information, the system will give recommendations on when and how much to order.
It will also consider the price and recommend the crop with the lowest price first.

When an order is placed, the system will use the weather API to predict how many days delivery may take. If one route takes more time because of weather conditions, we will choose an alternate route or switch the supplier.

Supplier Delay

A contract will be made, and a security deposit will be taken from the supplier. If a supplier delivers late, the security money will be seized.

The supplier must display how much quantity they have.
The supplier must also report any unlisted or unexpected delays.

Demand–Supply Gap

From previous years’ data, the system will provide recommendations to the businessman about which products’ demand is expected to increase in the coming days. Only raw materials for those specific products will be ordered.

In short:
Our inventory, weather, and demand–supply data will tell us how much quantity to order and when to order.

Inventory Data + Demand Data = How much to order

Weather Data = When to order

**Challenges we ran into**

Lot of bugs that we handled like during integration of Hacked our local host was not providing desired output for that we fixed the Node js integration error files and reviewing that particular section of Backed.

**AgriTech & Rural Innovation**

This project is particularly made taking the example of Food Industry Inventory Management Problem with root lie in Agriculture Outputs.

### CASCADE
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cascade-9a89) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sam240107/cascade---new) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Ezqzq9DfqIc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> SIMULATED CONTIGENCY ANALYSIS

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CASCADE helps organizations make safer infrastructure decisions when one component starts failing. Instead of relying on operators to manually trace dependencies and guess which response will cause the least disruption, it simulates the consequences of possible actions before they are taken.

For example, in a data center: if a cooling unit begins failing, CASCADE can determine which server clusters are at risk, simulate rerouting or isolating the cooling load, estimate the resulting downtime and business impact, and recommend the lowest-disruption action that contains the problem.

How it makes existing work easier and safer

• Faster incident response: Automatically identifies which connected components are most likely to be affected.

• Safer decisions: Operators can test a response virtually before applying it to the real system.

• Less guesswork: Compares multiple interventions using measurable disruption and impact.

• Protects critical operations: Prioritizes hospitals, production systems, customer services, or other high-impact facilities.

• Handles imperfect data: Accounts for missing, noisy, or stale sensor readings instead of assuming perfect telemetry.

• Prevents secondary failures: Shows whether fixing one problem could overload another component.

• Verifies the fix: Stress-tests the system after an intervention to check whether the network remains stable.

In short: CASCADE turns infrastructure incident response from “detect → decide → hope” into “detect → simulate → choose → verify.”

**Challenges we ran into**

One tricky bug was that the network visualization was showing blank MW values and incorrect load labels, even though the simulation itself had the correct data.

The issue was a field-name mismatch between the simulation output and what the UI component expected. The engine used fields like observedLoad and observedCapacity, while the UI was looking for different names.

We traced the data from the simulation → case study → React component, fixed the mapping, and then tested all three case studies to make sure the network values displayed correctly.

It was a good reminder that in a data-heavy project, the simulation can be correct while the dashboard is still wrong if the data contract between layers isn't consistent

SiteSync solves the problem of fragmented and inconsistent website data by automatically synchronizing content and updates across connected platforms, reducing manual effort, errors, and delays.

> "Your Needs. Your Campus. One Loop.”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

One of the main challenges we faced was getting all the different parts of the application to work together smoothly. Since CampusLoop has listings, rentals, user accounts, AI features, image uploads, and transaction-related data, making sure the data flowed correctly between the frontend and backend took quite a bit of testing.

We also had to deal with issues where changes made in one part of the application would sometimes affect another feature. We got around this by testing each feature separately, checking the data flow step by step, and fixing issues as we found them rather than trying to build everything at once.

Another challenge was making the AI features actually useful instead of just adding AI for the sake of it. We refined the way requests were handled so that a student's description could lead to relevant listings and a practical Buy, Rent, or Swap recommendation.

Using Lovable helped us move quickly, but we still had to spend time understanding the generated code, configuring the backend and database, and testing the complete user flow. In the end, repeatedly testing the application from a student's point of view helped us turn the individual features into one working product.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

As students, we often need things like calculators, textbooks, cameras, lab equipment, electronics, or formal wear for just a few days or weeks. But buying something for temporary use can be expensive, and after we’re done with it, it often just sits unused.

At the same time, there are already so many useful things within our campus that other students own but may not be using.

CampusLoop brings these students together in one trusted campus marketplace, making it easy to:

Buy or sell items within the student community
Rent things for as long as they are actually needed
Swap items instead of spending money on new ones
Find what you need easily without having to search through different groups or ask around
Build trust through student verification, ratings, transaction history, and condition checks
Exchange items safely at designated points within the campus

CampusLoop makes it easier and more affordable for students to access what they need, while helping existing resources get reused instead of sitting unused.

In simple terms, we want students to share what they already have instead of everyone buying what they only need temporarily.

### Exohabit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/exohabit-6906) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/BlazeGreen/exohabit) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/WoBZCD9Zj8U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Which exoplanets deserve JWST time — and why.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

- The score rewarded doomed worlds. A 2,000K lava planet scored around 50 because its orbit and star were well-measured. We added a viability gate, an extreme temperature or gaseous radius scales down no matter how good the other data is, it is dropped to about 5.
- The static build was 1.4GB, over GitHub's limit due to pre-rendering all the planet pages with the data fully included. Making the planet page fetch it's own JSON at load time cut each page to about 11KB and the build to 300MB.

**The problem it solves**

There are approximately 6,300 confirmed exoplanets and only a few dozen hours of JWST (James Webb Space Telescope) atmosphere time per cycle. Picking a target means answering two questions that normally take custom code and expertise to connect: is this world promising? and can we actually inhabit it? 
Today that's a notebook, the NASA Archive, and a lot of room to get it subtly wrong or overclaim.

**Exohabit puts both on one screen for every known planet:**
    
- Observation planners/ time-allocation committees filter 6,300 planets to the set that is both high habitability potential and above the Kempton (2018) JWST threshold, in seconds instead of a whole afternoon.

- Survey teams get a transparent, reproducible first-pass ranking with the weighting in one editable file

- Educators & Communicators get an honest, explorable alternative to false "Second Earth" headlines

Team **ARC** -- Anirudh Subramaniam, Shrivatsan. Balasubramanian, Saurav Kumar, Akshara N, Nikilesh R

The world's supply chains are a web. Destroy a strand. Watch the web adapt.**PROJECT SILK** is a visually immersive, browser-based supply-chain war-gaming platform. Instead of burying logistics data in static spreadsheets or traditional dashboards, SILK represents the entire Asia-Europe Mega-Corridor as a living, breathing, capacity-constrained graph.

### FirstDoor
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/firstdoor-2915) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shourya-dev7/FirstDoor) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Ce_Gc0btBb0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Most people wait because nobody tells them which d

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FirstDoor is an AI-assisted clinical decision-support prototype that helps users perform an early health-risk assessment, identify potentially urgent situations, receive specialty guidance, undergo psychological screening, analyze laboratory and imaging information, and find suitable hospital referrals.

The main problem FirstDoor aims to solve is the confusion people face when they first experience a health issue. They may not know whether their symptoms are serious, which specialist they should consult, or where they should go for appropriate care. Information from psychological screenings, laboratory reports, and imaging can also be difficult for a non-medical person to understand.

To address this, we developed FirstDoor as an AI-assisted clinical decision-support prototype. It performs an initial risk and safety assessment, detects potentially urgent situations, provides specialty recommendations, supports psychological screening, analyzes lab and imaging information, and helps with hospital referrals.

Our goal is not to replace doctors or provide a diagnosis, but to act as a first step that helps users understand their situation and navigate toward the appropriate healthcare service more efficiently.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges

Scope discipline. The obvious build is a symptom checker that names a
condition. We cut that on day one. Naming a disease without a clinician is both
unreliable and unlicensed practice of medicine, and a confident wrong answer is
worse than no answer. Repositioning as triage and referral cost us nothing
functionally and made the product something we could actually put in front of
real users.

Ordering the safety logic. Our red-flag check has to run before anything else,
because a model failure must never be able to suppress an emergency. We
implemented it as a gate that returns before any scoring code executes, so on
that path no score exists in the object to leak. The same structure covers the
crisis pathway. We tested it against every combination rather than asserting
it — including the case where a red flag is present alongside the mildest
possible answers.

Not inventing clinical content. It would have been easy to generate nine
plausible-sounding depression questions and label them PHQ-9. We refused, left
the item text as clearly marked placeholders, and filled them in from the
official public-domain instruments once we had the source. Same discipline on
severity cutoffs.

An edge case we found ourselves. A user aged under 18 could complete a mental
health screen and receive a psychiatry referral with no adult involved. We
added a second gate: minors halt before any instrument is administered and see
support contacts instead. It fails closed on a missing or unrecognised age.

Integration under time pressure. Field-shape mismatches between frontend and
backend cost us hours in an earlier sprint. Here we froze the response schema
first, then added a normalisation layer so a malformed response degrades to a
local fallback rather than blanking the page. The crisis screen cannot render
without a helpline number under any input.

Team **Semi-colon Survivors** -- Kinjal Sarkar, Sonhita Ghose, Abhrajit Sadhu, Shibasis Chatterjee, Shourya KumarGupta

### LexBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lexbridge-94cc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ayush-SR-1/Lex-Bridge) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/1IV4c_ByG4c?si=YxfANdVrDLLKfEiu) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Legal Ease AI Assistant

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

We built LexBridge using Lovable, an AI app builder, to move fast during the hackathon. The biggest challenge we faced was connecting the backend and APIs properly — things like syncing the client dashboard and lawyer dashboard to the same case data, getting login/authentication to work correctly, and pulling accurate data from the database. Lovable made it easy to generate the UI quickly, but once we tried to hook up real backend logic — like updating case status or verifying a lawyer's profile — we ran into a lot of errors and things kept breaking.

We debugged it step by step — starting with small, isolated parts first (like just testing login), and then gradually adding the rest of the features once each piece worked. Where Lovable wasn't generating the logic correctly, we made our prompts more specific and detailed, and manually reviewed and fixed a few things ourselves. This taught us that AI tools are great for building fast, but you still need to clearly define your backend logic yourself for it to work reliably.

**The problem it solves**

Getting legal help today is confusing and stressful. People struggle to find the right lawyer because it's hard to compare their experience, expertise, and fees. Many people even give up on filing a complaint because the process feels intimidating.
Once someone does hire a lawyer, things don't get much easier — hearings, documents, and case updates are scattered across calls, messages, and paperwork, so clients are left in the dark about what's happening with their own case.
On top of that, free legal help (pro bono) and new lawyers looking to gain experience aren't properly connected — so people who need help can't easily find it, and young lawyers don't get enough opportunities to build real experience.
This isn't a small issue either — India alone has around 97,000 pending cases in the Supreme Court and over 4 crore pending in lower courts, so people often wait years without clarity.
In short: legal help is fragmented — finding a lawyer, tracking a case, and getting access to free legal support all happen in different places with no connection between them. LexBridge brings all of this into one simple, trustworthy platform.

### FAULTLINE
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/faultline-24e1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vatsalpareek/FaultLine) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://faultline-q0fl.onrender.com/overview) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_i77tkGEdvo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> MULTIVERSAL PROBLEMS. ONE SOLUTION.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building FaultLine involved several challenges beyond simply injecting faults.

1. Distinguishing Faults from Failures

A fault being injected does not mean the predicted failure occurred. We had to separate fault confirmation from mechanism confirmation and validate the expected symptoms independently.

2. Establishing Reliable Baselines

Telemetry naturally fluctuates. We needed a baseline that could distinguish normal system behaviour from experiment-induced anomalies without producing excessive false positives.

3. Connecting Predictions to Real Evidence

It was not enough to detect an anomaly. The system had to determine whether the observed signal actually supported the hypothesis being tested.

4. Measuring Blast Radius

A dependency graph shows what can be affected, but not necessarily what was affected during execution. We therefore had to compare predicted impact with observed runtime behaviour.

5. Making Experiments Reproducible

Each experiment needed a consistent sequence of baseline capture, fault injection, workload generation, telemetry collection, and system reset so that results could be compared reliably.

6. Turning Complex Telemetry into an Understandable Result

Raw telemetry can contain hundreds of signals. We had to transform those signals into a clear chain of prediction → evidence → mechanism → verdict that a user can understand quickly.

7. Balancing Automation with Explainability

Automating the entire process was only useful if users could understand why FaultLine reached a particular conclusion. This led us to expose the evidence behind every major result.

**The problem it solves**

Distributed systems are difficult to test because a single failure can propagate through multiple services. Finding the actual failure mechanism usually requires manually setting up faults, generating traffic, collecting telemetry, comparing it with a baseline, and investigating the resulting signals.

This makes reliability testing slow, repetitive, and difficult to interpret.

FaultLine simplifies this by automating the process:

Understand the system → Predict risks → Run controlled faults → Collect evidence → Validate the mechanism → Explain the result

Instead of manually asking:

“What might fail, how do I test it, and did the failure actually happen?”

FaultLine provides a structured answer from prediction to evidence-backed verdict.

How FaultLine Makes Testing Easier
Automatic system understanding — Maps services and dependencies.
Predictive testing — Identifies likely failure modes before testing.
Controlled experiments — Injects faults consistently and safely.
Automatic telemetry analysis — Detects abnormal behaviour against a baseline.
Mechanism validation — Checks whether the predicted failure actually occurred.
Root-cause investigation — Connects anomalies to the suspected cause.
Evidence-backed verdicts — Shows why a result was reproduced, partial, or not reproduced.

This turns reliability testing from a manual investigation process into a guided, repeatable workflow.

Team **GoodFellas** -- Sreeshyam P, Sreetanvi Balantrapu, Vatsal Pareek, Rabeeh B, Prateek Mathapati

> we have evacuated everyone

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

During Flood times, people face difficulty in finding a safe shelter for protection from the rain. Google Maps is not effective in this scenario as it does not contain real-time data about location of shelters. Our system calculates the most effective path (least flooded path) to the nearest shelter. The path chosen also depends on the user profile, wherein someone on foot/elderly people are given different paths as compared to people on 2 wheeler or 4 wheeler. We have also included dynamic re-routing wherein shelter capacity and sudden hazards in the calculated path lead to re-routing.

**Challenges we ran into**

since each of our teammates took on different roles, while integrating all of them together along with the frontend we faced lots of difficulties due to the discrepancies of different output form each person. This we mainly faced during the first round. We got over this problem by communicating beforehand about the respective outputs so we had a smooth last round.

### Web of Trust
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/web-of-trust-f323) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mrthundereditz-source/web-slinger-truth.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Spidey sense for what's true.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People are asked to treat online claims as True or False. Real claims are mixed: one part can be right while another is overstated.
Web of Trust takes a sentence, splits it into parts, pulls sources, and scores each part. You see what is supported, contradicted, or unclear, and which phrase is doing the damage.

Example: “Humans must drink 8 glasses of water every day.”
Hydration matters. The rigid “8 glasses for everyone” rule does not. A binary fact-check hides that. A trust score plus an evidence graph does not.
Use it to check health advice, news lines, or anything you are about to share, without a black-box True/False stamp.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Gemini key had to stay in a server `.env`, not in Lovable, or it would leak in the browser. Live search started as a stub, so we seeded the 8-glasses demo and only call Gemini when the key is present.

A guardrail treated “this can be tested scientifically” as an error and killed the demo. We flipped that to a pass and scored the load-bearing subclaim (“exactly 8 glasses”), so the result sits around 35–45 Mixed instead of a fake 90% True.

On Windows, PowerShell quoting and `npm.cmd` spawn errors broke the API wrapper; engine logs also sat in front of the JSON. We parsed from the first `{` to the last `}` and verified with `npm run analyze` first.

Lovable’s UI was generating its own random score. We replaced that with the engine’s `score` + `subclaims` so the page shows the real pipeline, not a mock.

Team **Source? Trust Me Bro** -- Harish Sm, Ram Karthik, Vaarun R, Badhrinadan B

> personal auditing taken to the next step

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

One of our biggest challenges was integrating the AI assistant with LEDGR's existing financial system. The frontend used a nested financial-profile structure, while the backend expected a different, flatter structure. This mismatch caused requests to fail before reaching the backend, while the UI only displayed a generic “service unavailable” message.

We diagnosed the issue by tracing the complete request flow using browser Network tools, backend logs, and direct API tests. We then introduced a small, versioned API contract containing only the financial information required by the assistant. Strict frontend guards and backend validation were added to ensure both sides used the same structure.

Another important challenge was preventing the AI from inventing or modifying financial calculations. We solved this by keeping Ledgr's deterministic calculation engine as the source of truth. The AI is used only to explain results and interpret user requests; it cannot directly change allocations, risk scores, portfolio values, or goal calculations.

This process taught us the importance of clear API contracts, end-to-end testing, privacy-aware data minimization, and separating AI-generated explanations from authoritative financial logic.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

LEDGR helps people understand their financial situation and make better planning decisions without manually analysing scattered information about income, expenses, debt, savings, investments, and goals.

Users can use LEDGR to:

* View their complete financial position in one place.
* Understand monthly cash flow and available investment capacity.
* Check whether goals such as buying a house, purchasing a car, or building an emergency fund are financially achievable.
* Receive risk-aware asset-allocation guidance based on their financial profile.
* Simulate how changes in income, expenses, savings, or timelines may affect future goals.
* Understand complex financial results through simple, AI-assisted explanations.
* Monitor investments and identify areas that may require attention.

LEDGR makes financial planning easier by automating calculations that would otherwise require spreadsheets or professional knowledge. It also makes the process safer by keeping deterministic financial calculations as the source of truth—the AI explains results but cannot invent figures, alter calculations, execute trades, or guarantee returns.

> Explaining Why it Works

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building CodeDNA presented hurdles across graph schema synchronization, graph visualization physics, and frontend-backend contract integration.

First, integrating live Git repositories with Slack discussions caused schema mismatches—backend Cypher queries looked for non-existent relationship types, returning empty evidence. We resolved this by auditing Neo4j directly and rewriting queries with multi-hop fallback traversals across AUTHORED and RELATED_TO edges.

Second, displaying interconnected repositories caused severe visual clutter. We implemented a custom D3 force-directed simulation, calibrating repulsive charge (-800) and link distances for a readable layout.

Finally, complex nested API models led to frontend data-mapping and React lifecycle crashes. Through systematic debugging, we stabilized component state management and enforced defensive type mapping, ensuring seamless data flow.

**The problem it solves**

Software development suffers from "context rot"—critical architectural decisions and tribal knowledge become fragmented across GitHub PRs, Slack messages, and documentation wikis, leading to slow onboarding and high-risk refactoring.

CodeDNA solves this by uniting code, documentation, and developer history into an interactive Neo4j knowledge graph. It automatically creates curated Onboarding Reading Paths highlighting key commits and Subject Matter Experts, visualizes blast radiuses through Impact Analysis to prevent breaking changes, and provides an AI Architectural Assistant that explains why components exist with traceable graph provenance.

By linking code directly to its human and historical context, CodeDNA eliminates tribal knowledge bottlenecks—making engineering teams faster, refactoring significantly safer, and codebases transparent.

Team **IGNÉLIX** -- Pravinbalaji R, Mohamed Rayhan S, SAM S, Vishal D, Sri Hari Nikesh S S
