### ChronoRx
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chronorx-e829) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TejasP208/ChronoRx) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://chronorx.netlify.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/nap4Ea2xej8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Bytecamp'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://bytecamp-26.devfolio.co)

> Your prescription was written for the clock

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

What ChronoRx solves and who uses it
Every doctor writes prescriptions with timing instructions — morning, afternoon, night — but no tool has ever told them whether that timing actually matches the patient's biology. ChronoRx fills that gap.
For doctors, it acts as a silent second opinion at the prescription desk. Before printing, the system cross-checks each drug's timing against the patient's personal enzyme activity curve and raises a flag if the window is clinically suboptimal — backed by the same trial data the doctor trained on, surfaced in under 10 seconds instead of requiring a manual literature search that never happens in a 10-minute consultation.
For patients, it removes the guesswork from "take with food" and "once daily in the morning." The patient portal shows their personal 24-hour body clock — when their liver enzymes are active, when their cortisol peaks, when their melatonin rises — so they understand not just what to take but why the timing on their prescription was chosen for their biology specifically.
For the healthcare system, it converts a passive prescription into an active clinical decision. A blood pressure drug prescribed in the morning and the same drug prescribed at night are not the same treatment — one reduces cardiac events by 67% more than the other. ChronoRx makes that distinction automatic, auditable, and available to every doctor regardless of whether they have read the chronopharmacology literature.
The tasks it makes easier:

Doctors verify timing accuracy without opening a single research paper
Patients arrive at appointments with their circadian data already prepared
Pharmacists receive prescriptions with biologically justified timing rather than convention-based defaults
Follow-up consultations become data-driven — the Contact Doctor trigger sends the physician a pre-filled clinical summary the moment the patient's rhythm shifts significantly

The tasks it makes safer:

Eliminates the 29% efficacy loss from morning statin prescriptions
Prevents the cardiac risk window that morning antihypertensives routinely miss
Catches the 20% absorption gap in morning thyroid medication before it becomes a year of subtherapeutic dosing
Flags missed-dose scenarios with biological reasoning rather than a generic "take it now" instruction that ignores where the patient is in their circadian cycle

**Challenges we ran into**

1. ChromaDB dimension mismatch
Switching from Ollama to HuggingFace embeddings mid-build caused ChromaDB to reject queries — the stored collection expected 3072 dimensions, the new model returned 384. Fixed by deleting the persisted folder and rebuilding. Added a dimension check at startup so this cannot silently break again.
2. LangExtract API rename
Hit an immediate AttributeError — the installed version had renamed ExampleData to Example and extracted= to output= with no changelog entry. Diagnosed it by running dir(lx) directly in the shell, found the correct names, fixed in under five minutes.
3. Featherless model gating
Our first model choice returned a 403 requiring HuggingFace OAuth. Rather than interrupt the build, we swapped to Mistral-7B which is ungated and immediately available. Clinical reasoning quality was identical.
4. Sunrise API returning UTC
The sunrise-sunset.org API defaults to UTC, so Mumbai's 06:50 sunrise was coming through as 01:20 — shifting the entire enzyme curve by 5.5 hours and producing wrong medication windows. Adding &formatted=0 to the URL returns ISO 8601 local time, which datetime.fromisoformat() parses correctly.
5. FastAPI blocking on first request
The embedding model was loading lazily inside the route handler, freezing the server for up to 12 seconds on the first call. Moving initialisation to module level fixed it — model loads once at startup, zero overhead per request after that.
6. Negative enzyme activity from sine wave
The body temperature formula returned values below the 36.1°C baseline at certain hour combinations, producing a negative efficacy score. Added a max(0.85, enzyme) floor — grounded in Baraldo 2008 which shows CYP450 never drops below 85% of baseline — turning a math patch into a clinically accurate constraint.

**HealthTech**

How ChronoRx fits the HealthTech Track — HT1
The HT1 problem statement asks for a solution to chronobiology-aware medication scheduling. ChronoRx does not interpret this loosely — it addresses it directly and completely.
Every feature in the product traces back to a single clinical truth: the body processes medicine differently depending on the hour, and that hour is different for every person based on their biology and location. The prescription cross-verification engine takes that truth and puts it at the exact moment a doctor writes a timing instruction. The Two-Process simulator makes the pharmacological consequence of wrong timing visible in real time. The patient portal personalises the circadian data so the doctor has biological context, not just a name and a condition. The Contact Doctor trigger closes the loop when the patient's rhythm shifts after the prescription was issued.
The track asks for tools that translate chronobiology evidence into daily clinical practice. The HYGIA trial, Baraldo 2008, Reinberg 1982, and Bolk 2010 are not background reading for ChronoRx — they are the data source the RAG pipeline runs on. Every flag the system raises, every correction it suggests, and every chatbot answer it gives is grounded in a specific published finding, not a language model's generalisation.
ChronoRx fits HT1 not because it mentions circadian rhythms — because it is built from them.

> THE SCIENCE OF TIMING, THE FUTURE OF MEDICINE

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MERN stack](https://img.shields.io/badge/MERN%20stack-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Medication errors and harmful drug interactions are a major challenge in healthcare, especially for patients who take multiple medicines. Most people do not have easy access to tools that clearly explain whether their medications are safe to take together or when they should be taken for maximum effectiveness. Existing drug databases are often complex, technical, and designed primarily for healthcare professionals, making them difficult for everyday users to understand.

MediClock solves this problem by providing an AI-powered medication safety assistant that helps users check drug interactions, understand potential risks, and receive simplified explanations of complex medical information. It also considers chronobiology (the body’s natural biological rhythms) to suggest optimal times for taking medicines so treatments can be more effective.

By combining drug interaction analysis, risk scoring, and clear patient-friendly explanations into an easy-to-use PWA app, MediClock helps reduce medication errors, prevent harmful drug combinations, and support safer, smarter medication management for patients.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced while building MediClock was integrating reliable drug interaction data and converting it into patient-friendly insights. Most available datasets provide highly technical medical descriptions that are difficult for normal users to understand. This created a hurdle because our goal was to make the system accessible for everyday users, not just healthcare professionals.

**HealthTech**

MediClock fits into healthcare as a digital medication safety assistant that helps patients and healthcare providers manage medicines more safely and effectively. It analyzes drug interactions between multiple medications to prevent harmful combinations, provides patient-friendly explanations of potential risks, and recommends optimal medicine timing based on chronobiology so drugs work better with the body’s natural biological rhythms. By combining AI-driven analysis with easy accessibility through a PWA app, MediClock helps reduce medication errors, adverse drug reactions, and missed doses, ultimately improving patient safety and treatment effectiveness in everyday healthcare management.

> Synchronizing medicine with your biological clock.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many medications are prescribed with standardized schedules (e.g., once or twice daily) without considering a patient’s individual biological rhythms, lifestyle, or health conditions. However, human physiology follows circadian cycles — hormone levels, blood pressure, metabolism, and enzyme activity all fluctuate throughout the day. This can make medications less effective or increase the risk of side effects if taken at suboptimal times.

ChronoMed AI solves this problem by:

Predicting the most optimal medication timing for each patient based on their lifestyle, sleep patterns, and medical health data.

Ensuring doctor oversight, so all recommended schedules are approved and customized to the patient’s needs.

Helping patients adhere to personalized schedules with reminders and alerts, improving treatment effectiveness and reducing adverse effects.

In short, it bridges the gap between medical knowledge, patient lifestyle, and real-time medication adherence, enabling smarter, safer, and more personalized healthcare.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced While Building ChronoMed
1. Integrating Multiple Biomedical Datasets
One major challenge was combining different healthcare datasets such as drug information, disease data, sleep patterns, and physiological indicators.
Each dataset had different formats, features, and structures, so we had to clean, normalize, and map them together to create a unified knowledge base.
2. Modeling Circadian-Based Medication Timing
Another challenge was designing a system that could predict medication timing based on circadian rhythms.
Since most existing datasets do not directly provide medication timing recommendations, we had to derive relationships between physiological patterns and drug effectiveness using our knowledge base.
3. Training the Machine Learning Model
Building the Random Forest Regression model required selecting the right features from the datasets and ensuring the model could generate meaningful medication timing predictions rather than random outputs.

**HealthTech**

ChronoMed AI fits into this track by leveraging AI and data-driven healthcare solutions to improve patient outcomes.
Our system combines machine learning, biomedical datasets, and circadian biology to create personalized medication schedules. By aligning medication timing with a patient’s biological rhythms, we move beyond traditional one-size-fits-all prescriptions toward personalized and preventive healthcare.
Additionally, our platform integrates AI predictions with doctor supervision, ensuring that technology enhances medical decision-making while maintaining patient safety.
This approach demonstrates how AI-powered digital health systems can make treatments smarter, more personalized, and more effective.

### PolyGlot
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/polygot-d8eb) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ShreyashSingh857/SIES-ByteCamp) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://sies-byte-camp.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/GQ2MzCyLBSA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Bytecamp'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://bytecamp-26.devfolio.co)

> Visualize & predict impact of code changes

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Neo4j](https://img.shields.io/badge/Neo4j-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Polyglot solves the critical lack of visibility into cross-language and cross-service dependencies in modern software architectures. Because traditional static analysis tools are siloed by language, engineers often spend hours manually tracing the ripple effects of code changes, yet still risk pushing blind merges where a backend or database update silently breaks a downstream frontend component. Furthermore, architectural documentation quickly becomes stale and unreliable. Polyglot addresses these hidden dependencies by scanning your entire repository to build a unified, AI-powered knowledge graph. This allows teams to instantly visualize their complete architecture and accurately trace the exact "blast radius" or impact of any code change across all services, APIs, and databases before they commit.

**Challenges we ran into**

The main challenges were mostly integration and sequencing issues across auth, routing, and data ownership: once scan APIs were protected, a few frontend calls still used direct fetch without bearer headers, which caused unexpected 401s even though login worked; at the same time, route mounting order let the generic protected scan router intercept unrelated endpoints like events/SSE, so valid connections failed until route precedence was corrected. On the OAuth side, we hit two classic pitfalls in sequence: strict SameSite state-cookie behavior blocking callback state validation, and Neo4j MERGE clause ordering (ON CREATE SET placement) causing Aura syntax errors during user upsert. After those were fixed, we still had stability friction from small runtime bugs (like a scoped header variable not defined in one path), plus hardening work to enforce per-user ownership for scan-bound resources so authenticated users could not access each other’s scan metrics/impact data. Overall, the difficult part was less “single big bug” and more aligning many moving parts (cookie policy, route order, auth headers, database query syntax, and authorization boundaries) so the full flow remained secure and functional end-to-end.

**GenAI**

This project is a Gen AI-powered code intelligence platform — think of it as a "second brain" for developers that understands an entire codebase structurally and then lets an LLM reason over it.
1. The knowledge graph is the foundation
Before any AI runs, the AI Engine performs classic static analysis — it scans repo files, parses ASTs, extracts imports, function calls, API routes, DB schemas — and loads all of it into Neo4j as a richly connected graph. Nodes are files, functions, services, endpoints. Edges are IMPORTS, CALLS, EXPOSES_API, USES_TABLE, etc. This graph is the grounding data that stops the LLM from hallucinating — it reasons over real, verified relationships.
2. LLM reasoning runs in two modes
Batch (graph intelligence): After a scan, the entire compressed graph is sent to Qwen3 with a prompt asking it to infer hidden dependencies, API contracts, database lineage, impact predictions, and an architecture summary — things the static analysis alone can't deduce. The LLM functions as an inference engine on top of structured graph data.
Real-time (on-demand analysis): When a developer selects a symbol in the UI, the backend pulls that symbol's graph context from Neo4j and fires multiple LLM calls — analyzeDependenciesWithLLM, inferImplicitDependencies, generatePerFileDependencyInsights, and generateDetailedImpactRefactorPlan. The model returns risk levels, per-file explanations, rename candidates, and exact line-level edit suggestions.
3. The Gen AI design pattern being used
This is a classic RAG-adjacent pattern, but instead of a vector store, the retrieval is graph traversal. The Neo4j queries pull precise, structured context (up to 500 nodes, 1000 edges per call) which is then serialized into the LLM's prompt. The model never sees raw code files — it sees a curated, pre-filtered graph payload, which keeps costs low and reasoning focused.
The model in use (Qwen3-0.6B via Featherless AI, a lightweight open-model hosting service) is quite small, which explains why the system prompt demands strict JSON output — larger models can tolerate looser prompting, but tiny models need heavy schema enforcement plus the fallback parsing logic you see in extractFirstJsonObject.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

For citizens:

Ever tried to get a company to delete your data? You send an email and hear nothing back. DPDP Guard gives citizens a formal, trackable way to exercise their legal rights — no account needed, just submit and track with a token.
For companies:

DPOs today manage data requests manually — spreadsheets, email threads, zero audit trail. DPDP Guard replaces that chaos with a structured dashboard, automatic SLA countdowns, and one-click status updates. When the Data Protection Board asks for proof of compliance, the report is already generated.
Specifically it enables:


Citizens to submit Access / Correction / Erasure requests in under 2 minutes
Real-time tracking of request status without any login
Admins to manage the full request lifecycle with AI-powered recommendations from Claude
Automatic 30-day SLA enforcement with color-coded urgency alerts
Public compliance reports that can be shared directly with regulators
Complete audit trail of every action taken on every request

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-time status sync across citizen and admin

The hardest technical challenge was making the citizen's tracking page update live when the admin changed the request status — without the citizen refreshing the page.


We solved this using Supabase Realtime's Postgres subscription, filtering by the unique request token so each citizen only receives updates for their own request

**Digital Privacy and Data Protection**

DPDP Guard is built ground-up for India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023. Every feature maps directly to a legal requirement — citizens have the right to access, correct, and erase their personal data, and companies have 30 days to respond or face penalties up to ₹250 crore.

Today most Indian companies have no system to handle these requests. Citizens send emails that get ignored. DPOs manage requests in Excel sheets. There's no audit trail, no SLA tracking, no proof of compliance.

DPDP Guard solves this end-to-end — a citizen submits a request in under 2 minutes without creating an account, gets a tracking token, and watches their request resolve in real time. The admin side gives DPOs a structured workflow with AI-powered guidance, SLA countdowns, and a public compliance report ready for the Data Protection Board at any time.

### Aegis-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegisai-72de) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/08bbfabff2014ba0a6d440e870483a4b) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Bytecamp'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://bytecamp-26.devfolio.co)

> - Enable AI Innovation dissension Data security

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Organizations today struggle to manage the growing use of generative AI tools like ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and Google Gemini within their internal networks.

Employees often use these tools to improve productivity in tasks such as coding, debugging, research, and documentation. However, this unsanctioned usage—commonly known as Shadow AI—can lead to accidental exposure of:

Proprietary source code

Internal documents

API keys and credentials

Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

Traditional security systems like firewalls and network proxies can block access to AI platforms, but they cannot understand the context of AI prompts. As a result, organizations face a difficult choice:

Block AI tools and reduce productivity, or

Allow AI tools and risk sensitive data leakage

**How Our Solution Helps**

Our platform introduces a smart proxy and browser extension architecture that allows organizations to safely enable AI tools instead of banning them.

People can use this system to:

Safely access AI tools without exposing sensitive information

Automatically detect and mask confidential data before it reaches external AI models

Monitor and govern AI usage within organizations

Ensure compliance with data protection and security policies

The system makes existing workflows safer and smarter by allowing employees to use AI for tasks like coding, writing, and analysis while protecting sensitive enterprise data.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. Detecting Sensitive Data in Real Time

One of the biggest challenges was detecting sensitive information (PII, API keys, passwords, etc.) in user prompts before they were sent to AI tools. Prompts can be written in many formats, making pattern detection difficult.

Solution:
We implemented a hybrid detection approach using regex-based pattern matching combined with contextual analysis. This allowed the system to reliably identify common sensitive data patterns and replace them with masked tokens before submission.

2. Intercepting Prompts from AI Platforms

Another challenge was capturing user prompts from AI platforms like ChatGPT before they were submitted. Since these platforms frequently update their UI and DOM structure, the extension sometimes failed to locate the correct input fields.

Solution:
We built a flexible DOM detection mechanism in our Chrome extension that dynamically identifies prompt input areas and intercepts submissions in real time.

3. Ensuring Masked Data Is Actually Sent

During testing, we discovered a bug where the original prompt was sometimes submitted instead of the masked version, which defeated the purpose of the security layer.

Solution:
We added a verification step in the extension that confirms the masked prompt successfully replaces the original text before submission.

4. Designing a Smart Proxy Workflow

Traditional enterprise proxies completely block AI platforms, which goes against our goal of enabling productivity while maintaining security.

Solution:
We developed a context-aware proxy layer that asks users to explain their intent before granting access. This allows controlled AI usage while still enforcing security policies.

5. Balancing Security and User Experience

If the system was too strict, it would interrupt users too frequently. If it was too lenient, sensitive data might slip through.

Solution:
We introduced a risk scoring system that evaluates prompts and only triggers warnings or masking when necessary, ensuring security without disrupting workflow.

**Digital Privacy and Data Protection**

How Our Project Fits into Digital Security and Data Privacy

Our project addresses a growing challenge in modern organizations: protecting sensitive data while enabling the use of generative AI tools like ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and Google Gemini.

1. Preventing Sensitive Data Exposure

The system detects and masks sensitive information such as PII, credentials, API keys, and proprietary code before it is sent to external AI platforms. This ensures that confidential organizational data never leaves the secure environment.

2. Enabling Secure AI Adoption

Instead of blocking AI tools completely, our solution enables controlled and secure access through a smart proxy and browser extension. This helps organizations adopt AI technologies without compromising security policies.

3. Strengthening Data Privacy Protection

By automatically identifying and masking personal or confidential information, the system helps organizations comply with data privacy standards and regulations.

4. Context-Aware Security Monitoring

Traditional firewalls cannot understand the context of AI prompts. Our platform adds context-aware monitoring, analyzing prompts and user intent to prevent misuse or accidental data leaks.

5. Supporting Enterprise Governance

The platform logs interactions and risk scores, providing organizations with audit trails and monitoring capabilities to maintain transparency and accountability in AI usage.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neocred-e409) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ViratSonawane/NeoCred) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/guLLiTz_Zxw?si=G_zaeRZ4tmDPwOxO) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Bytecamp'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://bytecamp-26.devfolio.co)

> Adaptive AML

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Neo4j](https://img.shields.io/badge/Neo4j-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern financial crime has evolved beyond simple suspicious transactions. Instead of transferring illegal funds through a single abnormal transaction, criminals now use complex networks of legally registered shell companies across multiple jurisdictions. In these systems, each individual transaction may appear legitimate when viewed separately, making traditional detection methods ineffective.

For example, money may move from one company to another as consulting fees, then appear as loan repayments or service payments between other companies. While each transfer looks normal on its own, analyzing the entire network may reveal suspicious patterns such as circular fund flows, hidden ownership links, or multiple entities controlled by the same beneficiary.

Traditional Anti-Money Laundering (AML) systems mainly analyze transactions individually, which makes it difficult to detect coordinated laundering activities embedded within complex corporate networks. Detecting such activities requires analyzing relationships between entities, ownership structures, and the overall flow of funds across the network.

This problem focuses on building intelligent systems that analyze financial transactions at the network level by combining transaction data with corporate registry and ownership information. The goal is to construct entity relationship graphs, identify structurally suspicious money flows, and provide investigators with clear insights into potential laundering networks and compliance risks.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Neo-Cred, one of the biggest challenges we faced was working with the graph database Neo4j. The free tier of Neo4j allows only around 200,000 nodes, but our dataset contained over 31 million transaction rows, making it impossible to directly load the full dataset into the graph database. Because of this limitation, we had to design strategies to reduce and restructure the data while still preserving the relationships required for detecting suspicious financial patterns.

To process and reduce the dataset, we initially used Google Colab. However, the large dataset quickly exceeded the free RAM limits, which forced us to rethink how the data should be processed. We eventually developed a custom script that compressed and filtered the data, preserving critical relationship information while significantly reducing its size so it could fit within Neo4j's node limitations.

Another major challenge occurred during the integration of the machine learning system with the existing AI pipeline. The APIs and output formats of different components were not compatible, which caused several integration issues. We also faced errors while loading trained models using Joblib, and aligning the outputs from the ML model with the expected API response format required additional adjustments.

Beyond the technical implementation, one of the most time-consuming tasks was mapping and parsing the processed data into a form understandable for users and investigators. Instead of simply flagging suspicious sender accounts, we wanted the system to provide clear AI-driven explanations of suspicious transaction patterns. Designing this explanation layer required significant effort in interpreting graph relationships and converting them into meaningful insights that users could easily understand.

Overall, the most difficult parts of the project were data reduction, system integration, and building interpretable AI explanations, rather than the core model itself.

> RailBrainX

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bootstrap​](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bootstrap​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Railway systems manage thousands of trains daily, and a delay in one train can rapidly lead to a chain reaction of delays throughout the whole network. Traditional train traffic management systems depend largely on manual oversight and set schedules, making it challenging to swiftly address real-time issues like delays, congestion, or track conflicts.
Rail BrainX addresses this issue with an intelligent system for monitoring and redirecting train traffic. It constantly examines train movement data to detect instances where redirecting a delayed train might decrease congestion and total delay time. In such cases, the system issues an automatic alert that proposes an optimized rerouting choice, enabling operators to make quicker and more knowledgeable decisions.
This enhances railway traffic management by making it:  
Faster  with real-time identification of delays and potential alternative routes  
Safer  by lowering the risk of human mistakes in manual scheduling  
More efficient  by reducing the spread of delays throughout the network  
Smarter  through the use of intelligent algorithms to suggest improved routing choices

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing RailBrainX  an AI-based train traffic control system, we encountered multiple technical difficulties.

One of the main challenges was creating a system capable of mimicking real-time railway traffic and managing several trains on the same network dynamically. Effectively managing train priorities (Passenger > Express > Freight) and avoiding track conflicts demanded meticulous scheduling and conflict resolution strategies.

Another significant challenge involved putting the rerouting mechanism into place. The system had to evaluate if an alternate route could minimize delays without creating congestion on other tracks. Creating this logic involved several rounds of route assessment and delay computation to guarantee precise recommendations.

We also encountered difficulties in aligning the visual railway map with the backend system. Making sure that train movements, delays, and rerouting updates were accurately shown in the simulation interface involved debugging the event handling and state update processes.

By consistently testing, troubleshooting, and refining algorithms, we developed a system capable of tracking train traffic, identifying delays, and offering real-time suggestions for optimized route adjustments.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Our project RailBrainX – AI Based Train Traffic Control System fits perfectly into the Electrothon 8.0 Winners Track because it solves a real-world transportation problem using intelligent algorithms and automation.

The system prioritizes trains based on operational importance (Passenger >Express > Freight) and automatically analyzes whether rerouting can reduce delay time. If a better route is available, the system alerts the operator and estimates the delay reduction.

By combining data-driven monitoring, intelligent scheduling, and real-time rerouting, RailBrainX improves railway efficiency, minimizes delays, and enhances passenger experience. This innovative approach demonstrates how AI can transform traditional railway traffic control systems, making it highly aligned with the goals of Electrothon 8.0 to promote impactful and technology-driven solutions.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern cities are experiencing the **Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect**, where dense urban areas become significantly hotter than surrounding rural regions. This happens due to concrete infrastructure, asphalt roads, dense buildings, and limited vegetation.

**Urban heat islands can increase city temperatures by 5–8°C, leading to several serious consequences** including:

-increased energy consumption due to air conditioning
-higher carbon emissions
-heat-related health risks for pedestrians
-reduced urban livability

*While cities are aware of rising temperatures, urban planners often lack tools that show exactly where cooling interventions should be implemented and what impact those interventions would have.*

Existing approaches mostly rely on static satellite heat maps or generic climate reports, which do not provide street-level insights or simulation capabilities for evaluating cooling strategies.

**As a result, cities frequently invest in cooling infrastructure such as tree planting or reflective roofs without clear data on where these interventions will be most effective.**

**HeatGrid addresses this gap by providing a data-driven urban heat analysis platform that identifies heat hotspots, analyzes urban micro-climate conditions, and helps planners simulate the impact of cooling interventions before implementation.**

*HEAT MAP VISUALIZATION(HOTSPOTS)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/86b60522c88f44eb830dac4e568a1c7a/d1f9e60b-a08c-4596-ae0e-4833520f6819.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building HeatGrid required integrating geospatial data, climate indicators, and AI reasoning into a single analysis pipeline.

One major challenge was working with incomplete building geometry data from OpenStreetMap. Many buildings lacked height information, so we estimated building heights using the number of levels to approximate urban canyon geometry and compute metrics like Sky View Factor.

Another challenge was combining satellite-derived datasets such as Land Surface Temperature and NDVI with street-level building data. These datasets have different spatial resolutions, so we had to normalize and map them properly to evaluate heat exposure at the building level.

Integrating Gemini 3 Flash also required careful prompt design. Raw environmental metrics initially produced inconsistent outputs, so we structured prompts to generate meaningful cooling recommendations with reasoning and impact estimates.

Finally, rendering thousands of buildings with heat attributes on the map required optimization. Using MapLibre’s vector rendering, we were able to visualize large geospatial datasets smoothly without affecting performance.

During development, we also used Requestly to test and debug our /api/analyze-city endpoint and validate API responses quickly.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

HeatGrid addresses the growing **Urban Heat Island problem**, where cities become significantly hotter than surrounding areas due to dense infrastructure, concrete surfaces, and lack of vegetation.

Our project provides an **AI-powered urban climate analysis platform** that helps cities detect heat hotspots and design effective cooling strategies before implementing costly infrastructure.

**HeatGrid combines geospatial data, environmental indicators, and AI reasoning to analyze urban micro-climate conditions.** The system integrates:

-Land Surface Temperature from satellite datasets
-Vegetation density using NDVI
-Urban geometry through Sky View Factor
-Solar shadow modeling based on geographic location and time

Using these inputs, the platform identifies heat-vulnerable zones at the street and building level and visualizes them through an **interactive 3D map.**

The system then generates **AI-powered cooling recommendations** such as tree canopy expansion, reflective roofs, green corridors, and misting infrastructure. These interventions can be simulated in real time to estimate:

-temperature reduction
-energy savings
-CO₂ emission reduction

**With rising global temperatures and increasing urbanization, solutions like HeatGrid can help cities design cooler, more resilient, and sustainable urban environments.**

**Requestly Track**

During the development of HeatGrid, we used Requestly to test and debug our backend API responsible for **city-level heat analysis.**

Our system includes an endpoint:

**POST /api/analyze-city**

This endpoint triggers the entire urban heat analysis pipeline, which includes:

*-fetching map sub-sections
-analyzing building footprints
-computing heat vulnerability

Using Requestly, we were able to simulate API requests directly and verify the behavior of the backend without relying on the frontend interface.

> SurvivalMesh,Built for when everything else fails.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**THE PROBLEM SURVIVAL MESH SOLVES**

When Infrastructure Fails, People Die
Natural disasters, conflict zones, and large-scale emergencies share one brutal reality — the moment you need communication and information the most is exactly when the internet, cell towers, and power grids go down.
SurvivalMesh was built for that exact moment.

In conflict zones with persistent outages, SurvivalMesh lets teams stay coordinated without relying on the internet:

**Arrive and cache maps**: when you briefly have connectivity (or via satellite/hotspot), open the app and let it auto-download map tiles around your current area. Use “Auto-download” or “Select Region” to prefetch likely operating zones so you can navigate offline later.

**Operate offline**: with tiles cached, you can view maps, drop pins for safe routes, water, aid points, or hazards, and navigate without data.

**Mesh messaging**: send short updates and bulletins peer-to-peer over Bluetooth/LoRa/UDP mesh (as configured), so units can still communicate when cell towers are down or jammed.

**Local coordination**: share pins and notes within the mesh to maintain situational awareness—routes, checkpoints, med needs—even when completely disconnected.

**Resync when possible**: whenever you regain connectivity, refresh maps for new areas and sync messages so the wider team has the latest context.
The goal is to preserve navigation and comms in blackout conditions: pre-cache maps, keep talking over the mesh, and sync only during brief connectivity windows.


**No Medical Guidance in the Field**

Complete offline first aid triage system covering  trauma scenarios
Guided yes/no decision tree walks anyone through treating injuries

**Challenges we ran into**

**Rendering failures**: map stayed blank when Leaflet hadn’t loaded or when local tiles weren’t accessible; added retries and better error surfacing (tile fail counts, probe).

**Offline tiles**: initial code always fetched remote tiles; we had to switch to local-first URLs, normalize  paths, and enable file access in WebView so cached tiles render offline.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Cloud Messaging](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Cloud%20Messaging-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban Pulse transforms how cities manage intersections by replacing expensive, grid-dependent traffic cameras with a self-sustaining, decentralized micro-grid. It directly addresses the inefficiencies of modern traffic management by making road networks smarter, safer, and significantly cheaper to operate.
​How it makes urban infrastructure better, safer, and easier to manage:
​Eliminates Grid-Dependency (Fail-Safe Safety): Traditional traffic lights go dark during power outages, instantly creating dangerous, chaotic intersections. By harvesting kinetic energy directly from vehicle impacts via piezoelectric and triboelectric tiles, the system remains fully operational 24/7, ensuring continuous road safety even during city-wide blackouts.
​Eradicates "Phantom" Traffic Jams: Commuters no longer waste fuel and time waiting at fixed-timer red lights when there is zero cross-traffic. The system physically "feels" demand and instantly allocates green-light phases based on real-time vehicle presence, drastically reducing urban congestion.
​Guarantees All-Weather Reliability: Expensive optical AI cameras and LiDAR systems are frequently blinded by dense fog, heavy monsoon rains, or road dust. The physical weight of a vehicle, however, never changes. Tactile sensing guarantees 100% accurate traffic detection in zero-visibility conditions.
​Slashes Municipal Costs: City planners can deploy this system for a fraction of the cost of traditional smart junctions. It operates on an ultra-low-cost microcontroller framework, entirely removing the need for heavy road trenching, costly fiber-optic cabling, and expensive server maintenance.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a system that operates at the chaotic intersection of kinetic energy, analog hardware, and digital edge-computing was incredibly difficult. Here are the major hurdles I faced and how I overcame them:
​Hardware Hurdles: Taming Kinetic Energy
​Clamping the Wild Voltage Spikes: Piezoelectric and triboelectric tiles don't generate smooth, polite electricity—they output violent, high-voltage AC spikes when smacked. My first major hurdle was building a rugged full-wave bridge rectifier and Zener diode clamping circuit to "soften" and safely corral these chaotic spikes without instantly frying the microcontroller.
​The 5V Stabilization Act: Harvesting the energy was only step one; keeping the system alive was step two. I had to design a micro-grid (using a capacitor buffer, an MT3608 boost converter, and a TP4056 module) to translate sporadic physical impacts into a rock-solid, uninterrupted 5V supply for the board.
​Dual-Purposing Power as Data: I wanted the exact same energy pulse that charged the battery to also act as our traffic sensor. Designing a high-resistance voltage divider to safely "sip" a tiny fraction of that raw electrical spike into an analog pin without bleeding away my charging power took some serious breadboard gymnastics.
​The Infamous "Brownout" Reboot Loop: The absolute most frustrating point of the build! Right as the ESP32 tried to fire up its Wi-Fi antenna to send data, it would pull a massive current spike (up to 500mA). The breadboard couldn't deliver the juice fast enough, causing the voltage to sag and triggering the ESP32's internal Brownout Detector, sending it into an endless reboot loop. I solved this by adding an electrolytic capacitor directly across the power and ground pins to act as a localized energy reserve tank, and temporarily overriding the brownout register in the software during testing.  
​Software Struggles: The Physics of Traffic
​The Speed Calculation Algorithm: Figuring out the speed of the cars purely from impact data was a massive mathematical headache. Since I wasn't using optical cameras or radar, I had to write a C++ algorithm that tracked the exact millisecond a tire hit the first tile, and then calculate the time difference when it hit the second tile. Translating that raw timestamp difference into an accurate speed readout—while mathematically filtering out the "noise" of heavy multi-axle trucks triggering false peaks—required heavy tweaking of the

> AI That Turn Feedback into Product Requirements

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![n8n](https://img.shields.io/badge/n8n-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem:**

Companies receive large volumes of user feedback from multiple sources such as Reddit, app store reviews, support tickets, and social media.

This feedback is unstructured and scattered, making it difficult for product teams to analyze and extract meaningful insights.

Product managers must manually read, categorize, and interpret thousands of comments, which is time-consuming and inefficient.

Important insights and recurring problems are often missed or delayed, leading to slower product improvements.

Converting feedback into clear business requirements, epics, and user stories is still mostly a manual process in most organizations.

As a result, product decisions are sometimes based on limited analysis or intuition instead of real user data.

**Our solution:**

The system automatically collects feedback from different sources and processes it through an AI-driven pipeline.

AI agents cluster similar feedback, identifying recurring issues, feature requests, and product pain points.

The system automatically generates Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) from these clusters.

A Critic Agent validates the requirements to ensure clarity, feasibility, and business value.

The approved requirements are converted into epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria ready for development teams.

The entire process creates a traceable pipeline from feedback → requirements → engineering backlog.

This enables companies to transform the voice of the customer into actionable product decisions automatically, saving time and improving product development speed.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1: Connecting Frontend, Backend, and n8n**

One of the biggest challenges was getting the frontend dashboard, backend API, and n8n workflow to communicate properly.

When the user clicked “Execute Pipeline”, the system initially failed because the backend could not reach the n8n webhook endpoint.

The issue turned out to be a mismatch between the webhook URL used by the backend and the actual webhook path in n8n.

To solve this, I carefully checked the webhook configuration, ensured the workflow was published and active, and tested the endpoint manually using curl/Postman.

After correcting the URL and verifying the ports, the pipeline could successfully trigger the n8n automation.

**Challenge 2: Making AI Agents Produce Structured Output**

Another challenge was ensuring that the AI agents (Gemini) consistently returned structured JSON output required by the pipeline.

Early responses sometimes included extra text or formatting, which broke downstream processing in n8n.

To fix this, I improved the prompts by adding strict output schemas and validation rules, forcing the model to return only valid JSON.

This significantly improved reliability and allowed the pipeline to automatically parse results from each agent.

**Challenge 3: Designing the Multi-Agent Workflow**

Designing the agentic pipeline itself was challenging.

The system required multiple AI agents—Cluster Agent, Analyst Agent, Critic Agent, and Story Writer Agent—to work sequentially.

Initially, some agents produced outputs that were not fully compatible with the next stage.

I solved this by standardizing the JSON data structures between agents, ensuring each stage produced outputs that could be directly consumed by the next agent.

**Challenge 4: Making the Demo Pipeline Real (Not Mocked)**

For the demo dashboard, I wanted the pipeline visualization to show real processing rather than simulated steps.

This required connecting the UI to actual execution data from the n8n workflow and AI outputs.

I implemented a backend summary generator that collects the pipeline results and displays a true execution log and summary in the dashboard.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

AutoFlow Intelligence is an AI-powered system that automatically converts raw customer feedback into structured product requirements.

The platform uses an agentic AI pipeline where specialized AI agents analyze feedback, cluster similar issues, and extract meaningful insights.

From these clusters, the system automatically generates Business Requirement Documents (BRDs), which are then reviewed and validated by a Critic AI agent.

Approved requirements are further converted into engineering-ready epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria, helping development teams move directly into implementation.

n8n is used as the automation backbone, orchestrating the entire workflow—from feedback ingestion to AI processing and result storage.

A real-time dashboard allows users to trigger the pipeline, monitor each stage of the workflow, and view generated outputs.

Uniqueness of the Project:

Unlike typical feedback tools that only collect data, AutoFlow automatically transforms feedback into actionable development tasks.

The system uses a multi-agent AI architecture (Cluster Agent → Analyst Agent → Critic Agent → Story Writer Agent) to ensure accuracy and quality.

It provides traceability from user feedback → requirement → engineering backlog, which is rarely automated in current product tools.

The integration of AI agents with workflow automation (n8n) creates a fully automated pipeline that reduces manual product management effort.

This enables product teams to identify user pain points faster and accelerate feature development.

**n8n**

AutoFlow Intelligence uses n8n as the core automation engine to orchestrate the entire AI pipeline. When the user executes the pipeline from the dashboard, n8n workflows automatically collect feedback data, process it through multiple AI agents (clustering, BRD generation, validation, and story creation), and store the results. n8n manages the step-by-step workflow execution, triggers the AI agents, connects backend services, and tracks the pipeline status in real time. This allows the system to transform raw feedback into structured product requirements through a fully automated workflow.

Gemini 3 is the core intelligence powering AutoFlow Intelligence. Modern companies receive
massive amounts of customer feedback from reviews, forums, and support tickets, but converting

analysts read feedback, identify patterns, write Business Requirement Documents (BRDs), and
then convert them into epics and user stories, a process that can take several weeks. Our solution

Business Requirement Documents including problem statements, business value, and
measurable success metrics.
• AI Self Verification: A second Gemini 3 prompt reviews the generated requirement for
clarity, ambiguity, and completeness, creating an AI validation loop that improves reliability.
• Agile Development Output: Gemini 3 transforms approved requirements into epics, user
stories, and acceptance criteria that development teams can directly implement.

Uniqueness of Using Gemini 3
• Performs deep semantic reasoning rather than simple keyword based NLP analysis.
• Automates the entire pipeline from feedback → requirements → development tasks.
• Uses a multi stage AI reasoning and validation loop powered by Gemini 3.
• Acts as the central intelligence layer bridging customer insights and engineering execution.

For JEE Aspirants

Before CampusKin AI:
Student wants NIT info → Opens NIT website (hard to navigate) → Can't find data → Googles it (gets 2020 data) → Checks Reddit (gets 5 conflicting answers) → Gives up after 2 hours → Makes decision based on wrong information

After CampusKin AI:

**Challenges we ran into**

The Biggest Bug We Hit was the "Wrong Answer" Problem

The hardest bug we faced had nothing to do with code syntax or missing packages.
It was about the AI giving confidently wrong answers.

The Problem

When a user typed:

> "placements at NIT Trichy"

The system was returning the NIT Trichy Overview entry instead of the
Placements entry. It was giving a generic "NIT Trichy was established in 1964..."
answer instead of placement statistics.

This happened because the overview entry had keywords like "nit trichy" and "about nit trichy"
which scored higher than the placement entry for short queries.

The chatbot looked confident but was completely wrong. For a project meant to
help students make college decisions, this was a critical failure.


-Why It Was Hard to Fix

We could not just delete the overview entries — users genuinely ask
"tell me about NIT Trichy" and need that answer.

The challenge was:

- Short queries like "NIT Trichy placements" → should return placements entry
- Long queries like "tell me about NIT Trichy" → should return overview entry

The same keywords were matching both. We needed the system to be
smart enough to know the difference.


How We Fixed It — The Overview Penalty System

We built a custom Intent Signal Dictionary — a list of 70+ words that
strongly indicate the user wants a specific category answer, not a generic overview.

For example:
- "placement", "package", "lpa", "salary" → weight 3 (very strong — user wants placements)
- "hostel", "mess", "accommodation" → weight 3 (user wants hostel info)
- "fee", "tuition", "scholarship" → weight 3 (user wants fees)
- "apply", "join", "eligibility" → weight 2 (user wants admissions)

Then we calculated the total intent weight of every query:

- If intent weight = 0 → user is asking about the institute generally → no penalty
- If intent weight 1-2 → mild penalty on overview entries (0.6x score)
- If intent weight 3-5 → strong penalty (0.3x score)
- If intent weight 6+ → heavy penalty (0.1x score) → specific entry always wins

This meant "placements at NIT Trichy" had intent weight of 6+
so the overview entry got 10x de-boosted and the placements entry won every time.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

We started with a simple idea — students waste too much time searching multiple websites for basic NIT information.
So we built a chatbot to fix that.

Our first version was just keyword matching with a Python dictionary.
It worked but it was not really AI. So during this hackathon
we pushed ourselves to upgrade it into a real generative AI system.

We used RAG, vector search, and LLM integration from scratch
during the hackathon itself. We faced a lot of errors along the way —
missing packages, wrong folder paths, API keys not loading,
the AI giving wrong answers. 

By the end we had built a working RAG pipeline using FAISS,
SentenceTransformers, and LLaMA 3.3 70B — all running for free.

The best part is we will actually use this chatbot ourselves
to help our batchmates find information about NITs.

Armed with this visual evidence and backed by the platform's security badges, consumers can confidently discover local talent and connect instantly via direct call or WhatsApp to get their jobs done right.

Beyond the consumer-to-pro dynamic, Xchange acts as a local economic engine through its B2B partnership ecosystem. Local hardware stores, material suppliers, and contracting agencies can plug directly into the platform to offer exclusive material discounts, sponsor specific service categories for lead generation, or manage their own fleets of verified workers under an agency account. This three-sided architecture creates a self-sustaining network where local businesses, independent professionals, and consumers all continuously drive value for one another.

**The problem it solves**

People suffering from Blindness often face difficulties in understanding their surroundings. Simple tasks such as identifying objects nearby, navigating safely, or recognizing currency during transactions can become challenging.
Existing tools like white canes help detect physical obstacles, but they do not provide information about the environment.
Our project aims to solve this problem by using AI and smartphone cameras to detect objects, describe the surroundings, and provide voice guidance so that visually impaired users can perform daily activities more safely and independently.

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing this project, we encountered several challenges.
The first challenge was accurately detecting objects from camera input, especially in different lighting conditions and environments.
Another challenge was designing an interface that is accessible and easy to use for visually impaired users, since the app needs to rely more on audio than visual elements.
We also faced challenges in integrating AI voice generation using the API from ElevenLabs to convert the detected information into clear spoken guidance.
Additionally, implementing real-time processing for live navigation and currency detection required optimizing the system so that responses are fast and reliable.

**ElevenLabs**

Our project strongly fits the ElevenLabs track because it uses advanced AI voice technology to assist people with visual impairments.
The application analyzes the user’s surroundings using the smartphone camera and converts the detected information into clear and natural voice guidance using ElevenLabs’ text-to-speech capabilities.
This allows visually impaired users to receive real-time audio instructions about objects, obstacles, and currency detection, making navigation safer and easier.
By integrating ElevenLabs voice technology as the primary communication method between the system and the user, our project demonstrates a meaningful real-world application of AI voice for accessibility.\

**The problem it solves**

# MeetingMind AI

### *AI that turns talk into tasks.*

---

## 🚨 The Problem

Every team knows this pain:

- You finish a 1-hour meeting. **Nobody remembers who was supposed to do what.**
- Someone has to manually write down notes, create Jira tickets, and send follow-up emails — **that takes another 30–60 minutes.**
- Action items get lost in chat threads. Deadlines get missed. People say *"I didn't know that was assigned to me."*
- Developers, PMs, and founders are **spending hours per week just managing meeting aftermath** instead of actually building.

> **The average professional wastes 4.8 hours per week on meeting follow-ups.** MeetingMind eliminates that entirely.

---

## ✅ What MeetingMind AI Solves

MeetingMind is a Chrome Extension that **sits inside your Google Meet** and does everything that happens *after* a meeting — automatically.

| Without MeetingMind | With MeetingMind |
|---|---|
| Manually write notes after meeting | AI summary generated instantly |
| Forget who said what | Full per-speaker transcript saved |
| Create Jira tickets one by one | Tickets auto-created & assigned |
| Send follow-up emails manually | Emails sent to every assignee automatically |
| Action items lost in Slack/WhatsApp | Everything stored in cloud DB, forever |

---

## 👥 Who Is It For?

### 🧑‍💻 Software Development Teams
Stop context-switching between your standup and your Jira board. MeetingMind listens to your sprint planning meeting and **auto-creates every task in Jira** with the right assignee and deadline — before you've even closed the Meet tab.

### 📋 Project Managers
Run 5+ meetings a day? MeetingMind tracks decisions, blockers, and action items across **all of them**, builds a searchable history, and makes sure no follow-up ever falls through the cracks.

### 🚀 Startup Founders
Small teams move fast and can't afford missed tasks. Use MeetingMind to keep everyone aligned — it **automatically emails each teammate their assigned tasks** so there's zero confusion about who owns what.

### 🎓 Students & Hackathon Teams
Group projects fall apart when communication does. MeetingMind gives every team member a clear written record of **what was decided and what they need to build**, with AI-generated summaries of every session.

### 🏢 Remote & Async Teams
When people are in different timezones, meeting notes matter more than ever. MeetingMind creates a **permanent, searchable, AI-analyzed record** of every meeting so anyone can catch up instantly.

---

## 💡 What It Makes Easier

### ⚡ Task Assignment — from 30 min → 0 min
Instead of manually creating Jira tickets after a meeting, MeetingMind reads the transcript, uses Gemini AI to figure out who should own each task based on the conversation, and creates + assigns the tickets automatically.

### 📧 Follow-up Emails — automated & professional
No more copy-pasting action items into emails. Every attendee gets a **beautifully formatted email** listing exactly what they're responsible for, with their Jira ticket link included.

### 🧠 Never Lose Context Again
Ever been in a meeting where someone says *"wait, didn't we decide this last month?"* MeetingMind stores every meeting in a cloud database with full transcripts, summaries, and decisions — fully searchable, forever.

### 🎙️ Per-Speaker Accountability
MeetingMind doesn't just transcribe — it tracks **who said what**. Each speaker gets their own transcript lane, so you can see exactly what commitments each person made during the meeting.

### 💬 Ask Questions About Any Meeting
Using the built-in **"Chat with Meeting"** feature, you can ask Gemini AI questions like *"What did Aryan say about the database?"* or *"What were the blockers from last Tuesday?"* — and get instant answers from the transcript.

---

## 🔧 Built With Free APIs — Zero Cost to Run

> No paid subscriptions. No per-seat pricing. No vendor lock-in.

- **Chrome Web Speech API** — free, built into the browser
- **Google Gemini 2.5 Flash** — 1,500 free requests/day
- **Neon.tech PostgreSQL** — free cloud database tier
- **Gmail SMTP** — free with an app password
- **Jira REST API** — free on Atlassian's free plan

**MeetingMind is the only AI meeting assistant that costs ₹0 to run.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🐛 Challenges We Ran Into

---

### 1. "Receiving End Does Not Exist" — The Chrome Extension Messaging Nightmare

This was the first major blocker. When the user clicked **Start Recording** in the popup,
the background service worker was trying to send a message to the content script
to trigger speech recognition:
```js
chrome.tabs.sendMessage(tabId, { type: "START_RECORDING" })
// ❌ Error: Could not establish connection. Receiving end does not exist.
```

The problem was a **race condition** — the content script hadn't fully loaded yet
when the background tried to message it, so the message went nowhere and the
whole recording flow broke silently.

**How we fixed it:**
We flipped the architecture entirely. Instead of the background *telling* the content
script to start, the content script now **starts itself** when the user clicks record
in the popup. The background service worker became a pure data store — it only
*receives* data, never initiates communication to the content script. This eliminated
the race condition completely.

---

### 2. Speaker Detection Was Returning Random Garbage

The per-speaker transcript feature depended on scraping the Google Meet DOM to
detect who was currently speaking. The problem: **Google Meet's DOM changes
constantly** with every UI update, and our CSS selectors kept breaking or picking
up wrong elements — meeting titles, button labels, random UI text — instead of
the actual speaker name.

**How we fixed it:**
We built a multi-selector fallback system with **length validation**. Instead of
relying on one selector, we query 5 different known selectors in order and only
accept a result if the text is between 2 and 60 characters long (filtering out
button labels and empty strings). We also added a debounce so the speaker only
updates after being detected consistently — not on a single noisy poll.

---

### 3. Gemini Returning Broken JSON That Crashed the Whole Analysis

The entire post-meeting analysis depended on Gemini returning a clean JSON object.
But Gemini kept wrapping its response in markdown code fences, so calling
JSON.parse() on that crashed the app and the meeting saved with zero analysis —
no summary, no action items, nothing. Users would finish a 1-hour meeting and
see a blank dashboard.

**How we fixed it:**
We added a cleaning step before every JSON.parse() call that strips markdown
fences, trims whitespace, and extracts just the JSON object using a regex fallback.
We also wrapped the entire analysis in a try/catch that saves a graceful error
state to the DB with a **"Retry Analysis"** button on the dashboard — so even if
Gemini fails, the transcript is preserved and the user can try again.

---

### 4. execute_route.js Was Written But Never Connected

After building all the Jira + email logic in execute_route.js, the
**"Approve All & Create Tasks"** button did absolutely nothing. No errors,
no Jira tickets, no emails — complete silence.

After tracing the full request path we realised execute_route.js was
a fully working module that was **never actually registered on the Express app**.
The file existed, the code was correct, but server.js never imported it,
so POST /api/execute returned 404 every time.

**How we fixed it:**
Adding one line in server.js activated the entire Jira + email system:
require("./execute_route")(app)

The lesson: always verify your routes are actually mounted — a missing require()
is completely invisible until you trace the 404 manually.

---

### 5. Attendee Emails Not Being Captured from Google Meet

The Jira + email automation depended on having real attendee email addresses.
But when we tested, meeting.attendees was full of **display names only**
("Devyani K", "Aakarsh V") with no emails — because Google Meet doesn't
expose participant emails in the DOM to extensions by default.

**How we fixed it:**
We expanded the content script to scrape emails from **every visible surface**
in the Meet UI — participant panel, invite dialogs, profile tooltips — using
a regex email extractor that runs continuously during the meeting. We also
added a fallback in extractAttendeeEmails() that scans the speakerMap keys
and any stringified attendee objects for email patterns, so even partially
captured data can yield valid addresses.

---

### 6. Web Speech API Cutting Out Every 60 Seconds

Chrome's Web Speech API has a **hard timeout** — it stops listening after
roughly 60 seconds of continuous use and fires the onend event. In a
45-minute meeting, this meant transcription would silently die after the
first minute with no error shown to the user.

**How we fixed it:**
We implemented an **auto-restart loop** — the recognition.onend handler
checks if recording is still supposed to be active and immediately calls
recognition.start() again. We added a small delay before restarting to
avoid the browser's abuse detection, and a session counter so we could
track how many times it had restarted for debugging. The transcript is

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem Being Solved**

This project addresses the challenge of predicting and explaining cyberattack behavior within enterprise systems. The goal is to develop a system that helps security analysts understand ongoing threats more effectively by combining anomaly detection, graph-based attack modeling, and explainable artificial intelligence.
The system identifies suspicious patterns in security events such as failed login attempts, lateral network connections, privilege escalation activities, and suspicious processes. Instead of simply flagging an alert, the system analyzes how these events relate to each other and models them as part of a potential attack progression.
By analyzing these relationships, the system can predict the next possible attacker technique or target asset using structured cybersecurity knowledge such as the MITRE ATT&CK framework. In addition, the system provides explainable AI (XAI) insights that clearly show why the model made a particular prediction, what evidence supports it, and how trustworthy the prediction is.
This approach helps transform security monitoring from a reactive alert-based system into a proactive and explainable threat analysis platform.
Key Problems Addressed
The project specifically addresses the following cybersecurity challenges:
Alert Overload in SOC Systems
Security teams receive a large number of alerts, making it difficult to identify critical threats quickly.
Lack of Attack Progression Prediction
Most existing systems detect isolated anomalies but cannot predict the attacker’s next move.
Black-Box AI Models
Many machine learning systems lack transparency, making their decisions difficult for analysts to trust.
Limited Contextual Analysis of Security Events
Security events are often analyzed individually instead of being connected into an attack chain.
Slow Incident Response
Without clear explanations and predictive insights, analysts take longer to understand and respond to attacks

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of this project, several technical and practical challenges were encountered. These challenges were related to data availability, model reliability, system integration, and the complexity of implementing explainable artificial intelligence for cybersecurity analysis.
**1. Lack of Realistic and Labeled Cybersecurity Data**
One of the main challenges was obtaining high-quality cybersecurity datasets that accurately represent real-world attack scenarios. Many publicly available datasets are either outdated, incomplete, or lack proper labeling for different types of attack behaviors. This made it difficult to train and validate the anomaly detection model effectively. As a result, synthetic data generation and feature simulation were used during the initial development phase.
**2. Detecting Anomalies Without High False Positives**
Anomaly detection models can easily classify normal variations in system activity as malicious behavior. Achieving a balance between detecting real threats and minimizing false positives was a significant challenge. Proper feature scaling, model tuning, and parameter adjustments were required to ensure that the system could distinguish between legitimate user behavior and suspicious activities.
**3. Interpreting Black-Box Machine Learning Models**
Many machine learning models used for anomaly detection operate as black-box systems, meaning their decision-making processes are difficult to interpret. Since cybersecurity analysts need to understand the reasoning behind alerts, implementing explainable AI techniques and designing meaningful explanations for predictions required additional effort.
**4. Modeling Complex Relationships Between Security Events**
Cyberattacks often involve multiple stages and interconnected actions, such as credential compromise, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Representing these relationships and understanding the sequence of attack behaviors was challenging. Designing a structure that could capture these relationships while still allowing efficient analysis required careful system design.
**5. Integrating Multiple System Components**
The project involves multiple components including anomaly detection models, explainable analysis modules, API services, and database storage. Integrating these components into a cohesive system while maintaining performance and scalability presented architectural challenges. Ensuring smooth communication between services required careful API design and data management.
**6. Generating Meaningful Explanations for Security Analysts**
Another challenge was converting technical model outputs into explanations that are understandable to human analysts. Raw model outputs such as anomaly scores or probabilities are often not meaningful for decision-making. The system therefore needed additional logic to convert these outputs into structured evidence, confidence scores, and human-readable explanations.
**7. Ensuring System Reliability and Trust**
Security analysts must be able to trust automated systems before relying on them for incident response. Designing mechanisms such as validation scores and trust indicators required careful consideration to ensure the system provides reliable and verifiable insights
