### Deadlock
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/deadlock-6761) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Aayush20072701/deadlock) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> First to solve, last to fall

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Piston API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Piston%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most coding practice platforms are solo experiences you grind alone, 
with no pressure and no competition. Deadlock changes that by turning 
coding into a real-time 1v1 battle.
Two players are matched, given the same problem, and race to solve it 
first. You can see your opponent's live progress, use power-ups to 
disrupt them (Freeze their submissions, Fog their editor), and earn 
ELO rating based on your performance.
It solves the motivation gap in competitive programming by adding 
stakes, real-time pressure, and a ranked system that makes every 
problem feel like a match.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest challenge was building reliable real-time matchmaking. 
Initially, lobby pairing was stored in server memory, so every 
nodemon restart would wipe active lobbies and disconnect players. 
We fixed this by moving all lobby state to Redis with TTL keys, 
so the server can restart without losing match context.

The second major challenge was synchronizing the code judge (Piston API) 
with live socket events making sure submit results, opponent progress, 
and power-up effects all arrived in the right order without race conditions.

Team **captchakings** -- Aayush Dhawan, GOURI VERMA, Kriyanshu ., palak bisht

### Truth AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/truth-ai-4448) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shivam_hkr/truth-AI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Everytging  u see is not real

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

With the rapid growth of generative AI, fake images, videos, audio, and text can be created and spread online very easily. This makes it difficult for people to identify whether digital content is real, AI-generated, or manipulated, which increases the risk of misinformation.

Most existing tools detect only one type of media. RealityCheck AI solves this problem by providing a multimodal detection platform where users can upload image, video, audio, or text and instantly analyze its authenticity and misinformation risk using techniques from Machine Learning, Computer Vision, and Natural Language Processing.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Multimodal Integration
One of the biggest challenges was combining detection for image, video, audio, and text into a single system. Each type of media requires different AI techniques from Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and Machine Learning, so designing a unified pipeline that routes the content to the correct model was complex.

2. Dataset Availability
High-quality datasets for deepfake and misinformation detection are limited and often inconsistent. Collecting and preparing datasets for training models across different media types required significant preprocessing and validation.

3. Processing Large Files
Video and audio files are computationally heavy. Extracting frames from videos and converting audio into spectrograms increased processing time, so we had to design efficient pipelines for faster inference.

4. Model Accuracy vs Speed
In a hackathon setting, we needed models that were both accurate and fast. Balancing performance with real-time usability required selecting optimized architectures and reducing model complexity.

5. Explainability of Results
AI models often behave like a “black box.” To make our predictions trustworthy, we needed to add explainability techniques so users can understand why the system flagged certain content as suspicious.

6. Scalable Architecture
Since the platform is designed to integrate more models in the future, structuring the backend to remain modular and scalable was another key design challenge.

### Krishi-Verify
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/krishiverify-cc3a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SHARONALGO/krishi-verify.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> MSP calculation

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small farmers often sell their crops in mandis without knowing the correct price they should receive. Even though the government announces a Minimum Support Price (MSP), the actual amount farmers receive can vary depending on crop quality factors such as moisture content, grain size, purity, and weight. Because farmers usually lack tools to verify these parameters or calculate the expected value of their crop, they are vulnerable to underpayment, lack of transparency, and manipulation by middlemen.

Krishi-Verify solves this problem by giving farmers a way to estimate the value of their crop before selling it. The platform analyzes measurable crop quality parameters such as moisture level, grain size, purity percentage, and weight to determine a quality grade and calculate an approximate price based on MSP guidelines.

Using a simple web interface, farmers or mandi officials can input crop details or upload images, and the system will generate:

A quality grade for the crop

An estimated price based on MSP

A transparent breakdown of how the value was calculated

This helps farmers make informed selling decisions, increases transparency in agricultural markets, and reduces the chances of unfair pricing.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was determining how to accurately estimate crop value using multiple quality parameters like moisture content, grain size, purity, and weight. Converting these agricultural factors into a reliable grading and pricing formula required researching MSP guidelines and crop quality standards. Another difficulty was integrating both tabular data inputs and image-based analysis into a single web interface. We also had to ensure the system remained simple enough for farmers to use easily. Debugging data handling and model outputs during integration was another hurdle. Through iterative testing, research, and team collaboration, we refined the grading logic and successfully built a working prototype.

Team **Syntax Flux** -- Sharon Saji, Gurpreet Singh, KAPISH GUPTA, [Prem Burnwal](https://github.com/prembrnwal)

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/Electron-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![RAG](https://img.shields.io/badge/RAG-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Problem Statement

Students today have access to a vast amount of study material such as **PDFs, notes, textbooks, and slides**. However, extracting specific information from these resources remains **time-consuming and inefficient**. Understanding a single concept often requires navigating through lengthy documents, which significantly **slows down the learning process**.

## Challenges

- Large volumes of study material make it difficult to quickly find relevant information.
- Students must manually search through long documents to understand a single concept.
- The learning process becomes slower and less efficient due to scattered resources.

## Limitations of Existing Solutions

Most existing **AI tools**:
- Provide **generic internet-based responses**.
- Do **not effectively utilize a student's personal study materials**.
- Often require **continuous internet access**.
- Depend on **paid services or subscriptions**.

## Need for a Solution

There is a clear need for an **intelligent and accessible learning assistant** that can:

- Analyze **personal study resources** such as PDFs, notes, and slides.
- Provide **quick and accurate answers** based on those materials.
- Deliver **simplified explanations** to improve understanding.
- Work **efficiently without heavy reliance on internet connectivity or expensive services**.

Such a system would significantly **enhance learning efficiency and help students access knowledge faster and more effectively**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges When Studying with Online AI Tools

While AI tools like ChatGPT and other online models can assist students in learning, they also present several limitations that can affect the study experience.

### 1. Token and Usage Limits
Many AI platforms impose **token or message limits**, especially for free users. Long study sessions may get interrupted when the usage quota is reached.

### 2. Premium Feature Restrictions
Advanced features such as **larger context windows, better models, or faster responses** are often restricted to **paid or premium plans**, making them inaccessible for many students.

### 3. File and Image Upload Limits
Some platforms limit the number of files or images that can be uploaded within a certain period. For example:
- Only a limited number of **images or PDFs can be uploaded per day**
- Large documents may **exceed size limits**

This makes it difficult to analyze multiple pages of notes, slides, or textbook screenshots.

### 4. Chat or Conversation Limits
Certain AI tools limit the **number of conversations or messages per day**, which can interrupt continuous learning or problem-solving sessions.

### 5. Internet Dependency
Most AI tools require **constant internet access**, making them difficult to use in areas with **slow or unstable connectivity**.

### 6. Privacy Concerns
Uploading personal study notes, assignments, or project documents to online services may raise **data privacy concerns**.

### 7. Lack of Personal Study Context
AI models typically provide answers based on **general internet knowledge**, rather than focusing on the **student's own study materials**, which may lead to explanations that do not align with their syllabus or notes.

### 8. Session Memory Limitations
In long discussions, earlier context may be lost due to **context window limitations**, forcing students to **repeat information or re-upload materials**.

---

These challenges highlight the need for a **personalized AI learning assistant that can work with a student’s own study materials while minimizing external limitations.**

Team **EvolveX** -- Jaskaran Singh, Harshita Kheterpal, Manveer Singh, Himesh Sharma

> Fashion that fits on you

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded Javascript (EJS)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20Javascript%20(EJS)-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Compass](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Compass-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Last-Minute Clothing Need Problem

Many college students suddenly need clothes for presentations, interviews, college events, parties, or functions.
Traditional shopping takes too much time because:

Visiting multiple stores physically takes hours.

Online platforms like Amazon or Myntra take 2–5 days for delivery.

Students often realize the need at the last moment.

Problem: There is no platform that delivers clothing instantly within 1 hour for urgent needs.

2. Size, Fit, and Return Issues in E-Commerce

Online clothing shopping has major problems related to size and fit.

Around 30–40% of online clothing orders are returned mainly due to size or fit issues.

Returns take several days to process.

Customers cannot quickly replace items when needed urgently.

Problem: Current e-commerce systems make clothing purchases slow and inconvenient when size issues occur.

3. Lack of Digital Visibility for Local Clothing Vendors

Local clothing stores near colleges often have good products but low online presence.

Large platforms like Amazon and Flipkart dominate the market.

Small vendors cannot compete with big brands digitally.

Many shops depend only on walk-in customers.

Problem: Local vendors lose potential customers because they lack a digital platform to sell quickly and efficiently.

4. Inefficient Clothing Search Process

Most online platforms follow a store-first approach where users browse shops.

Users must visit multiple store pages.

Finding a specific clothing item takes time.

It is difficult to know which nearby shop has the product available.

Problem: There is no product-first platform that instantly shows nearby clothing availability.

5. No Quick-Commerce Model for Fashion

Quick commerce exists for groceries and food (Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart).

But fashion still follows a slow delivery model.

No platform provides hyperlocal clothing delivery within 1 hour.

Fashion shopping is not optimized for urgent situations.

Problem: The fashion industry lacks a quick-commerce infrastructure similar to food delivery.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Integrating Multiple Modules

The platform has three different modules:

Customer Module

Shopkeeper Module

Delivery Partner Module

Each module needs different features but must still communicate with the same database.

Problem: Ensuring smooth communication between all modules while keeping the system organized and bug-free.

2. Real-Time Data Handling

The platform must show real-time product availability from nearby shops.

Stock changes when a shopkeeper sells something offline.

The system must instantly update product availability.

Problem: Implementing real-time database updates so users don’t order out-of-stock items.

3. Location-Based Product Search

The platform needs to show products based on the user’s location.

The system must identify nearby shops.

It must filter products according to distance and availability.

Problem: Developing a location-based filtering system that works accurately and quickly.

4. Order Allocation Logic

When an order is placed, the system must decide:

Which shop should fulfill the order

Which delivery partner should pick it up

Problem: Creating a smart order allocation logic that reduces delivery time.

5. Vendor Dashboard Design

Shopkeepers need a simple interface to:

Add products

Update stock

Accept orders

Problem: Designing a simple and easy-to-use dashboard for vendors who may not be tech-savvy.

6. Testing the 1-Hour Delivery Workflow

The whole workflow involves multiple steps:

Customer → Shopkeeper → Delivery Partner → Customer

Even a small delay in one step can break the 1-hour delivery goal.

Problem: Testing and optimizing the complete workflow to ensure quick delivery.


Development Challenges

Integrating customer, vendor, and delivery modules

Managing real-time

Creating smart order allocation logic

**The problem it solves**

**For Students:**

See the weekly mess menu from their phone
Get instant notifications on request updates

**For Wardens:**

See all complaints in one place with priority levels

**Challenges we ran into**

01 📂 Empty Server — Nothing to Deploy
Backend code existed locally but was never pushed to GitHub. Render found an empty folder and returned 404s. Fixed by pushing the full codebase and setting the correct Root Directory in Render.

02 🔀 Backend Serving the Frontend
app.ts had an SPA fallback trying to serve client/dist/index.html on Render — which doesn't exist there. Removed it entirely since Vercel handles the frontend.

03 🚫 CORS Blocking All Requests
Production CORS origin was left as 'https://yourdomain.com'. Every request from Vercel was blocked. Fixed by reading the allowed origin from an environment variable.

04 💥 Express 5 Wildcard Syntax Breaking
app.use('/api/*') crashes in Express 5. Server wouldn't start on Render. Fixed by updating to the new named wildcard syntax: app.use('/api/*path').

05 🔗 API Calls Hitting the Wrong Server
Axios baseURL was set to '/api' — a relative URL that resolved to Vercel, not Render. Fixed by pointing it to VITE_API_URL with the full Render backend URL.

06 🔄 Vercel 404 on Page Refresh
Direct URL navigation returned 404s because Vercel didn't know to serve index.html for all routes. Fixed by adding a vercel.json rewrite rule.

07 🗄️ Switching from MongoDB to Supabase
Started with MongoDB + Mongoose, then migrated mid-build to Supabase (PostgreSQL) for better relational data handling, built-in auth, and real-time support. Rewrote all models, queries, and services using the Supabase JS client.

08 🖥️ Windows PowerShell vs Bash
Unix commands like find and grep don't work on Windows PowerShell, slowing down debugging. Switched to PowerShell equivalents (Get-ChildItem, Get-Content).

─────────────────────────────────────────────
Built with React + TypeScript · Node.js + Express 5 · Supabase · Vercel + Render

### Roundup Saving Simulator And Subscription Manager
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/roundup-saving-simulator-64b5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Arsks12/fintech) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://fintech2-drab.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co)

> Every purchase rounds up. Every coin counts.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Identified
The application addresses several key financial management challenges that individuals face:

Inconsistent Savings Habits: People struggle to save money regularly, often due to lack of automation and motivation
Subscription Management Complexity: Users have multiple recurring subscriptions across different services, making it difficult to track costs, renewal dates, and identify optimization opportunities
Poor Financial Visibility: Lack of clear insights into spending patterns, savings progress, and personalized financial recommendations
Data Privacy & Isolation: Need for secure, separate financial data when multiple users share devices

Approach Taken
The developers created a comprehensive fintech dashboard with two integrated systems:

1. Round-Up Savings Automation
Micro-Saving Logic: Automatically calculates and saves the "spare change" from transactions (rounding up to nearest ₹10 or ₹100)
Virtual Piggy Bank: Dedicated savings account that accumulates these small amounts
Real-Time Preview: Shows users exactly how much will be saved before transaction confirmation
2. Subscription Management System
Complete Lifecycle Tracking: Add, edit, pause, or cancel subscriptions with full details
Smart Notifications: Alerts for upcoming renewals within 7 days
Financial Analytics: Calculates monthly/yearly costs and identifies spending patterns
3. User Authentication & Data Isolation
Multi-User Architecture: Each user gets completely isolated data storage
Session Persistence: Maintains login state across browser sessions
Secure Data Separation: Uses user-specific localStorage keys
4. Smart Insights Engine
Behavioral Analysis: Provides personalized recommendations based on spending vs. savings ratios
Risk Assessment: Warns about unsustainable subscription spending
Optimization Suggestions: Recommends bundling deals and prepayment strategies


Technical Solution
Modern Tech Stack:

Next.js 14 with App Router for optimal performance
TypeScript for type safety and better developer experience
Tailwind CSS for responsive, modern UI design
Framer Motion for smooth animations and micro-interactions
Zustand for efficient state management with built-in persistence
Key Architecture Decisions:

Component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns
Context API for authentication state management
User-specific store creation for data isolation
Responsive design with mobile-first approach


Benefits of This Prototype
1. Behavioral Economics Integration
Leverages psychological principles (spare change effect) to make saving painless
Small, automatic savings that compound over time
Reduces friction in the saving process
2. Enhanced Financial Awareness
Clear visualization of spending patterns and savings progress
Monthly/yearly cost projections for subscriptions
Real-time balance tracking across multiple accounts
3. Intelligent Automation
Zero-effort savings through transaction round-ups
Proactive renewal notifications prevent missed payments
Smart insights provide actionable financial advice
4. Superior User Experience
Modern, gradient-based UI with smooth animations
Intuitive tabbed interface separating savings and subscriptions
Real-time feedback and confirmation dialogs
Fully responsive design for all devices
5. Scalability & Extensibility
Modular component architecture for easy feature additions
Type-safe codebase ready for team collaboration
Prepared for backend integration (currently uses localStorage for demo)
Easy to extend with charts, reports, and additional financial tools
6. Educational & Motivational Value
Teaches financial management concepts through interactive simulation
Demonstrates the power of compound savings
Shows practical subscription optimization strategies
Gamification elements through progress tracking
7. Privacy & Security Foundation
Complete user data isolation (no cross-contamination)
Secure authentication flow with session management
No external data sharing in demo version
Ready for production security implementations
This prototype effectively demonstrates how technology can transform personal finance management from a chore into an engaging, automated, and insightful experience. It combines behavioral science with modern web development to create a tool that could genuinely help users build better financial habits and achieve their savings goals.

**Challenges we ran into**

Development Challenges
Building this fintech dashboard presented several technical and design challenges that were overcome through careful planning and modern tooling:

1. User-Specific Data Isolation
Challenge: Ensuring complete data separation between users while maintaining performance with localStorage.
Solution: Implemented user-specific Zustand stores with unique persistence keys (roundup-savings-storage-{userId}).
2. Complex State Management
Challenge: Managing multiple interconnected state pieces (balances, transactions, subscriptions) with real-time updates.
Solution: Used Zustand with persistence middleware and computed properties for efficient state handling.

3. Authentication System Design
Challenge: Building a secure, session-persistent auth system without a backend.
Solution: Created a React Context-based auth provider with localStorage for user sessions and data initialization.
4. Responsive Animation Performance
Challenge: Maintaining smooth Framer Motion animations across different devices and screen sizes.
Solution: Optimized component rendering and used CSS transforms for hardware acceleration.
5. Type Safety Across Components
Challenge: Ensuring TypeScript coverage for complex data flows between components.
Solution: Defined comprehensive interfaces for all data structures and used generic hooks for type-safe state management.
6. Real-Time Calculation Accuracy
Challenge: Ensuring precise round-up calculations and subscription cost projections.
Solution: Created dedicated utility functions with thorough testing and validation.
7. Feature Integration Complexity
Challenge: Seamlessly combining round-up savings and subscription management into a cohesive UX.
Solution: Used a tabbed interface with shared state and consistent design patterns.
These challenges were addressed by leveraging Next.js 14's performance optimizations, TypeScript's type safety, and a component-first architecture that allowed for iterative development and testing.

**The problem it solves**

## What is Symptom-to-Specialist Mapper?

Symptom-to-Specialist Mapper is a smart healthcare web application that helps users identify the most relevant medical specialist based on the symptoms they experience. The platform simplifies the process of deciding which doctor to consult and helps users quickly find nearby clinics or specialists.

## What Can People Use It For?

- **Quick Symptom Guidance:** Users can enter their symptoms and receive suggestions about the most appropriate medical specialist (e.g., cardiologist, neurologist, dermatologist).
- **Finding Nearby Clinics:** The application helps users locate nearby hospitals or clinics where the suggested specialist is available.
- **Affordable Healthcare Access:** Users can discover affordable healthcare options near them.
- **Saving Time:** Instead of searching multiple websites or guessing which doctor to visit, the system provides direct recommendations.
- **Emergency Awareness:** It can help users quickly understand when a symptom might require urgent medical attention.

## How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

- **Reduces Confusion:** Many people are unsure which specialist to consult. This platform simplifies that decision.
- **Faster Healthcare Access:** Users can go directly to the correct specialist without multiple consultations.
- **Improves Efficiency:** It eliminates the need for long searches and helps users make informed healthcare decisions quickly.
- **User-Friendly:** The platform provides a simple interface where users just enter their symptoms and receive useful guidance.

## Goal of the Project

The goal of this project is to make healthcare navigation easier, faster, and more accessible for everyone by combining symptom analysis with smart specialist mapping.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

One of the main challenges during the development of this project was implementing the login flow and connecting different pages of the application. Initially, when the login button was clicked, nothing happened because the form did not have any JavaScript logic or navigation handling. This caused the page to simply refresh instead of moving to the next page.

To solve this issue, I implemented a JavaScript event listener on the login form that prevented the default form submission and redirected the user to the symptom input page. This allowed the application to simulate a proper login flow and improved the overall user experience.

Another challenge was organizing the project structure. At first, the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were written in a single file, which made the code difficult to manage and modify. I resolved this by separating the code into different files (`HTML`, `CSS`, and `JavaScript`) and organizing them into folders. This made the project more modular, easier to maintain, and closer to real-world development practices.

These challenges helped me better understand front-end structure, event handling, and how different parts of a web application interact with each other.

**Open Innovation**

### Open Innovation
Symptom-to-Specialist Mapper addresses a real-world healthcare challenge: many people are unsure which specialist to consult for their symptoms. The platform simplifies this process by connecting symptoms with the appropriate medical expertise and helping users find nearby clinics quickly. This open innovation approach improves healthcare accessibility and decision-making for patients.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Predictive Maintenance Lite is a simple yet effective system that uses sensor data to monitor equipment health and predict maintenance needs before a failure occurs. By analyzing parameters such as temperature, vibration, efficiency, and usage hours, the system helps identify potential problems early. This reduces unexpected downtime, lowers maintenance costs, and improves overall operational safety. The dashboard also makes it easy for users to visualize equipment status and take timely maintenance actions, making industrial monitoring more efficient and reliable.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of Predictive Maintenance Lite, we faced several challenges.
1. Handling Large Model Files
One of the main challenges was dealing with large Python machine learning model files and dependencies. When we tried to deploy the project on free hosting platforms, we discovered that most of them only provide around 500 MB of storage, while our model files and libraries required much more space.  
Solution: Instead of deploying it online, we ran the project locally using a local URL to demonstrate the working dashboard and prediction system.

2. Data Preparation and Cleaning
Another challenge was preparing the sensor dataset. The raw data needed preprocessing such as handling missing values and organizing it into a proper CSV format for the model.  
Solution: We performed data cleaning and preprocessing using Python, ensuring that the dataset was structured correctly before feeding it into the model.

3. Integrating the Model with the Dashboard
Connecting the machine learning prediction logic with the web dashboard was also challenging. At first, the sensor data and prediction results were not updating properly in the interface.  
Solution: We fixed this by improving the backend logic and ensuring proper data flow between the Python model and the dashboard interface.

These challenges helped us improve the system and gain a better understanding of  data processing, machine learning integration, and real-world deployment limitations.

### TRACEX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tracex-42f1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SoumyadipPaul01223322/tracex) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tracex-three.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co)

> Zero Trust Deep Intel

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem It Solves

Modern threat intelligence and OSINT investigations are often painfully slow, fragmented, and highly manual. When investigators or cybersecurity analysts start with a single piece of evidence—such as a burner phone number or a leaked email address—they typically have to manually query dozens of disconnected databases (telecom registries, bank APIs, vehicle vaults, dark web forums) and physically stitch the data together to understand the full identity profile. 

**TraceX** solves this by acting as an Autonomous Graph Expansion Engine. It eliminates manual data hunting and mental mapping by fully automating the intelligence gathering process:

*   **Zero-Touch Discovery:** It takes a single initial vector (e.g., a phone number) and uses automated breadth-first search (BFS) routing to autonomously crawl through 45+ live data endpoints. 
*   **Infinite Entity Resolution:** When it discovers a new node (like finding an Aadhaar number linked to the phone), it automatically uses that *new* data to trigger further recursive scans (finding bank accounts or vehicles linked to that Aadhaar), building out the entire digital footprint without human intervention.
*   **Visual Intelligence:** Instead of dumping raw JSON or CSVs, it maps the entire investigation in real-time onto an interactive, hierarchical DAGRE node graph. Investigators can instantly visually comprehend complex syndicates, aliases, and financial connections.
*   **Breach Intelligence Synthesis:** It cross-references generated identities against over 14 billion leaked records from the dark web, instantly highlighting compromised passwords and associations on the graph.

In short, TraceX turns what used to be a multi-day ordeal of manual cross-referencing into a 10-second visual scan, making high-end identity resolution fundamentally easier, faster, and more comprehensive for security professionals.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I ran into

Building TraceX required orchestrating a highly complex pipeline of live OSINT data, asynchronous recursive graph logic, and real-time frontend rendering. Here are the major hurdles and how they were overcome:

**1. Recursive Async API Cascading & Rate Limiting**
*The Challenge:* TraceX isn't just a single API call; it runs a Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm. A single phone number triggers an API call that returns 5 emails, which in turn trigger 5 separate API calls to a Dark Web database, resulting in a cascading multiplier of network requests. Running these concurrently would frequently crash the browser or hit strict rate limits on the external OSINT gateways.
*The Solution:* I implemented a strictly controlled, asynchronous BFS queue within the React state ([TraceXGraph.tsx](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/White%20Devil/Documents/XHIBIT/tracex/src/components/graph/TraceXGraph.tsx:0:0-0:0)). Instead of firing all promises concurrently, the engine processes nodes sequentially using `for...of` loops and `await`, inserting artificial delays if necessary to throttle request volume and prevent API blockades while still providing a fluid user experience.

**2. Dynamic Graph Layouts and State Desync**
*The Challenge:* As new intelligence nodes (Banks, Vehicles, Leaks, Identities) are discovered dynamically, injecting them directly into the React Flow (`@xyflow/react`) canvas caused erratic overlapping and chaotic visualizations.
*The Solution:* I integrated the `@dagrejs/dagre` engine to mathematically calculate hierarchical node positions in real-time. The hardest part was ensuring the layout engine only fired *after* React had flushed the new nodes to the DOM. I solved this by decoupling the layout function into a separate `useEffect` hook that triggers specifically when the `rawNodes` array mutates.

**3. Context Loss During PDF Exporting**
*The Challenge:* Generating an "enterprise-grade" intelligence report proved significantly harder than anticipated. Trying to screenshot the HTML DOM of the React Flow canvas using standard libraries (`html2canvas`) resulted in clipping, off-center viewports, and missing CSS elements due to the way React Flow handles transformation matrices.
*The Solution:* I pivoted entirely from a purely visual screenshot to a structured data export. I implemented `jspdf` and `jspdf-autotable`, extracting the raw intelligence data directly from the state management layer rather than the visual DOM. This allowed for the generation of clean, multi-page, text-based PDF reports complete with categorized data tables (Phones, Leaks, Banks) and sanitized unicode characters for maximum professional legibility.

**4. High-Performance Cinematic Scrolling**
*The Challenge:* Achieving the ultra-smooth "Apple-style" landing page presentation without causing jank or scroll-jacking was tricky, as standard CSS animations don't bind natively to the user's scroll depth.
*The Solution:* I utilized `ReactLenis` to hijack the native scroll wheel for inertial physics, and paired it with Framer Motion's `useScroll` and `useTransform` hooks. By mapping elements' opacity, scale, and Y-axis offsets directly via an interpolated array across a massive 600vh container, I created a flawlessly smooth cinematic tracking experience.

**Open Innovation**

TraceX fits perfectly into the **Open Innovation** track because it doesn't just iterate on an existing cybersecurity tool category—it invents a novel approach to threat intelligence by bridging the gap between flat OSINT data and autonomous visual mapping. 

While traditional OSINT platforms require analysts to manually query APIs and mentally piece together the findings, TraceX introduces an **Autonomous Graph Expansion Engine**. It takes a single string of data and independently cascades through 45+ endpoints, making recursive logical leaps on its own (e.g., *Phone → Aadhaar → Vehicle & Emails → Dark Web Breaches*), and mathematically plots them into an interactive DAGRE node hierarchy in real-time.

By merging automated recursive data gathering, real-time hierarchical UI rendering, and deep dark web intelligence synthesis into a zero-touch "fire-and-forget" pipeline, TraceX represents a leap forward in how we conduct identity resolution. It empowers small security teams to achieve the analytic throughput of a massive intelligence agency, demonstrating exactly the kind of out-of-the-box system architecture that open innovation is meant to champion.

**The problem it solves**

🚶‍♂️ The Problem Queless Solves
Every day, millions of people physically queue at service centers — hospitals, banks, government offices, post offices. This creates a cascade of real human problems:

⏳ Time Poverty
People spend hours doing absolutely nothing — just standing and waiting. For a daily wage worker, every hour in a queue is an hour of lost income. For a parent, it's time away from their children. Time is the one resource nobody can get back.
🏥 Health & Safety Risks
Crowded waiting rooms are hotspots for illness transmission. The elderly, immunocompromised, and sick are forced to sit in close proximity with strangers — ironically, at hospitals — for extended periods.
😓 Dignity & Stress
Nobody should have to wake up at 5 AM to "get a good spot in line." The anxiety of not knowing how long the wait will be, losing your place, or arriving only to be turned away is a daily source of stress for vulnerable populations.
📉 Inefficiency at the Institution Level
Service centers can't predict footfall, leading to either overwhelmed staff or idle resources. Crowds create chaos, complaints, and poor service quality.

✅ What Queless Enables
Use CaseHow Queless Helps🏥 HospitalsPatients register from home, arrive only at their slot — no crowded waiting rooms🏦 BanksCustomers plan their visit around a confirmed time, not luck🏛️ Government OfficesCitizens avoid half-day waits for a 10-minute task👴 Elderly & DisabledCan queue remotely without physically enduring long stands👷 Daily Wage WorkersKnow exactly when to arrive — protecting their work hours🤒 Sick PatientsReduce exposure time in crowded medical facilities

💡 The Shift Queless Creates

Before Queless: Show up → Wait → Hope → Maybe get served
After Queless: Register online → Get a slot → Arrive on time → Get served

It doesn't reinvent the queue. It just removes the suffering from it — making an unavoidable civic process humane, predictable, and respectful of people's time.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem
The world generates 2.5 million news articles every single day. Most people read zero of them. Not because they don't care — but because staying informed has become a chore. A wall of anxiety-inducing headlines, dry summaries, and zero personality. Gen-Z didn't stop caring about the world. They stopped tolerating boring delivery.
62% of people under 25 actively avoid the news. Not because they're uninformed — because the news is exhausting.

What People Deal With Today
Information overload — dozens of apps, hundreds of notifications, zero context on what actually matters today. News fatigue — every headline feels heavy, urgent, and draining. Late to every trend — the internet moves in 48-hour cycles; by the time you understand a meme or phrase, it's already cringe. No personality — every news app feels identical: blue links, gray text, stock photos. Passive consumption — you scroll, you forget, you learned nothing by evening.

What ContextCrash Does
ContextCrash is your daily AI-powered news brief — beautiful, voice-driven, and genuinely funny. Get 5 curated cards every morning — the only stories that actually matter today. Each card is visually rich with a full image, punchy headline, and 2-sentence summary written in plain human language. Tap "Read to me" and your chosen AI narrator reads the card aloud in one of 4 personalities: The Sarcastic, The Dramatic, The Conspiracy Guy, or The Aunty. The feed learns from every swipe and reaction, becoming more you every single day.

The Core Insight
The news doesn't need to change. The experience does. When your Aunty narrator says "arre yaar, the government did WHAT? Tch tch tch..." about a policy change — you remember it. That's not entertainment replacing news. That's entertainment making news stick.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges We Ran Into

---

### 1. 🤖 Claude API Rate Limits Killing the Live Demo

**The Problem**

During our first live test, we had 4 team members simultaneously
hitting the "Read to me" button to test different vibes on the same
article. Claude API rate-limited us mid-demo. The voice button just
spun forever. Worst possible timing.

**How We Fixed It**

We completely rethought when AI generation happens.
Instead of calling Claude *when the user taps the button*,
we moved all generation to the **scraping pipeline** —
the moment an article enters our database, we pre-generate
all 4 vibe contents immediately and store them in Redis.

By demo time, every article already had its Sarcastic, Dramatic,
Conspiracy, and Aunty text ready. Tapping "Read to me" became
a Redis cache hit — response under 50ms, zero API calls during
the demo. The rate limit problem became architecturally impossible.

> **Lesson:** Don't solve performance problems with faster code.
> Solve them by doing the work earlier.

---

### 2. 🎙️ Web Speech API Sounding Completely Robotic

**The Problem**

When we first implemented voice, every vibe sounded identical —
the same flat, robotic monotone regardless of whether it was
"The Aunty" or "The Dramatic." The personality was in the text
but completely lost in the audio. It defeated the entire point.

**How We Fixed It**

We spent an embarrassing amount of time tweaking
`SpeechSynthesisUtterance` parameters — rate, pitch, volume —
for each vibe until they felt genuinely different:

- Dramatic: rate 0.82, pitch 0.80 — slow and ominous
- Aunty: rate 1.08, pitch 1.30 — fast and gossipy
- Sarcastic: rate 0.90, pitch 0.95 — slow and unbothered
- Conspiracy: rate 1.00, pitch 1.05 — urgent and suspicious

The bigger fix was in the **prompt engineering** —
we instructed Claude to write "...sigh..." and "..." as literal
text in the output, which the speech engine reads as natural pauses.
The Dramatic narrator pausing before "This. Changes. Everything."
sounds completely different from the same words spoken flat.
Text structure became our audio direction.

> **Lesson:** The voice personality lives in the writing,
> not just the speech settings.

---

### 3. 🕷️ Reddit Scraper Returning Inconsistent Data

**The Problem**

Reddit's public JSON API was our primary source for viral and
culture content. But the response structure changed depending on
the subreddit, post type, and whether the post was a text post,
image, video, or external link. Our normalizer kept crashing on
edge cases — posts with no body text, deleted posts that still
appeared in the feed, NSFW posts slipping through, and crossposted
content with nested data structures three levels deep.

**How We Fixed It**

We built a defensive `cleaner.ts` normalizer that treated every
field as potentially undefined. Every access was optional-chained.
We added a validation step after normalization that checked
for minimum required fields — if a post didn't have a title,
a URL, and at least 100 characters of content, it was silently
dropped rather than crashing the pipeline.

We also added a content filter layer — checking post flairs,
subreddit tags, and a keyword blocklist to prevent inappropriate
content from entering the article database at all.

> **Lesson:** External APIs are contracts with strangers.
> Trust nothing. Validate everything.

---

### 4. 🔄 Preference Scores Converging Too Fast

**The Problem**

Early testing showed that after just 15-20 interactions,
the personalized feed became an echo chamber. If you swiped
right on 5 Tech articles in a row, your Tech score shot to 0.9
and the feed became almost entirely Tech content. Users in testing
said it felt "trapped" and "repetitive" after day 2.

**How We Fixed It**

Two changes fixed this completely.

First, we introduced **exponential moving average** for score updates:
`newScore = 0.9 × currentScore + 0.1 × newSignal`
instead of direct addition. This made scores change gradually,
preventing a single session of similar content from dominating
the entire profile.

Second, we hardcoded a **20% discovery quota** in the feed
generation algorithm. No matter what your scores say,
2 out of every 10 cards are randomly selected from categories
you haven't heavily engaged with. This keeps the feed feeling
fresh and occasionally surprises users with content they
didn't know they'd enjoy — which then naturally expands
their preference profile over time.

> **Lesson:** Personalization without diversity
> isn't personalization — it's a filter bubble.

---

### 5. ⏱️ 8-Hour Time Crunch — What We Cut and Why

**The Problem**

Our original scope included push notifications with vibe
personality, a social layer showing friends' saved articles,
and a full onboarding tutorial animation. By hour 5 it was
clear we couldn't ship all of it with the quality bar we'd set.

**How We Fixed It**

We made a ruthless prioritization call:
**cut anything that doesn't affect the demo's wow moment.

### SubTrack - Subscription Manager
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/subtrack-subscription-management-and-alert-system-1590) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/srinjoy2075/sub-sense/tree/main) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co)

> Your subscriptions, visualized and optimized.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![EmailJS](https://img.shields.io/badge/EmailJS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SubTrack is a smart subscription management dashboard designed to help users track, analyze, and optimize their recurring expenses. In today’s digital world, people rely on numerous subscription services such as streaming platforms, cloud storage, productivity tools, news platforms, and memberships. While each individual subscription may seem small, the combined cost often becomes significant over time. Unfortunately, many users lose track of these recurring payments, leading to unexpected charges and unnecessary spending. SubTrack was built to solve this problem by providing a centralized platform where users can monitor all their subscriptions and gain clear insights into their spending habits.

The core idea behind SubTrack is to transform hidden recurring costs into meaningful financial insights. The platform allows users to add and manage their subscriptions in a clean and intuitive dashboard. Each subscription displays important details such as the service name, category, price, renewal date, and the number of days remaining until the next payment. By organizing this information in one place, users gain immediate visibility into where their money is going and which services are due for renewal soon.

One of the most powerful aspects of SubTrack is its analytics capability. The dashboard automatically calculates the user’s total monthly spending and projects the yearly cost based on their current subscriptions. It also breaks down spending by categories such as productivity, entertainment, news, and cloud services. This allows users to quickly identify which types of services consume the majority of their budget. These insights help users make smarter financial decisions and potentially eliminate unnecessary subscriptions.

SubTrack also provides renewal awareness features to prevent unexpected charges. The system highlights subscriptions that are close to renewal and shows how many days remain before the next billing cycle. This gives users enough time to review their subscriptions and cancel services they no longer need. Instead of discovering a charge after it happens, users are empowered with advance visibility into upcoming payments.

The user interface of SubTrack was designed with clarity and simplicity in mind. The platform uses a modern dark-themed dashboard with minimal design elements, organized cards, and intuitive visualizations. Spending analytics, subscription lists, and smart insights are displayed in a structured layout that allows users to understand their financial activity at a glance. Interactive components and hover effects enhance the user experience while keeping the interface clean and professional.

This project was developed during an 8-hour hackathon with the goal of creating a practical tool that addresses a common real-world problem. SubTrack demonstrates how simple data organization and analytics can significantly improve financial awareness. By bringing subscription tracking, spending analytics, and renewal insights together in a single platform, SubTrack helps users regain control over their recurring expenses.

In the future, SubTrack can be expanded with additional capabilities such as automatic subscription detection from emails or bank statements, AI-powered spending recommendations, personalized cost-saving insights, and notification systems for renewal reminders. These enhancements would further strengthen the platform’s ability to act as a complete subscription intelligence tool for modern digital consumers.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1b27eec12b2740d2b84f7484ffc3488d/5e079a33-661f-4c82-be64-c32695697589.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced while building SubTrack was handling subscriptions with different billing cycles and converting them into meaningful analytics. Some services charge users monthly while others charge annually, which made it difficult to calculate total spending accurately. In the early stages of development, the dashboard simply summed up the subscription prices directly. This created misleading insights because a yearly plan like Amazon Prime (₹1499/year) appeared smaller compared to a monthly service like a ₹649/month streaming subscription, even though their long-term financial impact was different. To solve this, we introduced a normalization step in our calculation logic. Every subscription is converted into a monthly equivalent before performing analytics. Monthly subscriptions remain unchanged, while yearly subscriptions are divided by twelve. This allowed us to generate accurate metrics such as total monthly spending, yearly projections, and category-wise analytics.

Another hurdle we encountered was designing a dashboard that could present multiple analytics insights without becoming visually cluttered. As we added spending charts, subscription lists, renewal indicators, and advisor insights, the interface initially became crowded and difficult to navigate. We addressed this by restructuring the layout into modular dashboard cards and grouping related information into dedicated sections. Insights were moved into a separate advisor panel, while financial metrics were displayed in highlight cards at the top of the dashboard. This significantly improved readability and made the interface feel more structured and intuitive. Overcoming these challenges helped us create a system that not only performs accurate financial analysis but also presents information in a clear and user-friendly way.

**Sustainability**

Yes, the project can fall under sustainability because it promotes responsible financial consumption and resource awareness. SubTrack helps users track their recurring subscriptions, analyze their spending patterns, and identify services they no longer use. By giving clear insights into monthly and yearly expenses and highlighting upcoming renewals, the platform encourages users to cancel unnecessary subscriptions and avoid wasteful spending. This supports financial sustainability by helping individuals manage their resources more efficiently and develop more mindful digital consumption habits.

### STAZE
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/staze-c290) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Xtra-Org/staze) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co)

> Stabilize, Act, Save

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

STAZE solves the gap between an emergency happening and professional medical help arriving. In those first few minutes, bystanders often panic, search generic advice, or do not know what action to take first. STAZE turns a typed or spoken emergency description into immediate condition-specific guidance, CPR support, symptom check-ins, and nearby hospital recommendations, helping non-medical users act faster, safer, and with more confidence.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was reliability in real-world conditions. Voice recognition behaved differently across browsers, hospital lookup services could fail or rate-limit, and AI responses could sometimes become too generic for urgent medical scenarios. I handled this by adding offline fallback protocols, improving condition detection for trauma/burn/injury cases, switching hospital search to OpenStreetMap-based services, and making the UI continue working even when AI or network services were degraded.

### PlicyPilot

> See the unseen. Block the unwanted.

![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Room Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Room%20Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![jetpack compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/jetpack%20compose-333333?style=flat-square) ![material 3](https://img.shields.io/badge/material%203-333333?style=flat-square) ![Abuseipdb](https://img.shields.io/badge/Abuseipdb-333333?style=flat-square) ![WorkManager](https://img.shields.io/badge/WorkManager-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android PdfDocument API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20PdfDocument%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Mobile Privacy Black Box**

Modern smartphones operate as a black box. While users have granular control over app permissions like microphone or camera access, they have zero visibility into network activity. The moment an app is installed, it can silently communicate with third-party data brokers, telemetry servers, and hidden ad networks in the background.

Current solutions on the market are fundamentally flawed:

Traditional Ad-Blockers: Only operate at the browser level, leaving native applications free to harvest data.

Commercial VPNs: Require you to route all of your personal traffic through a third-party server, essentially asking you to trade one privacy risk for another.

DNS Sinkholes: Only block domain names (Port 53). If an app connects directly to a hardcoded malicious IP address, DNS blockers are completely blind to it.

Users lack a transparent, trustless, and local method to monitor and restrict the outbound data leaving their devices.

🛡️ The Solution: **Innova**
Innova bridges this gap by acting as a zero-trust, on-device network firewall.

By leveraging Android's local VpnService API, Innova intercepts raw TCP and UDP packets directly at the OS level. It analyzes the traffic, attributes it to the specific app that generated it, and evaluates the destination against a comprehensive Threat Engine. If a packet is flagged as malicious tracking or telemetry, Innova silently drops it before it ever reaches the network interface.

Because the interception and evaluation loop happens entirely on the local CPU, no user data is ever sent to a cloud server for analysis.

💡 **What Can People Use It For? (Real-World Applications)**
Innova transforms mobile security from a passive experience into an active, transparent defense mechanism. It makes digital life safer and more efficient in several ways:

1. Granular App Auditing & Transparency
Users can open the Innova Dashboard to view a real-time, packet-by-packet feed of their device's network activity. It demystifies app behavior by answering exactly which app is connecting to which server. If a simple calculator app is pinging a server in a foreign country, Innova exposes it instantly.

2. Proactive Privacy Protection
For the everyday user, Innova acts as an invisible shield. By automatically dropping connections to known trackers, ad-networks, and profiling domains, it prevents third parties from building digital fingerprints of the user's habits, location, and app usage.

3. Resource Optimization (Battery & Bandwidth)
Background tracking is incredibly resource-intensive. Apps constantly waking up the phone's cellular radio to send small telemetry payloads drain the battery and consume mobile data. By severing these connections at the IP level, Innova naturally extends device battery life and saves bandwidth.

4. Safer Usage of Untrusted Applications
Whether downloading a free-to-play mobile game loaded with SDKs or a utility app with questionable origins, users can run Innova in the background to ensure that the app is physically incapable of phoning home to malicious servers.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a packet-level firewall on Android is essentially fighting the Operating System at every turn. Because Innova processes raw network traffic in real-time, the margins for error were zero. Here are the major hurdles we faced and how we engineered our way out of them:

1. Mastering Java NIO and Buffer Management (Memory Exhaustion)
The Hurdle: To achieve zero-latency packet interception, we couldn't use standard Java I/O streams. We had to use Java NIO (Non-blocking I/O) and read raw ByteBuffer streams directly from the Android VpnService FileDescriptor. Initially, creating a new ByteBuffer for every single packet (thousands per second) caused the Android Garbage Collector to go into overdrive, creating massive micro-stutters and eventual OutOfMemory (OOM) crashes. Furthermore, manually tracking buffer positions, limits, and capacities often resulted in fatal BufferUnderflowExceptions when malformed packets arrived.
The Fix: We implemented a ByteBufferPool to reuse a fixed pool of memory blocks rather than allocating new ones. We also had to deeply understand Java NIO's state mechanics—meticulously calling .flip() before reading and .clear() before writing—to shuttle bytes between the OS and our Threat Engine without corrupting the payloads. Finally, we wrapped the NIO packet parsing in an impenetrable try-catch shield so that corrupted background packets would be safely discarded instead of crashing the main thread.

2. The "200 Packets-per-Second" UI Freeze (Performance Bottleneck)
The Hurdle: When routing an entire device's internet through our app, opening a single webpage triggers hundreds of TCP handshakes, DNS lookups, and image downloads. Initially, our Kotlin VpnBridge was analyzing every single packet, querying the SQLite database, checking the Threat Engine, and forcing the Jetpack Compose UI to redraw 200 times a second. This instantly melted the CPU and caused massive Application Not Responding (ANR) freezes.
The Fix: We implemented Aggressive Memoization and Async Fire-and-Forget Logging. We built a ConcurrentHashMap to cache the safety status of IP addresses. If packet #1 to Google is marked safe, packets #2 through #200 bypass the Threat Engine entirely. We then offloaded all database writes and App Attribution lookups to background Kotlin Coroutines (Dispatchers.IO), reducing packet processing time to literal microseconds.

3. The 3-Minute File Descriptor Leak
The Hurdle: During stress testing, the VPN would work flawlessly for exactly 3 minutes and then violently crash. We discovered a File Descriptor Leak. To figure out which app sent a packet, our AppAttributionHelper was reading Android's internal /proc/net/tcp files. With thousands of packets flowing, we hit Android's hard limit of 1,024 open files, and the OS instantly assassinated our network connection.
The Fix: We implemented a "Duct-Tape Cache" to limit file reads. We capped the attribution cache to 200 unique connections. Once the limit is reached, the app stops opening system files and gracefully falls back to labeling traffic as a "Background App."

4. The "No DNS" Blackhole
The Hurdle: When we first successfully established the VPN tunnel, the entire phone lost internet access. The VPN was running, but browsers simply said "This site can't be reached." We realized that by intercepting all traffic, we accidentally blinded the phone's ability to resolve Domain Names (DNS).
The Fix: We had to implement a DNS Failsafe. First, we updated the Kotlin packet bridge to completely ignore and auto-pass any traffic on Port 53 (the universal DNS port). Second, we injected public DNS servers (Google's 8.8.8.8 and Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1) directly into the VpnService.Builder routing table so the Android OS knew how to translate domains inside our custom tunnel.

5. The Silent 10-Second Background Execution Kill
The Hurdle: We noticed that if we started the VPN and then minimized the app to the background, it would die exactly 10 seconds later.
The Fix: We ran head-first into Android's strict background execution limits. Because we were running a heavy networking loop, Android assumed we were a rogue battery-draining app. We fixed this by elevating our Java VPN class to a Foreground Service, binding it to a persistent Notification Channel (startForeground). By fulfilling the OS's foreground contract, Android granted us the permissions needed to keep the firewall running indefinitely.

### cryptika
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cryptika-5de3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/KerberoSec/Cryptika) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> Burn the keys, not the UX

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem Cryptika Solves
Every mainstream messenger -WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal - asks you to hand over a phone number, an email, or some permanent identity before you can say a single word. That metadata alone is enough to build a social graph, trace connections, and surveil users — even if the message content is encrypted. The server always knows who is talking to whom, when, and how often.

Cryptika solves this by treating identity as disposable and communication as ephemeral:

No accounts, no passwords, no phone numbers. You pick a temporary secret name, connect with someone, and the name is replaced by a short UUID. There's nothing permanent to subpoena or leak.
Ephemeral 30-minute sessions. After a contact request is accepted, the session self-destructs — all messages, crypto keys, and contact records are wiped. Not "deleted" — the ratchet keys are zeroized in memory and the per-message Keystore entries are destroyed.
The server is a blind relay. It routes opaque binary blobs between identity hashes. It never sees plaintext, never stores messages, and after credential burning, can't even re-authenticate the JWT that was used.
Screen-off = full wipe. If the device screen locks, every session is destroyed, purge signals are sent to all peers, auth tokens are cleared, and the app restarts at the entry screen. A stolen locked phone yields nothing.
Peer-aware logout. When one user disconnects, the other user's messages are purged too — not just locally, but cryptographically. Neither side retains anything.
In short: Cryptika is built for conversations that should leave no trace — on the device, on the server, or in between.

Challenges We Ran Into
1. Passwordless auth that still works with a password-expecting server. The original design had full username/password registration and login. Stripping that down to "just enter a name" meant the client still had to satisfy the server's API contract. We solved this by deriving a deterministic password from the Ed25519 identity key (SHA-256(publicKey) → Base64), making the password invisible to the user while keeping the server happy. The client tries to register first and silently falls back to login if the name is taken.

2. Coordinating the DH handshake over an unreliable relay. Both peers send an X25519 offer simultaneously over WebSocket, but there's no guarantee of ordering. A late-joining peer might miss the initial offer entirely. We had to implement offer echoing — when a peer receives the other's offer, it re-sends its own stored offer so both sides can derive the same session key. Getting this idempotent (ignoring duplicate handshakes once a MessageProcessor exists) without race conditions across coroutines required careful @Volatile state management in BackgroundConnectionManager.

3. Forward secrecy with a single hash ratchet. A proper Double Ratchet (Signal protocol) wasn't feasible in the time frame, so we used a simpler SHA-256 hash ratchet where K_n = SHA-256(K_{n-1}). This gives forward secrecy (compromising K_n doesn't reveal K_{n-1}) but not post-compromise security. The bigger challenge was handling out-of-order messages — relay packets don't arrive in order. We implemented a lookahead buffer (up to 50 keys cached for 30 seconds) so the receiver can pre-compute future ratchet keys without breaking the chain.

4. Sending purge signals before the socket tears down. When a user logs out, we need to encrypt and send __PURGE__ to every connected peer before the WebSocket disconnects. But logout can be triggered from the screen-off broadcast receiver, which fires with very little time before the process is killed. We added a 300ms flush delay after sending purge packets, which is a tradeoff — too short and packets might not leave the buffer; too long and the OS kills the process. Wrapping this in a foreground service's lifecycle helped, but it's inherently best-effort.

5. Per-message encryption at rest with Android Keystore. Every message is encrypted in transit (ChaCha20-Poly1305 via the ratchet) and then re-encrypted at rest with a unique AES-256-GCM key from Android Keystore before being written to SQLCipher. This means even if someone extracts the database file and the database passphrase, each message row requires its own Keystore key to decrypt. The challenge was key lifecycle — on message expiry or purge, we need to delete the Keystore entry too, and orphaned keys (from crashed deletions) had to be handled gracefully.

6. Secure keyboard without breaking UX. System keyboards (GBoard, SwiftKey) can log keystrokes, predict text, and sync to the cloud. We built an in-app keyboard (SecureKeyboard) that bypasses the IME entirely. The input fields are readOnly = true and all input routes through the custom keyboard composable. The challenge was making this not feel terrible — supporting lowercase, uppercase, symbols, backspace, and done actions while keeping it performant inside a Compose bottom bar that coexists with chat input, expiry picker

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a truly ephemeral and identity-free system introduced several technical challenges. Removing traditional authentication meant we had to implement passwordless access while still satisfying a server API designed for username/password logins, which we solved by deriving a deterministic password from the user’s Ed25519 identity key. Establishing a secure Diffie–Hellman key exchange between peers over an unreliable WebSocket relay required idempotent handshake logic so both parties could derive the same shared secret even when messages arrived out of order. Achieving forward secrecy within limited development time led us to implement a SHA-256 hash ratchet with a lookahead buffer to handle out-of-order messages without breaking the chain. On the device side, securely storing messages required a layered approach: each message is encrypted again at rest using AES-256-GCM keys from Android Keystore before being stored in SQLCipher, creating complex key-lifecycle management during expiry or purge events. Finally, Android itself posed reliability challenges—maintaining WebSocket connectivity through Doze mode, ensuring purge signals are sent before logout or screen lock, and coordinating foreground services and coroutine scopes so that session state remains consistent without leaking sensitive data.

> Your Network. Your Rules.Total Visibility.

![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![CMake](https://img.shields.io/badge/CMake-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![jetpack compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/jetpack%20compose-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSocket](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSocket-333333?style=flat-square) ![IntelOwl API](https://img.shields.io/badge/IntelOwl%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![VPN Service API](https://img.shields.io/badge/VPN%20Service%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most Android users have no idea what their installed apps are doing behind the scenes like which app are silently connecting to tracking servers, leaking personal data to third-party domains, or communicating with known malicious infrastructure.

Traditional firewalls only block or allow traffic; they don't tell you where your data is going, what protocol is being used, or whether a destination is a threat. Users are left blind to the network behavior of the very apps they trust daily. 

NetSecure solves this by providing ***real-time, per-app deep packet inspection directly on the device i.e. capturing every connection***, classifying traffic using **nDPI protocol analysis**, geo-locating destination servers via **MaxMind**, and automatically scanning suspicious domains and IPs through **IntelOwl threat intelligence.**

It transforms an opaque, invisible attack surface into **a transparent, actionable dashboard ,giving users and security researchers full visibility into their device's network activity without requiring root access, external hardware, or cloud-based proxies.**

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Native Cross-Compilation : Getting four C libraries (zdtun, nDPI, libpcap, PCAPdroid engine) to compile under Android NDK across four CPU architectures required heavy CMake customization and header path patching.

2. Rootless Packet Capture : Android blocks raw sockets without root. We routed all traffic through a VPN TUN interface with split routes, feeding packets to the native engine while avoiding infinite loops from capturing our own traffic.

3. **DNS Visibility :** Android's Private DNS (DNS-over-TLS) hides domain names from the VPN tunnel. We had to force fallback to plain DNS so nDPI and IntelOwl can actually see what domains apps connect to.

4. **Real-Time UI at Scale :** Thousands of connections per second from native code would crush Compose. Solved with batched StateFlow updates and capped rendering to keep the UI at 60fps.

5. **JavaMail on Android :** SMTP via javax.mail conflicts with Android's internal stubs. Required the android-mail fork, META-INF packaging exclusions, and encrypted credential storage via AndroidKeyStore.

6. **Async Threat Intelligence :** IntelOwl API calls are slow. Scanning hundreds of domains/IPs needed fully async coroutine pipelines with cooldowns, retries, and reactive flows to avoid blocking the UI.

7. **MaxMind as Source Submodule :** Including the GeoIP reader as a source-level Gradle dependency instead of a JAR meant managing a secondary Java source tree alongside Kotlin and bundling the .mmdb asset correctly.

**The problem it solves**

The Invisible Network Threat

Modern mobile apps constantly communicate with remote servers, but users have no visibility into this network activity.

Key Issues

1. Hidden Data Transmission
Apps silently send data such as device information, usage behavior, and analytics to remote servers without user awareness.

2. No App-Level Network Transparency
Existing tools show network traffic but cannot tell which specific app generated each connection.

3. Limited Access to Security Tools
Advanced network analysis tools like Wireshark or tcpdump require root access or technical expertise, making them inaccessible to everyday users.

4. Growing Privacy Risks
Malicious apps or compromised updates can perform data exfiltration, DNS tunneling, or command-and-control communication without detection.

The Core Problem

Users cannot see, understand, or control how their apps communicate over the internet.

This creates a major transparency gap in mobile cybersecurity.
