Here is a formal, professional version of "The Problem It Solves" for your Devfolio submission. This version is written to appeal to technical judges by using industry-standard terminology like attack vectors, runtime behavioral analysis, and security-privacy gap.

🛑 The Problem It Solves
Mobile security remains a critical concern as application architectures become increasingly complex. Most existing security solutions suffer from a "Visibility Gap", leaving users vulnerable in two primary areas:

Static Opaqueness: Standard users have no way to inspect the "DNA" of an APK. Malicious elements—such as hardcoded AWS/Firebase credentials, embedded advertisement trackers, and insecure API endpoints—remain hidden within the compiled code, providing a permanent backdoor for data exfiltration.

Lack of Runtime Behavioral Analysis: Conventional antivirus tools often miss "Zero-Day" threats that appear benign during installation but exhibit malicious behavior once launched. There is a significant lack of tools that provide real-time alerts when high-risk applications initiate unauthorized background processes or access sensitive system UI.

The Complexity Barrier: Professional forensic tools like MobSF are typically restricted to security researchers and require complex server environments. There is no streamlined bridge that brings this enterprise-grade Deep Static Analysis to a mobile-first interface for real-time auditing.

Our Solution: We have engineered a Hybrid Vulnerability Assessment Tool that bridges this gap. By integrating the MobSF REST API, our platform deconstructs application binaries to expose latent code-level risks. Simultaneously, it employs a custom-built Dynamic Monitoring Engine that tracks application lifecycles in real-time. This dual-layered approach ensures that threats are caught both in the code (Static) and in action (Dynamic), providing a comprehensive security posture for the end-user.

**Challenges we ran into**

Gemini said
Bhai, Devfolio par content ekdum "Problem-Solution" aur "Technical Depth" wala hona chahiye. Judges wahan ye dekhte hain ki tumne sirf code copy nahi kiya, balki actual engineering challenges solve kiye hain.

Is content ko copy-paste kar le, ye tere NIT Hamirpur background aur project ki hybrid approach ko bohot achhe se highlight karega:

🛑 The Problem It Solves
Most mobile security apps are either too basic (just checking permissions) or too complex for a regular user. We identified three major gaps:

The "Black Box" Problem: Users don't know what happens inside an app's code (hardcoded keys, hidden trackers).

Lack of Runtime Awareness: Even if an app looks safe, it can perform malicious actions (like opening the camera or mic) the moment it is launched.

Fragmented Security: There is no single tool that combines Static Analysis (scanning the APK) with Dynamic Monitoring (tracking real-time behavior).

Our Solution: We built a Hybrid Vulnerability Scanner. It uses the industry-standard MobSF REST API to deconstruct APKs for hidden code vulnerabilities while simultaneously running a custom Android background engine to detect and log high-risk app launches (like WhatsApp/Telegram) in real-time.

🛠 Challenges I Ran Into
Bypassing Android's Background Restrictions: Modern Android versions (13/14) are very aggressive in killing background processes. Implementing a persistent tracker that doesn't drain the battery or get "killed" by the OS was a major hurdle. We solved this by implementing a lightweight thread architecture and using UsageStatsManager with a Handler loop to ensure efficiency without overhead.

REST API Integration for Large Binary Files: Uploading a 50MB+ APK file from a mobile device to a local server over a shaky Wi-Fi network often resulted in timeouts. I had to optimize the OkHttp client with custom connectTimeout and readTimeout settings (up to 5 minutes) and implement a MultipartBody POST request to ensure the binary data reached the MobSF engine intact.

Handling Restricted OS Settings: During development, we realized that sideloaded apps are blocked from accessing sensitive permissions (like Accessibility and Usage Stats) by default. Navigating the "Restricted Settings" UI and educating the user on how to safely grant these high-privilege permissions was a UX challenge that taught me a lot about Android's Security Sandboxing.

Local Environment Synchronization: Setting up a cross-platform communication bridge between an Android device and a local Docker/Python-based MobSF server required deep networking knowledge, specifically managing IPv4 addresses, port forwarding (8000), and bypassing Cleartext Traffic restrictions in the Android Manifest.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/antaaf-50c4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> Android Network Traffic Analyzer & Active Firewall

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ANTAAF is a privacy-focused Android network monitoring tool. It solves several key problems:

🔒 1. Network Privacy & Transparency
Most apps on your phone make network connections you don't know about — sending data to trackers, analytics servers, or unknown destinations. ANTAAF lets you see every connection every app makes, giving you full visibility into what's happening on your device behind the scenes.

🚫 2. No Root Required
Traditional packet capture on Android requires root access. ANTAAF works around this by simulating a local VPN — it intercepts all traffic locally on the device without needing root and without sending data to any remote VPN server.

🔍 3. Deep Traffic Inspection
Extract SNI, DNS queries, HTTP URLs, and remote IPs
Inspect HTTP requests/responses with built-in decoders
Decrypt HTTPS/TLS traffic (via mitmproxy)
View full payload as hexdump or text
📦 4. Traffic Export & Analysis
Dump traffic to PCAP files (Wireshark-compatible), stream to a remote receiver for real-time analysis, or download from a browser.

🛡️ 5. Traffic Filtering & Anomaly Detection
Create rules to filter known-good traffic, making it easy to spot suspicious or anomalous connections.

🌍 6. Geolocation of Servers
Identifies the country and ASN of remote servers via offline DB lookups, so you know where your data is going.

**Challenges we ran into**

🔴 1. Package Rename Gone Wrong
A package rename operation resulted in truncated/corrupted source files, causing widespread compilation errors across the project. This required restoring corrupted files and fixing package name mismatches to get the project building again. (Conversations: "Fixing Compilation Errors" x2)

🔴 2. Compilation & Build Issues
Even after fixing the rename, you dealt with persistent compilation errors from the ./gradlew assembleStandardDebug build — likely cascading issues from the corrupted files and mismatched references throughout the codebase.

🟡 3. Code Quality & Stability Bugs
You uncovered several bugs in core files like PCAPdroid.java and CaptureService.java:

Null pointer exceptions
Android 13+ API compliance issues
Thread-safety problems with lazy initialization and SharedPreferences mutation
🟡 4. UI Refactoring Complexity
Replacing the side drawer navigation with a bottom navigation bar required careful restructuring to:

Avoid toolbar/content overflow issues
Maintain secondary options via a "More" tab
Refine the dark mode theme for a premium look without breaking the layout
🟡 5. Adding Chart Visualizations
Integrating MPAndroidChart for network data visualization (per-app network graphs, data usage charts) was non-trivial — it required:

Wiring up data from ConnectionsRegister and StatsActivity
Adding a new "Network Graph" tab to AppDetailsActivity
Building export/share functionality for the graphs and reports
Fixing text visibility issues (e.g., white text on light backgrounds in app_overview.xml)
🟠 6. Feasibility of Web Conversion
You explored converting the Android app into a website with the same functionality — ultimately a complex challenge since ANTAAF relies heavily on Android-specific APIs (VPN service, packet capture, system app enumeration) that don't have direct web equivalents.

Summary

Build	Cascading compilation errors	🔴 Critical

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern smartphones contain dozens or even hundreds of installed applications. Many of these apps request access to sensitive device resources such as the camera, microphone, location, contacts, SMS, and storage. Most users grant these permissions without fully understanding the security implications.
This creates several risks:
Personal data exposure
Unauthorized location tracking
Contact and SMS data harvesting
Media capture and remote upload
Privacy violations through excessive permissions
Existing mobile security tools often provide either very limited insights or overly technical reports that are difficult for average users to understand.
SentinelAI solves this problem by providing an intelligent mobile app vulnerability scanner that analyzes installed applications and translates complex security information into clear and actionable insights.
The system scans installed apps, analyzes their permissions and behaviors, identifies risky permission combinations, and generates a security score and risk explanation.
Users can use SentinelAI to:
Identify potentially risky apps installed on their device
Understand why certain permissions may pose privacy risks
Detect suspicious permission combinations such as camera + internet or location + internet
Receive AI-generated explanations of security threats
Get recommendations for improving device privacy and security
By combining automated analysis with AI-based explanations, SentinelAI helps users make more informed decisions about app permissions and device security.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges during development was designing a meaningful risk scoring system for mobile applications.
Initially, the prototype used a simple rule-based approach where each risky permission reduced the security score using basic if-else logic. However, this approach was too simplistic and did not accurately represent real security risks.
To improve the system, we redesigned the risk model to consider multiple factors such as:
High-risk and medium-risk permissions
Permission density (apps requesting too many permissions)
Dangerous permission combinations
Network-related risks such as sensitive permissions combined with internet access
This required restructuring the analysis logic into a more modular architecture and designing a weighted risk scoring model.
Another challenge involved integrating AI-based explanations into the application. Since AI responses must be generated asynchronously, we had to handle API calls carefully to avoid blocking the UI. This was solved using Kotlin coroutines and asynchronous state handling in Jetpack Compose.
Finally, visualizing security insights in a way that users could easily understand was another challenge. To address this, we implemented features such as:
Risk distribution charts
Permission interaction graphs
Security dashboards
These visual components made the results much easier to interpret and improved the overall usability of the application.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lowkey-3169) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ayush00git/lowkey) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> a p2p e2e chat app. literal lowkey

![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebRTC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebRTC-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Here's a compelling "The Problem It Solves" for Lowkey:

---

## The Problem It Solves

Every mainstream messaging app — WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal — requires your **phone number**, stores your **metadata**, and routes messages through **centralized servers** they control. Even "end-to-end encrypted" apps know *who you're talking to*, *when*, *how often*, and *from where* (your IP address). This metadata alone is enough to build a complete social graph of your life.

**Lowkey eliminates all of this.**

- **No phone number, no email, no sign-up.** Pick a username and you exist. Close the app and you don't.
- **No server-stored messages.** Messages travel directly between devices via WebRTC peer-to-peer — the server only helps you *find* each other, never sees what you say.
- **No persistent identity.** There's no account to hack, no database to breach, no chat history to subpoena. Every session starts fresh.
- **Forward secrecy via DH Ratchet.** Each message turn generates fresh encryption keys. Compromising one key can't decrypt past or future messages.
- **IP anonymity via Tor.** With one toggle, your traffic routes through the Tor onion network — no single node knows both who you are and who you're talking to.

In a world where "private messaging" still means a corporation promising not to read your data, Lowkey takes a different approach: **there's nothing to read, nothing to store, and no one to trust.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. WebRTC Exposes Real IP Addresses

The biggest architectural challenge was realizing that even with E2E encryption, **WebRTC's ICE negotiation leaks both peers' real IP addresses** through ICE candidates — and the signaling server relays them, so it sees everything too. The fix was integrating Tor as a SOCKS5 proxy to route the signaling WebSocket through the onion network. This way, no single node knows both who's sending and who's receiving.

### 2. Auto-Connect Without Consent

I discovered that when User A entered User B's username, both users were **instantly connected without User B ever agreeing**. The server auto-joined both sides. The elegant fix turned out to be frontend-only — I used the existing `_isInitiator` flag to detect unsolicited connections on User B's side and gate the key exchange behind an **Accept/Decline dialog**. If User B declines, the public key is never sent, and the handshake simply never completes.

### 3. DH Ratchet: Keeping the API Clean

Implementing the Diffie-Hellman ratchet for forward secrecy was tricky because I wanted to **rotate X25519 keys on every turn change** without modifying the ChatScreen at all. The solution was encapsulating the ratchet entirely inside CryptoService — messages now carry the ratchet public key as JSON `{"rk": "...", "ct": "..."}`, but encryptMessage() and decryptMessage() still accept and return plain strings.

**Special Track**

## How Lowkey Fits Into the Track

Lowkey is a **privacy-first, zero-trust messaging application** that fits squarely into the **Security and Privacy** track.

Most messaging apps treat privacy as a feature toggle — Lowkey treats it as the architecture itself. There is no account creation, no phone number, no centralized message storage, and no metadata collection. The server's only job is to help two users find each other; after that, every message travels directly between devices over an encrypted peer-to-peer connection.

The project demonstrates three layers of applied cryptographic security:

**Layer 1 — End-to-End Encryption:** All messages are encrypted with XSalsa20-Poly1305 using a shared secret derived from X25519 key exchange. The server never sees plaintext.

**Layer 2 — Forward Secrecy via DH Ratchet:** Encryption keys rotate on every conversational turn. Even if an attacker compromises one key, they cannot decrypt past or future messages. This is the same principle used by the Signal Protocol.

**Layer 3 — Network Anonymity via Tor:** With a single toggle, all signaling traffic routes through the Tor onion network across multiple relay nodes. This ensures that no single server — not even our own — can correlate a user's real IP address with their conversation partner.

The result is a communication tool where privacy is not a promise made by a company, but a mathematical guarantee enforced by the protocol. There is nothing to log, nothing to subpoena, and nothing to breach — because the data simply never exists in a place anyone can access it.

> When chatting meets security.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

LINKUP SECURE is a comprehensive secure communication platform designed to address critical privacy and security concerns in modern digital communication. Here are the detailed problems it solves:

1. Insecure Message Communication

Problem: Traditional messaging applications often lack robust encryption, exposing sensitive conversations to interception and eavesdropping.
Solution: Implements end-to-end encryption using cryptographic protocols (as evidenced by crypto.py module) to ensure that only intended recipients can read messages. All messages are secured at the transport layer with military-grade encryption standards.
2. Weak User Authentication & Credential Management

Problem: Many communication platforms suffer from weak authentication mechanisms, leading to unauthorized account access and identity spoofing.
Solution: Provides a robust authentication system with secure credential management (see test_auth.py), protecting user accounts from unauthorized access and ensuring only verified users can communicate.
3. Lack of Privacy in Group Communications

Problem: Group conversations typically don't offer the same level of privacy and control as one-on-one messages, making sensitive group discussions vulnerable.
Solution: Enables secure group communications with managed conversations, allowing users to create and control secure group chats with encryption applied across all participants.
4. Data Exposure & Privacy Concerns

Problem: User data is often exposed in logs, analytics, or unencrypted storage, compromising privacy.
Solution: Implements intelligent data masking (as tested in test_masking.py) to automatically redact or obscure sensitive personal information while maintaining system functionality.
5. Limited Message Delivery Reliability

Problem: Messages may be lost, corrupted, or delayed without verification of safe delivery.
Solution: Provides a reliable message transport system with confirmation mechanisms (tested in test_message_transport.py) ensuring messages are delivered securely and completely.
6. Lack of Advanced Communication Features

Problem: Basic messaging doesn't support modern collaborative features like polls, surveys, or custom workflows.
Solution: Integrates AI pipelines and custom workflows (nova_ai.py), allowing users to create group polls, surveys, and custom communication pipelines for enhanced collaboration.
7. Cross-Platform Accessibility

Problem: Secure communication solutions are often limited to specific platforms, restricting user access.
Solution: Offers cross-platform support with both web and mobile applications, ensuring users can communicate securely regardless of their device.
8. Complexity in Security Implementation

Problem: Organizations struggle to implement complex encryption and security protocols themselves.
Solution: Provides an all-in-one platform with built-in encryption (crypto.py), authentication (test_auth.py), and secure transport mechanisms, eliminating the need for organizations to build these from scratch.
9. Lack of Username/Identity Management

Problem: Users need flexible identity management with the ability to update identities securely.
Solution: Implements secure username management with change capabilities (see test_username_change.py) while maintaining message history and security.
Technology Stack Used:

Backend: Python Flask (as shown in app.py, wsgi.py)
Database: SQLite (LINKUP.db)
Security: Custom cryptographic module (crypto.py)
AI/ML: Custom AI pipelines (nova_ai.py)
Deployment: Gunicorn WSGI server (gunicorn.conf.py, Procfile)
Testing: Comprehensive test suite for authentication, encryption, messaging, and features
In essence, LINKUP SECURE solves the fundamental problem of enabling secure, private, and reliable group communication for users and organizations that require enterprise-grade encryption and privacy protections while maintaining ease of use across multiple devices and platforms.

**Challenges we ran into**

Implementing dual modes likely hit UI/UX hurdles, like seamlessly switching between persistent group chats (with polls) and ephemeral Link Up rooms without confusing users. Real-time polling for groups demands efficient backend syncing (e.g., WebSockets) to handle majority votes without lag, especially in hackathons with limited testing . Encryption posed crypto challenges—choosing libs like AES or libsodium, managing keys per session, and ensuring termination deletes everything (including server-side caches) without data leaks. Edge cases like app crashes mid-chat or multi-device sync, plus scaling polls for larger groups, are common pain points in rushed prototypes .

### G-SEC
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gsec-e70b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Saksham-Chhabra/gsec) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> Privacy is never an option, it's a necessity

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

G-SEC is a high-security messaging platform designed for absolute digital privacy. Unlike standard messengers, G-SEC focuses on "invisibility"—both on the network and on the device itself. It combines military-grade end-to-end encryption (E2EE) with ephemeral "Shadow Rooms" to ensure that your conversations leave no digital footprint. The system is built on a zero-knowledge architecture, meaning the server only acts as a blind relay and can never read your messages or see your real identity.

PROBLEM STATEMENT: In an era of mass surveillance and data leaks, "private" messengers often fall short. Most popular apps still collect metadata, lack true forward secrecy, or require permanent user identifiers that link to your real-world identity. Furthermore, many apps are vulnerable to local forensics—if someone gets physical access to your phone, your chat history and identity are often exposed.

THE SOLUTION: G-SEC solves these problems through a multi-layered security

**Challenges we ran into**

Implementing the Double Ratchet Protocol: The biggest challenge was correctly implementing the Signal-style Double Ratchet algorithm from scratch using Libsodium. Managing two different "chains" (sending and receiving) and ensuring they stay synchronized across multiple devices without losing messages was difficult. I had to implement a "skipped message key" buffer to handle out-of-order delivery, which is common in mobile environments.

Asynchronous Key Exchange (X3DH): Allowing two people to establish a secure session while one is offline was a major hurdle. I had to design a "Pre-Key" system where the app generates bundles of public keys and uploads them to the server in advance. Coordinating the initial 3-way Diffie-Hellman (3DH) handshake so that both sides derive the exact same Root Key without ever communicating directly was a complex mathematical puzzle.

Native Module Compatibility & Tor Integration: I initially attempted to integrate "react-native-tor" for onion routing to hide the users' IP addresses. However, this required deep modification of the native Android build system and caused significant compatibility issues with the Expo Go environment. I spent hours debugging Gradle build failures and native bridge crashes before deciding to prioritize a stable messaging experience over the optional Tor layer for the initial demo.

Real-time Synchronization vs. Privacy: Balancing the need for real-time WebSockets for "Normal Mode" chat while using stateless HTTP long-polling for "Anonymous Mode" created a fragmented architecture. I had to build a custom MessageService that could abstract away the transport layer, so the UI wouldn't care if a message was arriving via a Persistent Socket or an HTTP fetch.

Secure Storage Size Limits: Android's hardware-backed keystore has strict limits on the size of the data it can store. I quickly realized I couldn't store entire chat histories in the SecureStore. I had to pivot to a hybrid model: storing the sensitive private keys and current Ratchet state in the hardware enclave, while storing the encrypted message local cache in a separate, less restricted storage area.

**The problem it solves**

Most people install apps without knowing what they do in the 
background. A flashlight app should never be uploading data 
at 3AM while your screen is off — but how would you know?

SentinelAI solves exactly this.

- For everyday users — shows a clear risk score for 
  every app on their phone. No technical knowledge needed. 
  Just open the app and see which apps are behaving 
  suspiciously.

- For privacy-conscious users — detects apps silently 
  uploading data in the background, running hidden services, 
  or waking your device repeatedly without your interaction.

- For everyone — existing solutions like Google Play 
  Protect only scan apps at install time using signature 
  databases. SentinelAI monitors behavior continuously at 
  runtime using on-device AI — catching threats that 
  activate after install or were never seen before.

What makes it different:
All analysis happens 100% on your device. No data is sent 
to any server. No internet required for scanning. Your 
behavioral data never leaves your phone — which is deeply 
ironic given that we are a privacy protection app.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Android blocks direct access to mic, camera and sensors**
Third-party apps cannot directly detect if another app is 
recording audio or accessing the camera. We had to rethink 
our entire approach — instead of detecting the act of 
spying, we detect the *consequence* of it. If an app is 
recording you, it must eventually upload that file. That 
upload appears in our TrafficStats signals. This pivot from 
direct detection to behavioral inference was our biggest 
architectural challenge.

**2. TFLite export of Random Forest completely broke**
The standard `tensorflow-decision-forests` library is 
incompatible with TensorFlow 2.20+. Our entire export 
pipeline failed silently. We had to manually rebuild each 
decision tree as pure TensorFlow Lambda operations using 
`tf.gather_nd`, `tf.where`, and `tf.one_hot` — essentially 
hand-translating 100 decision trees into TFLite-compatible 
tensor operations.

**3. TrafficStats returns cumulative bytes not rate**
`TrafficStats.getUidTxBytes()` returns total bytes uploaded 
since device boot — not since last scan. We were 
accidentally dividing cumulative bytes by uptime, causing 
risk scores to drop every scan even for the same behavior. 
We built a delta cache system that stores the previous 
reading and calculates actual upload rate per interval.

**4. TrafficStats returns zero on emulator**
Spent hours debugging why all risk scores were near zero 
before realizing Android emulators do not support 
TrafficStats. All real-device testing had to be done on 
physical hardware only.

**5. First scan always shows zero**
Since our network scoring is delta-based, the very first 
scan has no previous reading to compare against — producing 
zero network scores. We solved this by capturing a baseline 
reading during app startup before any scan runs, so the 
first real scan already has a reference point.

### Sura App
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sura-app-94d9) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://suragaming.com) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OM5cWGFe2c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Startup%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-startup-track-3.devfolio.co)

> Sura App

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sura App is a mobile-first growth and engagement platform for gaming communities and game partners in LATAM. We solve a simple but painful problem: games and esports communities struggle to retain attention daily, and most Web3 onboarding flows still feel complex for mainstream gamers. 
Sura turns community energy into measurable activity through missions, tournaments, rankings, rewards, and a unified user identity, giving players a reason to come back every day and giving partners a repeatable engine to activate audiences. 
Our objective is to become the operating layer for game activations in LATAM: a single place where players can compete, earn, redeem, and eventually spend in a gamer-friendly way (with fintech rails). For partners (Web2 or Web3), Sura provides a structured way to run campaigns without rebuilding mechanics from scratch: quest templates, reward logic, leaderboards, event modules, and performance insights.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles we encountered was designing a system that could measure and validate user participation in a reliable way without creating friction for mainstream gamers.
Early versions of Sura relied heavily on manual validation and fragmented tracking tools (Discord activity, screenshots, form submissions, event logs). This created three major problems:
Operational overload for our team

Delayed reward distribution

Inconsistent data integrity

As we transitioned from community operations to product infrastructure, this approach was not scalable.
The Technical Challenge
We needed to build a modular system capable of:
Tracking mission completion reliably

Preventing duplicate or fraudulent submissions

Maintaining a unified user identity across activations

Keeping UX simple for non-crypto-native gamers

The hardest part was balancing automation with flexibility — partners needed customizable campaign logic, but we couldn’t afford to create one-off backend flows for every activation.
How We Solved It
We shifted to a template-based architecture:
Standardized mission types (engagement, gameplay, referral, social, tournament-based)

Modular reward logic

Centralized user identity layer

Internal admin dashboard for validation overrides and real-time campaign tracking


This reduced manual ops significantly and allowed us to run repeatable activations instead of rebuilding systems each time.
The key lesson:
 Building engagement infrastructure is less about flashy mechanics and more about designing systems that can scale without increasing operational complexity.

Team **Mariano Rubinstein** -- Gerardo Mossotti

> Predict. Protect. Deploy.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🚨 The Problem It Solves

Modern software teams deploy new updates multiple times a day using CI/CD pipelines. While this accelerates development, it also introduces a major risk: many system failures happen immediately after deployment.

Common causes include:

⚙️ Misconfigured infrastructure or environment variables

🔗 Microservice dependency failures

💾 Memory leaks or resource exhaustion

🗄️ Database connection limits being exceeded

📈 Unexpected traffic spikes after release

The biggest challenge is that most DevOps tools detect these issues only after the system is already deployed in production.

Typical workflow today:

Code → Deploy → System fails → Monitoring alert → Engineers debug

By the time the issue is detected:

Users may already experience downtime

Critical services may become unavailable

Engineers must debug live production systems

This reactive approach makes deployments risky, stressful, and expensive.

💡 Our Solution

This project introduces a **Predictive DevOps System** that evaluates deployment safety before the application goes live.

Instead of reacting to failures, the system:

🔍 Analyzes the application codebase

🧩 Maps service dependencies

🐳 Simulates deployment in a sandbox environment

📊 Generates realistic traffic loads

🤖 Uses AI to predict potential failures

📈 Produces a Deployment Confidence Score

Improved workflow:

Code → Risk Analysis → Deployment Simulation → Failure Prediction → Safe Deployment

This allows teams to identify risks early and fix issues before they affect users.

🛠 What People Can Use It For
🚀 Safer Deployments

Teams can evaluate deployment risk before releasing updates, reducing production failures.

📊 Pre-Deployment System Testing

Developers can simulate real-world traffic and infrastructure behavior before launching new versions.

🔎 Dependency Risk Detection

The system identifies critical services whose failure could cascade across the system.

💰 Cloud Cost Awareness

Traffic simulation can reveal scaling issues that may cause unexpected infrastructure costs.

⚡ Faster Decision Making

Engineers receive a Deployment Confidence Score, helping them quickly determine if a deployment is safe.

🎯 Why This Matters

This system shifts DevOps from reactive monitoring to proactive risk prediction.

By combining code analysis, infrastructure simulation, traffic testing, and AI-based failure prediction, the platform helps engineering teams:

reduce production outages

improve system reliability

deploy software with greater confidence

**Challenges we ran into**

Building this project was exciting but also came with several technical and conceptual challenges. Since the idea aims to predict deployment failures before production, it required integrating multiple complex systems like code analysis, infrastructure simulation, traffic generation, and AI-based prediction into a single pipeline.

⚙️ 1. Simulating a Realistic Deployment Environment

One of the biggest hurdles was creating a sandbox environment that behaves like production without making the system overly heavy or difficult to run during a hackathon.

Modern applications often include:

-multiple microservices

-containerized deployments

-cloud infrastructure

-complex service dependencies

Replicating all of this realistically could easily become resource-intensive.

How I solved it:

Instead of reproducing full production infrastructure, I focused on simulating the most important signals that indicate system risk:

-CPU and memory usage

-service communication behavior

-API response latency

-error rates under load

Using Docker containers for sandbox deployment and k6 for traffic simulation, the system could still produce meaningful insights while remaining lightweight and practical for demonstration.

🔗 2. Integrating Multiple Components into One Pipeline

The project architecture includes several modules:

-Codebase Analyzer

-Dependency Graph Generator

-Sandbox Deployment Simulation

-Traffic Simulation

-AI Failure Prediction

-Deployment Confidence Scoring

Initially, these modules were built independently, which created challenges in passing structured data between components.

How I solved it:

I designed a clear pipeline-based architecture, where each component produces standardized outputs that feed directly into the next stage.

Example flow:

Code Analysis
      ↓
Dependency Graph
      ↓
Sandbox Deployment
      ↓
Traffic Simulation
      ↓
AI Risk Prediction
      ↓
Deployment Confidence Score

This made the system more modular and easier to extend.

🧠 3. Ensuring the System Is Predictive, Not Just Another Monitoring Tool

Many existing DevOps platforms already provide excellent monitoring and observability.
A key challenge was ensuring this project does something fundamentally different.

Most tools follow a reactive workflow:

Deploy → Failure happens → Monitoring alert → Engineers debug

Our goal was to shift this into a proactive workflow:

Code → Simulate deployment → Predict risk → Safe deployment

To achieve this, the system combines:

-infrastructure simulation

-traffic stress testing

-AI-based risk prediction

This allows the platform to generate a Deployment Confidence Score, giving engineers a clear signal about whether a deployment is safe.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

🤖 How We Used the **Gemini API**

In this project, we used the Gemini API as an **intelligent code analysis layer** to understand the structure and operational behavior of a repository before deployment. Instead of relying only on static parsers, Gemini helped extract high-level architectural insights from the codebase and translate them into actionable deployment intelligence.

When a repository is submitted to the system, the Codebase Analyzer scans important files such as:

source code directories

 -configuration files (Dockerfile, .env, docker-compose, k8s manifests)

-dependency files (package.json, requirements.txt, etc.)

-infrastructure configurations

These files are then summarized and sent to the Gemini API, which analyzes the project context and produces structured insights about the system.

🔍 What Gemini Helps the System Understand

Gemini is used to extract meaningful details such as:

**Framework detection**
(e.g., React frontend, Node.js backend, Python services)

**Service architecture identification**
Detecting APIs, microservices, background workers, and databases.

**Infrastructure inference**
Understanding whether the project is optimized for:

**serverless environments**

**containerized deployments**

**Kubernetes clusters**

**edge deployments**

**Deployment risk indicators**

Gemini can highlight potential concerns such as:

**heavy memory usage patterns**

**tight service coupling**

**missing infrastructure configurations**

The output from Gemini is then transformed into structured metadata that feeds into later stages of the system like dependency graph generation and deployment simulation.

⚙️ How Gemini Improves the Pipeline

Without Gemini, extracting architecture insights from a repository would require complex rule-based parsers for every framework and language.

By using Gemini, the system can:

**interpret codebases across multiple programming languages**

**summarize architecture automatically**

**detect hidden relationships between services**

**generate insights that traditional static analysis might miss**

This makes the Codebase Analyzer far more flexible and scalable.

📈 Why Gemini Was Productive for the Project

Using Gemini significantly accelerated development and improved system intelligence.

Key advantages include:

🧠 **Context-Aware Code Understanding**

Gemini can interpret entire project structures rather than analyzing files in isolation, enabling better architecture-level insights.

⚡ **Faster Feature Development**

Instead of writing hundreds of rules for parsing frameworks and configurations, Gemini allowed the system to extract structured insights using natural language reasoning.

🔄 **Adaptability to Different Tech Stacks**

Since Gemini understands many programming languages and frameworks, the system can analyze diverse repositories without custom parsers for each stack.

🚀 **Improved Failure Prediction**

By extracting richer architectural information from the codebase, Gemini improves the accuracy of later stages such as dependency mapping and deployment risk prediction.

🧩 Role of Gemini in the System Pipeline
Repository Input
        ↓
Codebase Scanner
        ↓
Gemini API Analysis
        ↓
Architecture & Infrastructure Insights
        ↓
Dependency Graph Generation
        ↓
Deployment Simulation
        ↓
AI Failure Prediction
🌟 Impact

Integrating the Gemini API allowed the system to move beyond basic static analysis and build a context-aware understanding of the application architecture. This makes the platform more capable of predicting deployment risks and preparing infrastructure simulations that closely reflect real-world behavior.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

🎙 How We Used ElevenLabs in Our Project

In our project, we integrated ElevenLabs to create a voice-based assistant for interacting with the DevOps pipeline and deployment analysis system. Since our platform performs complex tasks such as codebase analysis, deployment simulation, traffic testing, and AI-based risk prediction, we wanted to make it easier for users to understand the results without manually going through logs or dashboards.

We built a conversational interface where users can ask questions about their deployment pipeline, and the system responds with clear explanations. The responses generated by our system are then converted into natural, human-like voice output using the ElevenLabs text-to-speech API.

For example, after a deployment simulation is completed, a user can ask questions such as:

**“What risks were detected in the deployment simulation?”

“Which service has the highest probability of failure?”

“Why is the deployment confidence score low?”

“What should I fix before deploying?”**

The system processes the question, retrieves the relevant analysis results from the pipeline (such as dependency risks, infrastructure issues, or traffic simulation metrics), generates a response, and then uses ElevenLabs to convert the response into natural speech.

This integration transforms the platform into an AI-powered DevOps assistant, allowing developers to interact with their deployment pipeline in a more intuitive and conversational way.

Instead of reading complex logs or dashboards, engineers can quickly understand system insights through voice interaction, which improves usability and makes the platform more accessible—especially when debugging or reviewing deployment results.

Overall, ElevenLabs helped us add a human-friendly interaction layer on top of a complex DevOps analysis system, making it easier for users to explore insights, understand risks, and make safer deployment decisions.

**Best Use of Auth0**

🔐 Use of Auth0 in the Project

In our platform, Auth0 is used to handle secure authentication and user identity management. Since the system interacts with sensitive resources such as GitHub repositories, deployment configurations, and infrastructure simulations, it is important to ensure that only authorized users can access the workspace.

Instead of building a custom authentication system, we integrated Auth0 as a secure identity provider that manages login, session handling, and user verification.

⚙️ How Auth0 Works in Our System

When a user accesses the platform, they first arrive at the landing page and are prompted to log in.

The authentication flow works as follows:

User opens platform
        ↓
Redirected to Auth0 login
        ↓
User authenticates (Google / GitHub / Email)
        ↓
Auth0 verifies identity
        ↓
JWT access token issued
        ↓
User gains access to workspace

Once the user is authenticated, Auth0 issues a secure access token (JWT) that allows the platform to verify the user's identity when interacting with different services.

🔗 Why Auth0 Is Important for This Project

Using Auth0 provides several important benefits:

1️⃣ Secure Access Control

Only authenticated users can connect repositories, run deployment simulations, or trigger deployments.

2️⃣ Identity Management

Auth0 manages user accounts and authentication flows without requiring us to build a complex login system.

3️⃣ Social Login Support

Users can easily sign in using providers like:

Google

GitHub

email/password authentication

This improves usability for developers.

4️⃣ Token-Based Security

Auth0 provides JWT tokens, which are used by our backend services to securely verify user identity for API requests.

5️⃣ Scalability and Security Best Practices

Auth0 follows modern authentication standards such as:

OAuth 2.0

OpenID Connect

This ensures the platform remains secure and scalable.

🎯 Role of Auth0 in the Overall System

Within the system architecture, Auth0 acts as the identity and access management layer, protecting the DevOps workspace and ensuring that only authorized users can analyze repositories, run deployment simulations, and interact with the AI DevOps assistant.

This allows us to focus on building the core predictive DevOps features while relying on Auth0 for secure authentication and user management.

### Voyager
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trip-companion-1b57) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gaurav031/Acehack5.0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Your Trip , Our Safety

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, **millions of tourists** visit India with excitement — but no safety net. The challenges they face are real, serious, and largely unsolved:

- **No emergency access** — Finding embassy numbers, police contacts, or helplines in a crisis is slow, confusing, and stressful.

- **No safety awareness** — Tourists have zero knowledge of which areas, regions, or neighbourhoods carry genuine risk to their safety.

-  **No real-time alerts**  — When riots, unrest, or disasters break out, tourists in affected zones receive no warning whatsoever.

-  **No smart route guidance**  — Travelers navigate blindly without knowing the safest paths between cities or within unfamiliar localities.

-  **No price transparency**  — Language gaps and local knowledge gaps leave tourists routinely overcharged at markets, restaurants, and for transport.

-  **Language barriers**  — With 22+ official languages, basic communication, shopping, and emergency interaction becomes a daily struggle.

-  **No travel intelligence**  — There is no single platform that plans itineraries, answers doubts, translates languages, and scans prices all in one place.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.
During the training of the model for price detection of local products, one of the major challenges we faced was data collection. It is difficult to accurately identify the material of objects using a camera, which affects the model's performance. Currently, we are managing this limitation by using the Gemini API key to detect prices. In the future, this will be replaced with a custom-trained model focused on specific types of objects that can be easily identified through a camera, so material identification will not be a major concern.

2.
Access to recent and detailed data is currently unavailable because it is classified as government-confidential information. To scale the solution initially, we plan to collect data from a small group of users, such as their statistical spending patterns and budget information. This data can then be aggregated and presented to the government as insights, which may help us establish a partnership or collaboration with government agencies.

The problem it solves

It helps eliminate long waiting lines and overcrowding by introducing a structured digital appointment system that controls visitor flow. It also solves the problem of OTP authentication delays and costs by implementing a secure WhatsApp-based passwordless login method. Instead of requiring different applications for different services, the platform provides a single unified system where users can access multiple organizations within a city. Additionally, it improves transparency by giving users real-time visibility of their queue status and expected waiting time. At the same time, organizations benefit from a centralized digital appointment management system that replaces inefficient manual processes, enabling smoother operations and better service delivery


Long waiting lines & overcrowding: Shifts physical queues into a structured digital queue, reducing congestion and chaos at service centers.
OTP delays & costs: Replaces paid OTP with WhatsApp-based passwordless login, faster and cheaper.
Fragmented services: One platform supports multiple organizations in a city instead of separate apps for each.
No real-time visibility: Users see token number, queue order, and estimated wait time (5 minutes per token).
Manual appointment handling: Admins approve/decline tokens digitally and manage queues in FIFO order.
What people can use it for

Citizens/users:

Book appointments across different services (government or private).
Track their queue position and expected waiting time.
Access bookings and tickets in one place.
Organizations/centers:

Control daily crowd flow with digital tokens.
Replace manual registers with centralized appointment management.
Approve/decline tokens and print token lists easily.
How it makes tasks easier & safer

Faster entry through WhatsApp login (no OTP delay).
Less physical crowding due to staggered digital queue.
Clear transparency with real-time token visibility.
Better administration using a single dashboard instead of manual logs.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Real‑time queue consistency: Keeping token order and wait time accurate across users required centralized FIFO logic and careful updates on every booking.
WhatsApp passwordless authentication: Replacing OTP meant building a secure token-based session flow with reliable verification.
Multi‑organization support: Designing a flexible data model for multiple centers/services without fragmenting the user experience.
Indexing & query limits: Firestore composite index requirements forced a fallback listing + filtering approach.
UI complexity: Early booking flows were confusing; simplifying the steps and adding clear status feedback improved usability.

> Space Battle

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Meteor Madness is an interactive web-based asteroid simulation platform that combines real **NASA asteroid data, physics-based impact models**, and 3D visualizations to help users understand asteroid threats and planetary defense.

The platform uses     **NASA’s Near-Earth Object** API to allow users to explore real asteroids, view their size, velocity, distance from Earth, and hazard classification, and monitor a live feed of asteroids passing near Earth.

Users can visualize asteroid motion through an interactive 3D orbital simulation built with Three.js, and simulate asteroid impacts to analyze consequences such as impact energy, crater size, earthquake magnitude, tsunami height, and destruction radius. The system also displays impact zones on a world map to show how different regions may be affected.

Meteor Madness  integrates USGS seismic data 

so users can compare asteroid impacts with real earthquake events.

The platform also includes a planetary defense simulator, where users can test strategies like kinetic impactors, gravity tractors, and nuclear deflection to attempt to change the asteroid’s trajectory.

Users can additionally create custom asteroid simulations by entering parameters such as diameter, velocity, density, and impact location.

**A premium Classroom Mode**
 
 is also included, where teachers can create simulation assignments, allow students to run asteroid experiments, and analyze student reports based on asteroid parameters, energy calculations, and environmental effects. This feature turns the platform into an interactive STEM learning tool for schools.

Future improvements include population impact analysis, climate effect simulations, AI-based impact prediction, and augmented reality asteroid visualization.

**Challenges we ran into**

**NASA API Errors**

While integrating NASA’s Near-Earth Object API, we faced 403 errors and rate limits, which prevented asteroid data from loading.
Solution: We implemented proper API key handling, added error handling, and optimized API requests to reduce unnecessary calls.

**3D Simulation Performance**

Building the 3D asteroid and Earth simulation with Three.js initially caused performance and animation synchronization issues.
Solution: We optimized the animation loop and adjusted orbital calculations to ensure smooth and realistic motion.

**Impact Physics Modeling**

Converting complex asteroid impact physics into simplified formulas that run efficiently in the browser was challenging.
Solution: We researched simplified scientific models and implemented approximations for energy, crater size, earthquake magnitude, and tsunami height to keep the simulation both realistic and fast.

### Tag-In
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tagin-d7dd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Akshat12416/TagIn_AceHack) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Counterfeit product detection system (Solana+RFID)

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Counterfeit goods represent a multi-trillion-dollar (**USD 500 billion** in 2021-22) global crisis, severely damaging brand reputation and eroding consumer trust. Whether it's luxury fashion, sneakers, or critical pharmaceuticals, malicious actors seamlessly replicate physical products and traditional packaging. Conventional verification methods like barcodes, QR codes, or serial numbers fall short because they are static and easily cloned by counterfeiters.

TagIn solves this by bridging the physical and digital worlds using immutable blockchain technology. We embed encrypted NFC chips directly into physical merchandise, which act as a direct portal to a unique, cryptographically secure digital twin on the Solana blockchain.

When a consumer **taps their smartphone** to a TagIn-verified product, the system instantly cross-references the physical tap with the **immutable on-chain record** (Program Derived Address). This trustless, decentralized verification completely eliminates the possibility of replication, if a counterfeiter clones the physical NFC tag, the blockchain's deterministic signature will immediately flag the disparity, instantly alerting the consumer and updating the manufacturer's real-time counterfeit hotspot map.

TagIn restores absolute truth to the supply chain, empowering brands to protect their legacy and allowing consumers to confidently authenticate their purchases with a single tap.

**Challenges we ran into**

While making this product, there were multiple challenges : 

**1. Solana Memory & Stack Constraints**
While initializing the complex Product PDAs (Program Derived Addresses) in our Anchor smart contract, we consistently hit Access violation in stack frame and stack overflow errors. Solana enforces a strict 4KB stack frame limit per transaction. To solve this without compromising the product data, we implemented manual zero-copy-like memory management using Box<Account<...>> in Rust to allocate the accounts directly onto the heap instead.

**2. Crushing Unscalable Minting Costs**
We initially attempted to use the standard Metaplex Token Metadata program to mint standard NFTs for every physical product. However, initializing all the required SPL Token and Metaplex accounts cost around ~0.02 SOL per product, which fundamentally breaks the business model for mass manufacturing. We completely overhauled the architecture to drop Metaplex and design a pure, custom PDA structure. By only storing a lightweight 32-byte metadataHash on-chain, we dropped the minting cost by almost 100x (to ~0.0001 SOL) while retaining the exact same cryptographic security.

**3. Cross-Platform Cryptographic Mismatches**
Passing data from a React frontend connected dynamically via Phantom Wallet into a Python backend API created persistent mismatches. Solana's Base58 addresses are inherently case-sensitive, but traditional Javascript filtering methods (like .toLowerCase()) completely corrupt the string comparisons. This caused verified products to silently disappear from the Manufacturer's Inventory until we enforced strict equality and implemented rigorous parsing blocks across the stack.

**4. Local Network Routing for NFC Verification**
Testing the mobile NFC scanning flow presented a unique network routing challenge. When testing on development laptops, the frontend inherently queried 127.0.0.1 (localhost) for the Python api. However, when tapping the NFC tags with a smartphone, the phone's browser would attempt to query its own internal localhost instead of the laptop running the backend! We had to rewrite the networking requests to dynamically compile and inject window.location.hostname into the axios requests, allowing the mobile phones to resolve the backend over the local WLAN gracefully.

**BlockChain**

It uses Solana Blockchain to register every product on the chain itself by minting a NFT from a Solana Program

**Best Use of Solana**

We have used Solana blockchain to mint NFT's of each product because Solana provides us with numerous advantages with respect to other blockchains like lower finality time, low costs and faster speeds, that allows us to scale a project like Tag-In easily and efficiently.

> "Immutable Privacy, Explicit Consent."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**--Main Use Cases of Consent-Chain--**

**1. For Students (Data Owners)**

**Digital Vault**: Secure place to store transcripts, degrees, resumes, and portfolios.


**Consent Management:** Dashboard to approve or reject data access requests.

**Full Control:** Students can see who accessed their data, why, and for how long, and can revoke access anytime.

**2. For Recruiters & Employers (Data Consumers)**

**Verified Data:** Recruiters get real academic records directly from students and universities, reducing resume fraud.

**Compliant Hiring:** The system records cryptographic proof of consent, helping companies follow DPDP privacy laws.

**3. For Universities (Credential Issuers)**

**Verified Credentials:** Universities issue tamper-proof digital certificates using ARC-19 NFTs, proving a student's enrollment or graduation.

**4. For Academic Researchers**

Researchers can request permission to access student datasets for studies while ensuring ethical and consent-based data usage.
.
.
.
**--How ConsentChain Makes Tasks Safer--**
.
**Stops Unauthorized Data Selling:**
Student data is encrypted using AES-256-GCM before leaving the browser. Without the student giving the decryption key through an on-chain consent action, the data cannot be read.

**Permanent Audit Trail:**
Every action (upload, download, consent, revoke) is recorded on Algorand Box Storage, creating a tamper-proof history.

**Cryptographic Proof of Consent:**
Consent is stored as a Soulbound NFT (ARC-3) linked to a specific request, providing clear proof that permission was given.

**Instant Revocation:**
If a student clicks Revoke, the consent NFT is destroyed through a blockchain inner transaction, immediately stopping access.
.
.
.

**--How Consent-Chain Makes Tasks Easier--**
.

**Automatic Compliance:**
The platform automatically follows privacy rules like DPDP Act and GDPR by enforcing purpose limitation and time limitation in requests.

**Single Dashboard:**
Students can manage all their data sharing and permissions in one place.

**Trustless Verification:**
Recruiters can quickly verify credentials because only universities can issue the official credential NFTs.

**Simple User Experience:**
Even though it uses blockchain, users don’t need to understand wallets, gas fees, or private keys, making it easy for normal users to use.


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15eca0f43fe14a98a2a6374db60fc8d9/03835659-4ad7-4eed-a0e6-cf555f0cc8fe.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15eca0f43fe14a98a2a6374db60fc8d9/644dfe09-8ad3-4a2e-8249-3b977cca8339.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15eca0f43fe14a98a2a6374db60fc8d9/134b1a4a-9d1f-425d-8229-5c86170d5f20.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/15eca0f43fe14a98a2a6374db60fc8d9/58b89f47-c92f-488b-a92f-30ff0370317e.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was finding a way to store secure and permanent consent records on the blockchain without making transactions expensive or exceeding smart contract storage limits. At first, storing all consent details (like requester info, purpose, and expiry) directly in the contract took too much space and cost too much. To solve this, I used Algorand’s Box Storage, which allows storing data only when needed using a 96-byte key created from the student address. I also linked each consent to a Soulbound ARC-3 NFT created through an inner transaction. This design keeps the blockchain storage small, provides clear proof of consent, and allows instant revocation by deleting the box and destroying the NFT.

**BlockChain**

ConsentChain fits into the Blockchain Track because it uses blockchain to solve a real problem: secure and transparent data sharing. The platform uses Algorand smart contracts to record user consent on-chain, ensuring that permission records cannot be changed or tampered with. It also uses Soulbound NFTs (ARC-3) to represent proof of consent and Box Storage to maintain a permanent audit trail of data access.

By doing this, the system provides trust, transparency, and verifiable data sharing between students, universities, and recruiters—showing a practical use of blockchain beyond cryptocurrency.

**Algorand Bharat**

**1. Storing Consent Records Securely**
Algorand is used to store the record of user consent. When a student allows a recruiter or organization to access their data, that permission is saved on Algorand. This record cannot be changed or deleted, which makes the system transparent and trustworthy.

**2. Creating Verified Digital Credentials**
Universities can issue digital certificates (like degrees or marksheets) using Algorand. Because they are recorded on the blockchain, recruiters can easily verify that the credentials are real and not fake.

**3. Keeping an Audit Trail**
Algorand keeps a permanent log of all actions, such as who requested data, when permission was given, and when access was revoked. This helps organizations follow India’s DPDP data protection law.

**4. Secure and Fast System**
Algorand provides fast transactions, strong security, and very low fees, which makes it suitable for a system where many students, universities, and recruiters interact.

### Global-connect-ai
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/globalsync-1522) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Piyush00715/global-connect-ai.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://globalconnectai.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Real-time Cross-Cultural Chat

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zustand](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zustand-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In an increasingly connected world, language differences remain a massive hurdle for cross-cultural collaboration, global customer support, and personal relationships. 
Traditional chat translators are slow and disjointed. Voice calls between people who speak different languages are generally impossible without human interpreters. Existing translation tools lack the real-time, bidirectional fluidity needed for natural conversation.
Our Solution
Global Connect provides a unified, continuous interface for cross-linguistic communication:
1. **Real-Time Text Translation**: Users select their native language. All incoming text messages are instantly translated into their language using advanced LLMs (Google Gemini), preserving cultural context and warning against ambiguous phrasing.
2. **"Call Mode" (Continuous Speech-to-Speech)**: Instead of push-to-talk, users can switch on Call Mode for rapid, continuous voice interaction. The browser's Speech Recognition converts spoken sentences to text, the backend translates it, and the other user's browser reads the translated message aloud using an ultra-realistic AI voice.
3. **Interactive AI Avatar**: The platform is centered around a responsive AI Avatar that visually signals when the application is listening to your voice or translating/speaking to the recipient, making the whole interaction feel much more natural and human.
4. **Cultural Clarifications**: The underlying AI can parse the nuances of the text and warn a user if their sent message might be overly direct or confusing within the recipient's language context, offering better alternatives automatically.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/94ccd2fb8b0a4bfc9a6b9eb0ce661587/9f6d0ed6-f70f-4e88-8846-d55b5d44a828.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Continuous "Call Mode" vs. Browser Limitations
Challenge: The native browser Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition) is generally designed for short, push-to-talk commands. If you pause for a second, it automatically stops listening. Setting continuous: true is notoriously buggy across different browsers and often times out unexpectedly. Solution: We built a custom loop within the 

onend
 event handler of the speech recognition instance. When the speech recognition naturally stops, our code immediately checks if "Call Mode" is still active and, if so, restarts the engine with a slight delay (setTimeout). This forces the browser into a continuous listening state, allowing for hands-free conversations.

2. The Infinite Translation Echo Loop
Challenge: When building the continuous Call Mode, we ran into an edge case where the user's microphone would pick up the translated audio coming from the AI Avatar's text-to-speech out of their own speakers. The application would then translate the translation, causing an infinite, noisy feedback loop. Solution: We tied the speech recognition engine directly to the isSpeaking state. Whenever the ElevenLabs API or native browser TTS begins to play audio, we immediately pause the microphone listening loop. Once the audio finishes playing (audio.onended), the microphone is allowed to automatically restart.

3. Graceful Audio Degradation (ElevenLabs Fallback)
Challenge: Integrating ultra-realistic AI voices (like ElevenLabs) is fantastic for user experience, but it requires an API key and has rate limits. If a user didn't provide a key or exhausted their quota, the Avatar would simply go silent. Solution: We implemented a dual-layer Text-to-Speech system. The app first attempts to call the ElevenLabs API using fetch(). If the API key is missing or the response fails, we instantly catch the error and fall back to the native window.speechSynthesis engine. This ensures the voice features are always 100% operational regardless of third-party API availability.

4. Cultural Nuance in Real-Time
Challenge: Direct translations of sentences from one language to another often lose their cultural context, making some phrases seem overly blunt, confusing, or rude to the recipient even if the literal translation is correct. Solution: We didn't just use standard machine translation. We leveraged Google Gemini's LLM to dynamically evaluate the text before it's finalized. We added a debounced typing event that sends the draft input to the backend, returning an "ambiguity warning" and suggesting a more polite or clear alternative phrasing to the sender before they even hit send.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

**LLM / GenAI Integration**: [@google/genai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@google/genai) using Google Gemini to handle the logic for high-fidelity translations and ambiguity resolution.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

[ElevenLabs API](https://elevenlabs.io/) for high-fidelity multi-language voice synthesis

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vibesync-ebbf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/urvatembhare25-sys/VibeSync) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/B8R6CsitAUs?si=EHfRRrxgq10vAjCT) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> “Let Your Video Find Its Voice.”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VibeSync is an AI-powered platform that helps creators easily add the perfect background music to their videos. Instead of spending time searching for music or worrying about copyright issues, users can simply upload their video and let AI generate or recommend a soundtrack that matches the video’s mood.

Who Can Use It

VibeSync can be used by:

1. Content creators (YouTube, Instagram, Reels, Shorts)

2. Vloggers and video editors

3. Businesses producing promotional videos

It helps them save time, simplify editing, and avoid copyright risks.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge: A single video can have many possible music options.
Solution: We built a matching algorithm that calculates a video–music compatibility score, helping users pick the best track.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

VibeSync connects what you see in a video with what you hear in the music. Using Gemini, it analyzes the video frame by frame—looking at things like lighting, movement, objects, and emotions—to recommend music that actually matches the vibe of the scene.
It also solves a common problem for creators: finding the right music. Instead of spending hours searching, VibeSync quickly suggests tracks that fit the mood, whether it’s a Bollywood song for a wedding reel or a chill Lo-Fi beat for a travel vlog.
