![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Many people rely on food delivery platforms to order meals from nearby restaurants, but existing systems often have limitations such as high commission fees for restaurants, lack of transparency in payments, and limited control for small or local food businesses.

The **Cravings** platform aims to solve these problems by providing a **complete food ordering and delivery management system** where customers, restaurants, and delivery partners can interact efficiently within a single platform.

Customers can easily **browse restaurants, view menus, and place orders online**, making the food ordering process faster and more convenient. Restaurants get a dedicated dashboard where they can **manage menus, update food items, track orders, and manage their business digitally** without relying completely on third-party platforms.

The platform also helps delivery partners by providing a system to **manage delivery requests and track orders**, which improves the overall delivery process.

By combining these features into a single MERN stack application, **Cravings simplifies the food ordering workflow, improves operational efficiency for restaurants, and provides a convenient experience for customers** while maintaining a scalable and secure system for online food services.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

While working on the **Cravings MERN full-stack food delivery platform**, we encountered several challenges during development.

### 1. Environment Variables & Payment Configuration
One of the major issues occurred while integrating the payment gateway. The backend was throwing errors such as **“key_id or oauthToken is mandatory”**. This happened because the payment credentials were not properly loaded from the `.env` file.  
We solved this by carefully configuring environment variables, ensuring the correct variable names were used in the backend code and restarting the server so the environment variables could load properly.

### 2. Authentication & Role-Based Access
Since the platform supports multiple roles (Customer, Restaurant, Rider, Admin), managing **authentication and authorization** was challenging. Sometimes protected routes were not recognizing the logged-in user correctly.  
We fixed this by implementing **JWT-based authentication and middleware checks**, ensuring that each API route validates the user's role before allowing access.

### 3. Frontend–Backend Connection Issues
Another hurdle was connecting the **React frontend with the Express backend APIs**. Occasionally requests failed due to incorrect API URLs or CORS configuration.  
We resolved this by properly configuring the **API base URL, enabling CORS on the server, and testing endpoints with tools like Postman** before connecting them to the frontend.

### 4. Database Connection Problems
During development we also faced issues connecting the application to **MongoDB**, especially when the connection string or network access settings were incorrect.  
After reviewing the MongoDB URI and environment configuration, we successfully established a stable database connection.

### Learning Outcome
These challenges helped us gain deeper understanding of **environment configuration, authentication systems, API integration, and full-stack debugging**, which are essential skills for building scalable web applications.

**Algorand Bharat**

Our project Cravings is a full-stack food delivery platform that connects customers, restaurants, and delivery partners. A major requirement for such platforms is a secure and fast payment system.

To support this, our project aligns with the Algorand Bharat track by integrating Algorand blockchain-based payments. Using Algorand, transactions can be fast, low-cost, and transparent, allowing customers to pay securely while restaurants receive payments reliably.

Blockchain transactions can also help maintain tamper-proof payment records and reduce dependency on centralized payment gateways. This integration aims to create a secure and trustworthy digital payment experience for users on the Cravings platform while promoting blockchain adoption in real-world applications in India.

### BhashaBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bhashabridge-c835) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://9000-firebase-studio-1772948525248.cluster-cz5nqyh5nreq6ua6gaqd7okl7o.cloudworkstations.dev/?monospaceUid=780430&embedded=0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Not just translation. Cultural Intelligence.

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Cloud%20Platform%20(GCP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🌍 The Problem BhashaBridge Solves

Global teams lose **$1.2 Trillion annually** due to poor communication 
(Grammarly/SHRM). But the real problem isn't vocabulary — it's **culture**.

Existing tools like Google Translate and DeepL translate **words**, 
but completely miss:

- 🤔 **Sarcasm** — "Wah! Bahut achha kiya" sounds like a compliment 
  but isn't
- 🗣️ **Idioms** — "Break a leg" literally translated would confuse anyone
- 😶 **Implied meaning** — A Japanese colleague's silence means 
  disagreement, not agreement
- 🎭 **Politeness levels** — Hindi "aap" vs "tum" formality is 
  completely lost in translation
- 🌐 **Cultural references** — Festivals, local expressions, 
  social norms

## 💎 What BhashaBridge Does

BhashaBridge is an **AI-powered Cultural Mediator** — not just a 
translator. It:

- ✅ **Auto-translates** messages to each user's native language 
  in real-time
- ✅ **Detects nuance** — sarcasm, idioms, implied meaning, 
  politeness levels
- ✅ **Shows tone badges** — friendly, formal, sarcastic, apologetic
- ✅ **Sensitivity alerts** — flags messages that could offend 
  before misunderstanding happens
- ✅ **Cultural tips** — teaches users cross-cultural communication
- ✅ **Suggests adaptations** — offers culturally appropriate 
  alternative phrasing
- ✅ **Voice support** — speak in your language, listen in yours

## 👥 Who Can Use It

- 🏢 **Remote global teams** — daily standups across cultures
- 🎓 **International students** — communicating with professors 
  and peers
- 💼 **Freelancers** — working with international clients
- 🤝 **B2B companies** — cross-border business communication

## 🚀 Impact

BhashaBridge doesn't just break language barriers — 
it builds **cultural bridges**.

> *"Current tools translate WORDS. We translate INTENT."*

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. 🔴 Gemini API Quota Exhaustion
**Problem:** We were making 2 separate Gemini API calls per message 
— one for translation and one for cultural analysis. This quickly 
exhausted our free tier quota during testing.

**Solution:** We consolidated both calls into a single optimized 
prompt that returns translation + full cultural analysis in one 
JSON response. This reduced API usage by 50% while maintaining 
the same quality.

---

### 2. 🔴 Cultural Nuance Detection Accuracy
**Problem:** Getting Gemini to consistently detect sarcasm, idioms, 
and implied meaning across different language pairs was inconsistent 
in early attempts.

**Solution:** We engineered a detailed system prompt with specific 
examples for each nuance type — sarcasm in Hindi, indirect refusal 
in Japanese, British understatement in English. This dramatically 
improved detection accuracy.

---

### 3. 🔴 Real-time Translation Without Breaking Chat Flow
**Problem:** Showing both original and translated text while keeping 
the chat UI clean and readable was a design challenge. Too much 
information made the UI overwhelming.

**Solution:** We designed a layered card system — original message 
first, then translated text with a globe icon, then collapsible 
nuance cards below. This keeps the chat clean while making cultural 
intelligence visible when needed.

---

### 4. 🔴 Bot Personality Consistency
**Problem:** The 3 bot characters (Lukas, Yuki, Emma) needed to 
feel like real people from their cultures — not generic AI responses.

**Solution:** We crafted detailed personality prompts for each bot:
- **Lukas** — formal, direct, no small talk (German communication style)
- **Yuki** — polite, indirect, uses honorifics (Japanese style)
- **Emma** — friendly, uses British idioms and understatement

---

### 5. 🔴 Deployment Configuration
**Problem:** Next.js Server Actions are not supported with static 
export, which blocked our Firebase Hosting deployment.

**Solution:** Migrated to Vercel for deployment — which natively 
supports Next.js with zero configuration, giving us a live 
production URL instantly.

---

> *"Every bug we fixed made BhashaBridge smarter. 
> Every challenge made our team stronger."* 💎

### TruthLens
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/truthlens-7693) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TarunTheDev/truthlens-ai) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://truthlens-ai-nine.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Don't trust AI blindly — we mine for the truth

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Netlify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Netlify-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI-generated content is everywhere — but it lies. Confidently.

ChatGPT, Gemini, and other large language models routinely "hallucinate": they fabricate facts, invent URLs, misattribute quotes, and present outdated information as current — all with the same confident tone as accurate content. Most people have no way to tell the difference at a glance.

**TruthLens** is a real-time AI Hallucination Auditor that lets you paste any text and get a sentence-by-sentence breakdown of what's true, false, or unverifiable.

### Who is it for?

- 🎓 **Students & researchers** — verify AI-written summaries before submitting assignments
- 📰 **Journalists & writers** — fact-check drafts and AI-assisted articles instantly
- ⚖️ **Legal & medical professionals** — catch misquoted laws, fake case citations, or wrong drug dosages
- 🧑‍💻 **Developers & prompt engineers** — test how much an LLM hallucinates on a given topic
- 👤 **General users** — stop trusting AI blindly

### What it does differently

- **Sentence-level analysis** — not just "this text seems wrong", but exactly *which sentence* is false and *why*
- **5 hallucination types** classified per claim: Fabricated Fact, False Source, False Connection, Context Distortion, Knowledge Gap
- **Domain modes** — stricter rules for Medical, Legal, and Journalism content
- **Difficulty modes** — Creative (lenient) / Survival (normal) / Hardcore (brutal)
- **AI Rewrite** — one click to get a corrected version of any false sentence
- **Battle Mode** — compare two texts head-to-head to see which is more trustworthy
- **Trust Score** — an overall health bar score for the entire text

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Gemini treating March 2026 as "future"
Gemini's training data has a cutoff, so it was flagging real current events as 
"unverifiable future claims" and giving false confidence scores. Fix: we inject 
TODAY'S DATE into every audit prompt and added a new `KNOWLEDGE_GAP` hallucination 
type for claims that are plausible but too recent to verify — instead of wrongly 
marking them FALSE.

### 2. The 4-model fallback chain
Single-model Gemini calls failed constantly during high traffic (rate limits, 
model deprecations). We built an automatic fallback: `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` → 
`gemini-flash-lite-latest` → `gemini-2.0-flash` → `gemini-flash-latest`. If one 
fails, the next is tried transparently — users never see a raw API error.

### 3. `btoa()` crashing on emoji/Unicode text
The Share Link feature encodes results in a URL using base64. `btoa()` throws 
a hard crash on any non-ASCII character (emojis, accented letters). Fix: 
`btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(data)))` — a Unicode-safe encoding chain.

### 4. Three.js 3D background performance
The hero section runs 55 voxels + 600 stars in a WebGL canvas. Initial builds 
caused jank on mid-range devices. We separated the Three.js code into its own 
lazy-loaded chunk via Vite's `manualChunks`, reducing initial JS parse time 
significantly.

### 5. Gemini returning inconsistent JSON
The AI occasionally returns malformed JSON, omits fields like `uncertain_count`, 
or wraps the JSON in markdown code fences. We wrote a robust parser that strips 
code fences, normalizes missing fields, and retries on parse failure before 
surfacing an error to the user.

### 6. FloatingParticles re-render flicker
Background particle positions were generated with `Math.random()` inside the 
component body — so every state update (loading spinner, toast, etc.) regenerated 
all 30 particle positions, causing a visible flicker. Fix: moved the array to 
module scope so positions are computed once at startup.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

TruthLens is built entirely around the Gemini API — it's the core engine that powers everything.

**What we use Gemini for:**
- Every sentence in the pasted text is sent to Gemini with a carefully crafted prompt that asks it to act as a fact-checking auditor
- Gemini classifies each sentence as TRUE, FALSE, or UNCERTAIN, assigns a confidence score (0–100), identifies the type of hallucination, and suggests a source URL
- A second Gemini call rewrites any false sentence into a corrected version
- A third Gemini call generates a plain-English summary briefing of all the issues found

**How we push the API further:**
- We built a **4-model automatic fallback chain** — if `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` is rate-limited, it silently retries with `gemini-flash-lite-latest`, then `gemini-2.0-flash`, then `gemini-flash-latest` — so the app never goes down
- We inject **today's date** and **domain-specific expert rules** (Medical / Legal / Journalism) directly into the prompt so Gemini behaves like a specialist auditor, not a generic chatbot
- We introduced a custom hallucination type called **KNOWLEDGE_GAP** — instead of wrongly marking recent events as false, Gemini is instructed to flag them as "too recent to verify", making the output far more honest and useful

Without Gemini, TruthLens does nothing. The entire value of the product — sentence auditing, rewrites, summaries — comes from intelligent prompt engineering on top of the Gemini API.

### SignBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/signbridge-851f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aryangarg777/SignBridge) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://advances-slots-traveling-climate.trycloudflare.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> SignBridge - Bridging communication beyond words.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

"SignBridge breaks the 'silent wall' between the 70 million sign language users globally and the hearing world. Currently, the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) community relies on expensive physical interpreters or dry text-to-screen tools that lack speed and emotion. SignBridge transforms sign language into high-quality, real-time AI speech via ElevenLabs, allowing for fluid, two-way communication. Whether it’s a quick daily interaction, a remote video call, or a high-stakes medical emergency (via our SOS module), SignBridge provides a bridge to independence, dignity, and safety."

"Our primary audience is the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community, but the impact extends to healthcare providers, emergency responders, and educators. By providing a tool that 'listens' to signs and 'speaks' to the world, we enable smoother interactions in hospitals, schools, and workplaces, making the hearing world more inclusive and accessible."

"We integrated the ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech API to provide high-fidelity, real-time vocal output for our sign language translations. We use the eleven_multilingual_v2 model via a streaming endpoint in our Python backend. This allows our application to transform hand gestures into natural human speech with minimal latency, truly 'giving a voice' to the signer. We also implemented a robust fallback system to ensure accessibility remains functional at all times."

**Challenges we ran into**

Every complex project has its "dark ages." Here are the three most significant hurdles we faced while building SignBridge and how we overcame them.

1. The WebRTC "Signal Soup"
Hurdle: Implementing stable video calling was the most difficult task. We initially struggled with peer-to-peer connections failing due to NAT traversal issues and mismatched signaling states (e.g., both parties trying to be the "initiator"). Solution: We built a dedicated Socket.io signaling server hosted on Vultr. We implemented a robust "Role-Based Signaling" logic where the first person in a room is designated as the initiator, and others join as peers. We also implemented an ICE Candidate Queue (in 
script.js
) to store candidates that arrive before the remote description is set, preventing connection drops.

2. Training vs. Inference Mismatch (The "Ghost Gesture" Bug)
Hurdle: We encountered a frustrating bug where the AI model was 99% accurate during training but failed to recognize simple gestures in the live app. Solution: After deep investigation (and with Antigravity’s help), we realized the landmark normalization logic in our Python inference script (
app.py
) didn't perfectly match the training script (
train.py
). We had to re-implement a wrist-relative, scale-invariant normalization function that accounts for the user's distance from the camera. Aligning these two scripts exactly was the key to achieving real-time accuracy.

3. Zero-Latency Audio Streaming
Hurdle: Traditional Text-to-Speech (TTS) waits for the entire audio file to generate before playing. This created a 3-5 second "awkward silence" after a signer finished a gesture. Solution: We moved to a Streaming Response Architecture. Our Flask backend now streams raw audio chunks from ElevenLabs as they are generated. On the frontend, we use the Response object to handle the stream directly. This reduced the time-to-speech from seconds to milliseconds, making the conversation feel truly synchronous.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

Technical Implementation Summary
SignBridge leverages the ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech (TTS) API to bridge the communication gap between the Deaf/Hard of Hearing community and non-signers. The integration is built using a Python Flask backend and a JavaScript-powered frontend, utilizing the ElevenLabs streaming architecture for low-latency, natural-sounding vocalizations.

Key Technical Specs:
API Endpoint: /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream
Model: eleven_multilingual_v2 (chosen for its high-fidelity and global language support)
Delivery: Audio streaming via chunks for immediate playback, ensuring real-time conversational flow.
Robustness: Intelligent fallback to local browser TTS engines to maintain accessibility in low-connectivity environments.
3 Pillars of Impact (Best Use Cases)
1. Real-Time Sign-to-Voice Translation
SignBridge doesn't just display text; it gives the signer a voice. As our AI engine detects hand gestures in real-time, it aggregates them into sentences and immediately streams high-quality AI speech. This allows non-signers to listen to the translation while maintaining eye contact, making the interaction feel like a natural conversation rather than a "screen-reading" experience.

2. High-Stakes Accessibility (SOS & Quick Phrases)
In critical situations, clarity and speed are vital. We’ve integrated ElevenLabs into our SOS Emergency and Quick Phrases features. With a single tap, the app can project an urgent, human-like vocal alert (e.g., "I need a doctor, I cannot breathe properly"). ElevenLabs provides the emotional weight and clarity that generic system voices often lack, which is crucial for getting immediate attention in emergencies.

3. Multilingual Inclusion
By utilizing the eleven_multilingual_v2 model, SignBridge is architected for global impact. We can synthesize speech in over 29 languages with a single model. This means a signer in India can communicate with an English speaker, or a Spanish speaker, with the AI voice handled seamlessly by ElevenLabs' sophisticated linguistic processing.

**Best Use of Vultr**

SignBridge is a high-availability accessibility tool that requires low-latency processing and reliable uptime. We chose Vultr to host our entire containerized infrastructure due to its superior price-to-performance ratio and global network.

Performance & Scaling on Vultr:
Optimized Cloud Compute: Our AI engine performs complex landmark normalization and classification. Vultr’s High Frequency Compute provides the consistent CPU performance required to prevent lag in real-time gesture recognition.
Dedicated Signaling Infrastructure: We run a Node.js signaling server alongside our Flask AI. Vultr allows us to manage these concurrent processes with dedicated resources, ensuring video calls remain stable even under high AI processing loads.
Global Low Latency: For WebRTC video calls, every millisecond counts. Vultr’s global data center footprint allows us to deploy close to our users, minimizing the latency that can disrupt a sign language conversation.
Uptime for Accessibility: As a tool designed for emergency (SOS) and daily communication, Vultr’s 100% SLA is a mission-critical feature for SignBridge.

**Best Use of Auth0**

"SignBridge leverages Auth0 to solve the dual challenge of Global Accessibility and Data Privacy. By implementing an enterprise-grade identity layer, we've enabled three key capabilities:

Personalized Sign Libraries: Each user's custom-trained gestures are securely isolated to their profile. This ensures that a user’s specific way of signing is remembered and protected, preventing data cross-contamination in our AI engine.
Frictionless Entry: SignBridge is designed for high-stakes environments (like hospitals or SOS situations). Our Auth0 integration provides One-Tap Social Login, eliminating registration barriers for users who need to communicate immediately.
Security-First Architecture: We offloaded all sensitive credential handling to Auth0. This ensures our platform is 'Secure by Design' and follows industry standards for privacy, which is crucial for building trust within the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community."

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

SignBridge was developed with the assistance of Antigravity, Google’s Advanced Agentic Coding AI. Antigravity served as an autonomous pair-programmer, handling everything from architectural design to complex debugging.

How Antigravity Accelerated the Project:
Architectural Orchestration: Antigravity mapped out the hybrid-stack architecture, ensuring the Python AI engine and Node.js signaling server could communicate seamlessly via local proxies and Gunicorn.
Agentic Debugging: During the difficult phase of WebRTC signaling and ElevenLabs chunk-streaming, Antigravity autonomously researched documentation, ran diagnostic scripts, and implemented fixes that reduced development time by days.
Cross-Language Mastery: The project required deep expertise in both Python (for Mediapipe/ML) and JavaScript (for the React-style UI). Antigravity managed this context-switching perfectly, ensuring code consistency across the entire repository.
Rapid Prototyping: From generating the premium UI design tokens to implementing the SOS emergency logic, Antigravity acted as a force-multiplier, allowing a complex idea to turn into a production-ready application in record time.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Cyber fraud has become one of the fastest-growing crimes in India. Every day, thousands of people lose money through phishing links, fake messages, scam calls, and malicious files received on platforms like WhatsApp, SMS, email, and social media.

The biggest victims are senior citizens, rural users, and people with limited digital awareness, who often cannot identify whether a message or link is legitimate or a scam. Existing solutions are either too technical, reactive (after the fraud happens), or not designed for common users.

Our solution aims to detect and prevent scams before users fall victim, making digital communication safer for everyone.

How People Can Use It

Our system works as a real-time cyber fraud detection assistant on smartphones.

Users can:

Scan suspicious messages, links, or files received on WhatsApp, SMS, or email.

Automatically detect phishing links and scam patterns using AI/ML models.

Get instant alerts and warnings before opening potentially harmful content.

Verify unknown messages or attachments with one click.

Protect themselves from financial scams without needing technical knowledge.

How It Makes Existing Tasks Safer

This solution improves digital safety by:

Preventing scams before users click malicious links

Providing simple warnings that anyone can understand

Reducing dependency on cybercrime awareness knowledge

Helping vulnerable users (especially elderly people) avoid fraud

Creating a safer digital ecosystem for India's growing internet population

Instead of reacting after money is lost, our platform focuses on early detection and prevention of cyber fraud in real time.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Detecting Scam Messages Accurately

One of the biggest challenges was identifying scam messages and phishing links correctly. Many scam messages look very similar to legitimate ones, which made it difficult to design a reliable detection system.

To solve this, we worked on pattern-based filtering and AI/ML models that analyze message structure, suspicious keywords, and link behavior. This improved the system’s ability to flag potential scams.


2. Designing for Non-Technical Users

Since our target audience includes senior citizens and rural users, designing a simple and understandable interface was challenging.

To overcome this, we focused on clear warnings, simple buttons, and easy-to-understand alerts, ensuring that even non-technical users can easily identify potential scams.

n our project, Aptos blockchain is used to provide tamper-proof logging and trust verification for network security events detected by the WIDRS-X intrusion detection system.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vigiledrive-f77c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Shweta-Verma1309/VigilDrive) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> driver fatique and distraction

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem
Road accidents are largely driven by split-second human errors: distracted driving and driver fatigue. Current Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) are expensive and exclusive to luxury vehicles, leaving everyday drivers and commercial fleets vulnerable. VigileDrive bridges this gap by offering a low-cost, AI-powered safety net that retrofits into any vehicle.
Who Is It For?
Logistics & Trucking: Prevents cargo loss and fatal accidents by monitoring long-haul driver exhaustion.

Rideshare & Gig Economy (Uber/Lyft): Ensures passenger safety by strictly flagging phone usage during shifts.

Public Transit & School Buses: Adds an automated layer of oversight for operators.

Everyday Commuters: Provides enterprise-grade safety monitoring using just a standard webcam.
How It Makes Driving Safer
Proactive Prevention: Detects drowsiness via Eye Aspect Ratio and phone usage via YOLOv8 before an accident happens, triggering instant audio-visual alarms.

Zero Special Hardware: Runs efficiently on standard webcams without needing expensive infrared sensors or proprietary automotive hardware.

Objective Monitoring: Removes human bias. If your eyes close for too many frames, the system calculates the danger and forces you awake.

100% Privacy (Edge AI): Processes all video locally on the device. No video feed is ever recorded or uploaded to the cloud, ensuring total driver privacy.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a real-time safety system sounds straightforward in theory, but moving from a "tutorial script" to a functional Vigil-Drive Dashboard involved overcoming several technical hurdles. Here are the most significant challenges I faced and the engineering solutions I used to solve them:
1. The "Frozen UI" Problem (Multithreading)The Challenge: Initially, the system would "stutter" or completely freeze the video feed for 1 second whenever the alarm triggered. This happened because winsound.Beep is a blocking function—the entire program stops to wait for the sound to finish playing before moving to the next frame.The Solution: I implemented Threaded Alerting. By wrapping the alarm in a Python threading object, the sound runs on a separate CPU lane. This allows the video processing to continue at 30 FPS while the alarm plays in the background.Python# The fix: daemon=True ensures the thread dies if the main app closes
threading.Thread(target=play_alarm, daemon=True).start()
2. "One Size Doesn't Fit All" (Dynamic Calibration)The Challenge: I found that a fixed threshold for eye closure (e.g., 0.2) worked perfectly for me but failed for teammates with naturally "heavy" eyelids or different seating positions. A static system led to constant false positives, which makes a safety system untrustworthy.The Solution: I developed a Dynamic Calibration Phase. When the script starts, it doesn't begin monitoring immediately. Instead, it captures the user’s average $EAR$ over the first 100 frames.Calculation: It sets the "danger line" at 75% of the user's specific average.Result: This creates a personalized "baseline" for every driver, significantly improving accuracy across different ethnicities and lighting conditions.
3. Coordinate Mapping for the DashboardThe Challenge: Drawing the live EAR/MAR graphs directly on the video frame was difficult. OpenCV uses a coordinate system where $(0,0)$ is the top-left, but math graphs usually go "up" from the bottom.The Solution: I wrote a custom normalization function within draw_plot(). It maps the history of EAR values (typically decimals between $0.1$ and $0.4$) to pixel offsets. I used a "Bottom-Up" subtraction logic:py = int((y + h) - (value / max_scale) * h)This ensures that as your eyes open wider (higher EAR), the line on the graph physically moves upwards, making it intuitive for the user to read.
4. CPU Bottleneck & Model Optimization The Challenge: Running a full YOLOv8 model alongside MediaPipe Face Mesh was taxing the CPU, causing the frame rate to drop below 10 FPS. High latency is dangerous in a safety app; a 2-second lag could be the difference between a warning and an accident. The Solution: I shifted from the standard PyTorch (.pt) format to ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange).The Result: The ONNX weights are optimized for "Edge" devices (standard laptop CPUs). This, combined with setting verbose=False in the YOLO prediction, boosted the performance back up to a smooth 25–30 FPS.5. Handling "Face Visibility" Logic The Challenge: If the driver looked away or the camera lost the face, the EAR would drop to zero, triggering a false "Drowsiness" alarm. The Solution: I added a Visibility Guard. The system now distinguishes between "Eyes Closed" and "Face Missing". If the face is gone, it displays a "DRIVER NOT VISIBLE" alert. It only increments the closed eye frames counter if a face is actively detected in the frame. This logic prevents the alarm from screaming every time the driver checks their side mirror.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Job hunting is exhausting. Every application often means repeating the same cycle tailoring a resume, writing a cover letter, drafting an email, attaching files, sending it, and remembering to follow up later. Doing this manually for dozens of roles can take hours. As a result, many people either apply to very few jobs or send the same generic resume everywhere, which significantly reduces their chances.

Applyzer automates this entire workflow.

A user sets up their profile once adding their work experience, skills, and projects and the platform takes care of the rest.

### Tailored resumes on demand
Instead of relying on a single generic resume, Applyzer generates a LaTeX-compiled resume dynamically for each job. Using the job description, AI selects the most relevant projects and experience to highlight.

### AI-generated application emails
Each application includes a personalized email written by AI. The email follows a clear structure: a short introduction, three specific points based on the user’s experience, and a concise closing avoiding generic templates.

### Automated bulk sending
Users can review and approve multiple applications at once. After approval, Applyzer sends them through the user’s Gmail account with smart time gaps to reduce the risk of spam filters.

### Automatic follow-ups
If a recruiter doesn’t respond after a defined period, Applyzer automatically sends a follow-up and tracks replies in Google Sheets in real time.

### Human-in-the-loop control
Nothing is sent without the user reviewing and approving it first. This keeps the user fully in control while removing the repetitive manual effort.

In short: what once required hours of manual work can now be done with a quick review and a single click.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges Faced**


**Deploying & Configuring Vultr**
  Setting up the production server from scratch involved configuring the Vultr firewall, configuring Nginx as a reverse proxy, and fixing CORS conflicts arising from duplicate server blocks. Managing the Uvicorn process and running it indefinitely, as well as configuring the DuckDNS domain to redirect Google OAuth requests, were some other challenges.

**Database Connectivity**
  Connectivity to Supabase from the VM proved to be a challenge since ports were blocked, the pooler required a specific username format (postgres.PROJECT_REF), and troubleshooting "Tenant or user not found" errors was a challenge.

* Gmail API & Bulk Mail Sending
  Gmail API OAuth was another challenge since it did not allow us to authenticate without a registered domain, and sending bulk emails using background workers with time gaps between each worker was another challenge.

**Google Sheets Tracking & Apps Script**
  Using Google Sheets as a live tracker was another challenge since we had to manage OAuth scopes and service account permissions.

**Stitching It All Together**
  The biggest challenge was bringing together AI resume generation, LaTeX compilation, Gmail API, Google Sheets tracking, and follow-ups into a single pipeline running on a single Vultr instance.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

We leveraged the Gemini API as a foundational intelligence component in Applyzer, a tool using artificial intelligence to assist users in crafting high-quality, personalized applications in bulk from a selected list of jobs. For each job opening, Gemini processes job descriptions and matches them with users’ project and skill profiles, crafting personalized emails and accompanying application content in a professional tone. Rather than using templates, Gemini enables users to create relevant and personalized messages, saving users a considerable amount of time and effort in crafting context-specific messages per organization.

**Best Use of Vultr**

Applyzer is an agentic job application automation platform that utilizes a FastAPI backend server hosted on a Vultr Cloud Compute instance. The server performs compute-intensive tasks such as creating AI-optimized LaTeX resumes with Groq AI, sending automated job application emails through the user’s Gmail account with smart intervals for timing, and continuously running background workers to track replies and send follow-up emails.

This application utilizes Nginx as a reverse proxy server to manage incoming requests and DuckDNS to map the server’s IP address to a custom domain for Gmail OAuth. Vultr offers a cheap yet always-on Linux environment for the server to run long-running processes and background workers that serverless platforms do not support.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🌐 Progressive Web App for Offline Communities

Our Progressive Web App (PWA) is designed to keep communities connected even when internet connectivity is unavailable. In disaster-hit areas, remote regions, or during network blackouts, communication becomes extremely difficult, delaying help and coordination. This platform enables **offline messaging, local resource sharing, and emergency coordination** without relying on continuous internet access.
🚨 How People Can Use It

**1. Offline Messaging**
- Users can send messages to nearby devices using local networks such as Bluetooth, Wi-Fi Direct, or mesh networking.
- Messages sync automatically when devices reconnect to the internet.

**2. Emergency Alerts**
- Authorities or community leaders can broadcast emergency alerts to nearby users.
- Helps quickly share information about **danger zones, evacuation routes, or rescue updates**.

**3. Resource Sharing**
- Community members can post available resources such as:
  - Food supplies
  - Medical help
  - Shelter availability
  - Charging stations
- Others nearby can instantly see and access these resources.

**4. Local Community Coordination**
- Volunteers can organize rescue activities.
- People can report missing individuals or request help.

⚡ How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

- **Works without internet:** Essential communication remains available during outages.
- **Faster disaster response:** Critical updates spread locally even when networks fail.
- **Improved safety:** People receive real-time alerts and location-based help.
- **Community-driven support:** Encourages neighbors to help each other during crises.
- **Offline-first design:** Data is cached locally and synced automatically when connectivity returns.

🌍 Real-World Impact

This solution empowers communities to stay connected, informed, and coordinated during emergencies — ensuring that **lack of internet access never becomes a barrier to safety and support.**

**Challenges we ran into**

🐞 Challenge We Faced

One of the main challenges during development was implementing **secure peer-to-peer messaging without relying on a centralized server**. Since the system works in a decentralized mesh network, devices must handle identity verification, encryption, and message delivery on their own.

Initially, we used **Ed25519 keys for user identity**, but the encryption process required **Curve25519 keys**. This mismatch caused encryption and decryption errors, because the key formats and lengths were not directly compatible.

Another issue was handling **offline peers in Bluetooth communication**. If a device was temporarily unavailable, messages would fail to send and get lost.

🔧 How We Solved It

To solve the cryptography issue, we kept **Ed25519 keys for identity management** and converted them to **Curve25519 keys for encryption** using the `libsodium-wrappers-sumo` library. This ensured secure end-to-end encryption while maintaining a reliable identity system.

For the networking issue, we implemented a **message queue system** in the P2P layer. When a peer is offline, messages are temporarily stored and automatically sent once the peer reconnects.

✅ Result

After these improvements, the system can now **securely exchange encrypted messages between devices using Bluetooth**, support **QR-based identity sharing**, and **reliably deliver messages even when peers go offline temporarily**, making the mesh communication network much more stable and practical for real-world use.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meetpilot-f6b8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/kunalkarmaftw/meet-pilot) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Making interactions easier

![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mailgun API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mailgun%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![chromadb](https://img.shields.io/badge/chromadb-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deepgram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deepgram-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most AI meeting tools only give you a transcript or summary after the meeting is over. During the meeting, you still struggle with cognitive overload—trying to pay attention, take notes, remember past context, immediately figure out responses, and plan follow-up tasks all at the same time.

 MeetPilot acts as an active AI Co-Pilot during the meeting. It processes live audio in real-time to solve several specific in-meeting problems automatically:

"I spaced out / stepped away for a minute":
Uses Ghost Mode to give you an instant "catch-up" summary card of the part of the conversation you just missed.

"Haven't we talked about this before?":
Uses Déjà Vu Alert to search past meetings in the background and alert you if the team is repeating a previously discussed topic, avoiding redundant discussions.

"Someone just asked me a question, what should I say?":
Uses Response Generator to detect when a question is directed at you and instantly supplies you with 2-3 AI-generated response options.

"I don't have time to do all this post-meeting admin work":
As tasks are assigned or decisions are made live, the Decision Detector catches them and automatically acts on them:

Auto-Send Emails: Instantly drafts follow-up or assignment emails to team members.

Calendar Auto-Blocker: Finds a free slot in your Google Calendar and automatically blocks "Focus Time" for the task you were just assigned.

Document Generator: Automatically drafts a markdown file containing the new project plans or decisions made.

"I'm not prepared for this meeting":
Uses Pre-Meeting Briefing to pull context from past meetings and create a structured briefing card before the meeting even starts.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Capturing Live Audio (Hardest Part)

The biggest challenge I faced was capturing the audio of other participants from Zoom, Google Meet, or Teams and sending it to my Python backend. Normal microphone access only captures my own voice.

To solve this, I used virtual audio devices like VB-CABLE to route the system’s output audio as an input device. Then I captured that audio in my Python application using PyAudio so the backend could process the meeting conversation in real time.

2. LLM Rate Limits

Since MeetPilot continuously analyzes conversations, the system was hitting API rate limits quickly:

Groq: 30 requests/minute

Gemini 2.0 Flash: 15 requests/minute

To handle this, I implemented a fallback routing system so if Gemini fails or reaches its limit, requests automatically switch to Groq. I also used a priority queue with asyncio semaphores to ensure important tasks (like detecting questions) are processed before lower-priority tasks.

3. Context Window Overload

Sending an entire 45-minute meeting transcript to an LLM for every request would be slow and expensive.

To solve this, I built a 3-Layer Context Engine:

Rolling Buffer for recent conversation

Full Session Transcript for storage

Compressed Timeline that summarizes chunks every 60 seconds

### Safe-Travel
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/safetravel-435c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Itsorgnikhil/Sate-Travel) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Real people. Real reviews. Safer routes.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many people travel every day without knowing whether the route or area they are passing through is safe or not. Traditional navigation apps mainly focus on shortest distance, fastest time, and traffic, but they do not provide real-time safety information about locations.

This leads to several problems:

🚨 People unknowingly travel through crime-prone or unsafe areas.

🌙 Some locations are safe during the day but risky at night, and current maps do not reflect this.

🛣️ Roads may be dangerous due to poor lighting, accidents, or harassment incidents, but travelers are unaware.

🧭 There is no reliable platform where communities can share safety feedback about routes and places.

🏪 Shops, streets, or neighborhoods may have safety issues that are not visible in traditional navigation systems.

Because of this lack of safety awareness, travelers, especially women, tourists, delivery workers, and night commuters, may face dangerous situations.

Safe-Travel solves this problem by providing a community-powered safety navigation system that identifies safe and unsafe areas using real-time reviews, verified user feedback, and safety zone classification.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of Safe-Travel, several technical and design challenges were encountered:

🗺️ Integrating Map Services

Integrating the Google Maps API with the application was challenging, especially when trying to overlay custom safety zones (Red, Orange, Green) on top of the map and dynamically update them based on user feedback.

📊 Converting Reviews into Safety Scores

One of the biggest challenges was designing a system that can analyze user reviews and convert them into a safety classification. Determining whether a location should be marked as safe or unsafe based on keywords and sentiment required careful logic and experimentation.

👥 Ensuring Reliable Feedback

Since the platform depends on community reviews, there is a risk of fake or misleading feedback. Creating a system where verified users and local travelers have more influence was necessary to maintain reliability.

⏱️ Dynamic Safety Based on Time

Some places are safe during the day but unsafe at night. Designing a model that allows zones to change based on time and user reports required additional logic and data handling.

📍 Location Accuracy

Collecting and processing real-time location data while ensuring privacy and accurate zone classification was another challenge during implementation.

⚖️ Balancing Community and Predefined Data

The system needed to balance predefined red zones from news or reports with live community feedback, ensuring that zones could improve or worsen over time.

### MeshCall
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meshcall-3344) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Rishujha098/Mess_calling) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Stay Connected, Stay Offline

![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. 🚨 Emergency Communication Breakdown
Problem:

Natural disasters destroy cell towers and internet infrastructure
First responders can't coordinate rescue operations
Families can't locate each other during evacuations
Emergency services overloaded or non-functional
MeshCall Solution:

✅ Works completely offline - no infrastructure needed
✅ Device-to-device communication within 100m range
✅ Real-time location sharing to find family members
✅ Mesh relay can extend range through intermediate devices


2. 🏔️ Remote Area Communication Gap
Problem:

Rural areas, mountains, forests have zero cellular coverage
Hikers, trekkers, campers are isolated
Remote communities have no affordable communication
Emergency help can't be called
MeshCall Solution:

✅ Bluetooth + WiFi Direct work anywhere
✅ No need for cell towers or internet
✅ Group communication for expeditions
✅ Location tracking for safe

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges I Ran Into
1. WiFi Direct Discovery Intermittent Failures 🔴
The Problem:
WiFi Direct discovery would trigger only 3 times (at 5s, 15s, 30s intervals) and then completely stop. Devices would find each other briefly but couldn't maintain connections.

Root Cause:
Android automatically suspends WiFi Direct discovery after ~30 seconds to save battery. The flutter_p2p_connection plugin's discovery mechanism wasn't aggressive enough for reliable peer finding.

Solution:

Implemented aggressive continuous discovery with Timer.periodic triggering every 8 seconds
Added stop → 300ms delay → discover cycle to force re-initialization
Created 20-second retry loop in mesh service that restarts discovery if peers are lost
Result: ✅ Discovery now runs continuously and auto-recovers from suspensions

### SecureScope
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/securescope-d05f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sm-28601/hackhawk-v2.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> AI Vulnerability Scanner

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The problem it solves

In modern software development, security is a massive bottleneck. When Security teams run standard SAST and DAST scanners, they are bombarded with **Alert Fatigue**—hundreds of noisy alerts and false positives. Developers are then forced to waste countless hours manually triaging these alerts, reading OWASP documentation, and writing repetitive code patches. 

While existing AI tools attempt to solve this, they fail in three critical ways:
1. **They only *suggest* fixes**, forcing the developer to manually copy-paste code.
2. **They hallucinate or break builds** by inserting conversational text (e.g., `"Here is your fixed code:"`) directly into source files.
3. **They compromise privacy** by sending proprietary, PII-laden source code to cloud APIs.

**SecureScope** completely eliminates this bottleneck by acting as an autonomous, closed-loop DevSecOps engineer. It solves the problem by:
* **Filtering Noise:** Using a hybrid ML approach (SVM + Random Forest) to instantly kill false positives before they ever reach an expensive LLM.
* **Writing the Code:** Generating raw, functional patches and rewriting the actual source files.
* **Proving the Fix:** Generating adversarial fuzz tests (SQLi, XSS payloads) to mathematically prove the patch works. 
* **Zero-Touch Delivery:** Wrapping the verified code into a clean GitHub Pull Request, with a detailed markdown explanation in the PR body. 
* **100% Privacy:** Running completely offline using local inference (Ollama) and redacting PII via spaCy before scanning.

Developers simply paste a GitHub repo URL into our Streamlit dashboard, and SecureScope hands them a fully verified, ready-to-merge Pull Request.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I ran into

Building an autonomous AI agent that modifies production code is incredibly dangerous. I ran into several major hurdles trying to rein in the LLM's chaotic behavior:

**1. The "Chatty AI" Syntax Corruption**
* **The Hurdle:** LLMs are conversational by nature. When instructed to fix a `.js` or `Dockerfile`, the AI would constantly wrap the output in Markdown blocks or inject chatty comments like `// Fixed SQL injection here`. If pushed to GitHub, this immediately broke the compiler and syntax.
* **The Solution:** I engineered a strict separation of concerns. I built a Python Regex parser that acts as a "defensive wall," forcibly stripping all conversational English and extracting *only* the raw code. The AI's reasoning is dynamically pushed to the GitHub API to form the PR description, keeping the codebase completely pristine.

**2. LLM Laziness (Task Overload)**
* **The Hurdle:** When the scanners found 70+ vulnerabilities in a single repository and I fed them to the LLM in bulk, the model experienced task overload. It would fix the very first issue, get "lazy," and spit the rest of the vulnerable code back unmodified.
* **The Solution:** I refactored the Python orchestrator from "Bulk Patching" to "Iterative File-Based Patching." The pipeline groups vulnerabilities by file path and feeds them to the LLM in a loop—forcing it to address exactly one vulnerability at a time. The code state accumulates layer by layer, ensuring every single bug is patched before the PR is opened.

**3. Contextual Framework Hallucinations**
* **The Hurdle:** The AI correctly identified that running a Docker container as `root` was dangerous. However, it hallucinated a generic solution by adding `USER nonroot` to a Node.js Dockerfile. Official Node images don't have a `nonroot` user (they use `node`), so the fix caused the container to crash.
* **The Solution:** I enhanced the LLM's system prompt to be context-aware. I fed it explicit framework rules, preventing it from guessing users and forcing it to rely on the specific base image architectures.

**4. Flawed Test Verification**
* **The Hurdle:** I initially wrote verification tests that bypassed the application entirely and shot SQL injection payloads directly into the database driver. This created a false sense of security, as it wasn't testing the actual API surface.
* **The Solution:** I rebuilt the **AI Fuzzer** to attack the application layer directly. It now spins up the patched code and fires malicious payloads (like `' OR '1'='1`) at the API endpoints, ensuring the HTTP responses properly sanitize the input before authorizing the PR.

Team **Root_BIT** -- [sahil maurya](https://github.com/sm-28601), [Shivang Kathait](https://github.com/ShivangKathait29)

**The problem it solves**

MaskByte crafts a single output file that is simultaneously valid for multiple formats. Every parser only reads the bytes it cares about; everything else hides in plain sight.

*MaskByte breaks that assumption.*

### QRypt
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qrypt-09a4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PV-AKSHAYA/QRypt-Backend) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://qrypt-ecru.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Real-time contextual QR forensics analyzer

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every day, millions of us scan QR codes at parking meters, restaurants, and office lobbies as an act of pure faith, yet these codes are essentially "black boxes" that the human eye cannot verify. Attackers are exploiting this blind trust through "Quishing", physically pasting malicious stickers over legitimate ones to hijack payments or steal credentials. While we’ve been trained to check for suspicious emails, we have no way to see the "Double-Edge" of a physical sticker or the 10-hop redirect chain hidden behind a simple square. This creates a massive security gap where a simple sticker can bypass a multi-million dollar corporate firewall. QRypt closes this gap by treating every scan as a forensic investigation, checking the physical print, the digital route, and the brand's legitimacy in seconds to ensure that what you see is actually what you get.

**Challenges we ran into**

Initially we started working on a common GitHub repository and when the time came to merge the branches we had to face many many merge conflicts. Resolving this problem taught all of us about Git and GitHub. 
Later when we were integrating the LLM API layer, we faced issues with rate limiters of Gemini 1.5 API key as well as OpenAI API keys. After trying to work with these LLMs for a long time, we switched to Groq API and went ahead with the rest of the project. 
We wouldn't say that they were challenges, instead we would like to take them as learning experiences.

### Atlas
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/atlas-94d5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Janmitha-s/Atlas.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lCbohSA4ENU) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lCbohSA4ENU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> We hold up the heavens

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In the world of cybersecurity, we focus heavily on encryption; however, encryption is "loud" it screams that something is being hidden. To bypass modern security, malicious actors turn to Steganography, the art of hiding sensitive data within innocent-looking images formats, PNGs, BMPs etc. This creates a massive security blind spot where a database can leak in plain sight, masquerading as a standard email attachment.

ATLAS solves this problem by shifting defense from the network edge to the device level, stopping the leak before the data ever leaves the endpoint. By combining a highly specialized Google Chrome extension that monitors browser-based uploads with a high-performance backend that combines a multitude of Mathematical and statistical techniques, along with machine learning models to evaluate the risk of encoded information sneaking into an image. Furthermore, we utilized NLP to get rid of false positives, and heatmaps, to clearly visualize the presence of encoded bits.

The extension functions as a real-time Data Loss Prevention (DLP) gateway by intercepting browser-level file inputs. When a user attempts to attach a file, such as an encoded png image being sent across gmail, the extension captures the object, suspends the upload, and routes the data to a secure backend for heuristic analysis. 

If a security threat or sensitive data leak is identified, the extension programmatically aborts the network request, preventing the file from ever reaching the external server and ensuring corporate compliance minimizing loss.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cb7998e72a514e378f4baa4e4bbe1ca8/3466f809-724b-4958-a5ba-749a50e49185.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cb7998e72a514e378f4baa4e4bbe1ca8/f5613834-060d-4042-9bc9-177b9e2a721c.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cb7998e72a514e378f4baa4e4bbe1ca8/b6cd988f-6518-4ff9-8b3c-5b59676e3160.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/cb7998e72a514e378f4baa4e4bbe1ca8/b526044b-2a7a-45c7-912e-de84dad8d699.jpeg)


ATLAS makes sure that information is mathematically secured against even the most covert exfiltration attempts.

**Challenges we ran into**

Upon advice from our mentors, we reevaluated the use case of our project. 

The concept of a actual middleman seemed redundant considering the data had already left the device-level.                                                                            

This gave rise to the idea of a device level interface, using MITM(Man in the middle) Proxy to intercept emails. It was only after implementation that Gmail made it incredibly difficult for our on protocol to run for several reasons.                                       

Gmail's frontend code checks that the certificate comes from Google's own CA, not just any trusted CA. When the proxy presents its fake cert, Gmail sees it's not Google's real cert and refuses the connection entirely. Furthermore Chrome has built-in certificate transparency checks and HSTS preloading for Google domains. Even if you install the proxy's root CA system-wide, Chrome ignores it. WhatsApp Web, Slack, and most banking sites do the same thing. The proxy either breaks the site completely or the site refuses to load.

That's exactly why we switched to the Chrome extension approach, it intercepts uploads inside the browser at the JavaScript level (before encryption), so it never needs to touch TLS certificates at all. This approach also made it easily extendable to other web applications on Chrome. A consequence of both of these device level interceptors was reduced latency(due to the ML model) and vulnerability to bulk attacks.

### Shadow Permission Analyzer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shadow-permission-analyzer-95dd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Shashank0701-byte/Shadow-permission-analyser) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-zXz4bI123A) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Expose hidden cloud permission before attackers do

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![NetworkX](https://img.shields.io/badge/NetworkX-333333?style=flat-square) ![Boto3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Boto3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cloud environments like AWS use Identity and Access Management (IAM) to control who can access which resources. In large organizations, IAM configurations can contain thousands of users, roles, and policies, creating extremely complex permission structures.
Because these permissions are defined across many separate JSON policies and trust relationships, hidden privilege escalation paths can exist without being noticed. For example, a low-privilege user such as an intern might indirectly gain administrator access through a chain of role assumptions.
Manually auditing these relationships is nearly impossible for security teams, as they must analyse thousands of interconnected permissions.
Shadow Permission Analyzer solves this problem by:
1. Extracting IAM relationships from AWS environments.
2. Converting permissions into a graph model.
3. Using graph traversal algorithms to detect hidden privilege escalation paths.
4. Visually highlighting risky access chains so security teams can quickly identify and fix them.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was understanding and extracting the complex relationships within AWS IAM. IAM permissions are defined across multiple policies, roles, and trust relationships, often stored as large JSON documents. Mapping these scattered configurations into a meaningful structure required careful parsing and normalization of the data using boto3.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cyberclash-9288) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/eshaa7/Cyber-Clash) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rj__wtvwUG_SSkCS4i1tlsfA2dSVJuOX?usp=drive_link) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Train Like a Hacker. Think Like a Defender.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cybersecurity education today often relies on passive learning methods such as lectures, theoretical explanations, and static lab exercises. While these approaches help students understand concepts, they do not effectively simulate the dynamic and adversarial nature of real cyber attacks. In real-world cybersecurity environments, attackers and defenders constantly adapt their strategies in response to each other’s actions. However, most existing learning platforms focus primarily on isolated challenges or single-player environments where vulnerabilities are solved step by step without real-time opposition.

This gap makes it difficult for beginners and students to develop practical intuition about how attacks unfold and how defenders detect and stop them. Many learners know about vulnerabilities like SQL injection, cross-site scripting, or credential attacks in theory, but they lack experience in recognizing these attacks in live systems, analyzing logs, and responding quickly to evolving threats.

Cyber-Clash addresses this problem by providing a real-time multiplayer cybersecurity simulation platform where users actively perform attacks and defenses in a shared environment. Instead of solving static problems, players take on the roles of attacker and defender, interacting with a simulated system where vulnerabilities exist and must be exploited or mitigated dynamically.

The platform can be used by students, cybersecurity learners, and educators as an engaging way to practice cybersecurity concepts through competitive gameplay. It makes learning easier by breaking down complex security topics into progressive scenarios, allowing players to gradually build skills such as network reconnaissance, authentication attacks, vulnerability exploitation, and defensive monitoring. At the same time, it makes training safer by providing a controlled simulation environment where users can experiment with cyber attacks without affecting real systems.

By transforming cybersecurity education into an interactive and competitive experience, Cyber-Clash helps users develop practical skills, improve analytical thinking, and better understand how real cyber attacks and defenses occur in modern digital systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

-One challenge was designing the scenario randomization system. The game needed to generate different scenarios each round so players could not memorize solutions, but the randomness still had to stay within the correct cybersecurity topic for each tier. This was solved by structuring the system so that the tier defines the topic, the scenario defines the environment, and only the scenario parameters are randomized.

- Another challenge was implementing real-time multiplayer interaction between the attacker and defender. Since both players interact with the same environment simultaneously, the system needed a way to keep actions synchronized. This was solved using WebSockets, which allow the server to instantly send updates such as attacks, defenses, and logs to both players in real time.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/phantomshell-6218) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/visky904/phanton-shell2) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://phanton-shellv2.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> PHANTOM-SHELL!Hack the system. Control your nerves

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebRTC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebRTC-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern cybersecurity training platforms primarily evaluate technical knowledge, but they fail to simulate the psychological pressure of a real cyberattack. During actual incidents—such as ransomware outbreaks or live breaches—security analysts often experience intense cognitive stress that leads to syntax mistakes, slower decisions, and poor incident response. This gap between theoretical skill and real-world performance is known as the “Panic Gap.”

PHANTOM-SHELL addresses this problem by introducing a system that measures and reacts to the user’s stress in real time, forcing trainees to maintain composure while solving cybersecurity challenges.

**Challenges we ran into**

Traditional approaches attempt to estimate stress through physiological signals such as heart rate using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) via webcam. However, this method proved unreliable in practice—lighting conditions, darker skin tones, glasses, and camera quality significantly reduced accuracy.

To overcome this limitation, the project implements a privacy-preserving and hardware-free alternative stress estimation model that works entirely inside the user’s local browser. Instead of relying solely on rPPG, the system analyzes facial tension and behavioral cues from the webcam feed using computer vision. The model evaluates indicators such as eyebrow compression (focus/anger), eye squinting (strain), mouth tension, and agitation through head movement, combining them into an approximate stress score.
