> Detect Regimes. Adapt Strategies. Preserve Capital

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

📊 Pitch Deck / PPT: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1UhT-gc1Vy55vGxnvnSx8zyUFcpVsHMz2/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108309544140241004224&rtpof=true&sd=true

🧠 The Problem It Solves

Static portfolio models fail when markets change — CHRONOS fixes this.

Most retail investors rely on fixed 60/40 allocations or robo-advisors that treat bull markets and crashes the same way.
The result? 35% losses in March 2020 when correlations spiked to 1.0 and “diversified” portfolios collapsed together.

🚀 What CHRONOS Does Differently
Traditional Approach	CHRONOS Solution
One model for all market conditions	3 specialized models, each trained exclusively on bull, neutral, or bear market data
Mean-variance optimization (1952)	CVaR optimization — minimizes tail risk like hedge funds
Static “set it & forget it” allocation	Dynamic regime detection — rotates defensive before crashes
Black-box AI	SHAP interpretability — every decision is explainable
📈 Real-World Impact

Protects capital during market stress
2024 Rate Hike Selloff:
CHRONOS −0.62% vs SPY −1.46%

Captures upside in bull markets
14.25% total return in 2024

Democratizes institutional-grade risk management
Tools previously locked behind $1M+ minimums, now accessible to retail investors

👥 Who Uses This

Retail investors seeking hedge-fund style risk management

Financial advisors needing explainable AI for client portfolios

Researchers studying regime-switching financial markets

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into
⚠️ Challenge 1: Lookahead Bias (The Silent Killer)

The bug
Rolling features were created using:

rolling(window=20).mean()


without .shift(1), leaking future data into training.

How I fixed it

Enforced strict anti-leakage protocol — all features use .shift(1)

Added a validation layer in feature_engineering.py that raises a ValueError if leakage is detected

Used time-based splits only
(Train: 2019–2022 | Val: 2023 | Test: 2024)

⚠️ Challenge 2: HMM Convergence Instability

The bug
hmmlearn.GaussianHMM sometimes:

Collapsed into a single dominant regime

Failed to converge with default settings

How I fixed it

Implemented BIC-based state selection (tested 2–5 states)

Added convergence diagnostics (log-likelihood tracking)

Set random_state=42 and n_iter=1000 for stable convergence

⚠️ Challenge 3: CVaR Optimization Failure

The bug
PyPortfolioOpt.EfficientCVaR occasionally failed with
optimization infeasible due to tight regime constraints or ill-conditioned data.

How I fixed it

Added fallback heuristic allocations per regime:

Euphoria: 70 / 20 / 10 (SPY / TLT / GLD)

Complacency: 50 / 30 / 20

Capitulation: 10 / 60 / 30

Wrapped optimizer in try-except with logging
→ system degrades gracefully, never crashes

⚠️ Challenge 4: Real-Time Dashboard Performance

The bug
Streamlit app reloaded all models on every interaction → 8+ second lag.

How I fixed it

Used @st.cache_data for datasets

Used @st.cache_resource for models

Reduced HMM inference to <10ms via vectorization

Added lazy loading for SHAP plots (computed only when opened)

**Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning**

1️⃣ Core Track Alignment
Track Requirement	CHRONOS Implementation
Financial data analysis	Real-time processing of OHLCV, VIX, and Treasury yields using yfinance and FRED
Quantitative modeling	Bayesian HMM for regime detection + XGBoost ensemble for predictive modeling
Risk quantification	CVaR optimization minimizing Expected Shortfall in the worst 5% scenarios
Machine learning	3 specialized models, each trained on regime-specific data distributions
2️⃣ What “Quantifying the Markets” Actually Means (and How CHRONOS Does It)

The track emphasizes turning market chaos into measurable, actionable intelligence.
CHRONOS does this through four explicit quantification layers:

📊 Quantification Layer 1: Market Regimes

Most ML models assume stationary data — markets are not stationary.

CHRONOS identifies three market personalities:

Euphoria

Complacency

Capitulation

Uses Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) for regime inference

Outputs

Regime probability distributions

Transition matrices

Confidence scores (0–100%)

📈 Quantification Layer 2: Predictive Uncertainty

Instead of fragile point predictions, CHRONOS models probabilistic outcomes.

Predicts return quintiles with full probability distributions

Example

60% probability: Quintile 4–5 (bullish)
20% probability: Quintile 3 (neutral)
20% probability: Quintile 1–2 (bearish)

This explicitly quantifies uncertainty, not just direction.

⚠️ Quantification Layer 3: Risk-Adjusted Allocation

The key question is not “What will happen?” but
“How should we position given uncertainty?”

CVaR optimization answers:
“What is our average loss in the worst 5% of scenarios?”

Dynamic exposure constraints:

Euphoria: 60–80% equity

Capitulation: 0–20% equity

🔍 Quantification Layer 4: Explainable Metrics

Every decision is measurable and explainable.

SHAP values quantify feature contributions

“VIX contributed 68% to this Capitulation signal”

Performance attribution:

Crisis alpha

Sortino ratio

Calmar ratio

Rolling drawdowns

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nirvanacodes-e910) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/avnijainnn/offroad-segmentation-) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TYMnOeTisQWVyarruoSYL9aK1KDqykyb/view?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co)

> coding till nirvana

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

here we describe  Semantic Scene Segmentation for off-road environments, leveraging self-supervised learning with DINOv2 to reduce labeling cost and training time. The primary problems addressed include terrain understanding, obstacle avoidance, and safer navigation.

Methodology and Workflow:
The Duality Falcon Simulation Pipeline is used for digital twin creation, scenario execution, and generating synthetic data.
Simulated sensor outputs include RGB, Semantic (Semant.), Depth, and LIDAR data.
The training flow involves several key steps:
Load and Preprocess off-road images and segmentation masks.
Extract Rich Visual Features using the self-supervised Vision Transformer, DINOv2, which encodes the image into semantic patch-level features.
Cache Backbone Features to avoid repeated computation and for efficiency.
Train a Lightweight Segmentation Head (a small convolutional head) to map features to pixel-wise semantic classes.
Evaluate using Intersection over Union (IoU).
This approach decouples representation learning from task learning and, by caching DINOv2 features, reduces training time from hours to minutes while preserving semantic quality.
Results and Challenges:
The final validation mean IoU (mIoU) is 0.3979.

**Challenges we ran into**

Limited Spatial Resolution: DINOv2 patch tokens operate at a $14 \times 14$ stride, potentially losing fine details.
Frozen Backbone Constraint: Limits task-specific adaptation to off-road scenes, trading specialization for speed.
Class Imbalance: Biases learning toward frequent classes like Sky and Landscape, resulting in lower IoU for rare classes.
Ambiguous Class Boundaries: Visual similarity between classes (e.g., dry grass vs. bushes) leads to confusion.
Limited Training Epochs: Capped at 5 epochs for rapid iteration, not maximum accuracy.
No Temporal Context: Model processes single frames, causing inconsistent predictions in video.
Synthetic-to-Real Gap: If simulation data is used, differences in lighting, textures, and physics may require domain adaptation.

AURUM introduces a continuous cognitive loop:
Sense → Predict → Understand → Decide → Act

The system works by:
Detecting abnormal activity patterns in real time
Predicting future system stress before failure occurs
Evaluating cascading risk across interconnected components
Making autonomous governance decisions
Executing protective actions instantly without human delay

Rather than reporting problems, AURUM prevents them.

Existing infrastructures rely heavily on dashboards, alerts, and manual intervention, which leads to delayed responses and significant losses.

The key challenges addressed by AURUM include:
Post-event fraud detection, where threats are identified only after damage occurs
Lack of predictive intelligence to foresee system stress or cascading failures
Siloed monitoring tools that fail to understand system-wide risk impact
Human-dependent decision-making, limiting response speed during critical events
Inability to take autonomous protective action in real time

As financial complexity grows, these limitations expose institutions to fraud, instability, and operational failure.

### ScrollPause
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/scrollpause-6bdf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/afifaameer19/ScrollPause.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/Trqruj8P4WE?si=hpcBo3kPs1oNQFWE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Scroll. Pause. Breathe.

![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![XML](https://img.shields.io/badge/XML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Short-form content like Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts is designed to keep people scrolling endlessly. What usually starts as “just 5 minutes” often turns into 30–60 minutes without the user even realizing it. This leads to loss of focus, procrastination, mental fatigue, and a feeling of regret after excessive scrolling.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f42660f6e96d424683fee92419b2e795/6118acd0-d76c-4311-8294-043aabf6d5ca.png)

**How Its Different from other apps**

Most existing solutions either completely block apps or bombard users with strict warnings, which often feels frustrating and causes people to uninstall them. The real problem isn’t lack of discipline—it’s the absence of mindful interruption at the right moment.

ScrollPause helps users become aware of their scrolling habits without shaming or forcing them to stop.

When a user crosses a set scrolling time limit on Reels or Shorts, the app gently intervenes with a calm pop-up instead of an aggressive block. It first engages the user in a short, non-stimulating activity (two rounds of tic-tac-toe) to break the automatic scrolling loop.

After that, the app asks the user to reflect by entering a couple of tasks they actually want or need to do. The user is given a choice—continue scrolling or continue with their tasks—so they remain in control of their decisions.

If the user chooses to focus on tasks, the scrolling apps are temporarily locked for a short period (10–15 minutes), creating a safe space for self-reflection and productivity

**Challenges we ran into**

**Problems We Faced**

>One major challenge was detecting doom scrolling reliably, since apps like Instagram and YouTube don’t provide direct APIs for tracking Reels or Shorts. I had to use Android Accessibility Services and carefully filter events to avoid false triggers.

>Another hurdle was showing a pop-up over other apps. Android’s overlay permissions are strict, and getting the intervention to appear smoothly without crashes required multiple tests and permission-handling adjustments.

>Implementing the temporary app lock was also tricky, as it needed to block scrolling for a fixed time without permanently restricting access or affecting other apps.

**How We Solved Them**

We tackled these challenges through incremental testing and iteration, breaking features into smaller parts and testing them individually. We relied on Android documentation, simplified my approach when needed, and kept the user experience and mental well-being as the top priority.

Team **seashell** -- SriVyshnavi Mandadapu, Afifa Ameer

🔍 The Problem It Solves

Many people have valuable skills to share, but there is no simple, local, and trusted platform to connect with others nearby for learning, collaboration, or project work. Existing solutions are often global, impersonal, paid-only, or limited to courses, making real community interaction difficult.

This results in:

Underutilized skills

Limited peer-to-peer learning

Difficulty finding collaborators locally

Lack of trust and recognition in skill sharing

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges I Ran Into
🔹 Designing a Fair Skill Exchange System

One major challenge was creating a credit-based skill exchange model that felt fair and motivating. We wanted users to be rewarded for teaching, without making the system complex.
Solution: We simplified the credit logic by rewarding users per completed session and clearly displaying credit usage and balance.

🔹 Managing Local Discovery & User Matching

Connecting users based on locality while keeping the platform simple was challenging. Filtering and displaying nearby users without slowing down performance required careful handling.
Solution: We optimized queries and used lightweight location filters instead of heavy geospatial computations.

🔹 Handling Bookings & Conflicts

Managing session bookings and avoiding overlapping or conflicting schedules was tricky, especially within limited hackathon time.
Solution: We implemented basic validation checks and restricted overlapping bookings to ensure smooth scheduling.

🔹 Time Constraints During Hackathon

Building multiple features—profiles, credits, bookings, and collaboration—within a short time frame was demanding.
Solution: We prioritized core functionality, followed a modular approach, and focused on delivering a working, deployed product rather than incomplete extras.

**Open Track**

SkillLink fits into the Open Track as it addresses a real-world community problem without being limited to a specific domain.
The project focuses on enabling local skill exchange, collaboration, and continuous learning through a practical, scalable web platform.

It brings together multiple functionalities—skill discovery, bookings, reputation building, and project collaboration—into a single solution that can be applied across education, freelancing, and community development.
Built and deployed during the hackathon, SkillLink demonstrates end-to-end problem solving, usability, and real-world impact, which aligns well with the goals of the Open Track.

### Academic Twin
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/academic-twin-db08) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ayushaary/academic-agent-NEW.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://academic-agent-new-6rrwyyehermyi3g4enytjk.streamlit.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ydfqahfW87Y) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> FutureYou AI

![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Seaborn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Seaborn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit.io-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students often struggle to understand why their academic performance looks the way it does — and more importantly, what specific changes would actually improve it. Most tools only show grades or generic tips, but they don’t connect daily habits (study time, health, absences, lifestyle) with real outcomes.

**Academic Twin - FutureYou AI solves this by combining:**
 - Machine learning SGPA prediction.
 - Agent-based simulations for “what-if” scenarios.
 - A built-in AI chatbot for academic guidance.
 - Instead of just showing numbers, the app:
         - Predicts your next semester SGPA.
         - Simulates multiple future scenarios (study more, reduce absences, improve health, etc).
         - Recommends the single best action that gives maximum improvement.
         - Lets you chat with an AI assistant for personalized study advice

This makes academic planning data-driven, interactive, and practical, helping students turn habits into measurable results.

**Challenges we ran into**

This project came with a lot of real-world engineering challenges:
 - Integrating ML + Agent logic + Chatbot into one Streamlit app was tricky, especially managing data flow between prediction, optimization, and UI.
 - I faced multiple API issues while experimenting with Gemini, OpenAI, HuggingFace, and finally OpenRouter — including model availability errors, quota limits, authentication failures, and token restrictions.
 - Setting up environment variables securely (instead of hardcoding API keys) took time to understand properly for deployment.
 - Managing different Python versions, missing packages (xgboost, streamlit, etc.), and runtime errors required repeated debugging.
 - Making the chatbot behave like a real assistant (not dumping raw reasoning) involved prompt tuning and output cleanup.
 - Deployment across devices was challenging at first because local tunnels (ngrok) don’t scale — I had to shift toward proper Streamlit Cloud deployment with GitHub secrets.

**I solved these by:**
 - Switching to OpenRouter’s free DeepSeek model for chatbot stability.
 - Moving all API keys to environment variables.
 - Cleaning agent outputs to avoid type errors.
 - Structuring the project for Streamlit Cloud deployment.
 - Iteratively debugging based on real runtime errors instead of assumptions.

**Open Track**

FutureYou AI – Academic Twin also fits the Open Track as it explores an innovative application of AI in education without being limited to a single predefined problem domain. The project brings together machine learning, agentic simulation, and conversational AI to create a personalized academic assistant that helps students understand their future performance and take actionable steps to improve it.

The platform allows users to experiment with different lifestyle and academic choices, instantly visualizing how these changes impact predicted SGPA, while also receiving AI-powered guidance through an integrated chatbot. This open-ended approach makes the project flexible, creative, and broadly applicable to student well-being and learning optimization.

**Agentic AI / ML**

⁠FutureYou AI – Academic Twin, fits strongly into the Agentic AI / ML track as it combines machine learning prediction with autonomous decision-making to guide students toward better academic outcomes.

The system first uses an XGBoost-based ML model to predict a student’s next semester SGPA based on academic, behavioral, and lifestyle inputs. On top of this prediction layer, an agentic optimization module simulates multiple future scenarios by modifying controllable factors such as study time, health, and absences. The agent evaluates these actions and automatically selects the one that maximizes SGPA improvement, effectively acting as an intelligent academic decision-maker.

In addition, the project integrates an AI chatbot powered by a large language model to provide personalized academic guidance, study tips, and habit recommendations in real time. This creates a closed-loop system where prediction, optimization, and conversational intelligence work together to support students.

By combining ML forecasting, agent-based planning, and generative AI interaction, FutureYou AI demonstrates a practical application of Agentic AI to real-world student success and personalized education.

### ChronoPass Vault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/chronopass-vault-995b) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://chrono-pass-vault.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/0oC_nTD-quQ?si=_fRLpKaSsiqAIKQp) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> This is your own password manager

![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/PHP-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![phpMyAdmin](https://img.shields.io/badge/phpMyAdmin-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL%20Server-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

As digital accounts proliferate, users struggle to manage credentials securely. Common solutions like reusing passwords compromise security, while commercial cloud-based managers introduce third-party dependency and data breach risks. Users lack a streamlined, offline-capable tool that offers the convenience of a web interface without surrendering data sovereignty to external cloud providers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One specific hurdle I encountered was handling special characters within the credential storage system.

Since ChronoPass is designed to store complex passwords, I tested it with inputs containing symbols like single quotes ('), double quotes ("), and backslashes. Initially, these characters broke my SQL queries because I was using direct string concatenation to build the commands. This not only caused the application to crash but I realized it exposed the database to SQL Injection attacks—a critical flaw for a secure vault.

How I got over it: I refactored the backend logic to replace standard queries with Prepared Statements in PHP ($stmt->bind_param). This ensured that the database treated user input purely as data rather than executable code. This switch solved the syntax errors for complex passwords and simultaneously secured the application against SQL injection, significantly improving the vault's integrity.

Team **Syntax_Assassins** -- [Naman Awana](https://github.com/namanawana), Bhavya Mudgal, Daksh Garg, Mayank Pandey

### React Todo-App
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/react-todoapp-e3d1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Mehak9-12/Todolist-React) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://mehak9-12.github.io/Todolist-React/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Advanced Todo-App

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Managing daily tasks can become overwhelming when priorities, deadlines, and different types of work are mixed together. Many people rely on basic notes or simple to-do apps that lack structure, flexibility, and persistence, which often leads to forgotten deadlines, poor prioritization, and reduced productivity.

Another common issue is data loss — tasks disappear after a page refresh or browser restart, making task tracking unreliable.

This Advanced React To-Do Application helps users organize, track, and manage tasks efficiently in one place.

Users can:

Create tasks with priority levels (Low, Medium, High)

Assign categories such as Work, Personal, or Study

Set due dates to keep track of deadlines

Automatically highlight overdue tasks for better visibility

Edit tasks including text, priority, category, and due date

Toggle task completion to track progress

Delete individual tasks or clear all tasks at once

Store tasks using local storage, ensuring data persists across sessions

**Challenges we ran into**

🔹 Managing Editable State for Tasks

One of the main challenges was implementing the edit functionality while keeping the task data consistent. Each task included multiple fields such as text, priority, category, and due date. Handling temporary edit states without immediately mutating the main task list required careful state management.

How I solved it:
I introduced local state inside the task component to manage editable fields and only updated the main task list when the user clicked Save. This helped prevent accidental data loss and kept the UI predictable.

🔹 Local Storage Synchronization Issues

While adding local storage, I initially faced an issue where updating state inside a useEffect caused repeated renders and warnings about cascading updates.

How I solved it:
I separated the logic into two effects — one to load data once on initial render, and another to save tasks whenever the task list changes. This prevented infinite loops and ensured data persistence worked smoothly.

🔹 Highlighting Overdue Tasks Correctly

Comparing due dates and correctly identifying overdue tasks was tricky, especially when dealing with different date formats and ensuring completed tasks were not highlighted.

How I solved it:
I normalized dates using JavaScript Date objects and added conditions to check both the due date and completion status. This ensured only active overdue tasks were visually highlighted.

🔹 Responsive Layout and UI Consistency

Making the UI responsive while keeping it clean and readable across different screen sizes required multiple layout adjustments.

How I solved it:
I used flexbox layouts and media queries to adapt the design for smaller screens and tested the app across different viewport sizes to ensure a consistent user experience.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/airscore-6769) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lavanyanigam/AirScore) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/djR7iC-uYR8) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/djR7iC-uYR8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Save Your Breath, Score Your Workout

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People decide whether to work out based on motivation or schedule, not environmental safety.
Air quality (AQI) directly affects breathing, cardiovascular strain, and overall health during exercise, but most people:

- Don’t check AQI before working out
- Don’t know how bad AQI actually changes exercise risk
- Don’t know what to do instead when outdoor air is unhealthy

What my app does:
It combines two separate factors people usually consider independently:

1. Exercise benefit (type, intensity)
2. Air quality risk (real-time AQI)

AirScore

- Scores the workout, instead of just showing raw AQI numbers
- Provides alternatives, not just warnings:
   - Indoor workout recommendations

### Text to image generation using LORA weights
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/text-to-image-generation-using-lora-weights-65c8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/bbrokesoul/Text-to-Image-generator/tree/main#) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SHI1AFx1_wo?feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co)

> Custom image generation made simple with LoRA

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

General AI image generators struggle to create specific people, objects, or styles accurately.
They don’t understand your subject unless it already exists widely in their training data.

Training a full AI model to learn a new concept is:

Too slow

Too expensive

Requires huge datasets and powerful hardware

This project solves that by allowing users to teach an AI model a new concept using a small image dataset (50–70 images) and generate realistic, customized images using simple text prompts — all within a few minutes and on basic GPU hardware.

It makes personalized image generation practical, fast, and accessible.

**Challenges we ran into**

GPU memory limitations
Training diffusion models is heavy. Managing memory usage while keeping training stable on a basic GPU required careful choices like small batch sizes and LoRA fine-tuning.

Keeping training fast but effective
The challenge was to get good image quality using only 50–70 images and a few minutes of training, without overfitting or undertraining the model.

Handling long-running training in a web app
Training takes time, so it had to run in the background without blocking the server. Managing threads and keeping the UI responsive was tricky.

Model loading time during inference
Loading Stable Diffusion is slow. Caching the pipeline and LoRA weights was necessary to avoid long delays when generating images repeatedly.

Dataset consistency
Image quality and variation in the dataset heavily affect results. Ensuring the dataset was clean and consistent was more important than expected.

Debugging silent failures
When something breaks in training, errors are not always clear. Logging meaningful progress and errors took extra effort.

**Open Track**

This project fits the Open Track because it offers a flexible and open-ended AI solution rather than a single fixed application. It allows users to train custom image models using small datasets and generate personalized results through a simple interface. The approach is innovative, practical, and adaptable across creative, educational, and real-world use cases.

**Agentic AI / ML**

This project fits the Agentic AI/ML track because it demonstrates an autonomous learning and adaptation pipeline. Once the user provides a dataset and trigger word, the system independently prepares data, fine-tunes a diffusion model using LoRA, monitors training through logs, and reuses learned weights during inference. The model adapts its behavior based on new inputs and generates context-aware outputs without manual retraining steps, showcasing practical agent-like behavior in modern machine learning systems.

### MintLp
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mintlp-e840) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://mint-lp.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Svle7v8cjy0?si=7qAF5nRG4N4_2Qfk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Indonesia%20Hackathon%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-indonesia-hackathon-2025.devfolio.co)

> A decentralised AMM

![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional AMMs treat liquidity providers (LPs) like anonymous numbers by giving them fungible LP tokens.

This causes multiple issues:
LP positions are not unique, even though every LP has different deposit time, risk, range and fees.
No clear visibility of fees earned, PnL, impermanent loss, maturity, etc.
Transfers are confusing (LP shares don’t describe what you're actually holding).
New users find liquidity providing hard to understand and risky.

What MintLP solves
MintLP converts every liquidity position into a Data-Rich NFT.
So instead of receiving a basic LP token, users mint an NFT that represents their exact LP position.

How people can use it
MintLP makes liquidity providing more transparent, safer, and user-friendly:
Provide liquidity easily using a simple UI
Mint an LP Position NFT that contains:
Principal value
Accumulated fees
Impermanent loss stats
Age & maturity of position
Range/concentrated liquidity info
View LP holdings in a portfolio gallery
Trade/transfer LP positions as NFTs (future scope)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge 1: Wallet dependency / Demo usability
A major hurdle was that many judges/users don’t have an Aptos wallet installed (like Petra).
That would cause a poor first impression: project doesn’t run = rejected fast.

 How I solved it I implemented a Hybrid Architecture:
Smart Contract Mode (real wallet + onchain)
Mock Mode / Demo Wallet (no wallet needed)
So if wallet isn’t available, the app automatically switches to simulation and still demonstrates:
swap logic
liquidity minting
NFT metadata generation
This made the project judge-friendly and fully demoable.

Challenge 2: AMM math + stable/volatile behavior
Implementing two AMM engines created complexity:
Constant product: x*y=k (volatile pairs)
Stable swap: simplified stable behavior for stable pairs
Issue faced:
incorrect pool outputs due to wrong reserves update order
precision issues in simulation mode

How I solved it
standardized reserve update logic
added guard checks for invalid swap amounts
ensured consistent rounding/precision rules inside the simulation engine

Challenge 3: NFT metadata design
Creating metadata that is:
meaningful to user
clean UI friendly
still “data-rich”

 Solution I designed structured metadata fields and displayed them visually in a Portfolio NFT Gallery, instead of dumping text.

**Base Track**

MintLP is designed specifically to improve the onchain user experience for:
Complex DeFi processes (liquidity providing)
Poor onboarding
Accessibility for retail users
It also fits strongly as a Mini-App, because it’s UI-first and UX-focused.
If required: “MintLP can be deployed on Base as an EVM-based version in future; current MVP demonstrates the complete UX & mechanism using Aptos Move.”

### Nesto
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nesto-d7b7) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tanigusain2006-cloud.github.io/NESTO/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackJNU4.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackjnu4.devfolio.co)

> A calm space for curious minds

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![CanvasJS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CanvasJS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem NESTO Solves
Many existing digital learning platforms are not designed for the needs of young neurodivergent children, especially those aged 5–8, including children on the Autism Spectrum. These platforms are often visually overwhelming, text-heavy, competitive, or built around scores, timers, and performance tracking, which can create stress, confusion, or disengagement instead of supporting calm focus. They frequently rely on rewards, fast pacing, and constant feedback, while also collecting unnecessary data, making them unsuitable for children who need predictable, sensory-safe, and pressure-free environments. Parents, schools, and NGOs also lack simple, privacy-first digital tools that support everyday cognitive engagement without diagnosing, labeling, or turning learning into therapy. As a result, many children are left with either overstimulating “edutainment” apps or clinical tools that feel intimidating and inaccessible.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing a digital platform that genuinely supports neurodivergent children without becoming either overstimulating like many mainstream learning apps or overly clinical like therapeutic tools. Striking the right balance between being engaging yet calm required careful decisions around color usage, animations, layout density, and interaction speed. Another challenge was avoiding common gamification patterns such as scores, rewards, and timers, while still ensuring that the activities felt motivating and intuitive for young children. From a design and technical perspective, creating predictable, repeatable interactions that work offline and remain privacy-first—without collecting personal data or relying on backend services—also required simplifying features and prioritizing clarity over complexity. Finally, translating therapist-informed, sensory-friendly principles into a buildable, frontend-only working prototype was challenging, as it demanded constant validation that every interaction supported comfort, accessibility, and independence rather than performance or evaluation.

**The problem it solves**

Modern software developers face challenges in understanding large and complex code. This issue usually affects company teams and solo developers, and has increased with the rise of vibe coding. In companies, new developers struggle to understand massive code repo with outdated documentation. They need constant help from senior developers to understand system logic, code and design. Similarly, students and open-source contributors often generate large code files
 themselves using AI tools. While it allows rapid code generation, it also leads to long files with minimal logical explanations and code that works but they don’t know why or how it works.

Our solution is CodeFM. It is an AI/ML driven web based platform that helps developers understand large, unfamiliar and AI generated code by converting them into audio and story-like explanations. CodeFM turns code into a podcast experience, where developers can listen to explanations and the relevant lines of code are highlighted in real time. This makes understanding the code easier and faster.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/auditflow-2412) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/samidha-13/AuditFlow-Team-CODEBASE.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/CceW0afklY8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-KnowCode%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://knowcode-3.devfolio.co)

> Monitor Revenue, Not Just Servers

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Traditional *monitoring tools*** like Datadog, New Relic, and CloudWatch focus on infrastructure health—CPU usage, RAM, uptime, API latency, and error logs. They tell you if your servers are running, but they don't tell you if your business is actually making money.

**The Silent Failure Problem**:
Companies lose thousands of dollars daily to "silent failures"—critical user flows that break without triggering infrastructure alerts. Your servers show 100% uptime, databases respond normally, and CPU is healthy, but:
- Users can't login because the OTP provider timed out
- Checkout pages hang because the payment gateway is down
- Orders don't confirm because a webhook failed
- Customers abandon carts and you only discover it hours later when revenue drops

**The Gap AuditFlow Fills:**
AuditFlow monitors business outcomes, not just infrastructure. Instead of asking "Is the backend alive?", we answer "Can users actually complete their journey and generate revenue right now?"

**What We Track:**
The complete user journey that drives revenue:
- User visits → Login → Add to cart → Checkout → Payment → Order confirmation → Refunds
For each step, we capture: success/failure status, timestamps, error codes, device/browser info, and integration health (payment gateways, auth providers)—all without storing personal data.

**How It Helps:**
- Catch issues in minutes, not hours: Real-time alerts when user flows break
- See impact in dollars: Estimated revenue loss based on affected users and average order value
- Get exact root causes: *"Payment gateway timeout at checkout step 3" not just "Error 500"*
- Fix faster: Technical teams know exactly where to look, founders understand business impact immediately
- Reduce support load: Resolve issues before customers flood your support channels

**Example Alert:**
*"🔴 Payment Gateway Failure - 25 users affected in last 10 minutes, estimated loss $1,250/hour, root cause: Stripe API timeout at checkout step 3"*
AuditFlow makes existing infrastructure monitoring tools more effective by covering the business layer they miss—turning system health into revenue health.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced *several backend challenges* while connecting the API with MongoDB, especially around handling high event volume and keeping responses fast. 
Initially, we opened a new database connection on every request, which caused performance issues and random timeouts. We fixed this by using a single shared connection with pooling and by batching writes instead of inserting every event synchronously.
we also had to redesign our schemas and add proper indexes so that alert and analytics queries ran quickly enough for a real-time dashboard. 
Finally, we learned to simplify the architecture, add basic rate limiting, and use clear error logging so debugging became much easier.

**The problem it solves**

# CivicFlow

An AI-powered civic engagement platform designed to simplify issue reporting, improve governance efficiency, and create safer, smarter cities.

---

## 📌 The Problem It Solves

Traditional civic issue management systems are often **slow, fragmented, and inaccessible**. Citizens face difficulties reporting problems, tracking progress, or even knowing if their concerns are acknowledged. On the other hand, authorities struggle with **manual workflows, poor prioritization, duplicate complaints, and lack of actionable insights**.

### Key Challenges:
- Complicated and time-consuming reporting processes  
- Lack of transparency and real-time updates  
- Language and accessibility barriers  
- Manual verification and prioritization of issues  
- Delayed responses to critical civic problems  

These challenges result in **inefficient governance**, **citizen dissatisfaction**, and **unsafe urban environments**.

---

## 💡 What CivicFlow Can Be Used For

CivicFlow acts as a **single, intelligent bridge** between citizens and civic authorities.

### 👥 For Citizens
- Report civic issues via **voice, text, or images/videos**
- Use the platform in **multiple local languages**
- Automatic **geo-tagging** for precise location reporting
- Track complaint status in real time
- Receive transparent updates and notifications

### 🏛️ For Authorities
- AI-powered **issue classification and severity analysis**
- Smart prioritization based on urgency and impact
- Reduced duplicate or false complaints
- Faster resolution with automated workflows
- Data-driven planning using analytics and insights

---

## ⚙️ How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer

- **Frictionless Reporting:** Submit issues in seconds, no paperwork required  
- **Improved Accuracy:** AI-based damage analysis and location tagging  
- **Inclusive Access:** Voice and multilingual support for all users  
- **Transparency:** Citizens can track progress instead of waiting blindly  
- **Operational Efficiency:** Automation reduces manual effort  
- **Safer Cities:** Faster response to hazards and infrastructure failures  

---

## 🌍 Impact

CivicFlow empowers citizens while enabling authorities to act faster and smarter. By combining **AI, automation, and real-time communication**, it transforms civic engagement into a transparent, efficient, and collaborative process—building **safer and more responsive cities**.

---

## 🧠 Tech Highlights (Optional)
- AI-powered analysis & prioritization  
- Multi-modal input (Voice, Text, Image, Video)  
- Real-time tracking and notifications  
- Secure and scalable architecture

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 🔧 Handling Unstructured Citizen Reports
One major challenge was dealing with **unstructured inputs** like voice notes, images, and free-text complaints. Each report came in different formats and quality levels, making it difficult to categorize and prioritize issues accurately.

**How I solved it:**  
I used **AI-based preprocessing** to clean and normalize inputs, applied **NLP for intent detection**, and added **basic validation layers** to reduce noise before routing the issue.

---

### 🌍 Accurate Location Mapping
Users often didn’t specify locations clearly, or permissions failed, leading to incomplete reports.

**How I solved it:**  
I implemented **automatic geo-tagging with fallbacks**, allowing users to manually confirm or adjust locations when needed.

---

### 📊 Prioritization & Scalability
Not all issues are equally urgent, but treating them the same caused delays in critical cases.

**How I solved it:**  
I introduced **rule-based + AI-driven prioritization**, ensuring safety-critical issues are surfaced and handled first.

---

### 🔐 Privacy & Trust
Building a system that encourages reporting required strong **privacy guarantees**.

**How I solved it:**  
I added **optional anonymity**, minimized stored personal data, and followed a **privacy-first data flow**.

---

These challenges helped shape CivicFlow into a **more reliable, citizen-friendly, and scalable platform**.

> Cloud Security Intelligence

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Boto3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Boto3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem It Solves!

- Cloud adoption is growing rapidly, but **cloud security misconfigurations remain a major cause of breaches**.
- Services like **compute, storage, and identity access** are often misconfigured due to fast deployments.
- Common risks include:
  - Publicly accessible storage
  - Over-permissive IAM roles
  - Open ports and weak network rules
  - Missing encryption and security logs
- Security checks are often **manual, fragmented, and reactive**.
- Startups and growing teams usually **lack dedicated security expertise**.
- Issues are frequently discovered **after incidents occur**, increasing security and compliance risks.

---

## Solution!

- SentinelOps provides a **centralized cloud security monitoring platform**.
- It continuously scans cloud infrastructure across:
  - Compute resources
  - Storage services
  - Identity and access management
- Scan results are processed using **intelligent analysis** to:
  - Clearly explain the security issue
  - Provide **step-by-step remediation guidance**
- Users receive **actionable insights**, not raw technical data.
- **Real-time alerts** are sent via:
  - Slack
  - Email
- Notifications integrate directly into existing team workflows.
- The platform is designed to:
  - Support **multiple cloud providers** in the future
  - Include a **community section** for discussion and shared learning

---

## Impact It Makes!

- Helps teams move from **reactive security to proactive risk prevention**.
- Reduces reliance on specialized security engineers.
- Improves visibility into overall cloud security posture.
- Enables faster detection and response to vulnerabilities.
- Supports better compliance readiness.
- Makes cloud security **simpler, safer, and more accessible** for teams of all sizes.

---

## Why SentinelOps Differs?

- Focuses on **clarity and usability**, not complex enterprise tooling.
- Converts technical scan data into **human-readable explanations**.
- Provides **guided remediation**, not just problem detection.
- Integrates security alerts into **tools teams already use**.
- Designed to grow from a hackathon MVP into a **scalable SaaS platform**.
- Combines **automation, intelligence, and collaboration** in one place.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

## Key Challenges We Faced and How We Solved Them

### 1. Turning the Idea into a Real Product
- **Challenge:**  
  SentinelOps started as a concept. Bringing together **AWS security scanning, intelligent analysis, backend services, frontend dashboards, and alerting** into one working system was initially overwhelming.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We broke the project into **small, manageable components** such as scanning, backend processing, UI, and notifications, and built each part step by step.
- **Result:**  
  The idea gradually evolved into a **functional end-to-end platform**.

---

### 2. AI Data Not Saving in MongoDB
- **Challenge:**  
  Although the scanner was generating **AI-based remediation data**, only basic findings were being stored in the database.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We identified that **Mongoose was dropping fields not defined in the schema**, so we expanded the schema to include all required AI-generated fields.
- **Result:**  
  **All enriched scan data is now stored correctly**, enabling complete insights across the platform.

---

### 3. Unstructured PDF Reports
- **Challenge:**  
  The initial PDF reports appeared **unstructured and unprofessional**, with spacing issues and broken text.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We rebuilt the reports using **proper ReportLab styling**, ensuring each issue was clearly formatted and placed on a single page.
- **Result:**  
  The reports are now **clean, readable, and professional**, suitable for sharing and documentation.

---

### 4. Static Dashboard Data
- **Challenge:**  
  Dashboard graphs were using **hardcoded values**, so they did not reflect actual scan activity.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We connected the dashboard to **real scan history data**, allowing metrics to update dynamically.
- **Result:**  
  The dashboard now displays **real-time trends and meaningful insights** over time.

---

### 5. Non-Functional UI Buttons
- **Challenge:**  
  Some UI buttons appeared clickable but had **no functionality**, creating confusion.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We removed or properly hid non-functional elements and ensured only working actions were visible.
- **Result:**  
  The UI feels **cleaner, more reliable, and more user-friendly**.

---

### 6. Email and Slack Alert Issues
- **Challenge:**  
  Email alerts contained **undefined values**, and Slack messages were **plain and unclear**.
- **How We Solved It:**  
  We fixed **field name mismatches**, added fallback values, and enhanced Slack notifications using **rich message formatting**.
- **Result:**  
  Alerts are now **clear, informative, and delivered in real time** across communication channels.

---

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FunnelDenk is a lightweight web analytics platform that helps small website owners understand user behavior without using invasive tracking methods. Traditional analytics platforms often overwhelm non-technical users with complex dashboards and jargon. They also raise privacy concerns because they rely on cookies, user identifiers, and behavioral tracking.

FunnelDenk closes this gap by focusing on clarity and actionable insights instead of complexity and raw data. Rather than showing charts and numbers, the system provides simple explanations and practical recommendations based on overall website activity. The platform is built with privacy in mind. It collects no personally identifiable information, does not store cookies, and avoids all forms of cross-site or user-level tracking.
FunnelDenk mainly addresses the need for accessible and privacy-friendly analytics tools for small websites, early-stage startups, personal portfolios, and non-technical founders who need guidance rather than detailed metrics.

**Implementation Plan**
FunnelDenk uses a modular, event-driven structure that focuses on simplicity and scalability.
System Flow
1.	A lightweight JavaScript snippet is added to the target website.
2.	Every time a page loads, the script sends a single anonymous event to the backend.
3.	The backend checks and stores events without keeping IP addresses or user identifiers.
4.	Events are combined into summary metrics regularly.
5.	The combined data is sent to an AI-based insight engine.
6.	The AI creates easy-to-understand explanations and improvement suggestions.
7.	Insights appear on a simple dashboard and can be compiled into weekly reports if desired.

**Key Features**
1.	One-line script installation  
2.	Anonymous event collection (page, device, referrer, country, time)  
3.	Server-side gathering of metrics  
4.	AI-driven pattern interpretation  
5.	Text-based insights and recommendations  
6.	Weekly performance summaries  
7.	Simple, non-technical dashboard interface  
Flowcharts can be included to show the data pipeline from event collection to insight generation.

**Dataset / Technologies**

FunnelDenk works without relying on third-party user datasets. It creates all data organically through anonymous website events. 
Technologies Used
1.	Frontend: Next.js with Tailwind CSS for a lightweight and responsive dashboard
2.	Backend: FastAPI for handling asynchronous event ingestion and API services
3.	Database: PostgreSQL (via Supabase) for storing and aggregating structured events
4.	Analytics Logic: Custom aggregation queries for basic behavioral metrics
5.	AI Layer: Large Language Models (LLMs) for turning aggregated data into natural-language insights
6.	Hosting: Vercel (frontend) and a cloud-based backend deployment
The system is built to be cloud-native, scalable, and easy to extend.  
4. Business Model and Unique Selling Proposition (USP)

**Business Model**

FunnelDenk uses a subscription-based SaaS pricing model:
1.	Free Tier: Limited monthly page views for small or personal websites.
2.	Pro Tier: Affordable monthly subscription for growing sites.
3.	Business Tier: Multi-site analytics and detailed reporting.
4.	This model aims to ensure accessibility while supporting long-term sustainability.

**Unique Selling Proposition**

FunnelDenk stands out with these features:
1.	Privacy-first architecture: No cookies, no IP storage, no fingerprinting.
2.	Insight-focused analytics: Explanations and actions instead of charts.
3.	Low learning curve: Designed for non-technical users.
4.	Regulatory friendliness: Reduced compliance burden due to minimal data collection.
5.	Lightweight integration: Minimal impact on website performance.
By focusing on ethical analytics and user-friendliness, FunnelDenk offers a practical alternative to traditional analytics platforms for small-scale web applications.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The “Fail-Safe” Timeout Challenge**

Our biggest challenge was designing a zero-crash architecture that remained responsive even when external services (Postgres, Redis) were unavailable.

The problem

Initially, our API routes had hard dependencies on the database:

db: Session = Depends(get_db)


When running the app in Demo Mode without a local database, FastAPI would block for ~30 seconds waiting for a connection timeout before falling back to mock data. This made the dashboard effectively unusable.

**The solution**

We refactored the entire dependency injection layer to use lazy loading instead of enforcing DB connectivity at the route level.

Database checks were moved inside the business logic

A Fail-Safe Wrapper attempts a DB connection only when needed

If the connection fails—or DB_ENABLED=false—the system immediately switches to a Mock/Stub Provider (<50 ms response)

**The result**

We shipped a hybrid backend that:

Runs instantly in Demo Mode (mocked services)

Seamlessly upgrades to Production Mode (real services)

Requires zero code changes—only environment variables

Static Generation vs. Runtime APIs (Vercel)

We also encountered a subtle but critical issue during deployment.

**The problem**

Our Next.js frontend used relative API paths:

fetch('/api/v1/...')


This worked in the browser, but during Vercel’s Static Site Generation (SSG) phase, Node.js executed these fetches server-side. Since there’s no implicit “current domain” in that context, the build failed with:

TypeError: Failed to parse URL

The solution

We built a context-aware API client that adapts to its execution environment.

Introduced NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL

Explicitly defined the backend host at build time

Ensured SSG could hydrate the dashboard without crashing the build pipeline

**The result**

The frontend now works consistently across:

Client-side rendering

Server-side rendering

Static generation on Vercel

No broken builds, no runtime surprises.

**The problem it solves**

❓ The Problem It Solves

Organizations store critical knowledge across documents, wikis, chats, and internal systems. Finding accurate answers is slow, risky, and often unreliable. Traditional AI tools make this worse by generating responses without citations, ignoring access controls, and offering no auditability — making them unsafe for enterprise use.

Teams struggle with:

Searching through scattered documentation

Trusting AI-generated answers without verification

Preventing data leaks across teams or tenants

Meeting compliance, audit, and security requirements

Reusing past answers or understanding how decisions were made

✅ How LUMIXAI Solves It

LUMIXAI provides secure, verified, and auditable AI-powered answers from authorized knowledge only.

People use it to:

Ask natural language questions and get citation-backed answers

Access only the documents they are permitted to see

Verify responses using confidence scores and source references

Track every query with request IDs and processing traces

Review past queries and reuse validated answers

Interact with AI directly inside tools like Slack

Monitor system usage, refusals, and performance through admin dashboards

🔐 Why It’s Safer and Better

Security-first: Blocks prompt injection and unauthorized access

Transparent: Every answer is traceable to its sources

Auditable: Full request logs for compliance and review

Enterprise-ready: Multi-tenant, role-based access control

Efficient: Reduces time spent searching documentation

LUMIXAI turns organizational knowledge into a trusted, searchable, and compliant intelligence layer — without sacrificing security or control.

**Challenges we ran into**

We ran into issues like inefficeint embeddings, pinecone storage of data, formatting metadata, implementing Langgraph flow.
1. Preventing Unsafe or Unauthorized AI Responses

One of the biggest challenges was ensuring the AI never answered questions using unauthorized or cross-tenant data. Early versions could respond even when context quality was poor or permissions were unclear.

How I solved it:
I introduced a strict validation pipeline before response generation, including permission checks, context quality scoring, and security pattern detection (like prompt injection). If any step fails, the system blocks the request and returns a clear, user-friendly refusal instead of a risky answer.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Cloud%20Platform%20(GCP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

KLAIM is a privacy-first identity verification infrastructure that lets applications, organizations, and AI agents verify specific user claims without requiring access to the user's underlying identity documents.

Today, verification often means collecting and storing sensitive documents even when an application only needs a small fact — for example, whether someone is over 18 or whether a licence is valid. KLAIM changes this into a claim-based verification flow:

A verifier requests only the claims it needs.
The user reviews and gives consent through the KLAIM PWA.
KLAIM orchestrates credential access, payment, proof generation, and verification.
Zero-knowledge proofs allow claims to be verified without exposing the underlying personal data.
Verifiers receive the minimum information required instead of raw identity documents.
x402 enables pay-per-verification payments, with settlement on Algorand.
MCP exposes the same verification infrastructure to AI agents.
Idina, our Google ADK-based orchestration service, coordinates the verification workflow while security-critical operations remain handled by deterministic services.

For example, a delivery platform can request:

identity_verified
age_over_18
license_valid

and receive the verification result without needing the user's complete identity document

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was turning an initial prototype into a real, deployable end-to-end system without breaking the existing verification flow.

1. Moving from a prototype to distributed infrastructure

Our initial system was largely locally hosted. We had to separate the system into independently deployable services and move the complete stack to Google Cloud Run.

This required defining clear contracts between the KLAIM API, Idina, ZKP, payment, MCP, and frontend services.

2. Making verification stateful

The original prototype could perform verification, but a real verification workflow needs to track states such as:

Request
→ Consent
→ Payment
→ Verification
→ Proof Generation
→ Verification Result

We introduced an explicit verification lifecycle so that each stage can be tracked and handled safely.

3. Integrating AI without letting AI perform security-critical operations

We wanted Idina to provide intelligent orchestration using Google ADK, but we did not want an LLM to directly decide that a payment was successful or that a cryptographic proof was valid.

We therefore separated the system into three Idina harnesses:

Wallet / Credential Access
Payment Verification
ZKP Generation

The principle is:

AI orchestrates. Deterministic services execute.

4. Integrating multiple protocols

We had to make x402 payments, Algorand settlement, ZKP generation, Midnight infrastructure, MCP, and the core verification lifecycle work together without creating separate flows.

We solved this by keeping each capability behind a clear service boundary and making the KLAIM API the central verification interface.

5. Keeping the privacy model honest

Another challenge was ensuring that the system did not accidentally turn into another document-storage KYC platform.

The final flow focuses on sharing verified claims and proof information, rather than unnecessarily passing the user's underlying identity documents to the verifier.

**Trace Commons AI**

KLAIM provides privacy-preserving identity verification infrastructure where applications and AI agents can verify trusted user claims without receiving the underlying identity documents. It combines reusable credentials, zero-knowledge proofs, user consent, and verifiable verification results into a common verification layer that applications can integrate through APIs and MCP.

> a bridge which connects

![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Most of what follows is not "it didn't compile". It is bugs that looked like
they worked — which, in an app holding a pregnant woman's medical record, is the
dangerous kind.

### 1. The app knew who the worker was in two different places

Registering a mother failed with `42501: new row violates row-level security
policy`. The database was right and the app was wrong: "signed in" was an email
in SharedPreferences, which decided what the screen showed, while authorisation
was the Supabase session, which decided what the server accepted. Nothing
reconciled them, and nothing cleared a session left behind by whoever used the
shared handset last. **The phone could display one ASHA's caseload and write to
the server as somebody else** — and the code swallowed it, because the identity
check ended in `catch (_) { return null; }` and pushed the mother anyway.

Sign-in now drops a session belonging to a different address before asking for a
code, and her name and sub-centre come from her own `staff` row rather than from
seed data — which had been stamping the same invented worker onto every visit
recorded on every handset.

### 2. Making an offline sync safe to retry, in both directions

The field app writes to local SQLite with text ids (`m-1755364…`); Supabase keys
on `uuid`. Every id is mapped through **uuid v5 against a fixed namespace**, so
the same local row resolves to the same uuid on every device and every attempt,
and every write is an **upsert** — a push that succeeded server-side but lost
its reply on a dropping link lands on the same row instead of a duplicate.

Pulling *down* was harder, and we nearly got it wrong three ways. The hash is
one-way, so recognising a woman the handset already holds means hashing every
local id forward and looking the server id up in that map — keyed any other way,
she comes back down under her uuid as a second identical row. The obvious key,
the Thayi card number, was wrong too: a supervisor can edit it in the admin
portal, and the pull would start inserting duplicates a release later. And
"was this row created by the worker or seeded?" had been inferred from the shape
of the id — roughly one server uuid in three hundred would have matched, and
pushed a phone's stale copy straight back over the server's.

We also keep a mock sync service with a **deliberate failure rate**, because the
Sync Status screen exists to answer "what happens when this fails", and that
answer is only honest if failures actually happen.

### 3. A full upsert that quietly took away a mother's verified email

Her verified address is the *only* thing that opens her own record. The push was
a full upsert that re-ran on every retry and sent `email_verified: <local> ??
false` — so a handset whose local row hadn't caught up **wrote `false` over the
server's `true`**. She was then refused at login with "this email is not
registered — ask your ASHA worker", having already done the one thing her ASHA
could do for her, with nothing on either screen explaining it.

Worse, there was a second path: if her record hadn't synced yet, the
registration screen said *"Code confirmed. It will be saved when her record
syncs"* — and then never set the flag, anywhere, ever. She had read the code
back, which is the entire proof, and was locked out permanently by a screen that
had just told her it was fine.

The rule now is that **nothing in the field app has the authority to un-verify an
address**: the flag is sent only when `true`, and `email` only when that phone
actually holds one.

### 4. The QR code was a permanent credential

The card originally rendered her record id plus a token that never changed —
a permanent, un-revocable credential printed on a screen she is asked to hold up
in a queue. Photograph it once and her file is readable for as long as the
record exists.

Rebuilding it as a five-minute HMAC-signed token cost us something real, and we
decided to pay it rather than hide it: the screen used to say "works without
internet", and a server-minted token cannot. We cache and reuse the token until
it genuinely expires, refresh it 45 seconds early so the code on display is
never the one that fails at the counter, and when it can't refresh, the screen
says she needs a moment of signal — instead of showing a code that will be
refused. Keeping a permanent offline fallback was the alternative, and it would
mean the stealable credential still exists.

Then we found the hole underneath it: the mint endpoint took a `mother_id` and
checked the caller was an administrator — so **any admin could manufacture any
woman's consent** and hand it to a partner. There is no `mother_id` parameter
any more. The token is minted for whoever holds the session, and staff and
administrators are refused by name.

### 5. Two RLS policies that disagreed, and the work that vanished in the gap

The doctor's console listed every mother, he assigned a task, and the insert was
refused. The read policy allowed a bare `is_doctor()`; the write path re

**The problem it solves**

In rural Karnataka, a pregnant woman's health record exists in three places at
once, and no two of them can see each other.

- **She** carries a paper **Thayi Card** — the government's mother-and-child
  card. It gets wet, it gets lost, and she cannot read most of what is on it.
- **Her ASHA worker** keeps a register in her bag. What she records at a
  doorstep in a village stays in that bag until she next reaches the health
  centre.
- **Her PHC doctor** has whatever sheet of paper is in front of him at the
  visit, and no way to send anything back.

*Setu* means bridge. Setu is three apps over one database, so that what the ASHA
records at a doorstep with no signal is what the doctor sees at the PHC, and
what the mother reads on her own phone.

### What it changes, for each of the three people

**For the mother — Thayi Setu (ತಾಯಿ ಸೇತು)**
Her record, on her own phone, in Kannada by default, read aloud if she cannot
read it. One idea per screen, 18sp text, 56dp targets, icon *and* text on every
action — built for a woman with limited literacy sharing a low-end Android
handset with her family. She can ask questions in Kannada and get an answer
grounded in clinician-reviewed material rather than a model's own guesses. And
if she types or says a danger sign — bleeding, blurred vision, no fetal movement
— the message is **not sent anywhere**: a full-screen interrupt with call
buttons appears instead. That check is a hard-coded keyword matcher on the
device, not a model call, so it still fires in a village in airplane mode.

**For the ASHA worker — ASHA Setu**
The whole app is local-first: every screen reads and writes to on-device SQLite,
nothing in the UI ever waits on the network, and a background outbox drains when
signal returns. She can register a mother by photographing her paper Thayi Card,
record a visit, and have the **risk engine fire the alert offline** — it is a
pure function over the visit, with thresholds in a tunable JSON file, so a red
rule takes the whole screen before she can move on and raises a referral that
syncs later. She also finally receives work *back* from the doctor.

**For the doctor — Setu Care**
The real caseload of his facility: who is high-risk, what is overdue, every
visit and lab behind each name. He assigns a task by picking the **mother**, and
the ASHA is resolved from her assignment — so work can never be sent to someone
who does not cover her. At the counter he can scan the code on her phone to open
her record without knowing her name, and photograph the prescription she is
handed, because that sheet of paper is what gets lost between the clinic and the
chemist.

### The part we care most about: consent is a physical act

Reading a woman's medical file is a disclosure, and Setu treats it as one.

- The QR she shows carries **no personal data** — no name, no phone number, no
  clinical data.
- It is a **server-signed token valid for five minutes**, minted only for
  whoever holds *her* session. Not her record id. Photograph it over her
  shoulder and it stops working before she has left the building.
- **Nobody can mint it on her behalf** — not her ASHA, not an administrator.
  Her holding her phone out *is* the permission, and that is not something
  anyone can do for her.
- Any other access is an **access request she approves or rejects in her own
  app**, and every single read lands in an access log.

Roles and scope are decided in the database by Row Level Security — `mother`
reads only herself, `asha` reads her sub-centre, `doctor` reads his facility —
not by a flag in any app. Delete the app and the rules still hold.

### And the bits around the edges
- An **admin portal** (React + Vite) for PHCs, staff, ASHA-to-doctor
  assignments, partner access and a full audit trail.
- A **partner API** so a hospital can resolve a mother's summary from the code
  she presents — where every request is backed by the **KMC registration of a
  named, registered doctor**, because a hospital is not a person and cannot be
  struck off.
- Keys that matter (Gemini, ElevenLabs, email, service-role) live in Edge
  Functions and never reach a handset, because anything shipped in an APK can be
  pulled back out of it in a minute.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem 

Students have difficulty finding suitable teammates for hackathons. Current websites depend too much on students declaring their own skills, WhatsApp/Discord groups, and manual searches.

This causes three main problems: skill mismatch, time wastage, and misleading declarations about skills.

What KEVIN Does

KEVIN takes a project-first perspective.

A team uploads their problem statement for the hackathon. KEVIN utilizes AI to determine the necessary skills, analyze the skills of the current team members, identify skill gaps and recommend the students capable of filling these gaps.

Instead of relying on students saying, "I know Machine Learning," KEVIN checks on GitHub evidence like contributions, repositories and coding activities.

KEVIN tackles common challenges such as low contribution forks and cosmetic README commits when making skill recommendations.

KEVIN recommends teammates based on the requirements of the project and actual coding activity on GitHub.

**Challenges we ran into**

KEVIN — Logical Problems with AI
AI Project Analysis — Gemini transforms hackathon concept into needed skills and roles, with fallback AI logic in case of failure.
Skill Normalization — Similar terms such as React.js, ReactJS and React JS are considered the same skill.
Smart Candidate Scoring — Candidates are scored on Skill Match (60%) + GitHub Evidence (25%) + Project Relevance (15%).
GitHub Authenticity Engine — Checks contribution %, uniqueness, code depth, consistency, and project relevance.
Cheating/Loophole Detection — Finds projects with low contribution forks and README-only/ cosmetic commits.
Code Contribution Analysis — Finds out which files and modules were used by the student.
Commit History Analysis — Finds out if a student did suspicious single commit project dump.
Skill Gap Detection — Finds out what skills needed for the project are missing from current team skills set.
Flexible Skill Matching — Supports aliases, partial matching, and different ways to name skills.
Team State Management — Manages team invitation flow with state machine like pending → accepted → removed, and enforces team limitations and rules.
