### Winter of Code 5.0
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/winter-of-code-0f42) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JbT7jQidHhoMtSa_YZrDunUgel3dARmokcOTY6v1gg4/edit?tab=t.0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Making Mixxx playback more realistic, consistent.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![CMake](https://img.shields.io/badge/CMake-333333?style=flat-square) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-333333?style=flat-square) ![Qt](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qt-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Mixxx currently supports realistic turntable spin-up and spin-down only in some controller-specific JavaScript mappings. This means keyboard and GUI users get instant, robotic playback while controller users experience inconsistent behavior depending on their hardware.
This project brings spin simulation into the Mixxx C++ core so it works consistently for everyone.
This makes Mixxx better by:

1.**Giving keyboard and GUI users realistic playback behavior**-  No more instant starts/stops
2. **Smooth, natural transitions** – Gradual acceleration like real turntables
3. **Consistent behavior everywhere** – Same feel across controllers, keyboard, and mouse
4. **Cleaner codebase** – One implementation instead of duplicated controller logic
5. **More professional software** – Competitive with commercial DJ tools like Serato

Bottom line: Every Mixxx user gets the same realistic, professional turntable feel, making the software more accessible and polished.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
**1. Understanding Mixxx Architecture**

The real-time audio engine and ControlObjects required careful study to understand signal flow, prevent threading issues, and manage asynchronous data exchange.

**2. Replicating Turntable Physics**

Linear spin produced unnatural behavior, so I tested exponential and S-curve models iteratively and refined them with mentor feedback to achieve realistic results.

**3. Maintaining Compatibility**

New core features were made compatible with existing controller mappings using opt-in flags and migration paths, ensuring system stability.

**4. Learning C++**

I developed understanding of memory management, smart pointers, and RAII through code analysis, hands-on practice, and mentor guidance.

**5. Debugging Real-Time Audio**

Non-invasive logging, offline testing, and visualizations were used to analyze and validate real-time playback behavior.

**6. Handling Play/Pause State Transitions**

Ensuring smooth spin-up and spin-down behavior during rapid play/pause actions required careful state handling to avoid abrupt audio jumps or timing inconsistencies.

[Kartika Choudhary](https://github.com/KartikaChoudhary)

### Keploy Blog Website
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/keploy-blog-website-ceae) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1y2B89ADxe3qTZRljX9OkDezubm6ihAin/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108201277425752729663&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Making Keploy’s blog faster and accessible

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Markdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/Markdown-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Keploy blog website serves as a key platform for sharing technical knowledge, tutorials, and updates with the developer community. However, as the content grows, issues such as suboptimal performance, limited accessibility, inconsistent SEO practices, and unclear contribution workflows can reduce its effectiveness.

This project addresses these challenges by improving page load performance, ensuring accessibility compliance, implementing SEO best practices, and enhancing documentation for contributors. As a result, developers can consume content more efficiently, discover blogs more easily through search engines, and contribute to the platform with less friction. Overall, the project makes the blog more usable, inclusive, and scalable for long-term community growth.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the initial challenges was understanding the existing project structure and content flow, especially how Markdown-based blogs are rendered through reusable frontend components. Another challenge was identifying performance and accessibility gaps without disrupting the existing layout and functionality.

I addressed these challenges by thoroughly exploring the repository, reviewing existing components, and using tools such as Lighthouse and browser developer tools to identify bottlenecks. Incremental changes, frequent testing, and mentor feedback helped ensure that improvements were implemented without breaking existing features.

**AOPS**

This project fits into the AOPS track as it focuses on improving the performance, accessibility, and maintainability of an existing open-source platform. By optimizing the Keploy blog website, enhancing documentation, and refining developer experience, the project contributes to long-term operational stability and community-driven development.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/winter-of-code-aa1c) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VHb518Aifw3P3z_uhuSWFdkjbGMy-CfB/view?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Making OWASP Nest’s backend more reliable, maintai

![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

“OWASP Nest provides access to information about projects, mentoring, as well as contributions via web APIs. Some of the key backend problems that currently impact it include,” according to Yang Wang.

Some APIs provide outdated information because cache update mechanisms for when the underlying data has changed are inefficient. This results in outdated or inconsistent information being viewed by the mentor and the student, including in the mentorship portal.

Backend models suffer from the same inconsistency in logic while processing data from GitHub. There are several models that support a from_github() function but work in a different manner throughout the codebase.

Moreover, API response against error can neither be documented nor standardized. For instance, the format of the error response also keeps changing depending on the API endpoint being called.

With regard to OWASP Nest, this project intends to enhance its backend by resolving cache invalidation problems and establishing standard logic for backend model ingestion as well as standardizing API responses for errors that might occur.

**Challenges we ran into**

There is also the problem of understanding data flow within the backend with the cache application points, as cache logic is scattered over various modules. The task is complicated when it is required to find the missing cache invalidations.

The other issue that may arise could be inconsistency in the patterns used in the back-end, such as how models handle the from_github() method.

Another challenge of standardizing API errors is that there are many different formats that errors for different endpoints are returned in, and modifications must not affect legacy clients.

I intend to deal with these problems in my project by creating the backend environment locally and focusing on reproducing problems that exist, adding tests and then improving gradually.

### Quizora
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/quizora-94ac) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eHMX1J1GrZlzjfb5qcGL_RDwcJuezEwz/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116282563695377335685&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> “Making assessments fast, fair, and engaging.”

![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional online quizzes and examinations often suffer from low student engagement, lack of real-time feedback, and poor exam integrity. Static question formats and slow interfaces fail to motivate learners, while manual question creation increases the burden on educators. Additionally, many existing platforms lack effective mechanisms to prevent unfair practices such as tab switching, impersonation, or absence during online exams.

Quizora addresses these challenges by offering a fast-paced, gamified quiz experience with real-time interactions. It improves engagement through relay-based timers, leaderboards, and smooth UI transitions. AI-powered question generation reduces manual effort and enables dynamic assessments. To ensure fairness and security, Quizora integrates tab-switch detection and webcam-based live face monitoring to detect suspicious behavior, issuing warnings and automatically submitting exams after repeated violations.

By combining engagement, automation, and exam integrity, Quizora makes online assessments more interactive, efficient, and secure for students, educators, and organizations.

> Proposal Submission

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Figma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Figma-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Proposal 1: WallGodds

WallGodds addresses the challenge of discovering and managing high-quality wallpapers in a way that benefits both end users and creators.

For users, browsing wallpapers across different devices can often feel inconsistent, cluttered, or overwhelming. WallGodds simplifies this process by offering a centralized platform where wallpapers are categorized, visually consistent, and optimized for multiple screen sizes. A refined UI helps users discover relevant content faster while maintaining a visually pleasing experience.

For designers and contributors, many open-source projects lack clear documentation and consistent UI patterns, making contributions difficult. By improving UI consistency and documentation structure, WallGodds lowers the barrier for new contributors, making it easier for designers and developers to understand the project, contribute effectively, and maintain long-term quality.

Proposal 2: Cooketh Flow

Cooketh Flow tackles the problem of organizing complex ideas, workflows, and brainstorming sessions in a way that is both powerful and intuitive.

Visual thinking tools often become difficult to use as features grow, leading to cluttered interfaces and increased cognitive load. Cooketh Flow provides a unified canvas for brainstorming, diagramming, and workflow design, but refining its UI/UX is essential to ensure users can focus on ideas rather than interface complexity.

By introducing a structured design system and clearer interaction patterns, this proposal improves onboarding for first-time users, enhances consistency across features, and enables teams to collaborate more effectively. For developers, a well-defined design system reduces ambiguity and speeds up feature implementation, making future development more efficient and less error-prone.

**Challenges we ran into**

Proposal 1: WallGodds

One of the key challenges during analysis was identifying UI improvements that enhance visual appeal without compromising usability. As WallGodds is a visually driven platform, design changes must balance aesthetics with clear navigation, accessibility, and content focus. During planning, careful attention was given to layout hierarchy and color theme to avoid visual clutter.

Another challenge was evaluating the existing documentation from the perspective of new contributors. Planning documentation improvements required structuring information in a way that remains concise yet informative, ensuring clarity without oversimplification.

Additionally, proposing UI enhancements without direct implementation context required consideration of scalability. To address this, the planned designs align with common React-based layout and component patterns, keeping them practical and developer-friendly.

Proposal 2: Cooketh Flow

A primary challenge during planning was understanding Cooketh Flow’s interface complexity and ensuring that UI/UX improvements simplify workflows rather than add cognitive load. As a visual productivity tool, clarity and consistency were prioritized while identifying areas for refinement.

Another challenge involved planning a design system that supports future growth while aligning with Flutter’s component-based architecture. The proposal therefore emphasizes modular, reusable components instead of rigid layouts.

Finally, planning within an open-source environment required anticipating diverse user and contributor needs. This was addressed by focusing on iterative feedback, clear documentation, and adaptable design decisions.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mimic-6805) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Saikat-Bera04/mimic) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/xD5wGwz724k?si=mCXV4I_gls4C9QjV) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> your personalized ai friend

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embeddings](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embeddings-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square) ![Convex](https://img.shields.io/badge/Convex-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Current AI tools are generic and forgetful

No reliable long-term memory across sessions

AI personas drift or hallucinate personality traits

Learning from chats is uncontrolled and unsafe

No clear ownership over AI identity

No safe way for others to contribute to training

**What This Project Enables**

Explicit, memory-based AI learning

Clear separation between chat and learning

AI avatars defined by a master personality prompt

Gradual, controlled evolution of AI behavior

Trust-based contribution (owner > trainer)

Read-only trainer access without accounts

**What People Can Use It For**

Personal AI avatars that reflect real opinions and values

Long-term memory and knowledge backup

Mentorship and structured learning (MCQs, coaching)

Creator and professional AI personas

Consistent AI behavior across time and sessions

Ethical experimentation with evolving AI systems

**How It Makes Tasks Easier and Safer**

No repeated re-explanation of preferences

Reduced AI hallucinations and drift

Controlled collaboration without security risks

Faster, more relevant AI responses

Lower cost without model retraining

Full user control over what the AI learns

**Impact**

More trustworthy AI systems

Stronger alignment with human identity

Safer AI collaboration models

Scalable approach to personal AI identity

**Challenges we ran into**

***Challenges I Ran Into***

Separating chat from learning
Initially, it was tempting to treat every conversation as learning data. This quickly caused personality drift and noisy context. I solved this by clearly separating short-term conversations from long-term memories and allowing only explicitly saved inputs to become learning data.

Retrieving the right context from growing memory
As the number of memories increased, passing all past data to the AI became inefficient and inaccurate. I addressed this by using embeddings with cosine similarity to retrieve only the most relevant memories per query, combined with trust-based weighting and recency scoring.

Handling trainer contributions without accounts
Trainers needed visibility into the avatars they contributed to, but adding full authentication increased complexity and risk. I solved this by introducing token-scoped, read-only access tied to a single avatar, which allowed secure viewing without user accounts.

Preventing identity drift from conflicting inputs
Conflicting memories from owners and trainers caused inconsistent responses. I introduced memory weights so owner-provided memories always take priority, ensuring the AI stays aligned with the real person.

Balancing technical depth with hackathon constraints
Advanced features like real-time streaming and microservices were unnecessary and risky under time pressure. I chose a monolithic architecture with minimal dependencies, which made the system easier to debug, explain, and demo.

Keeping the system explainable to judges
Complex AI systems can be hard to justify during evaluation. I overcame this by designing clear, layered workflows for memory storage, retrieval, and permission checks, making each decision easy to explain and defend.

### HoliCal+ — Open World Holiday Enhancements
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/holical-open-world-holiday-enhancements-4b85) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xkh0af5gkQYq_1MKdN5Xbo97BETx2c-mMTCzoMoHcps/edit?tab=t.0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Accurate and localized global holiday detection.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Open World Holidays Framework addresses a common but complex problem faced by developers worldwide: accurately identifying public holidays across different countries and regions.

In many applications—such as payroll systems, booking platforms, financial software, attendance tracking, and global scheduling tools—date-based logic is critical. Manually maintaining holiday calendars is error-prone, time-consuming, and difficult to scale, especially when regional rules, movable feasts, and country-specific exceptions are involved.

This project simplifies and secures that process by:

Eliminating manual holiday management
Developers no longer need to hardcode holiday dates or maintain separate datasets for each country or region.

Ensuring correctness and consistency
The framework encodes official holiday rules programmatically, reducing errors caused by outdated calendars or incorrect assumptions.

Supporting regional and subdivision-level holidays
It handles country-level as well as state/province-level holidays, which are often overlooked but essential for real-world use cases.

Improving safety in critical systems
Accurate holiday detection prevents costly mistakes in payroll calculations, banking transactions, deadlines, and compliance-related workflows.

Saving development time and effort
A single, well-tested library replaces repetitive custom implementations across projects.

By enhancing the accuracy, localization, and extensibility of this framework, the project further reduces friction for developers building global applications, making date-based decisions reliable, maintainable, and scalable.

**Challenges we ran into**

While working with the Open World Holidays Framework, several challenges emerged, primarily due to the complexity and global nature of holiday data.

Understanding diverse holiday rules
Holidays are not simple fixed dates; many depend on lunar calendars, religious observances, or region-specific rules that vary even within the same country. Understanding how these rules were encoded in the existing codebase required careful study of multiple modules and real-world references.
Resolution: I reviewed the internal rule structure, cross-checked logic with official government calendars, and traced existing implementations to ensure consistency before making changes.

Handling regional inconsistencies and edge cases
Some holidays differed across subdivisions or had conditional observance rules (e.g., holidays moving to weekdays). These edge cases were not always obvious at first glance.
Resolution: I added focused test cases for edge conditions and validated outputs across multiple years to ensure correctness.

Maintaining backward compatibility
Improving or correcting holiday definitions risked breaking existing behavior relied upon by users.
Resolution: All changes were implemented incrementally with minimal API changes, supported by tests to ensure existing functionality remained unaffected.

Balancing extensibility with simplicity
Introducing improvements while keeping the framework easy to use required careful design decisions.
Resolution: I followed existing design patterns within the project and documented changes clearly to help contributors and users understand new behavior.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aielth-9f8e) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Your thinking copilot

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Edge function](https://img.shields.io/badge/Edge%20function-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern AI chat systems respond well to single prompts but lose context over time.

For developers and power users, this creates a gap:
AI can answer questions, but it cannot reason with continuity, detect patterns across sessions, or behave consistently as the user’s context evolves.

AIELTH Core explores how to build a chat-first AI system that:
- Maintains longitudinal context safely
- Uses deterministic logic instead of prompt-only intelligence
- Separates fast LLM responses from slow, rule-based intelligence

The focus is not on features, but on building a reliable system for long-term reasoning.

**Challenges we ran into**

The main challenge was designing intelligence that is predictable and safe over time.

LLMs are probabilistic, but behavioral systems require determinism.
To solve this, the system separates fast LLM responses from a slower, rule-based intelligence layer that runs independently and is version-frozen.

Another challenge was handling guest users safely.
This was addressed using anonymous authentication with strict row-level security, allowing continuity without exposing identity or relying on spoofable client data.

**AOPS**

AIELTH Core is a systems-level AI project focused on building reliable, observable, and deterministic intelligence over time.

The project involves:
- Edge-function orchestration
- Clear separation between fast LLM paths and slow deterministic logic
- Strong authentication and row-level security
- System observability and safety gates

The work aligns with AOPS through its emphasis on system reliability, controlled execution, and long-term operational behavior rather than single-run demos.

### Keploy Blog Website
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/keploy-blog-website-6e7a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1j2NWJBvXZPS_-xf7H5rXzR24FBM89ROQ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=100433419285360774718&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Modern. Fast. Developer-friendly Blog

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The current **Keploy Blog Website** serves as a knowledge hub, but it faces challenges regarding user engagement, performance, and contributor onboarding. My project solves three key problems:

1. **User Retention & Experience**: By modernizing the UI with Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion, I am creating a "vibe-coded," visually stunning reading experience that keeps developers engaged longer.
2. **Performance & SEO**: The project addresses Core Web Vitals issues (LCP, CLS) by optimizing image loading and bundle sizes. This solves the problem of slow load times and improves organic search rankings.
3. **Developer Contribution Barrier**: The current codebase can be difficult for new students to navigate. By refactoring to TypeScript and standardizing components, I am lowering the barrier to entry, making it significantly easier for the community to fix bugs and add features.

### Keploy

> “Improving Keploy Blog Readability and Speed”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Keploy blog contains valuable technical content, but limitations in code block usability, layout consistency, and performance make it harder for developers to read, understand, and reuse code efficiently. This project improves the blog’s UI and performance to reduce friction in content consumption.

By enhancing code readability, navigation, responsiveness, and page load speed, the project makes it easier and safer for developers to learn concepts, copy code snippets, and access content across devices, ultimately improving the overall developer experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was improving code block UI without breaking existing blog styles or affecting performance. Since the blog contains multiple article formats, ensuring consistent code block rendering across different pages and screen sizes required careful testing.

Another challenge was optimizing performance while adding new UI features. To address this, I introduced changes incrementally, validated them using Lighthouse, and ensured that performance optimizations such as reducing layout shifts and avoiding unnecessary re-renders were applied alongside UI enhancements.

### Winter of Code 5.0
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/wallgoods-9941) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://surl.lu/zoycnr) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> By Kulshree Nakshane

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🔧 The Problem It Solves

WallGodds currently operates more as a **static wallpaper showcase** than a fully interactive platform. While the visual quality of wallpapers is strong, multiple usability, performance, and functionality gaps reduce user engagement and limit contributor participation.



## ❗ Key Problems Faced by Users and Contributors

### 1️⃣ Cluttered Navigation & Forced Device Categorization

Users must manually select device types (mobile, tablet, desktop), which interrupts natural browsing and makes wallpaper discovery cumbersome.

### 2️⃣ Non-Functional or Incomplete Core Features

* Search UI exists but is not implemented
* Upload pages lack backend integration
* User registration and profile management are incomplete

### 3️⃣ Poor Mobile & Tablet Experience

The platform lacks full responsiveness, resulting in broken layouts, slow interactions, and poor usability on smaller screens.

### 4️⃣ Performance Bottlenecks

Unoptimized images, absence of lazy loading, and no caching lead to slow page loads and high bounce rates.

### 5️⃣ Limited Community Engagement

Without profiles, likes, saves, feedback, or creator recognition, users have little incentive to return or contribute.


## 🚀 How This Project Solves These Problems

The **WallGodds UX Enhancement Project** transforms the platform into a **fast, intuitive, and community-driven experience** by systematically addressing UI/UX friction, performance issues, and missing backend functionality.


## 🎯 What People Can Use It For

### 🔍 Effortless Wallpaper Discovery

Browse wallpapers seamlessly across all screen sizes using advanced search, real-time filters, and smart recommendations—without device restrictions.

### ⚡ Fast & Smooth Browsing

Lazy loading, optimized images, and modern performance techniques ensure page load times under **2 seconds**, even on mobile networks.

### 🎨 Creator-Friendly Uploads

Designers can upload wallpapers, manage content, and gain visibility through user profiles, analytics, and community interaction.

### 👤 Personalized User Experience

Registered users can like, save, and organize wallpapers into collections, turning WallGodds into a personalized creative hub.

### ♿ Inclusive & Accessible Usage

WCAG AA-compliant components ensure accessibility for users with disabilities, making the platform safer and more inclusive.

## 🔄 How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

### 🔍 Finding Wallpapers

**Before:**
Manual browsing with no working search

**After This Project:**
Instant search with filters and autocomplete


### 📱 Mobile Browsing

**Before:**
Broken layouts and slow loading

**After This Project:**
Fully responsive, touch-optimized user interface


### ⬆️ Uploading Content

**Before:**
Upload UI exists but backend functionality is missing

**After This Project:**
Fully functional and secure upload system



### 👤 User Engagement

**Before:**
No user profiles or interaction features

**After This Project:**
Likes, saves, user profiles, and creator analytics



### ⚡ Performance

**Before:**
4–6 seconds page load time

**After This Project:**
Optimized experience with load times under 2 seconds



### ♿ Accessibility

**Before:**
Limited accessibility support

**After This Project:**
WCAG AA–compliant interface ensuring inclusive access



## 🌍 Overall Impact

This project removes friction at every stage of the user journey—from discovery to download to contribution. By completing missing features, optimizing performance, and redesigning the user experience, WallGodds becomes a **safe, efficient, and engaging platform** for both users and creators.

Ultimately, it enables WallGodds to evolve into a **scalable, community-powered, open-source wallpaper ecosystem**, rather than remaining a static gallery.

**Challenges we ran into**

## ⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into

### 🔧 Removing Forced Device Categorization

**Challenge:**
The gallery logic was tightly coupled with device-based categories (mobile, tablet, desktop). Removing this caused layout breaks and incorrect data rendering.

**How I Overcame It:**
I refactored the gallery to be device-agnostic and handled responsiveness purely at the UI level using adaptive grid layouts. This preserved existing routes while enabling seamless browsing across screen sizes.

---

### 🔍 Implementing Search with No Backend Support

**Challenge:**
The search UI existed, but there was no backend logic to support searching or filtering wallpapers.

**How I Overcame It:**
I optimized Firestore queries with proper indexing, implemented debounced search input, and structured wallpaper metadata (tags, categories) to enable fast and accurate filtering.

---

### ⚡ Performance Issues with High-Resolution Images

**Challenge:**
Large wallpaper files caused slow page loads and layout shifts, especially on mobile devices.

**How I Overcame It:**
I implemented lazy loading using Intersection Observer, introduced WebP image formats with fallbacks, and optimized responsive image delivery. This significantly improved load times and Core Web Vitals.

---

### ⬆️ Building a Secure Upload System

**Challenge:**
Handling large image uploads securely while providing progress feedback was difficult.

**How I Overcame It:**
I used Firebase Storage with file size and MIME-type validation, implemented upload progress tracking, and added Cloud Functions for post-upload processing and metadata validation.

---

### ♿ Ensuring Accessibility Without Compromising Design

**Challenge:**
Achieving WCAG AA accessibility while maintaining a clean and minimal UI required careful component design.

**How I Overcame It:**
I added ARIA roles, ensured keyboard navigation, improved color contrast, and validated components using automated accessibility tools and manual testing.

---

### 🧩 Balancing Features with Performance

**Challenge:**
Adding features like likes, saves, profiles, and analytics risked increasing bundle size and slowing down the application.

**How I Overcame It:**
I introduced route-based code splitting with `React.lazy()`, optimized shared components, and minimized unnecessary re-renders through efficient state management.

**The problem it solves**

**PlatformX** improves the reliability and usability of web platforms by fixing incomplete or inconsistent core features and strengthening user trust. It makes browsing, interaction, and participation smoother across devices while introducing **safeguards** and **structured feedback** that help users engage more confidently and fairly.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was working with partially implemented features and understanding existing application flows without complete documentation. In some cases, **UI components** appeared functional but were not fully wired to backend logic, which required careful code tracing and testing to identify the root cause.

Another challenge involved implementing **behavior-based **features such as **responsiveness** fixes and **proctoring mechanisms** without disrupting the existing user experience. This was addressed by incrementally introducing changes, testing them across different scenarios, and refining the logic to handle edge cases while maintaining stability.

**Ethereum Track**

The project aligns well with the **Partner Track** as it focuses on improving real-world **open-source **platforms by addressing existing gaps rather than building a solution from scratch. The contributions enhance usability, reliability, and integrity of partner-maintained projects through feature completion, fairness mechanisms, and maintainability improvements. This approach directly supports partner organizations by strengthening their products and making them more production-ready for real users.

### Anushka Maity
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/anushka-maity-436c) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://waste-food-management-iota.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Anushka Maity

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Food wastage remains a serious issue where usable food is discarded daily while many individuals and communities face food insecurity. This platform provides a digital solution to efficiently connect food donors with recipients, ensuring surplus food reaches those in need instead of going to waste.

**It solves these  problems :**

1. Reduces food wastage by enabling donors to share surplus food easily
2. Connects donors and recipients through a real-time, centralized platform
3. Simplifies the food donation and request process with an intuitive interface
4. Improves transparency and trust through user authentication and donation tracking
5. Supports NGOs, volunteers, and communities in organized food distribution
6. Encourages sustainable practices and social responsibility

**Challenges we ran into**

**Authentication & Authorization:**
Implementing secure user authentication using JWT was challenging, especially managing protected routes and token handling. This was resolved using backend middleware and frontend context for consistent auth state management.

**Frontend–Backend Communication:**
Integrating the React frontend with the Express backend caused issues like API errors and CORS problems. These were fixed by properly configuring API routes and middleware.

**State Management:**
Keeping donation and request statuses updated across the dashboard required careful state handling, which was improved by refetching data after key user actions.

**Database Design:**
Structuring MongoDB schemas for users, donations, and requests took multiple refinements to ensure data consistency and smooth querying.

**The problem it solves**

Open-source projects often become difficult to maintain and extend as they grow in complexity. This project focuses on improving reliability, usability, and developer experience by refining existing systems and adding better automation and documentation.

**Challenges we ran into**

While working on understanding multiple open-source codebases and their workflows, one of the main challenges was setting up local development environments and becoming familiar with large, unfamiliar code structures. Many projects have complex build systems and dependencies, which can be difficult to configure correctly for first-time contributors.

Another challenge was understanding how different modules interact internally, especially in projects that combine compiled languages with higher-level APIs. This required careful reading of documentation, studying example implementations, and reviewing existing issues and pull requests to understand design decisions.

To overcome these challenges, I followed contribution guides, set up small test programs to experiment with APIs, and actively explored issue trackers to understand common problems faced by users and maintainers. This helped me gain confidence in proposing realistic solutions and planning meaningful contributions.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The writers.keploy.io platform is a core space for community members to write.
publish and share technical content. However, the current UI/UX can feel
slightly cluttered and inconsistent, which affects readability, usability,
and contributor engagement.

Writers may find it harder to focus on content creation due to layout
inconsistencies, suboptimal typography, and limited responsiveness on
smaller devices. New contributors may also face friction while navigating
the platform, which can reduce participation.

This project solves these problems by improving visual hierarchy.
typography, spacing, and responsiveness. The goal is to make the platform
cleaner, more modern, and intuitive, enabling writers to focus on creating
quality content while readers enjoy a smoother reading experience.

### Civic Ledger
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/civic-ledger-eb25) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14Lj6owWauvk4fKENBXTyUKlGIqeSuxae/view?usp=drivesdk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> CivicLedger ensures every public service request

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Visual Studio Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Visual%20Studio%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Solving the Transparency Gap in Public Administration
CivicChain (implemented here as CivicLedger) addresses the fundamental lack of trust and traceability in government processes. In traditional systems, administrative requests and fund allocations often exist in "black boxes"—centralized databases that can be retroactively edited, deleted, or obscured by bad actors.

This prototype provides a decentralized framework where accountability is automated rather than promised.

1. For Citizens: Frictionless Accountability
Citizens often feel powerless after submitting a request for public services. CivicChain transforms this experience:

Immutable Proof of Submission: Once a citizen submits a request for a business license or road repair, it enters a public "Mempool." It cannot be "lost" in a stack of paperwork.

Real-Time Tracking: Citizens can use the Ledger Explorer to see exactly when their request was moved from pending to "committed" on the blockchain.

Auditability: Every record is cryptographically linked. If a government official tries to prioritize one request over another unfairly, the chronological history on the ledger provides the evidence needed for oversight.

2. For Government: Radical Transparency
Public officials can use the Consensus Node to manage and validate community needs without the risk of internal tampering:

Fraud Prevention: Because each block contains the hash of the previous one, changing a record from six months ago would require re-mining the entire chain. This makes retroactive corruption mathematically difficult and highly visible.

Centralized Verification, Decentralized Trust: Officials retain the power to "Mine" (verify and commit) transactions, but the results are broadcasted to a public ledger that they do not exclusively control.

Streamlined Audits: Instead of weeks of manual paper audits, internal and external auditors can verify the entire history of public works or land titles in seconds using the cryptographic hashes.

3. Key Use Cases
Land Registry: Preventing "land grabbing" by ensuring property titles are recorded on an immutable ledger that can't be altered by bribing a local official.

Public Works & Infrastructure: Tracking the lifecycle of a project from the initial citizen complaint (e.g., a pothole) to the allocation of funds and final completion.

Business Licensing: Providing a transparent queue for entrepreneurs, ensuring that licenses are granted based on the order of application and fulfillment of criteria.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a functional blockchain simulation within a single index.html file presented several unique architectural and logic hurdles. Here are the specific challenges encountered and how they were resolved:

1. Maintaining State During Re-renders
A significant hurdle was preventing the loss of user input when switching between the "Citizen" and "Government" tabs. Because the application uses a renderApp() function that clears and overwrites the innerHTML of the #app-root element, any text typed into the "Details" textarea would vanish if the user navigated away.

The Fix: I implemented a simple state management object (state.formType and state.formDetails).

The Implementation: I added oninput listeners to the form fields that update the global state in real-time. When the tab is re-rendered, the script checks these state variables and manually re-populates the input values.

2. Simulating Consensus Failures
In a real-world government blockchain, nodes might disagree or network latency might cause a block to fail. Initially, the "Mine Block" button worked 100% of the time, which felt unrealistic for a demonstration of robust technology.

The Fix: I introduced a simulated 10% failure rate in the mineBlock function using Math.random() < 0.1.

The Implementation: This required creating a more complex UI state for the button, transitioning from "Mining..." to "Consensus Failed" with a red error toast notification to teach the user that blockchain operations are not always instantaneous or guaranteed.

3. Cryptographic Visualization
A core challenge was making the "invisible" math of a blockchain visible to a non-technical user. Raw hashes are long strings that can break UI layouts and look intimidating.

The Fix: I created a simpleHash function to generate consistent 32-bit integer hashes and then formatted them as truncated hexadecimal strings.

The Implementation: In the Explorer, I used Lucide icons (lock and link) next to the hashes and utilized Tailwind’s truncate class and font-mono styling to make the cryptographic links look like a professional audit trail.

4. DOM Syncing with Lucide Icons
Because the UI is generated dynamically via JavaScript strings, the Lucide icons would often fail to render after a tab switch. The library looks for i tags when the page loads, but it doesn't automatically watch for new elements added to the DOM.

The Fix: I wrapped the icon initialization in the main rendering loop.

The Implementation: Every time renderApp() or showToast() is called, I explicitly trigger lucide.createIcons() to scan the new HTML and inject the SVG graphics.

**AOPS**

1. The Citizen-to-Government Pipeline
The project tracks the lifecycle of a civic request through three distinct stages:

Submission (The Request): Citizens select a service type (e.g., Business License, Land Registry) and provide details. This creates a digital transaction signed by a "Citizen Wallet".

Verification (The Mempool): Submitted requests are held in a "Mempool," a staging area for pending transactions. This ensures that once a request is made, it is visible to the public even before it is officially processed.

Commitment (The Block): A government official (acting as a consensus node) reviews the queue and "mines" the transactions into a block. This permanently seals the data into the chain.

2. Cryptographic "Proof of History"
The project uses specific technical mechanisms to ensure the track cannot be altered:

Hashing: Each block generates a unique hexadecimal hash based on its index, timestamp, data, and a random nonce.

Immutability: Every new block stores the previousHash of the block before it. This creates a mathematical link; if a past record is tampered with, the hashes for all subsequent blocks would break, immediately alerting auditors.

Validation: The system tracks which official node validated the block (e.g., "Gov-Node-01"), creating a clear trail of administrative responsibility.

3. Public Accessibility (The Audit Trail)
The Public Ledger Explorer serves as the project's tracking UI, allowing any user to:

Inspect Block Height: View the total count of blocks to see the system's growth.

Verify Timestamps: See exactly when a service request was officially recorded.

Trace Connections: Visually follow the "connecting line" between blocks, representing the unbroken chain of governance.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/wallgodsweb-0130) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xoae9Tupm0OSXyE2A5Um3plymtIBQfjXcTjZh4Q5tGc/edit?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Wallpapers, done right.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Finding high-quality wallpapers on the internet is often frustrating. Users usually have to deal with cluttered websites, inconsistent image quality, intrusive ads, slow loading times, or unclear usage rights. At the same time, designers and artists lack a simple platform to showcase their work and reach the right audience without losing credit or control over their creations.

WallGodds Web addresses these issues by providing a clean, fast, and creator-friendly platform dedicated entirely to wallpapers.

### What People Can Use It For

- **Discover high-quality wallpapers**  
  Browse a curated collection of wallpapers across different categories and resolutions, optimized for both desktop and mobile devices.

- **Download wallpapers safely and quickly**  
  Download optimized images without redirects, pop-ups, or misleading buttons, ensuring a smooth and secure experience.

- **Upload and showcase creative work**  
  Designers can upload their wallpapers, build a visible presence, and share their work with a wider community.

- **Use across all devices**  
  A responsive design ensures the platform works seamlessly on mobile phones, tablets, and desktops.

- **Save time and bandwidth**  
  Optimized image delivery and efficient loading reduce unnecessary data usage and waiting time.

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

- Eliminates the need to search across multiple unreliable websites  
- Removes friction caused by poor UI and slow performance  
- Simplifies the upload and discovery process for creators  
- Provides a focused platform without distractions or ads  

WallGodds Web turns wallpaper discovery and sharing into a straightforward, efficient, and user-friendly experience for both users and creators.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Since the project is actively evolving, my initial challenge was understanding the existing UI structure and identifying areas where the user experience could be improved. Rather than jumping directly into changes, I focused on exploring the application from a user’s perspective.

### Identifying UI and Responsiveness Issues

While testing the core application across different screen sizes, I noticed several UI and responsiveness issues, especially on mobile and tablet devices. Some layouts did not scale well, spacing was inconsistent, and certain components behaved differently across breakpoints.

**How I approached it:**
- Tested the application on multiple screen sizes and browsers
- Reviewed existing UI components and layout structure
- Noted patterns where fixed dimensions caused layout breaks
- Mapped out key pages that required responsive improvements

---

### Understanding an Existing Codebase

Another challenge was navigating a codebase built by multiple contributors. Understanding component structure, styling decisions, and data flow took time.

**How I approached it:**
- Read through existing components before proposing changes
- Compared UI behavior with design intent
- Documented findings instead of making rushed changes

---

### Planning Before Implementation

Instead of making quick fixes, the challenge was deciding **what to fix first** without breaking existing functionality.

**How I approached it:**
- Prioritized issues based on user impact
- Planned changes that align with the current design system
- Prepared to discuss findings with maintainers before implementation

---

Identifying and documenting these issues early helped build a clear roadmap for improving the UI and responsiveness of WallGodds Web in a structured and maintainable way.

### ORYCON
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/orycon-fad3) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IrILmXZwoHVp91ZsPmC863xefyUa0GOG/view?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> OSC Internal Event Management Tool

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Student communities and college societies often rely on scattered tools such as WhatsApp, Google Sheets, and manual processes to manage events. This leads to miscommunication, duplicated work, poor visibility across teams, and errors in attendance and task tracking.

This project solves these problems by providing a **single, centralized event management platform** that streamlines planning, execution, and post-event analysis.

**Key problems addressed:**
- Fragmented communication across multiple platforms
- Manual and error-prone attendance tracking
- Lack of role clarity and access control for teams
- Unstructured content creation and social media planning
- No unified system for feedback and event insights

**How the project helps:**
- Centralizes all event workflows in one platform
- Automates attendance using QR-based real-time verification
- Uses role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure secure and organized collaboration
- Enables structured task tracking, content drafting, and social media scheduling
- Provides feedback collection and analytics for continuous improvement

Overall, the platform reduces operational overhead, improves coordination between teams, and makes event management faster, more reliable, and scalable for student communities.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a multi-module, role-based system introduced several technical and architectural challenges.

**Key challenges faced and how I solved them:**

- **Designing scalable RBAC:**  
  Managing permissions for multiple teams required careful role mapping. I implemented a modular RBAC system that keeps authorization logic centralized and extensible.

- **Real-time attendance tracking:**  
  Ensuring accurate QR-based attendance with walk-in support was challenging. I optimized the verification flow to prevent duplicate entries and ensure real-time updates.

- **Managing complex workflows:**  
  Coordinating event planning, content, social media, and logistics in one system required clear separation of concerns. I solved this using a modular backend architecture and shared interfaces.

- **Monorepo management:**  
  Handling frontend and backend in a single codebase initially caused dependency issues. Using a Turborepo structure helped streamline builds and improve scalability.

- **Ensuring maintainability:**  
  To keep the project easy to extend, I focused on clean code practices, documentation, and Docker-based setup for consistent development and deployment.

These challenges helped me improve my understanding of system design, scalability, and real-world development practices.

**AOPS**

This project strongly aligns with the **Art of Problem Solving (AOPS)** track by applying **structured thinking, logical decomposition, and systematic problem-solving** to a real-world challenge.

Managing student communities and events involves **multiple interconnected problems** such as access control, real-time attendance, workflow coordination, and data organization. Instead of treating this as a single task, the project breaks it down into **independent, well-defined modules** that work together as a cohesive system.

**Key AOPS-aligned aspects of the project:**
- **Problem Decomposition:** Breaking a complex event management workflow into smaller, manageable components such as attendance, content, social media, and logistics.
- **Logical System Design:** Designing clear data flows, role-based permissions, and structured workflows to ensure correctness and reliability.
- **Optimization & Automation:** Replacing repetitive manual processes with automated, rule-driven systems like QR-based attendance and task tracking.
- **Scalability & Abstraction:** Using modular architecture to ensure the solution remains scalable as users, teams, and events grow.

By combining **analytical thinking** with **practical system design**, the project demonstrates how core problem-solving principles can be applied beyond mathematics to build efficient, scalable, and real-world software solutions.

### Winter of Code 5.0
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/winter-of-code-565a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1R1kt8cij0sPrYARog-ofHE_LN3zmDHxN/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116722295876881163507&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Proposal

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most traditional quiz and assessment systems are static and lack interactivity, leading to poor engagement and delayed feedback. Users often lose interest, and educators struggle to create exciting assessment experiences.

Rapid Quiz Relay introduces a real-time, gamified quiz environment that makes learning engaging and competitive. By incorporating relay-based gameplay, live leaderboards, and time-bound challenges, it transforms routine quizzes into interactive learning sessions.

This approach helps users learn faster, stay motivated, and participate actively, while enabling organisations to host scalable and engaging quizzes with ease.

**Challenges we ran into**

While working on Rapid Quiz Relay, I faced a few challenges:

Real-time leaderboard delays: Initially, scores only updated after a quiz ended. I solved this by integrating WebSockets to push live updates to all users.

Relay timer synchronization: Timers were inconsistent across users due to network latency. I implemented a server-side timer to ensure fairness.

UI performance issues: Frequent updates caused lag in React components. Refactoring state management and using React.memo improved responsiveness.

These experiences strengthened my skills in real-time web development, state optimization, and problem-solving under constraints.

[Satelli Nikhil](https://github.com/Nikhilll-dev-code)

> Accuracy in data. Confidence in code

![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Markdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/Markdown-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyPi](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern software systems rely heavily on APIs, yet ensuring that API behavior, testing, and documentation remain consistent over time is a persistent challenge. Teams often depend on manual testing or fragmented tools, which leads to unreliable integrations, outdated documentation, and delayed detection of breaking changes. This project addresses these challenges by focusing on improving the reliability and developer experience of automated API testing using specification-driven approaches. By validating real API behavior against defined specifications, developers can detect inconsistencies early, reduce manual testing effort, and maintain accurate, up-to-date documentation. The work improves how API test failures are reported, how edge cases in API specifications are handled, and how developers interact with testing results. This makes API testing more predictable, transparent, and suitable for real-world production environments.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the primary challenges was understanding and navigating a mature, production-grade open-source codebase with established conventions, testing pipelines, and CI workflows. Gaining clarity on how different components interacted required careful study of documentation, existing tests, and previous contributions. Another challenge was identifying meaningful improvements without introducing breaking changes. Since the project is used in real-world scenarios, even small changes needed to be carefully validated through automated tests and CI pipelines. Additionally, balancing feature improvements with clear and maintainable documentation required thoughtful design decisions to ensure that new contributors and users could easily understand and adopt the changes. These challenges were addressed through incremental development, frequent testing, and adherence to existing contribution guidelines, ensuring stability while delivering measurable improvements.

### ReZygisk
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rezygisk-2f03) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PerformanC/ReZygisk) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VUgwd5RvPs8lx8TF5dwYIqrMbklaw7NN/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=117310481471034988488&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Beyond Zygote: Enhanced Android Process Injection

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ReZygisk traditionally injects code only into processes that are created by the Android zygote system, which limits its ability to interact with system-level and non-ART processes. This restriction makes it difficult for developers to hook, monitor, or modify processes that are started outside the zygote, such as certain native services or init-spawned processes.
This project solves this limitation by enabling non-zygote process injection, allowing ReZygisk to attach to a broader range of Android processes.
How It Helps:
Enables developers to hook and analyze system and native processes
Improves compatibility with newer Android versions
Makes advanced instrumentation tasks easier and more flexible
Reduces dependency on closed-source or proprietary tools
Provides a safer, open-source solution for Android process modification
Overall, this enhancement expands ReZygisk’s capabilities, making Android development, debugging, and security research more powerful and accessible.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was understanding the existing ReZygisk codebase, as it involves low-level Android internals and process lifecycle management. The interaction between the zygote process, native services, and system-level processes was complex and required careful study.

Another major hurdle was identifying a safe and reliable way to inject code into non-zygote processes without affecting system stability. Since these processes are not forked from the zygote, the traditional injection mechanism could not be reused directly.

To overcome these challenges, I spent time analyzing related documentation, studying existing implementations, and reviewing discussions in GitHub issues. I broke the problem into smaller parts, tested changes incrementally, and relied on mentor feedback to validate the approach. This iterative process helped ensure compatibility while maintaining system safety.

**AOPS**

This project fits into the AOPS track as it involves contributing to a real-world open-source system-level project (ReZygisk). The work focuses on enhancing low-level Android process injection mechanisms by extending support beyond zygote-based processes. It requires understanding existing open-source code, proposing improvements, and implementing system-level enhancements. By addressing a confirmed GitHub issue and contributing to an active open-source repository, the project aligns with the goals of AOPS—promoting advanced open-source development, collaboration, and practical system programming skills.

[Paluru Tejaswini](https://github.com/Tejaswinipaluru)

**The problem it solves**

The current WallGodds web platform provides access to a large collection of wallpapers, but users face difficulty in discovering and managing wallpapers due to a cluttered interface and lack of proper categorization based on screen sizes. Navigation is not intuitive, and the absence of optimized UI/UX design leads to a confusing browsing experience.

In addition, performance issues such as slow image loading and inefficient data handling affect user satisfaction, especially for users with limited bandwidth or mobile devices. The backend system also needs better structure to support user uploads, authentication, and scalable data management.

This project addresses these challenges by redesigning the user interface, introducing clear wallpaper categorization, optimizing performance, and strengthening backend APIs. The goal is to transform WallGodds into a clean, fast, and user-friendly platform for discovering and sharing wallpapers.

By designing a modular backend that can integrate blockchain components, our project aligns with Ethereum’s goal of building trustless, transparent systems for real-world social impact use cases like donations and community-driven initiatives.

> Your emergency browser

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

LifeLine solves the problem of information chaos during crises.

Existing search engines prioritize clicks and SEO, which often buries life-saving protocols under ads or unverified rumors. LifeLine makes safety easier and faster by:

- Emergency Intent Detection: Instantly detects a crisis and prioritizes "Survival Protocols" over standard links.

- Voice-First Accessibility: Hands-free searching via the Web Speech API for users in high-stress or physical danger.

- Trust Filtering: Uses Pogo-sticking (Bounce) detection to identify "At-Risk Sources" and promotes verified data over misinformation.

- Reduced Friction: A Trie-based N-Gram model predicts technical safety terms before the user finishes typing, saving critical seconds.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle was the "Dual-Mode" State Desync, where the UI theme and search results wouldn't update simultaneously during a crisis detection. I solved this by making the Backend AI Classifier the "Source of Truth" through a React Context that forces the UI to wait for the data confirmation before switching. Additionally, implementing Pogo-Sticking Detection proved difficult due to tracking limitations, which I overcame by using a localStorage timestamp logic to catch users returning within 10 seconds, successfully identifying and downranking "Fake News" sources in real-time. Finally, I optimized the N-Gram suggestion engine by adding a Debounce timer to prevent server lag from rapid keystrokes.

> A reimagined version of Vanishing Tic-Tac-Toe

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Based on the Problem Statement **E01(The Chakravyuh of Shunya)**, we addressed the problem by building an AI Agent capable of playing Vanishing Tic-Tac-Toe optimally under dynamic board constraints. 
**The Rules of the Game are:**

- **THE 3-PIECE LIMIT**: Each player (X and O) can only have a maximum of three pieces on the board at any given time.
- **THE VANISHING ACT**: When a player places their 4th piece, their  1st piece (the oldest one) immediately vanishes from the board.
- **THE WIN CONDITION**: The first player to align three of their symbols in a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal row wins.
- **THE THREEFOLD REPETITION RULE**: To prevent the game from going on forever, if the same board state occurs three times during a match, the game is declared as a draw.

**The Features of the application are**:

- **GAME MODES**: We provide the user the ability to choose between 3 different modes.
      1. Player vs Player 
      2. Player vs Bot
      3. Bot vs Bot
- **FADING MECHANISM**: fading of the crown is going to vanish in the next move.
- **DEPLOYMENT**: Deployment on the web, allowing players to experience the game anytime, anywhere through a browser interface.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Brainstorming an efficient minimax algorithm where the bot has the most chances of winning.**
          We solved the issue by researching the algorithm in depth, understanding its working, and experimenting with different solutions while testing them side by side and optimizing the algorithm for better performance. 
2. **Merging branches across GitHub effectively.**
We addressed this by ensuring that all team members stayed up to date with the latest version of the code. This was achieved by regularly performing **git pull** after each commit and carefully resolving merges to avoid conflicts.
3. **Writing individual codes in different branches of git and then syncing them all to work as a single project.**
We solved this issue by trying to maintain consistency of the code throughout all the branches and regularly pushing and synchronizing commits.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**RapidSOS: Emergency Assistance at Your Fingertips**
**RapidSOS** is a Django-based web application designed to provide a fast, reliable way for individuals to alert their loved ones during emergencies. By bridging the gap between a user's real-time location and their emergency contacts via WhatsApp, it ensures that help can be coordinated instantly when every second counts.

**The Problem It Solves**
In many emergencies such as medical crises, accidents, or personal safety threats, individuals may be unable to make a phone call or provide precise location details verbally.

**Communication Barriers**: Traditional calling can be difficult in high-stress or loud environments.

**Location Accuracy**: Users often don't know their exact coordinates when in an unfamiliar area.

**Information Lag**: Relying on bystanders or manual messaging takes valuable time that could be saved with automation.

**How It Makes Tasks Easier**
**Centralized Management**: Users can manage their emergency contacts and view past alerts through a secure personal dashboard.

**Accessibility**: Since it is a web app, it doesn't require a heavy installation; it can be accessed from any mobile browser, making it highly portable.

**Automated Bridging**: By integrating with the Twilio API, the project automates the task of sending messages that would normally require manual typing and navigation, significantly reducing user effort during a crisis.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Twilio Sandbox Session Limits**
**The Problem**: Initially, SOS messages were not reaching the emergency contacts even though the Python logic was correct. I discovered that the Twilio Sandbox requires recipients to opt-in by sending a specific "join" code every 72 hours. If the session expired, the API would return a 403 Forbidden error.

**The Solution**:  I added detailed print debugging in the views.py loop to catch specific Twilio error codes in the VS Code terminal.
I implemented a pre-check step where I verified that all emergency contacts had an active sandbox session before conducting live tests.
